efforts.effort_name: Labor Reallocation, Care Bottlenecks & Offshoring Spillovers

wave1.lens_self_description: I answered purely as an outside-view base-rate scout: every CQ is anchored on the frequency of the widest defensible historical reference class (5-year OECD+China PPP growth windows since 1960, G7 real-yield decade averages since 1960, MOVE 10-year windows since 1988, ≥25% MSCI World drawdowns and their bond co-movement since 1970, OECD unemployment 5-year averages since 1999, sectoral real-wage divergences since 1980, capex-supercycle impairment episodes), adjusted ONLY for the near-deterministic arithmetic in the locked priors (headcount and PPP weights, debt/interest accounting); I forbade myself any reasoning about AI capability trajectories, model scaling, diffusion mechanisms, or any episode-specific causal story.
wave1.cq1_reasoning: Conjunct 1 (OECD-38 harmonized unemployment 5-yr average ≤5.5% over 2032-36). Reference class: OECD total harmonized unemployment rate, annual, 1999-2025 (FRED LRHUTTTTO1A156N/S, discontinued 2017, continued via OECD MEI). Observed: 6.6% (1999), 8.1% (2009), 8.3% (2010), 6.3% (2016), 5.5% (Dec 2017, OECD release Feb 2018), ~5.4% (2019), 7.1% (2020), ~4.9-5.0% (2023-25, series record lows). Of ~23 rolling 5-yr windows 1999-2025, only those ending 2022-2025 average ≤5.5% → unconditional base rate ~20%; extending the class pre-1999 (OECD 6-8% through the 1980s-90s) drops it to ~15%. Two mechanical adjustments UP: (i) starting level is the lowest in the series' history (~4.9%), and (ii) a shrinking OECD working-age headcount is near-deterministic over 10 years and mechanically suppresses the measured rate (Japan 1995-2025 ran 2.5-5.4% for three decades on exactly this arithmetic). Adjustment DOWN: the base rate of at least one OECD-wide recession year (growth <1%: 1974-75, 1980-82, 1991-93, 2001, 2008-09, 2020 → ~6 episodes/65 yrs) in any 5-year window is ~40%, and one recession adds 1.5-2.5pp for 2-3 years, pushing a 5-yr average to ~6.0-6.5%. Net conjunct 1 = 45%. Conjunct 2 (F+Q real median hourly wage growth exceeding J+K+M by ≥10.0pp cumulative, 2025-2036). Reference class: 11-year sector-group real wage divergences in OECD data since 1980. Divergences ≥10pp are COMMON but the sign has run the OTHER way in nearly every 11-year window for 45 years (skill-biased technical change: finance/professional services over construction/care). The base rate of the sign FLIPPING and holding ≥10pp for 11 years has one modern precedent only — the 2020-2024 US low-wage compression (bottom-decile real gains outpacing the top by roughly 5-8pp over 3-4 years, Autor-Dube-McGrew class of evidence), which is shorter and smaller than required and occurred at a decile, not sector-group-median, cut. Against it: ISIC Q is ~70% public/quasi-public financed and administratively wage-set — UK/Italy/Spain health-sector real median wages FELL over 2010-2019 — and the locked 2A fiscal block (subsidies already ~10.1% of Chinese fiscal expenditure; OECD net interest 2%→3% of GDP) says the transfer that would clear a care-wage repricing is already strained; Baumol means care-sector productivity cannot fund it internally. ISIC K real median wages are rent-protected. Conjunct 2 = 14%. Correlation: positive, +0.3 to +0.4 — tight labour markets are exactly the state in which bottom/physical wages compress upward (2021-24). Independent product 0.45 × 0.14 = 6.3%; correlation lift ≈ 1.4x → 8.8%. ANSWER 9.
wave1.cq2_reasoning: Conjunct 1 (GDP-weighted OECD-38 core CPI/PCE ≥2.50%/yr average, 2027-2036). Reference class: rolling 10-year windows of GDP-weighted OECD core inflation. Pre-1990 almost all windows clear 2.5% (1970-79, 1975-84, 1980-89, 1985-94 all ≥2.5%) → base rate ~45% over 1970-2025. Post-inflation-targeting (windows starting 1990 onward): 1990-99 ~2.8% yes; 1995-2004 ~2.0% no; every window from ~1996 to 2015 no; 2016-2025 ~2.3% borderline-no. That is roughly 3-5 of 26 → ~15%. Central-bank reaction functions are a structural feature, so I weight the post-1990 regime ~70/30 → ~24%. Mechanical adjustment UP: the window opens with 2026 core still elevated, so the first 2-3 years carry inertia that a mid-window regime shift cannot fully undo; also the locked 2A labour-supply arithmetic (old-age ratio 31%→39-41%) is a services-wage level-pusher. Conjunct 1 = 35%. Conjunct 2 (China headline CPI <1.50%/yr average, 2027-2036). Reference class: 10-year CPI windows for demographically contracting, high-savings, excess-capacity economies. Japan 1995-2025: all three decade windows <1.5% (3/3). China's own most recent window 2015-2024 ≈1.4% (yes, narrowly); 2022-2025 ≈0.4%. China 2000-2019 averaged ~2.6%, so the pre-2015 base rate is against it, but the locked 2A arithmetic (population −60M over 2026-35, worker/retiree 4.4→2.8) is the Japan configuration. Conjunct 2 = 65%. Correlation: mildly NEGATIVE, not positive. The channel that makes China <1.5% likely (contraction → excess goods capacity → exported disinflation) is the same channel that pushes OECD core DOWN. The offset is weak because OECD core is ~70-75% services, so I use ρ ≈ −0.1. Joint = 0.35 × 0.65 × 0.9 = 20.5%. ANSWER 20. Note this is the one place where coupling, rather than independence, makes a conjunction LESS likely than the naive product.
wave1.cq3_reasoning: Reference class 1 (unconditional): rolling 5-year windows of PPP-weighted combined OECD+China real growth since 1960. Approximate decade-average combined rates: 1960s ~5.3%, 1970s ~4.0%, 1980s ~3.6%, 1990s ~3.4%, 2000s ~3.0%, 2010s ~2.8%, 2019-2023 ~2.3%. The historical MINIMUM 5-year window is ~2.2-2.6% (2007-2011: OECD ~0.5% × 0.78 + China ~10.3% × 0.22 = 2.66%; 2019-2023: 1.3% × 0.72 + 4.7% × 0.28 = 2.26%). Unconditional distribution: median ~3.4%, P10 ~2.3%, P90 ~5.0%. The combined aggregate has never averaged below ~2.2% over five years, because the China catch-up leg always cushioned the OECD cycle. Reference class 2 (mechanical weight-and-headcount arithmetic, which I am permitted to apply): by 2032-36 China is ~30-32% of combined PPP GDP and OECD-38 ~68-70%. (i) OECD-38 leg: locked 2A gives per-capita 1.0%→0.6%/yr; OECD-38 population growth is ~0.25-0.30%/yr and falling → aggregate ~0.85-0.95%; allowing a modest productivity offset (2B AI-Q1 is only 23% for ≥+0.50pp, so the expected offset is ~+0.15-0.25pp) → OECD ~1.1%. (ii) China leg: reference class is post-peak-workforce converging economies at ~55-65% of frontier income — Japan 1992-2002 (1.0-1.3%), Korea 2015-2024 (~2.5%), Taiwan 2010-2020 (~3.0%); combined with 2A's stated −2.7pp/yr China aging drag → China P50 ~3.0%, P10 ~1.2%, P90 ~4.5%. Combined P50 = 0.70 × 1.1 + 0.30 × 3.0 = 0.77 + 0.90 = 1.67%, i.e. the arithmetic points BELOW anything in the historical record. I split the difference between the never-seen-before arithmetic and the strong historical level-persistence of OECD aggregate growth (1.8-2.0% in both the 2010s and 2020s despite a decade of identical aging warnings), landing P50 = 1.9%. Left tail: the ~40% base rate of an OECD-wide recession year inside any 5-year window, plus 2B AI-Q4's 66% capex-impairment marginal, gives P10 = 1.0% (a window containing one recession year). Right tail: P90 = 2.8% requires BOTH OECD ~1.8%+ and China ~4.5%+ — historically ordinary, arithmetically demanding — so I do not extend above 2.8%. The honest finding: this is a case where the reference class and the near-deterministic arithmetic disagree, and the arithmetic is the harder constraint.
wave1.cq4_reasoning: Starting level (locked 2A + GDP weights, arithmetic): US 10y TIPS 2.60% (FRED DFII10, Oct 30 2026). G7 market-GDP weights ≈ US 0.45, Japan 0.12, Germany 0.11, UK 0.08, France 0.08, Italy 0.06, Canada 0.05; with Japan ~0.8%, Germany ~0.5%, UK ~1.4%, France ~0.9%, Italy ~1.7%, Canada ~1.5% the weighted start is ≈1.68%. Reference class (decade averages of G7 real 10y, definitions vary across sources and I preserve that caveat): 1960s ~1.5% (RBA, "Three Decades of Real Interest Rates," 1991: real rates near a long-term average of about 1.5% in the 1960s); 1970s negative for much of the decade (same source); 1980s ~5% on a post-inflation-realized basis for the US (Macrobond decade chart: "the average post-inflation return was 5 percent in the 1980s" — best of the decades charted); 1990s ~4%; 2000s ~2%; 2009-2021 US TIPS ~0.2% (QIC); long-run US averages +2.0% for 1953-2025 on a nominal-minus-CPI basis (eco3min dataset) and 2.52% since 1958 (Cambridge Associates, which also gives JGB real 1.36% against a post-1982 Japanese average of 3.17%). Unconditional 5-year-window distribution: mean ≈ +1.7%, sd ≈ 1.8%, range −1.5% to +5.5%. Base rate of a decade average staying near its starting level: LOW. Decade-to-decade shifts have been 1.7-5.0pp (1970s→1980s ≈ +5pp; 1990s→2000s ≈ −2pp; 2000s→2010s ≈ −1.7pp). The probability that a 5-year-ahead 5-year average sits within ±50bp of today's level is only ~30% on this record, so I do NOT anchor tightly on 1.68%. Mechanical content of locked priors, both directions: debt accounting (gross public debt >100% of GDP by 2029, ~142% US / ~127% China by 2031, net interest 2%→3% of GDP, 3-yr P95 Debt-at-Risk ~117%, eroding convenience yields, levered basis-trade absorption) is a duration-supply and term-premium level-RAISER; against it, the 1945-1970s advanced-economy precedent is that high debt resolved through sustained NEGATIVE real yields (financial repression), and Japan 1995-2025 shows debt/GDP above 200% coexisting with ~0-1% real yields. IMF 2A also states that (r−g) worsens by ~+1.0pp "even where a frictionless r* eases," which is an r−g claim, not an r claim, so it does not pin the level. P50 = 1.9% (starting level plus a small debt-arithmetic tilt, anchored by the +2.0 to +2.5% long-run US mean). P10 = 0.4% (repression / secular-stagnation tail, well inside the 2010s realized range). P90 = 3.4% (term-premium normalization toward 1990s levels, still far below the 1980s).
wave1.cq5_reasoning: Conjunct 1 (ICE BofA MOVE 10-year average ≥105 over 2027-2036). Reference class: MOVE since 1988. I could not retrieve an authoritative year-by-year series back to 1988 — the only yearly archive found (Convextrade) starts in 2002 and is not a primary source, and I flag that limit. Cited long-run levels: lifetime average ~93 (Investcentre citing LSEG Refinitiv), long-run commonly put at 85-100, historical median ~80 (low-reliability source), with the post-QE pre-2022 era routinely 50-70 and 2022-23 spiking 120-190. Reconstructing rolling 10-year averages from these levels: 1988-1997 and 1990-1999 likely ≥105; 1995-2004 ~100; 2000-2009 ~95; 2005-2014 ~85; 2010-2019 ~70; 2015-2024 ~85. So roughly 6-9 of ~28 ten-year windows clear 105 → base rate ~25-30%. Current level ~75-90, so clearing 105 for a decade requires a sustained return to the pre-2003 rate-vol regime. Mechanical tilt UP from 2A duration-supply/plumbing arithmetic → conjunct 1 = 33%. Conjunct 2 (at least one ≥25% MSCI World peak-to-trough drawdown during which G7 GDP-weighted 10y nominal yields FAIL to fall ≥50bp, or rise ≥25bp). Step one, drawdown base rate: MSCI World declines ≥25% — 1973-74 (−43%), 1980-82 (~−27% USD), 1987 (~−24%, borderline), 1990 (−26%), 2000-02 (−49%), 2007-09 (−57%), 2020 (−34%), 2022 (−27%) → ~7-8 episodes in 55 years, ~1 per 7 years. Vanguard's MSCI-based chart counts 13 declines of 20%+ since 1972, consistent. Of ten 10-year windows since 1970, nine contained a ≥25% episode (only 2010-2019 did not: max ~−22%) → P(at least one) ≈ 80%. Step two, the CONDITIONAL bond-failure frequency: fails — 1973-74 (yields rose sharply), 1980-81 (rose), 1987 (US 10y rose ~90bp Aug-Oct, fell only AFTER the crash), 1990 (flat-to-up, Gulf oil shock), 2022 (rose ~200bp); passes — 2000-02 (fell >150bp), 2007-09 (fell >180bp), 2020 (fell ~100bp). That is 5 of 8 ≈ 62% unconditionally, but the split is entirely regime-sorted: every fail sits in an inflation-salient regime and every pass in the 1998-2021 disinflation regime. Schwab notes only two "triple bear" periods, both in the 1970s; Betashares/Lombard Odier over 118 years finds bonds fell with equities in only 3 of 34 negative-equity years, and that 2022 was the ONLY year in 118 with both down more than 10% — so the flight-to-quality regime is the historical default and the correlated regime is the exception. Using my own CQ2/CQ6 inflation-regime weights (~30% inflation-salient), blended conditional ≈ 0.30 × 0.80 + 0.70 × 0.22 = 0.39; allowing ~1.4 expected qualifying drawdowns per decade → conjunct 2 ≈ 0.80 × 0.53 ≈ 45%. Correlation: strongly positive, ρ ≈ +0.6 — both conjuncts are the same rate-vol/inflation-salient regime. P(conjunct 2 | MOVE ≥105) ≈ 0.70. Joint = 0.33 × 0.70 = 23%. ANSWER 23. Note the independence product would have given 15%, so here the conjunction discount is partly offset by regime co-movement; I report 23 rather than 15 for that reason, and rather than 33 because the MOVE leg binds.
wave1.cq6_reasoning: Applied the lexical-priority lock in order, using my own CQ3 (P10/P50/P90 = 1.0/1.9/2.8, implied σ ≈ 0.70pp) and my CQ2 inflation reference class. Step 1, A (growth ≥2.6%): from my CQ3, P(z ≥ (2.6−1.9)/0.70 = 1.00) = 15.9%. I mark that DOWN to 11% because A is a genuine arithmetic conjunction at the 0.70/0.30 weights: growth ≥2.6% needs China ≥5.6% if OECD is 1.3%, ≥4.5% if OECD is 1.8%, or ≥3.5% if OECD is 2.2% — i.e. BOTH a material OECD productivity offset AND China escaping the Japan/Korea post-peak-workforce path. Historical base rate of combined windows ≥2.6% is high (most windows since 1960), but every one of them was carried by a China/catch-up leg of 7-10%, which the locked headcount arithmetic removes. A = 11. Step 2, C (OECD core ≥2.7% AND growth <2.0%): base rate of true stagflationary 5-year windows since 1970 is ~3 of 11 non-overlapping windows (1974-78, 1979-83, and arguably 1990-94 in Europe/Japan) ≈ 27%, but 0 of 6 in the inflation-targeting era; blending ~70/30 toward the targeting regime gives ~15-18%. P(growth <2.0) from my CQ3 is ~55%, and conditional on core ≥2.7 the growth condition is partly self-selecting. C = 17. Step 3, D (growth <1.7% AND core <2.0%): P(growth <1.7) = Φ((1.7−1.9)/0.70) = Φ(−0.29) ≈ 39%; P(core <2.0) ≈ 45-50% on the 2000s-2010s reference class, and conditional on sub-1.7% growth it rises to ~55% (demand shortfall produces both, strong positive correlation). Joint ≈ 0.39 × 0.55 = 21%; marked UP to 24% because 2B AI-Q4 sits at 66% for capex impairment and the post-bust excess-capacity configuration is exactly D, and because my CQ3 P50 of 1.9% leaves D only 0.2pp away. D = 24. Step 4, B = residual = 100 − 11 − 17 − 24 = 48. Sum check: 11 + 48 + 17 + 24 = 100 exactly. CONSISTENCY CHECKS PERFORMED. (i) Against my CQ3: P50 = 1.9% falls inside B's residual cell (and 0.2pp above D's threshold), so B must carry the plurality and A cannot — it carries 48% and A carries 11%. The mass I assign to growth ≥2.6% (11%) is below the 15.9% my own CQ3 σ implies, which I justify above by the weight arithmetic; it is NOT above it, so no inconsistency in the permissive direction. (ii) Against my CQ2: CQ2's OECD conjunct (core ≥2.50% over 2027-2036) I put at 35% marginal; CQ6-C requires the stricter ≥2.70% over the shorter, later 2032-2036 window, at 17%. 17% < 35% as required, and the gap is the right size: a 2032-36 average ≥2.70% would almost certainly drag the 2027-36 average above 2.50% given the elevated 2026-28 starting inertia, so C ⊂ (CQ2 conjunct 1) is respected. (iii) C and D are disjoint by construction (C needs core ≥2.7, D needs core <2.0), and both are checked after A, so no double-counting.

hypothesis_critique.a: "SMOOTHLY" carries the entire failure. Reference class for large-scale occupational reallocation across a credential wall: the base rate of smooth transition is approximately zero. US manufacturing displacement 1999-2011 (the China-shock literature) shows displaced workers did NOT reallocate into growing sectors — local labour markets and the workers themselves showed persistent earnings losses a decade later; Trade Adjustment Assistance evaluations found target-sector reemployment well under a quarter and negative net earnings effects; Appalachian and Rust Belt retraining cohorts never closed the gap. Stock-flow mismatch is the binding arithmetic: the OECD care deficit is a FLOW of entrants needing 2-4 years of accredited training plus licensure, while displacement is a STOCK with median age in the 40s. A 45-year-old displaced paralegal faces a 3-5 year largely unpaid transition against a ~15-20 year remaining working life, which fails the private NPV test at any plausible care wage; US nursing programs already turned away tens of thousands of QUALIFIED applicants annually for want of clinical placements and faculty, so the licensing queue is supply-capped independently of demand. Three further frictions all point the same way: gender composition (ISIC Q is roughly 77-90% female; displaced ISIC J/K/M is near gender-balanced, so the reallocation requires a historically unprecedented male inflow into care), physical strain (nursing-aide musculoskeletal injury rates run several multiples of the all-industry average, and rise steeply with worker age), and geographic immobility plus housing costs (care demand is distributed with the elderly, cognitive employment is metro-concentrated, and OECD interregional mobility has FALLEN for 40 years). Finally Baumol plus the locked 2A fiscal strain means the wage signal that would have to clear the market cannot be funded: ISIC Q is ~70% public or quasi-public financed, and 2A already has net interest going 2%→3% of GDP and China's pension subsidies at ~10.1% of fiscal expenditure. Score 4.
hypothesis_critique.b: "BLOCKS" and "SEVERELY" both fail, and they fail for the same reason: the plank nets two legs that move in OPPOSITE directions and then reports only one. Virtual leg (compression): India IT-BPM exports at ~$280B scale and Philippine BPO at ~1.7M+ workers are genuinely exposed, but the reference class for trade-exposure shocks to emerging-economy service exports is recovery, not destruction — the Y2K-bust hit Indian IT for 1-2 years before growth resumed, and the 2016-2020 wave of BPO-automation forecasts did not materialize at the predicted scale. Physical leg (expansion): the locked 2A demographic arithmetic (OECD old-age ratio 31%→39-41% by 2036, on track for 52% by 2060) is a near-deterministic increase in OECD demand for nurses, care aides and skilled trades, and the base rate of OECD destination countries loosening health-worker and trades migration under a visible care shortage is high (Germany, Japan, UK, Canada, Gulf all did so in the 2010s-20s). Remittance arithmetic decides the net: Philippine remittances ~$38-40B are ~8-9% of GDP and overwhelmingly from PHYSICAL migration (seafarers, nurses, domestic and construction workers in the GCC), not from BPO; Indian remittances ~$125B are only ~3.3% of GDP and likewise physical-migration-driven. So the channel the plank says is blocked is the smaller one for the Philippines on a GDP basis and the diversifiable one for India, while the channel aging mechanically expands is the remittance channel. Net external shock is materially negative for Philippine BPO EMPLOYMENT (urban, young, English-speaking, female-skewed, politically salient) and roughly neutral-to-positive for Philippine and Indian GDP and external accounts. The distributional story inside each country is real; "severely suffer" at the national-aggregate level is not. Score 15.
hypothesis_critique.c: No single word fails outright — this is the most-often-correct plank, which is why it scores highest, but "HOT" carries the risk at the front end and the implicit "and stays down" at the back. The reference class strongly supports the shape: in every inflation-targeting-era overshoot (1990-94, 2008, 2011, 2021-25) GDP-weighted OECD core inflation reverted toward target within a decade, and 10-year windows averaging ≥2.5% are rare post-1995 (roughly 3-5 of 26). So "then falls in the 2030s" is the modal path and I would put ~65-70% on the back half alone. The front half is what pulls the score down. "The next few years" starting from a late-2026 vantage asks for a NEW hot stretch, not the continuation of one, and the locked 2A China leg cuts against it: a −60M population contraction with pension subsidies at ~10.1% of fiscal expenditure is the Japan configuration, and the exported-goods-disinflation channel from that is a direct drag on OECD core. The plank also omits the asymmetric alternative my CQ6 puts 24% on — that the next decade is DISINFLATIONARY throughout (post-capex-bust excess capacity, BIS-style labour-income demand shortfall), in which case the plank is wrong at the front and accidentally right at the back for the wrong reason. Joint probability of the full stated shape (hot first, falling later) ≈ 0.55. Score 55.
hypothesis_critique.d: "EVENTUALLY" and "WINS" are both unfalsifiable as written, and "EXPONENTIAL" is the mechanism claim my lens forbids me to evaluate — so I score the plank on the base rate of its reference class, which is the single most reliable result I have. Reference class: dated forecasts that technology would offset demography or restore aggregate growth. Japan, 1990s, robotics-and-automation-will-offset-aging: FALSE on the stated metric — Japanese GDP per working-age person grew respectably but aggregate real growth averaged ~0.8%/yr for three decades, which is precisely the "demography won" outcome. The 1960s automation-will-cause-mass-unemployment forecasts: FALSE. ICT-will-restore-productivity, 1987-1995 (the Solow paradox decade): FALSE, then true for one window 1995-2004, then false again. Of roughly six to eight named episodes in this class, at most one or two resolved true within their own stated decade → base rate ~20%. "Eventually" with no date removes any resolution criterion, and "wins" specifies no level, so the plank is constructed to survive the resolution it would fail. Read strictly — aggregate combined real GDP growth returning to or exceeding its pre-aging path by Dec 31 2036 — my own CQ3 P50 of 1.9% and CQ6-A at 11% say it does not. Score 18.

key_drivers: PPP weight arithmetic in CQ3: by 2032-36 the combined aggregate is ~70% OECD-38 / ~30% China, so the China catch-up leg that kept every historical 5-year window above ~2.2% has shrunk to a third of the weight at a third of its former growth rate. This single mechanical fact drives my CQ3 P50 of 1.9% below anything in the 1960-2025 record and forces B+D to carry 72% of CQ6.

The ~40% base rate of at least one OECD-wide recession year inside any 5-year window (6 episodes in 65 years), which is the dominant left-tail driver of CQ3's P10 (1.0%) and the dominant reason CQ1's unemployment conjunct is 45% rather than 70% despite a record-low 4.9% starting level.

Regime-sorting of the equity/bond correlation: ALL five historical ≥25% drawdowns in which G7 yields failed to rally sit in inflation-salient regimes (1973-74, 1980-81, 1987, 1990, 2022) and all three flight-to-quality passes sit in 1998-2021. CQ5 is therefore not an independent conjunction but a single bet on which regime 2027-2036 is in, which is why I report 23 rather than the 15 independence would give.

Administrative and fiscal wage-setting in ISIC Q plus Baumol: ~70% of care-sector compensation is publicly financed, 2A already has net interest going 2%→3% of GDP and Chinese pension subsidies at ~10.1% of fiscal expenditure, and the 2010s precedent is FALLING real health-sector median wages in several OECD members. This caps CQ1's wage-divergence conjunct at 14% and is why I expect the barbell to run through hyperscaler/finance rents rather than through care-wage repricing.

Low base rate of decade-average real-yield persistence: decade-to-decade G7 shifts have run 1.7-5.0pp, so I give CQ4 a 3.0pp P10-P90 span around a P50 only 22bp above the ~1.68% GDP-weighted starting level, with the 1945-70s repression precedent and Japan 1995-2025 both live in the lower tail.

Base rate of dated 'technology offsets demography' claims resolving true within their own decade (~1-2 of 6-8 episodes, ~20%), which is the binding constraint on hypothesis plank (d), on CQ6-A at 11%, and on my refusal to lift CQ3's P90 above 2.8%.

falsification_signposts.signpost: OECD-38 or large-member accredited nursing/care-worker program COMPLETIONS (not enrolments, not announced seats) rise by more than 25% above their 2025 level, with the share of entrants aged 40+ exceeding 15%, as reported in OECD Health at a Glance 2034 or national regulator registers.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: Directly falsifies my licensing-queue and stock-flow argument, which is the load-bearing reason CQ1's wage-divergence conjunct is only 14% and hypothesis (a) is 4. Would move CQ1 from 9 to ~20-25, (a) from 4 to ~25, and shift ~5pp of CQ6 mass from D into B.

falsification_signposts.signpost: Real median hourly wage growth in ISIC F+Q exceeds ISIC J+K+M by >=5.0pp cumulative over 2025-2031 (half the CQ1 threshold at roughly half the horizon) in OECD Earnings or national median-hourly series, WITHOUT a concurrent rise in the public health/care share of GDP of more than 1.0pp.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: Falsifies my Baumol-plus-fiscal-cap claim that care wages cannot clear without an unaffordable transfer. Would roughly double CQ1 (9 to ~18-20) and move CQ6 mass from D toward B; it would also raise my score on the barbell reading implicit in 2B's AI-Q5.

falsification_signposts.signpost: A MSCI World peak-to-trough decline of >=25% occurs and G7 GDP-weighted 10y nominal yields FALL by >=100bp during the drawdown window (clean flight-to-quality), while the trailing 3-year MOVE average sits below 95.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: Falsifies my inflation-salient-regime weighting, which drives both CQ5 and my CQ4 upper tail. Would cut CQ5 from 23 to ~10-12, pull CQ4 P50 down ~40bp to ~1.5% and P90 to ~3.0%, and move ~4pp of CQ6 mass from C into D.

falsification_signposts.signpost: Combined OECD-38 + China PPP-weighted real GDP growth averages >=2.6%/yr over Jan 1 2029 - Dec 31 2032 (IMF WEO PPP-weighted aggregates, constant-PPP basis), with China above 4.0%/yr in at least three of those four years.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: Falsifies my core claim that the weight arithmetic has removed the catch-up cushion. Would move CQ3 P50 from 1.9 to ~2.4 and P90 to ~3.3, raise CQ6-A from 11 to ~25 at the expense of D (24 to ~12), and raise hypothesis (d) from 18 to ~35.

falsification_signposts.signpost: OECD-38 harmonized unemployment prints a 3-year average at or below 4.6% over 2030-2032 (below anything in the 1999-2025 series) with no OECD-wide recession year, confirming that the shrinking working-age headcount mechanically dominates the cycle.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: Confirms the demographic-arithmetic leg I used to lift CQ1's unemployment conjunct to 45% and would push it to ~65%, raising CQ1 from 9 to ~13-14 even with the wage conjunct unchanged; it would also strengthen the labour-scarcity adoption pull that is my stated coupling tension against 2B's AI-Q2.

falsification_signposts.signpost: Cumulative announced-hyperscaler-buildout impairments, cancellations and abandoned-site write-offs stay BELOW 10% of announced capacity through 2032, with net external AI software/API revenue exceeding 1.0x annualized AI compute D&A in every year 2029-2032.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: Falsifies my claim that 2B's AI-Q4 at 66% sits BELOW the ~80% capex-supercycle impairment base rate. Would remove the capex-bust support for CQ6-D (24 to ~16), move that mass to B and A, and lift CQ3 P50 by ~0.15pp.

wave1.coupling_tension: The sharpest tension is 2B's AI-Q2 (OECD-38 share of firms >=10 employees using AI directly in production >=50% by 2036) at 21.3% raw. Held with demographics EXOGENOUS that number is defensible as an adoption-skepticism prior. Once the 2A block is endogenous it is too LOW, and the direction is unambiguously UP. Two reasons, both outside-view only. First, the general-purpose-technology diffusion base rate over an 11-year window is far faster than 21%: EU/OECD firm-level adoption of broadband went from near zero to ~80% of firms with 10+ employees in about a decade, cloud computing from ~19% (2014) to ~45% of EU firms in ten years, ERP and e-invoicing similar — the base rate of a cheap, vendor-pushed, horizontally applicable business input reaching a 50% firm-count threshold in 11 years is on the order of 50-65%, not 21%. Second, and this is the coupling proper, the locked 2A demographic arithmetic is a DEMAND PULL on adoption, not merely a growth drag: an old-age ratio going 31% to 39-41% with a shrinking working-age headcount is a near-deterministic labour-scarcity and reservation-wage signal, and the historical reference class for forced mechanization under labour scarcity (post-Black-Death factor substitution, 1950s-60s European guest-worker-constrained manufacturing, Japanese industrial-robot density after its 1995 workforce peak reaching the world's highest, US agricultural mechanization after the 1964 Bracero termination) shows scarcity raising ADOPTION reliably. A firm-count adoption threshold is also the easiest of the six 2B marginals to clear, because it counts firms, not value. I would put AI-Q2 at 38-45% once demographics are endogenous, versus the locked 21.3%. Crucially, this upward revision does NOT propagate to AI-Q1 or to my CQ3, and that asymmetry is itself the finding: broad firm-count adoption under labour scarcity is fully compatible with thin measured TFP (2B AI-Q1 at 23%) and with my CQ3 P50 of 1.9%, because the sectors absorbing the demographic burden — ISIC Q care, ISIC F construction — are precisely the Baumol-exposed, licensure-gated, physically embodied sectors where adoption changes headcount requirements least. In short: endogenizing demographics raises ADOPTION and leaves PRODUCTIVITY roughly where 2B put it, which pushes the joint distribution toward the Hulten-ceiling and bifurcated-barbell cells (my CQ6 B+C+D = 89%) rather than toward A. A second, non-demographic tension worth flagging: 2B's AI-Q4 at 66.0% sits BELOW its own reference-class frequency. The base rate of announced capex supercycles ending >=20% impaired is roughly 5 of 6 named episodes (British railway mania 1840s, US rail 1870s-90s, telecom/fibre 1999-2002 where the large majority of laid fibre stayed dark, US shale 2014-2020 with hundreds of billions in write-downs, US nuclear 1975-85 with around 100 cancelled reactors; Japan's 1980s domestic capex is the partial exception) → ~80%. Coupling with 2A's financial-plumbing block (~$1.4T of circular vendor/cloud/chip commitments against ~$300B equity and ~$650B debt, plus the +2.4pp Debt-at-Risk sensitivity to a 20% AI-led equity valuation shock) pushes it higher still, not lower. Direction: UP, to ~78-82.

wave1.lens_self_description: Pure inside-view causal-mechanism modeling: I built an explicit signed transmission chain from the 65+/80+ wave through care-labour demand, the non-substitutable hands-on care task, credentialing throughput, reservation-wage gaps and Baumol pass-through into prices, yields and the India/Philippines virtual-vs-physical export legs, and I forbade myself any appeal to base rates or reference-class frequencies (no "MOVE has averaged X", no "recessions occur every N years", no "OECD unemployment has historically been Y") so every number is the model's output.
wave1.cq1_reasoning: CAUSAL CHAIN (sign, magnitude to 2036). [65+ pop +2.2%/yr, 80+ +3.5%/yr] --(+, e_caredemand|65+ = 1.25)--> [required OECD-38 formal care FTE +2.6%/yr = +30%, i.e. +22-25M FTE]. [20-64 pop -0.3%/yr] --(-, mechanical)--> [domestic entrant pool -4% cumulative]. [AI in J/K/M] --(-, 15-30% of task-hours, entry-level culled first)--> [6-12M gross displaced cognitive workers 2025-36]. [displaced cognitive worker] --(+, e_cross = 0.07 ONLY)--> [hands-on care/construction entrant]; the gates on that arrow are the reservation-wage gap (J/K/M median ~$35-45/hr vs aide tier ~$16-19/hr, -55%), the licensing queue (RN 3-4yr + licensure; LPN/PSW 0.5-1yr; trades apprenticeship 3-4yr), age of the displaced (modal 42-55, so 10-20yr amortization of retraining vs 25-40 for a school-leaver), gender composition (care 77-88% female; displaced pool in K and IT male-skewed), injury/strain (aide MSD rates among the highest of all occupations; construction DART ~2.5x services), and geographic immobility (care demand is suburban/rural/low-wage, cognitive workers sit in high-housing-cost metros). [care FTE gap ~20-25%] --(+, 1/e_supply)--> [shadow wage of a care FTE +60-90% real by 2036] --(blocked by 2A fiscal strain, ~70-80% of LTC publicly financed)--> [OBSERVED real care wage only +15-25%; residual clears as rationing: LTC waitlists, bed-blocking, and 1.5-3M OECD prime-age informal family carers (disproportionately women 45-60) leaving paid work, a second-round -0.3 to -0.5% hit to employment]. CONJUNCT 1 (unemployment avg <=5.5% over 2032-36): the shrinking 20-64 denominator mechanically suppresses the rate (-0.4pp over the decade), and the care/construction sinks absorb low-skill slack; against it, structural frictional unemployment from the e_cross=0.07 blockage adds +0.3-0.6pp of long-duration white-collar joblessness, and the 2A capex-impairment channel plausibly puts one recession inside the window. Headroom above the current ~4.9-5.0% level is only ~0.6pp. Mechanism marginal: 0.55. CONJUNCT 2 (F+Q median real hourly growth exceeds J+K+M by >=10.0pp, 2025-36): within-job scarcity wedge is large (F+Q +19-26% cumulative vs J+K+M +3-9%, gap +12-19pp) BUT the measure is a MEDIAN, and composition runs against it in both sectors: Q's median is diluted by 30-35% growth in aide/migrant employment at ~45% of the sector median (-3 to -5pp), while J/K/M's median is mechanically LIFTED by culling the bottom quintile (entry-level cut ~25% moves the median up ~5 percentile points, +3 to +4pp). Composition wedge -7 to -9pp. Net measured gap distribution centres on +4 to +9pp: marginal 0.25. CORRELATION: the scarcity common factor couples them positively, but the displacement leg couples them negatively (the displacement big enough to flatten J/K/M real medians is the displacement that raises unemployment); net rho = +0.15, so P(both) ~ 0.55 x 0.25 x 1.15 = 0.158. CQ1 = 16.
wave1.cq2_reasoning: Conjunct A: OECD-38 GDP-weighted core >=2.50%/yr avg 2027-36. Mechanism decomposition of core: care/health/social services + shelter/construction are ~45-50% of the core basket. Bottleneck arithmetic: excess care wage growth of ~2pp/yr over economy-wide, 0% measured care productivity growth (Baumol), 70% labour share in care, 13-14% core weight -> +0.20pp/yr on core; the F channel (construction cost -> shelter/repair/imputed rent) adds +0.08pp. Total bottleneck contribution +0.28pp/yr on top of an AI-and-China-deflated goods core of ~0.0-0.5% and a non-care services core of ~2.3%. Weighted result sits at ~2.45-2.60%, i.e. the threshold is almost exactly the mechanism's central value, with the 2027-32 capex-digestion interval (2B AI-Q4 at 66%) pulling the first third of the window down. Marginal 0.53 unconditional. Conjunct B: China headline CPI <1.50%/yr avg 2027-36. Mechanism: -60M population 2026-35 with worker/retiree 4.4->2.8; retiree consumption baskets are care- and service-heavy but income-constrained by a pension system already absorbing 2.9T RMB of subsidy, so the dissaving channel is weak; manufacturing capacity built for a larger domestic cohort plus a deleveraging property stock makes the output gap chronically negative; the labour-scarcity wage channel that is inflationary in the OECD is in China swamped by the demand-side contraction and by automation substitution. Marginal 0.78. CORRELATION: negative on the dominant transmission channel - China's excess capacity is exported as OECD goods deflation, so the world in which China prints <1.5% is also the world in which OECD core goods pull the OECD aggregate below 2.5%. rho ~ -0.10, so P(A|B) ~ 0.49. Joint = 0.49 x 0.78 = 0.382. CQ2 = 38.
wave1.cq3_reasoning: PPP weights 2025: OECD-38 ~65% (US ~26pp), China ~35%. OECD-38 build-up for 2032-36: per-capita baseline 0.6%/yr (2A, post-aging) + population +0.2%/yr (migration-driven, itself partly the physical-care inflow) = 0.80%; plus AI TFP contribution, which I take as +0.28pp - slightly above a pure 2B read because labour scarcity is a demand pull for automation (e_adoption|realwage = 0.4-0.6, so a 20% real care-wage rise induces ~10% labour-saving capital deepening), but net of a Baumol REALLOCATION DRAG of -0.15 to -0.20pp/yr. That drag is explicit: moving 3.5-4pp of hours into a sector with ~0% productivity growth and ~0.6x average output per hour costs ~0.05pp/yr in growth-rate terms plus ~0.13pp/yr in level-convergence terms over 11 years; plus retirement-age extension adds ~+0.15pp of hours. OECD-38 P50 = 1.2%/yr. China build-up: labour force -1.2 to -1.5%/yr, capital contribution decaying to ~+2.3pp as the property and infrastructure stock overshoots a shrinking cohort, TFP +0.9 to +1.2pp with heavy automation substitution, aging drag per 2A (-2.7pp/yr relative to a no-aging counterfactual) already embedded. China P50 = 2.8%/yr. Combined P50 = 0.65(1.2) + 0.35(2.8) = 1.76 -> 1.8%. P10 = 1.0%: a within-window recession plus a harder China landing plus post-impairment excess capacity (the D-regime mechanism). P90 = 2.8%: AI TFP at the top of the 2B range (+0.6pp), the documentation/monitoring channel converting into real measured care output, and a 2032-36 migration surge that relieves the care constraint. The distribution is left-skewed because the weakest-link structure caps the upside (see weakest link) but the fiscal/financial channel has no symmetric floor.
wave1.cq4_reasoning: Starting point reconstructed from 2A plus G7 GDP weights (US ~45%, Japan ~10%, Germany ~10%, UK ~7%, France ~7%, Italy ~5%, Canada ~5%): 0.45(2.60) + 0.10(0.6) + 0.10(0.9) + 0.07(1.6) + 0.07(1.2) + 0.05(1.9) + 0.05(1.7) = ~1.70% today. Mechanism to 2032-36, decomposed into r* and term premium. r* DOWN: the 50-64 pre-retirement bulge keeps desired saving high through the early 2030s (the dissaving cohort is not yet dominant in the OECD, unlike Japan/Italy); g falls to my CQ3 1.2% OECD figure, and capital-concentrated income per BIS Box C has a higher saving propensity, so the demand-shortfall channel is worth -40 to -70bp. TERM PREMIUM UP: gross public debt >100% of GDP by 2029 with net interest 2->3% of GDP and P95 Debt-at-Risk 117%, care and pension claims that cannot be deferred because the care shadow price is rising (my weakest link is itself a fiscal object), eroding sovereign convenience yields, and basis-trade/hedge-fund absorption replacing price-insensitive official and bank demand - worth +70 to +110bp. IMF's (r-g) worsening by +1.0pp is the net of these in the same direction I derive. Net P50 = 1.70 - 0.55 + 0.90 = ~2.05 -> 2.0%. P10 = 1.1%: post-impairment demand shortfall plus financial repression / renewed central-bank duration absorption (the D regime, where the care bottleneck is suppressed by rationing rather than spending). P90 = 3.1%: fiscal dominance with the care/pension claim monetized at the long end and the term premium repricing, which is the same world as CQ6-C. Japan's weight is the main anchor keeping the P50 near 2 rather than above it, and that anchor is itself eroding.
wave1.cq5_reasoning: Conjunct A: MOVE averaging >=105 over a full 10 years. Mechanism for structurally higher rate vol: (i) the inflation process becomes two-sided rather than one-sided - care/construction bottleneck inflation at +0.28pp/yr pushing up against China/AI goods deflation pushing down, so each data print is informative about which force dominates, which is exactly what raises implied rate vol; (ii) supply-driven duration risk from 2A debt dynamics with a price-insensitive marginal buyer absent; (iii) levered basis-trade intermediation converts flow shocks into yield gaps. Against: vol is multiplicative and mean-reverts hard in quiet years, and a 10-year AVERAGE of 105 requires roughly half the window at stress levels. Marginal 0.42. Conjunct B: at least one episode with MSCI World -25% peak-to-trough where G7 10y nominals fail to fall >=50bp (or rise >=25bp) inside the drawdown window. Sub-step 1: P(at least one -25% drawdown in 10 years) = 0.72 on mechanism - 2B AI-Q4 at 66% already posits an impairment/revenue-coverage failure, index concentration in AI-levered names is high, and the $1.4T commitment stack rests on ~$300B equity and ~$650B debt, so the equity leg is nearly implied by the locked priors. Sub-step 2: P(the no-rally type | a -25% drawdown occurs) = 0.55. A pure capex-bust drawdown is disinflationary and bonds rally hard (that is the D regime and it FAILS the condition); the no-rally version requires the drawdown to be driven by, or to collide with, the fiscal/term-premium channel - a Debt-at-Risk repricing, a care/pension fiscal claim shock, or an inflation-bottleneck print. Given my CQ4 term-premium mechanism and the fact that over 10 years there are likely 2-3 drawdown episodes of differing type, 0.55 for at least one being no-rally. Conjunct B = 0.72 x 0.55 = 0.40. CORRELATION: strongly positive, rho ~ +0.55, because the same fiscal/term-premium mechanism generates both high rate vol and the bond-fails-to-rally signature; P(A|B) ~ 0.70. Joint = 0.40 x 0.70 = 0.28. CQ5 = 28.
wave1.cq6_reasoning: Applied the lexical lock in order. Step 1, A: P(coupled growth >=2.6%) read off my own CQ3 distribution (P10 1.0 / P50 1.8 / P90 2.8, left-skewed): 2.6% sits near the 87th percentile, so P(A) = 12. Step 2, C: requires OECD-38 core >=2.7% over 2032-36 AND growth <2.0%. From my CQ3, P(growth<2.0) = 0.62. My CQ2 work puts the 10-year OECD core central value at ~2.45-2.60%, and the 2032-36 sub-window is the MORE inflationary half (the 65+/80+ wave and the care shadow price peak late, while the capex-digestion disinflation is front-loaded in 2027-31), so P(core>=2.7% over 2032-36) = 0.32 - and it is positively correlated with low growth through the supply-wall mechanism (grid, care, construction), so P(both) = 0.32 x 0.70 = 0.22 -> 23. Step 3, D: requires growth <1.7% AND core <2.0%. P(growth<1.7) = 0.45; P(core<2.0 | growth<1.7) = 0.40, since the low-growth branch splits between the stagflationary supply-wall version (already counted in C) and the post-impairment demand-shortfall version where BIS-style labour-income deficit suppresses the care wage pass-through through rationing rather than spending -> 0.18 -> 18. Step 4, B = residual = 100 - 12 - 23 - 18 = 47. CONSISTENCY CHECK PERFORMED: (i) my CQ3 P50 of 1.8% falls inside B's 1.7-2.5% band, and B is correctly my modal cell - it is also literally the regime my mechanism describes (physical/care scarcity rents plus hyperscaler rents coexisting with white-collar compression, with the steep real term premium of my CQ4 P50 of 2.0%), so the mass placement is not an artifact. (ii) Against CQ2: C requires core >=2.7% on the 2032-36 window, a strictly tighter threshold than CQ2's >=2.50% on 2027-36, and C=23 is correctly below CQ2's 38 (and below the 53 unconditional OECD-core marginal inside CQ2). (iii) A+B = 59 versus P(growth>=1.7) = 0.55 from CQ3 - the 4pp wedge is exactly B's residual low-growth/moderate-inflation leftover cell (growth <1.7% with core between 2.0% and 2.7%), which the lock assigns to B, so the two are consistent. (iv) I could NOT put large mass on A given a 1.8% P50, and did not.

hypothesis_critique.a: The failure word is SMOOTHLY, and secondarily SUPPLY. The cross-occupational transition elasticity from displaced cognitive workers into hands-on care is e_cross = 0.07, i.e. essentially zero: a -55% reservation-wage gap at the aide tier, an 18-42 month credential queue (3-4 years for RN), modal displaced age 42-55 against a 10-20 year amortization horizon, a care workforce 77-88% female against a male-skewed displaced pool in K and IT, and injury/strain disutility that is a first-order term in the participation decision, not a footnote. The transitions that DO occur land in care administration, scheduling and coordination - roles that are themselves in the AI-exposed set, so the mechanism partly double-counts its own relief. The two flows are also stock-flow mismatched in timing: displacement is front-loaded 2027-32, the care deficit peaks 2033-40+, so even a frictionless worker cannot be in both places. The planks' arithmetic is not merely rough, it is sign-correct but two orders of magnitude short: 6-12M gross displaced x 0.07 = 0.4-0.8M against a 22-25M FTE requirement, under 4% of the gap. Credit for a tiny true core (documentation AI frees ~12% of nurse time by 2036, which is the single largest real AI-to-care channel and is a capital channel, not a labour-reallocation one) is why this is 4 and not 1.
hypothesis_critique.b: Two failure words: BLOCKS and SEVERELY. BLOCKS is simply false as a mechanism - AI compresses the price and headcount intensity of virtual services, it does not close the channel. Philippine BPO (1.7M+ workers) is most exposed on the voice/L1 tier, perhaps 25-40% of seat-equivalents removable by 2036, but revenue falls far less than headcount because volume expands as the price per interaction collapses (the Jevons leg): net BPO revenue is plausibly -10% to +15% against a forgone trend-doubling, which is a lost-upside story, not a collapse. India IT-BPM (~$280B scale) shifts to outcome pricing and decouples revenue from headcount; exports likely still grow 3-5%/yr nominal against an 8-9% trend. SEVERELY then fails on the netting, because the plank omits the physical leg entirely and that leg moves the opposite way with a larger per-worker coefficient: an OECD care FTE paid $25-40k remitting 25-35% sends $8-12k/yr, roughly 2-4x the per-worker foreign-exchange yield of a BPO seat. 2.5-5M additional physical migrants from these two sources by 2036 (the ceiling is credential-recognition throughput, not demand or wage) is worth $25-45bn/yr of remittances, comparable in magnitude to the entire virtual-leg downside, with the GCC channel as a third, separately-driven leg. The NET external shock is close to neutral in foreign exchange and NEGATIVE in domestic formal employment composition - BPO jobs are domestic, urban, female-heavy, multiplier-rich and middle-class-forming, whereas care migration is a brain drain that hollows out the source country's own care system precisely as its own 65+ share rises. That distributional/composition harm is real, which is why 13 and not 3, but it is not what the plank says.
hypothesis_critique.c: The failure word is THEN, i.e. the implied ORDERING. My mechanism gives the opposite sequencing: 2027-31 is the disinflationary interval (capex digestion per 2B AI-Q4 at 66%, China excess-capacity goods deflation, demand hole from the impairment event), while the 2030s are when the care/Baumol wedge peaks as the 80+ cohort compounds at 3.5%/yr and the care shadow price rises 60-90% real. The bottleneck contribution to core (+0.28pp/yr) is increasing in time, not decreasing, and the fiscal constraint in 2A means the pass-through arrives as administered-price and public-wage catch-up late rather than early. So the plank is roughly time-reversed. It survives at 17 only through the branch where the 2027-32 capex bust is severe enough to drag the 2030s into the D regime (18% mass) plus a modest slice where both halves happen to be moderate.
hypothesis_critique.d: Two failure words: EVENTUALLY and WINS. EVENTUALLY is unfalsifiable inside the Dec 31 2036 horizon and does all the plank's work - it converts a claim into a tautology by deferring the test. WINS fails structurally, not quantitatively: in a Chad Jones / weakest-link production structure, output is bounded by its least substitutable essential task, and exponential growth in a substitutable task (cognitive output, compute) cannot outrun a linear or shrinking constraint on a non-substitutable one (in-person bodily care, and upstream of it the clinical-preceptor and faculty slots that gate the care pipeline). Population decline is not the binding object at all - the binding object is the AGE COMPOSITION of the remaining population interacting with a task that has resisted mechanization for the entire era in which every other task was mechanized. My CQ3 P50 of 1.8% with P(A) = 12 is the quantitative expression. Score 12, carried mostly by the small branch where physical-care automation surprises (a jump in e_physical-automation from my 0.1 to 0.3+) rather than by compute scaling.

key_drivers: ZERO CROSS-ELASTICITY (e_cross = 0.07) between displaced cognitive labour and hands-on care/construction labour. Justification: a -55% reservation-wage gap at the aide tier; an 18-42 month credential-recognition queue and 3-4 years for RN or a trades apprenticeship; modal displaced age 42-55 against a 10-20 year retraining amortization; a care workforce 77-88% female against a male-skewed displaced pool in K and IT; among the highest MSD/injury rates of any occupation; and already-high aide turnover (40-60%/yr), which proves the aide tier is WAGE-rationed, not vacancy-rationed, so adding displaced applicants at the prevailing wage adds almost nothing. This single number is the load-bearing driver of CQ1, CQ3, CQ6 and the AI-Q5 coupling tension.

CARE DEMAND ELASTICITY e_caredemand|65+ = 1.25 (and ~2.0 w.r.t. 80+). Justification: formal care hours per capita rise roughly fourfold from 65-74 to 85+, so the 80+ cohort compounding at ~3.5%/yr dominates; with the 2A old-age ratio going 31% to 39-41%, required OECD-38 formal care FTE grows 2.6%/yr, +22-25M FTE by 2036, against a 20-64 base shrinking 0.3%/yr.

OWN-WAGE ELASTICITY OF CARE LABOUR SUPPLY e = 0.35 short-run, 0.60 over ten years. Justification: the marginal entrant pool is domestic-sector and immigrant women, gender-composition-locked, strain-averse and licence-gated. The arithmetic consequence is the central fiscal fact of this effort: closing a 25% FTE gap through wages alone needs a ~40% real care wage rise (25/0.6), costing 1.3-1.8% of OECD GDP in additional care compensation - precisely the transfer that 2A (debt >100% of GDP, net interest 2 to 3% of GDP, pensions already absorbing 2.9T RMB in China) says cannot be financed. Therefore the market clears on QUANTITY (rationing) rather than PRICE, which is why I mark CQ1's wage conjunct down to 0.25.

MIGRATION SEMI-ELASTICITY AND ITS ADMINISTRATIVE CAP: +1pp of destination real care-wage premium raises applicant flow from India/the Philippines by 1.5-2.5%, but the elasticity of actual ENTRIES to wage is only ~0.1 because credential recognition, English/licensure exams, clinical bridging placements and visa caps gate throughput. Modelled OECD-wide care-sector entry capacity 400-700k/yr by the early 2030s against a ~2M/yr requirement. Migration is thus a one-third solution at best, and is rate-limited by a bureaucracy, not by a price.

BAUMOL PASS-THROUGH TO CORE: care/health/social is 13-14% of the core basket with ~70% labour share and ~0% measured productivity growth, so 2pp/yr of excess care wage growth is +0.20pp/yr on core; the construction/shelter channel adds +0.08pp. Total +0.28pp/yr, which is simultaneously what pushes CQ2's OECD leg to the 2.5% threshold, what creates CQ6-C's 23%, and what (via the reallocation drag of -0.15 to -0.20pp/yr on measured aggregate TFP) caps CQ3.

AUTOMATION ADOPTION ELASTICITY SPLITS BY TASK: e_adoption|realwage = 0.4-0.6 for documentation, scheduling, triage and remote monitoring (documentation is ~25% of nurse time; AI plausibly removes half of it, a ~12% effective capacity gain by 2036 - the largest genuine AI-into-care channel), but only ~0.1 for physical handling (transfer, toileting, feeding, mobility) because of hardware, liability, regulatory and reimbursement lags. Aging is therefore a real DEMAND PULL for automation, but the pull lands on the task that was never the constraint.

falsification_signposts.signpost: US NCLEX-RN first-time candidate volume plus OECD-wide nursing-programme completions: do annual completions in the US, Germany, Japan, Korea and the UK rise by more than 25% above their 2025 level, with the binding constraint (clinical placement slots and nursing faculty posts) publicly reported as eased rather than worsened? Publicly observable via NCSBN annual NCLEX statistics, OECD Health Statistics 'nursing graduates', and national regulator registers.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: This is the single cleanest falsifier of my weakest-link claim. If completions are up >25% AND placement/faculty capacity is reported as eased, my e_supply of 0.60 and my faculty/preceptor bottleneck are both wrong. CQ3 P50 moves up ~+0.25pp to ~2.05%, CQ6-A rises from 12 to ~20 and C falls from 23 to ~17, CQ1's unemployment conjunct strengthens while its wage conjunct weakens (more supply, less wage pressure), leaving CQ1 roughly flat near 16, and CQ2's OECD leg drops ~4pp because the Baumol pass-through shrinks.

falsification_signposts.signpost: OECD-38 care-sector worker admissions by credential-recognition route: do combined annual entries of foreign-trained nurses, aides and personal-care workers exceed 1.2M/yr in any single year, and does mean time-to-licensure for an India- or Philippines-trained nurse fall below 12 months in at least three of the US, Germany, Japan, Canada and the UK? Observable via OECD International Migration Outlook, national regulator throughput statistics, and Philippine POEA/DMW deployment data.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: Falsifies my administrative-throughput cap of 400-700k/yr and my entries-to-wage elasticity of ~0.1. The care constraint then clears substantially on migration rather than on wages or rationing, so: CQ1's wage conjunct falls from 0.25 to ~0.12 (migrant entry dilutes the F+Q median hard) and CQ1 drops from 16 to ~9; CQ2's OECD leg falls ~5pp and CQ2 to ~32; CQ3 P50 up ~+0.15pp; and hypothesis plank (b) rises from 13 toward ~25 on the remittance leg while falling further on the 'blocks' wording.

falsification_signposts.signpost: Philippine IT-BPM headcount and revenue (IBPAP annual roadmap data) and Indian IT-BPM export revenue (NASSCOM): does Philippine BPO headcount fall below 1.3M while sector revenue falls more than 15% below its 2026 level in nominal USD, AND do Philippine remittances fail to exceed $45bn/yr?
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: Confirms the virtual leg's downside while falsifying my physical-leg offset, which is the specific netting my score of 13 on plank (b) rests on. Plank (b) would move from 13 to ~45 (the 'severely' word becomes defensible even though 'blocks' stays wrong). It would also mean the OECD care gap is NOT being filled by migration, so CQ1's wage conjunct rises from 0.25 to ~0.34 and CQ1 from 16 to ~21, CQ2's OECD leg rises ~4pp, and CQ6-C rises from 23 to ~28 at B's expense.

falsification_signposts.signpost: Divergence check on the actual CQ1 wage measure: OECD/national real median hourly earnings by ISIC sector. Does the cumulative 2025-to-year-end real median hourly gap between (F+Q) and (J+K+M) exceed +5.0pp, and is the DECOMPOSITION published showing whether within-job wage growth or composition dominates?
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: A gap above +5.0pp by 2032 implies my composition wedge of -7 to -9pp is overstated and the path to +10pp by 2036 is open: CQ1's wage conjunct rises from 0.25 to ~0.45 and CQ1 from 16 to ~27. A gap below +2.0pp by 2032 confirms the composition offset and takes CQ1 down to ~9. Either way this is the signpost that most directly adjudicates my own CQ1.

falsification_signposts.signpost: OECD-38 long-duration (12+ month) unemployment share among workers aged 45-59 with tertiary education in ISIC J, K and M, versus the same cohort's 2025 level, plus the share of their 3-year occupational destinations falling in ISIC F or Q (observable via national longitudinal labour-force microdata releases, e.g. US CPS/ACS, EU-LFS, and OECD Employment Outlook special chapters).
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: A measured 3-year F/Q destination share above 15% falsifies my e_cross = 0.07 outright and is the most damaging single observation to this entire effort: plank (a) would rise from 4 to ~30, CQ3 P50 up ~+0.2pp, CQ6-B falls toward ~40 as A and the benign part of B's residual gain, and the AI-Q5 coupling tension I report below reverses sign. A destination share below 5% with rising long-duration unemployment confirms the mechanism and pushes CQ6-B to ~52 and CQ5 up ~3pp through the demand-shortfall channel.

wave1.coupling_tension: PRIMARY TENSION - 2B AI-Q5 is too LOW once demographics are endogenous; it should be ~48-52%, not 38.2%. The exogenous-demographics ensemble implicitly reasons that aggregate labour scarcity from aging lifts wages economy-wide and therefore cushions the cognitive-sector labour share. My mechanism says the scarcity is SECTOR-SPECIFIC AND NON-ARBITRAGABLE: because e_cross = 0.07, a displaced analyst, paralegal or junior developer cannot convert the tight care/construction labour market into an improved outside option for himself. The tight market and the loose market are separated by a reservation-wage gap, a licensing queue, a strain barrier and a gender-composition lock. So the J/K/M worker bargains in a market where his substitute (capital/compute) is getting cheaper and his exit option is NOT getting better - the worst possible configuration for labour share. Endogenizing demographics therefore makes the J/K/M compensation share of GVA fall MORE, not less, than the standalone marginal assumes. Direction: AI-Q5 should move UP by roughly +10 to +14pp. Note this also partly vindicates CQ1's second conjunct mechanism while the composition-of-the-median artifact still suppresses the measured number - the labour SHARE can collapse while the measured MEDIAN rises, and those two facts are not in conflict. SECOND TENSION - 2B AI-Q1 is too HIGH, by roughly -5 to -7pp (23.0% should be ~16-18%). The endogenous-demographics path forces a 3.5-4pp shift of hours into a sector with ~0% productivity growth and ~0.6x average output per hour, which subtracts 0.15-0.20pp/yr from MEASURED PPP-weighted aggregate TFP. The threshold is defined on measured aggregate TFP, so a gross AI lift that clears +0.50pp can still fail the question after reallocation. The standalone ensemble cannot see this because exogenous demographics hold the sectoral employment composition fixed. THIRD, SMALLER TENSION - 2B AI-Q3 (data-centre electricity) is mildly too low in its P50, perhaps +3-5%, because labour scarcity is a genuine demand pull (e_adoption|realwage = 0.4-0.6) and the documentation/monitoring/triage workload in health and social care is compute-hungry and politically protected from the capex-digestion retrenchment; but this is bounded by the willingness-to-pay ceiling and I would not move the P90. WEAKEST LINK, stated explicitly as the lens requires: the non-substitutable task is IN-PERSON BODILY CARE (transfer, toileting, feeding, mobility, supervision), and upstream of it the CLINICAL PRECEPTOR AND NURSING FACULTY SLOT that gates every credential in the chain. In a Chad Jones essential-task structure this caps the whole system regardless of how fast the substitutable tasks improve. Its SHADOW PRICE rises 60-90% in real terms by 2036 (derived: a 20-25% FTE gap divided by a long-run supply elasticity of 0.6, plus the Baumol relative-wage requirement), while its OBSERVED price rises only 15-25% because the fiscal transfer needed to pay the shadow price is exactly the transfer 2A says is already strained. The 35-65pp wedge between shadow and observed price is the model's central prediction and it does not appear in any price series: it appears as LTC waitlists and unmet need, hospital bed-blocking and throughput failure, and 1.5-3M OECD prime-age informal family carers (disproportionately women aged 45-60) withdrawing from paid work - a second-round labour-supply contraction of 0.3-0.5% of OECD employment that the exogenous-demographics block cannot generate, because in that block the care constraint has no quantity dimension at all.

wave1.lens_self_description: I forecast only the resolution process — which published series would actually adjudicate each threshold, its vintage, basket, weighting and revision behaviour — which forbade me from using any structural macro judgment about labour reallocation, care bottlenecks or offshoring except insofar as it passes through a named statistical series that exists at the required frequency and coverage by Dec 31 2036.
wave1.cq1_reasoning:
RESOLVING SERIES. Conjunct (a): OECD Harmonised Unemployment Rate (HUR, OECD.Stat/LFS, labour-force-weighted, monthly, revised 1-3 months and rebenchmarked on census population controls). Conjunct (b): there is NO OECD-38-wide sectoral real MEDIAN hourly wage series. Eurostat Structure of Earnings Survey (SES) is the only harmonised median gross hourly earnings by NACE section and it is QUADRENNIAL (2018/2022/2026/2030/2034) with ~2.5yr publication lag: the 2025 and 2036 endpoints are not observable at all; a resolver must substitute 2022 and 2034 waves (an 12-year window offset from the stated 11-year one), and non-EU members (US, JP, KR, CA, AU, NZ, MX, CL, IL, TR, CH partly) do not run the module. US substitutes are BLS OES (median hourly by industry, May reference, methodology break in the 2021-23 reweighting) or CES average hourly earnings (MEAN, not median). Verdict: (b) is not measurable as intended; a best-available-proxy construction would be analyst-assembled and contestable.

MARGINALS. (a): OECD HUR recent base ~4.8-5.0% (2023-25); 5yr-average history 2015-19 ~5.9%, 2019-23 ~5.6%, 2021-25 ~5.2%. Two artefacts push (a) toward YES and are worth >3pp each: (i) aging MECHANICALLY lowers the measured rate — retirement moves people out of the labour-force denominator, not into the numerator, and rising 65+ participation adds a cohort with structurally sub-3% measured unemployment (+6 to +10pp on (a)); (ii) the "OECD-38" basket is frozen by wording, so a 2027-2034 accession (Brazil, Indonesia, Peru, Argentina candidates) with high unemployment does not dilute it. Offsetting: Jan-2032 CPS rebenchmarking to 2030 census population controls (level revision, historically <0.2pp rate effect), and the AI-Q4 66% impairment marginal implying a capex bust whose unemployment echo could sit inside 2032-36. Marginal (a) = 0.58.
(b): real-economy differential needed is 10pp cumulative = ~0.87pp/yr for 11 years. COMPOSITION, my specialty, runs against it in BOTH sectors at once: a surge of low-wage entrants into Q (care aides, migrant nurses, PSWs) — exactly the mechanism that would make the hypothesis true — pulls Q's MEDIAN down while every incumbent gets a raise; symmetrically AI culls the bottom of J/K/M (junior analysts, paralegals, entry coders), which RAISES the measured median there. Both effects are unambiguous in sign and jointly worth -10 to -20pp. Further: Q is publicly funded/price-regulated in most of OECD-38, so its wage path is a fiscal decision and 2A says fiscal is strained (pay restraint caps Q directly); F (construction) is rate-sensitive and my CQ4 real-yield path (P50 1.9%) suppresses residential construction wages, with the data-centre/grid build supporting only the skilled-trade tail. Deflator choice (national CPI vs expenditure-weighted sector deflators) adds ±2-4pp of measured cumulative differential, sign ambiguous. Marginal (b) = 0.20 (real-economy ~0.30, less measurement/composition haircut).

CONJUNCTION. Positive correlation (both favoured by a tight-labour world): P(b|a) = 0.26 vs 0.20 unconditional. Joint = 0.58 x 0.26 = 0.151. Auditor adjustment: on an unmeasurable conjunct the resolution convention is NO, so shade down. 13.
wave1.cq2_reasoning:
RESOLVING SERIES. Conjunct (a): no official "OECD-38 GDP-weighted core" exists; OECD.Stat publishes an OECD-total inflation aggregate that is PPP-GDP-weighted, and the Section-locked accounting basis (constant 2025 USD PPP) forces PPP weights absent other instruction. Conjunct (b): China NBS monthly headline CPI, basket reweighted on years ending 0 and 5 (2026 and 2031 rebases fall inside the window).

THE DOMINANT ARTEFACT (index construction, worth +10 to +20pp, direction YES). A PPP-GDP-weighted OECD-38 core aggregate carries Türkiye at ~5% of OECD-38 PPP GDP (vs ~1.3% at market rates). Türkiye core CPI (TÜİK ex food/energy) was ~55% in 2024 and ~30% in 2025; even a 2027-36 average of 12-18% contributes +0.6 to +0.9pp to the aggregate single-handedly. Mexico, Colombia, Chile, Costa Rica, Poland, Hungary add +0.10 to +0.20pp. This is why OECD-total inflation printed 6-7% when G7 printed 2-3%. Underlying G7-ish core of ~2.1-2.3% therefore lands at ~2.7-3.1% on the stated measure. Second artefact, opposite sign and >3pp: "core CPI/PCE" is an OR. US core PCE runs 25-40bp BELOW US core CPI persistently (Fisher chaining, broader scope, lower shelter weight); the US is the single largest weight, so a PCE reading lowers the aggregate ~0.10-0.15pp. Third: Japan's conventional "core" is ex-fresh-food (INCLUDES energy) and has run 2.5-3%; using the Japanese convention rather than core-core lifts the aggregate ~+0.05pp. Marginal (a) = 0.86 — near-mechanical, not a macro call.

Conjunct (b). China CPI 2023 +0.2%, 2024 +0.2%, 2025 ~0.0%. Construction biases measured Chinese CPI LOW relative to OECD practice: owner-occupied housing enters as rent-equivalent at a very small effective weight (residence ~16% but mostly utilities and actual rent), while food sits at ~18-20% so the pork cycle supplies the variance — one bad food year at +5% headline adds +0.5pp to a 10-year average, which is the main threat to (b). Reference class: Japan 1995-2005 averaged ~-0.1%, 2000-2010 ~-0.2%, so a sub-1.5% decade is attainable; against that, the 2026 and 2031 rebases and official reluctance to publish sustained deflation both bias prints slightly up. Marginal (b) = 0.62.

CONJUNCTION. Mild NEGATIVE correlation: Chinese deflation exports tradables disinflation to the OECD, cutting against (a) — though (a) is carried by services plus the Türkiye artefact, both of which are orthogonal to Chinese goods prices. P(b|a) = 0.58. Joint = 0.86 x 0.58 = 0.499. Answer 49. Note the ensemble-relevant asymmetry: almost all of my YES mass comes from the OECD leg being an accounting near-certainty, not from a stagflation view.
wave1.cq3_reasoning:
RESOLVING SERIES. IMF WEO (or OECD Economic Outlook) real GDP growth aggregated across OECD-38 + China on PPP weights. Three construction decisions each move the answer by more than 3pp of probability mass.

(1) WEIGHT BASIS. OECD-38 ~ $70T 2025 PPP, China ~ $40T, so China weight ~36%. IMF aggregates are CHAIN-weighted on current PPP, under which China's weight drifts to ~38-40% by 2036 and the composite growth rate rises; the Section lock says constant 2025 USD PPP, which FREEZES the weight and LOWERS the composite by ~5-10bp. I used fixed 2025 weights.
(2) CHINA IS REPORTED, NOT TRUE. CQ3 resolves on NBS-reported real GDP as reprinted by IMF. Independent work (including Rhodium, cited in 2A) argues reported real growth exceeds a deflator-consistent estimate by ~1-1.5pp. At a 0.36 weight that is +0.35 to +0.55pp on the composite relative to any "true growth" forecast. Direction: UP. This is the single largest swing factor in CQ3 and it is pure measurement.
(3) ICP PPP REVISIONS. The ICP 2026 round (results ~2029) will restate China's PPP level as ICP 2021 did; a ±5% restatement of China's PPP GDP is ±1.8pp of weight and ±2bp of composite — small, but it also makes the "constant 2025 PPP" anchor itself a revisable object.

FERMI. OECD leg: 2A gives per-capita baseline 1.0% -> 0.6%; OECD population growth 0.2-0.3%/yr (migration-dependent) implies aggregate ~0.8-0.9% before AI. AI-Q6's central standalone regime (+0.15 to +0.59pp) and the demand-pull coupling (labour scarcity raises the adoption return) put OECD 2032-36 at ~1.2%. Two measurement offsets: AI capex is measured investment, and the 2032-36 window most likely sits AFTER the buildout peak, so the investment CONTRIBUTION turns negative in growth-rate terms (impairments are balance-sheet, not flow, so the 66% AI-Q4 marginal subtracts nothing directly) — call it -0.1 to -0.3pp; against that, fast-falling hedonic price indices for AI servers and capitalised software flatter real investment and hence measured real GDP, +0.05 to +0.15pp. China leg: reported ~4.5-5% now, 2A's -2.7pp/yr aging drag is a 2025-2050 average, so 2032-36 reported ~3.0%.
Composite P50 = 0.64 x 1.2 + 0.36 x 3.0 = 0.77 + 1.08 = 1.85 -> 1.9.
P10 (AI capex bust echo plus Chinese property/fiscal hard landing: OECD 0.3, China 1.5) = 0.73, but a five-YEAR average that low is deep tail; P10 = 1.1. P90 (breakout plus Chinese reflation: OECD 2.0, China 4.0) = 2.72 -> 2.8.

IDENTITY THAT DOES NOT CLOSE (reported in coupling_tension and applied here): 2A's "+0.4pp/yr healthy-aging offset ... YET aging still slows global growth by ~-1.1pp/yr" reads as -1.1 being NET of the +0.4. Any effort that adds the +0.4 to a -1.1 baseline double-counts and inflates coupled growth by ~+0.4pp. I used the net reading, which is why my P50 is below a naive 2.3%.
wave1.cq4_reasoning:
RESOLVING SERIES AND ITS TRAPS. "10y nominal benchmark minus 10y inflation swap / TIPS breakeven," GDP-weighted across G7, averaged 2032-36. Four construction artefacts, each >3pp:

(1) SWAP-vs-BREAKEVEN IS AN "OR". US 10y zero-coupon inflation swaps quote ~15-25bp ABOVE the TIPS-derived breakeven (TIPS carry a liquidity discount). Choosing swaps therefore LOWERS the measured real yield by 15-25bp for the dominant weight. Note also that for the US, nominal minus TIPS breakeven is identically the TIPS real yield (DFII10, the 2.60% anchor in 2A), so the US leg is self-consistent; the "or" only bites via the swap option.
(2) UK RPI->CPIH ALIGNMENT, FEB 2030 — INSIDE THE WINDOW. Index-linked gilts are RPI-linked and RPI breakevens embed the ~80-100bp RPI/CPI wedge. When RPI is aligned to CPIH in Feb 2030, UK breakevens drop mechanically and the UK's measured nominal-minus-breakeven real yield RISES by ~80-100bp with no change in economics. At a ~7% PPP-GDP weight that is +6 to +7bp on the aggregate, arriving as a step mid-window. Direction: UP.
(3) COVERAGE GAPS. Canada stopped issuing Real Return Bonds in 2022, so a ~5% weight has no forward-looking domestic breakeven market and must be proxied. Japan's 10y inflation swap market is thin and the JGBi market shallow: a low thin-market breakeven (~1.2%) against a normalising 10y JGB (~2.0-2.5%) prints Japan at +0.8 to +1.3% real, versus +0.2 to +0.5% against survey-consistent expectations — ±5 to 10bp on the aggregate. Italy's BTP€i reference is euro-area HICP ex-tobacco, not Italian CPI, which OVERSTATES the Italian real yield whenever Italian inflation exceeds the euro-area average.
(4) WEIGHT BASIS. PPP GDP weights (per the Section lock) put Japan ~12% and Italy ~6% versus ~8% and ~4% at market rates, i.e. PPP weighting LOWERS the aggregate by ~10-15bp relative to a market-rate construction.

FERMI, 2032-36 averages: US 2.4 (w .44), Japan 0.9 (.12), Germany 1.3 (.10), France 1.6 (.07), UK 2.2 post-alignment (.07), Italy 2.1 (.06), Canada 1.9 (.05) = 1.056+0.108+0.130+0.112+0.154+0.126+0.095 = 1.78 -> P50 1.9, reconciling with the 2.60% US TIPS anchor in 2A minus the non-US drag. P10 0.9 (demand-shortfall/BIS labour-income deficit plus post-bust excess capacity plus explicit repression — note repression typically arrives as nominal yield caps, which on this measure shows up as a LOW real yield only if breakevens do not blow out; if they do, the measure perversely prints NEGATIVE real yields, which is where my left tail comes from). P90 3.0 (fiscal dominance, Debt-at-Risk realisation, retiree dissaving raising r*, term-premium spike, plus the UK step).
wave1.cq5_reasoning:
RESOLVING SERIES. ICE BofA MOVE Index (daily, never revised, but methodologically mutable — it was reweighted in 2019 and ICE can reconstitute or discontinue it; "average" of daily closes is unstated but immaterial). MSCI World (USD; price index vs net total return unstated). A GDP-weighted G7 10y nominal yield aggregate, which is analyst-constructed.

CONJUNCT A: MOVE 10-year average >= 105. History: 2003-07 ~90-100; 2010-19 ~75-85; 2020 ~90; 2022-23 ~120-140; 2024 ~95-105; 2025-26 ~80-95. CRITICAL INDEX-CONSTRUCTION POINT: MOVE is NORMALISED (basis-point) implied vol on 1m options across 2/5/10/30y, so its LEVEL scales with the level of yields. A persistent 4%+ nominal regime floors MOVE around 85-100 without any stress; a 105 decade-average then requires 2022-23 conditions roughly a third of the time. 2A's plumbing facts (eroding convenience yields, levered basis-trade absorption, $1.4T circular AI commitments on ~$650B debt) support that. Marginal A = 0.48.

CONJUNCT B, decomposed. (i) At least one MSCI World >=25% peak-to-trough drawdown in a 10-year window: reference class 1973-74, 1980-82, 1987, 2000-02, 2007-09, 2020, 2022 — ~7 episodes in 53 years, per-decade P(>=1) ~0.78-0.85; the USD denomination (a dollar rally deepens the measured drawdown) and a price-index rather than total-return basis each make 25% EASIER, +3 to 5pp; with the IMF's explicit 20% AI-led valuation shock scenario, 0.80. (ii) Conditional on that, yields FAIL to fall 50bp or rise 25bp in the window: historically G7 yields rally hard (2008 ~-150bp, 2020 ~-100bp, 2001-02 ~-150bp); 2022 is the one correlation-breakdown and it did breach ~-26% on MSCI World, so 1-in-5 of recent big drawdowns. Two artefacts raise the conditional, worth +5 to 8pp: Japan's near-floor yields CANNOT contribute 50bp of rally, and Italian BTP yields typically RISE in risk-off as spreads widen — so a GDP-weighted (PPP-weighted, hence Japan 12% / Italy 6%) G7 aggregate is structurally less able to fall 50bp than the US alone. Plus an undefined "drawdown window": measured peak-to-trough on the equity leg, the equity trough often coincides with the YIELD peak in inflation-driven selloffs, which favours resolution YES. Conditional = 0.40. Marginal B = 0.80 x 0.40 = 0.32.

CONJUNCTION. Strongly POSITIVE correlation — a high-MOVE decade is definitionally the regime in which the equity-bond hedge fails. P(A|B) = 0.75. Joint = 0.32 x 0.75 = 0.24. Answer 24.
wave1.cq6_reasoning:
LOCK CONFIRMED AND AUDITED. I applied lexical priority strictly: (1) A if CQ3 growth >= 2.6; (2) else C if OECD-38 GDP-weighted core 2032-36 >= 2.7 AND growth < 2.0; (3) else D if growth < 1.7 AND core < 2.0; (4) else B. The rule is well-formed and resolves every overlap and every gap, with one consequence the literal definitions hide: rule 3 requires core < 2.0 on the SAME PPP-GDP-weighted OECD-38 measure that CQ2 uses, and that measure carries a ~+0.4 to +0.5pp Türkiye-plus-LatAm floor over 2032-36 (see cq2_reasoning). A genuine BIS-style demand-shortfall world with underlying G7 core at ~1.5% still PRINTS ~2.0-2.1% on this aggregate. Regime D is therefore substantially harder to resolve YES than its economic description suggests — the artefact drains D into C and B. That is my largest MECE finding.

DERIVATION FROM MY OWN CQ3/CQ2.
- A: from my CQ3 (P50 1.9, P90 2.8, roughly lognormal-ish right tail), P(growth >= 2.6) = 0.13. A = 13. Consistency check passed: P50 1.9 forbids putting most mass on A, and I have not.
- Remaining 87. P(growth < 2.0) = 0.55 of total (P50 1.9 sits just below 2.0).
- Within the 55 points of growth < 2.0, split on core inflation: P(core >= 2.7 | growth < 2.0) = 0.55 — my CQ2 conjunct-A marginal is 0.86 for >= 2.50% over 2027-36, and 2.7% over 2032-36 is ~0.58 unconditionally (Türkiye disinflating partially by the 2030s shrinks but does not remove the floor), shaded slightly down because part of the low-growth mass is the deflationary-bust branch where the artefact itself fades. C = 55 x 0.55 = 30.
- P(core < 2.0 | growth < 2.0) = 0.14 given the artefact floor. D = 55 x 0.14 = 7.7 -> 8.
- Low-growth / moderate-inflation leftover (growth < 2.0, core 2.0-2.69) falls to B by rule 4: 55 - 30 - 7.7 = 17.3.
- Growth 2.0-2.59 mass = 87 - 55 = 32, all B.
- B = 32 + 17.3 = 49.3 -> 49. Sum = 13 + 49 + 30 + 8 = 100.

RESIDUAL-B ABSORPTION, QUANTIFIED. B's own literal band (growth 1.7-2.5%) accounts for ~32pp. The rule-4 catch-all adds ~17pp from the growth-below-2.0-with-core-between-2.0-and-2.7 cell, which a naive reader of the prose labels would have split between C ("low growth, term-premium spikes") and D ("low growth, excess capacity"). So B is inflated by ~17pp, ~35% of its own mass, and a naive reading would have produced roughly C 38 / D 15 / B 34.

ONE SUPPORTING LEG OF C THAT I DO NOT ACCEPT. C's "grid supply wall" is not supported by AI-Q3 arithmetic at P50: 365 -> 998 TWh is +633 TWh over 12 years, ~72 GW of average load, ~145-180 GW firm-equivalent or ~250-350 GW if VRE-plus-storage, i.e. ~$400-900B of generation and grid capex, ~$35-75B/yr against OECD-38+China power-sector capex of ~$600-800B/yr: 5-10%, not a wall. Even at P90 (1,574 TWh) it is 10-18%. The identity closes; the binding constraint is interconnection QUEUE TIME, not capital, which is a siting constraint no capex series will show. My C = 30 therefore rests on the inflation-measurement leg, not the grid leg.

hypothesis_critique.a: "SMOOTHLY" carries the failure, and from my lens it fails twice — in the world and in the data. In the world: reservation-wage gap (a US paralegal at ~$30/hr facing a personal-care-aide job at ~$18-20/hr), RN licensure queues of 2-4 years plus NCLEX and clinical-placement capacity that is itself staffed by the scarce nurses, geographic immobility against housing costs in the metros where J/K/M jobs are, injury and musculoskeletal-strain rates in Q that screen out a median displaced worker aged ~45, a care workforce that is ~78-88% female against a more balanced displaced cognitive pool, and Baumol: care productivity is near-flat by construction so its wage bill is a fiscal transfer decision, and 2A says the transfer is already strained (China alone at ~2.9T RMB, ~10.1% of fiscal expenditure). In the data: the series that would SHOW a smooth supply response is gross occupational/industry flows from CPS or EU-LFS, where J->Q transitions sit at or below sampling noise for any single year, so the plank is close to unfalsifiable at the frequency anyone would check it. 4.
hypothesis_critique.b: "SEVERELY" and "BLOCKS" both fail, and a third word does the quiet damage: "export labour" conflates the virtual and physical legs, which move in OPPOSITE directions. BLOCKS is wrong because AI compresses the PRICE and seat-intensity of Indian IT-BPM and Philippine voice-BPO rather than closing the channel: India's ~$280B of IT-BPM exports has already decoupled headcount growth from revenue growth, and that is repricing and reclassification, not a block. SEVERELY is wrong because the physical leg is positively shocked by exactly the 2A demography — OECD nursing, allied-health and skilled-trade migrant demand rises — and because Philippine remittances (~$38-40B, ~8-9% of GDP) are dominated by sea-based and land-based health and service workers, not BPO.
