MEASUREMENT POINT: the resolving series, BOP "telecommunications, computer and information services" exports plus "other business services," cannot distinguish AI in-housing from captive-GCC relocation — work pulled in-house into an Indian global capability centre still books as an Indian services export, so the series may record no damage even if the independent-vendor model is gutted. 14.
hypothesis_critique.c: "THEN FALLS" carries it, and the failure is an index-construction one that cuts BOTH ways. On the stated OECD-38 PPP-GDP-weighted aggregate, Türkiye's disinflation from ~30% toward single digits would deliver a visible "falls in the 2030s" of ~0.3-0.5pp by composition alone, with G7 core services inflation completely unchanged — so the plank can be MEASURED true for reasons that have nothing to do with the mechanism its proponents mean. Against that, my own CQ2/CQ6 put the same aggregate at >= 2.7% through 2032-36, and the coupled demography pushes care and health services prices UP in the 2030s precisely as the plank says they fall (Baumol plus a scarce, licence-gated, politically wage-indexed care workforce). Net: the arithmetic of the basket partly rescues a plank the economics does not support. 30.
hypothesis_critique.d: "EVENTUALLY" and "WINS" carry it, and both are resolution failures rather than economic ones. EVENTUALLY names no date, so the plank is unfalsifiable at the Dec 31 2036 horizon — it survives any observation inside the window. WINS names no threshold and, worse, does not say WHICH aggregate: population decline makes real GDP PER CAPITA growth mechanically EASIER to win and real AGGREGATE GDP growth harder, so the plank is true or false depending on an unstated denominator. Pinning it to the only measure on the table, my CQ3 P50 of 1.9% sits below the 2.6% "renaissance" bar, and ~0.4pp of even that 1.9% is reported-China measurement rather than output. 17.

key_drivers: Türkiye (~5% of OECD-38 PPP GDP, core CPI ~30% in 2025) plus Mexico/Colombia/Chile/Costa Rica inside a PPP-GDP-weighted 'OECD-38 core' aggregate add ~+0.4 to +1.0pp of pure composition. This single artefact carries CQ2's OECD conjunct to ~0.86, lifts CQ6-C to 30, and makes CQ6-D (which requires core < 2.0 on the same measure) nearly unreachable even in a genuine demand-shortfall world.

CQ1-b's two composition effects run against resolution SIMULTANEOUSLY: a low-wage entrant surge into ISIC Q pulls its measured MEDIAN hourly wage down while every incumbent gets a raise, and AI culling the bottom of J/K/M pulls their median UP. The mechanism that would make the plank true is the mechanism that hides it in the data.

No OECD-38-wide sectoral real MEDIAN hourly wage series exists at the required frequency: Eurostat SES is quadrennial (2018/2022/2026/2030/2034, ~2.5yr lag) with neither a 2025 nor a 2036 endpoint, and the non-EU members do not publish the measure at all. A 10pp cumulative F+Q vs J+K+M gap over 11 years is not observable as specified.

Reported (NBS) Chinese real GDP, at a ~36% fixed-2025-PPP weight, is the largest single swing in CQ3: a ~1 to 1.5pp reported-versus-deflator-consistent wedge is +0.35 to +0.55pp on the composite. Chain-weighted current PPP (IMF's own practice) versus the Section-locked constant 2025 PPP adds a further 5-10bp.

Two dated index mechanics inside the CQ4/CQ5 windows: the UK RPI->CPIH alignment in Feb 2030 collapses UK breakevens and mechanically RAISES the UK's measured real yield ~80-100bp (+6-7bp on the G7 aggregate), while Japan's yield floor and Italy's risk-off spread widening make a PPP-GDP-weighted G7 10y nominal aggregate structurally less able to rally 50bp in an equity crash (+5-8pp on CQ5's second conjunct).

A double-count latent in Section 2A: 'adds ~+0.4pp/yr ... YET aging still slows global growth by ~-1.1pp/yr' reads as -1.1 being NET of the healthy-aging offset. Any coupled path that adds +0.4 to a -1.1 baseline overstates growth by ~0.4pp. I used the net reading, which is the main reason my CQ3 P50 is 1.9 and not ~2.3.

wave1.coupling_tension: The sharpest tension is with AI-Q1 (2032-36 PPP-weighted TFP lift >= +0.50pp/yr, locked at 23.0% raw). Once demographics are endogenous, 2A's +0.4pp/yr healthy-aging effect and AI-Q1's TFP lift stop being separate accounting objects, because they are measured by the SAME residual. Growth accounting measures labour input as bodies and hours, with at best an education-share quality adjustment; it has no cognitive- or physical-capacity adjustment. So the "70 in 2022 = 53 in 2000" gain in effective capacity per hour — which is what the 41-country, N~1M result describes — is an unmeasured labour-quality improvement, and whatever share of it is not absorbed by the education adjustment lands in the Solow residual and is PUBLISHED AS TFP. Even a conservative quarter-attribution puts +0.10pp/yr of pure demographic health gain into measured TFP, which is 20% of the 0.50pp bar, with no AI causation whatever. Direction: AI-Q1's standalone 23.0% is too LOW on the measure that would resolve it — endogenising demographics should raise it to roughly 28-31%, and the lift is an attribution artefact, not a technology forecast. The same artefact is why CQ6-A survives at 13 despite my CQ3 P50 of only 1.9%. A secondary, smaller tension runs the other way on AI-Q2 (50% of OECD-38 firms with 10+ employees using AI directly in production, locked at 21.3%): the demographic coupling is a genuine demand pull that argues the marginal is too low, but the resolution mechanics argue it is too high — the only harmonised source is the Eurostat ICT-usage module, which 10-plus non-EU OECD members do not run; the UNWEIGHTED country mean down-weights the large adopters and up-weights laggards at 5-9%; and "directly in producing goods or services" is a strictly narrower sub-question than the "uses AI technologies" headline that printed ~13.5% for the EU in 2024 after a question redesign. Measurement dominates demand pull here, so 21.3% ends up roughly right for the wrong reason — which means the ensemble should not read it as evidence about adoption.

wave2.lens_self_description: Adversarial red-team falsifier: I treated the three Wave-1 panelists' shared premises as the object of attack rather than as evidence, and forbade myself from averaging them, from adopting any number as a prior merely because all three converged on it, and from accepting a causal story as likely merely because it was coherent (the "bifurcated barbell" narrative in particular).
wave2.cq1_reasoning:
THE SINGLE STRONGEST SHARED ASSUMPTION I ATTACK (applies across all six CQs, stated once here): all three Wave-1 panelists treat REQUIRED formal care FTE as a near-deterministic function of headcount demography. Panelist 2 makes it explicit (e_caredemand|65+ = 1.25, fixed age-specific care hours per capita, "+22-25M FTE", "~2M/yr requirement"); Panelist 1 inherits it ("Baumol-exposed, licensure-gated sectors absorb the demographic burden"); Panelist 3 never touches it. None of the three noticed that the SAME 2A bullet they all cite for the growth arithmetic ("70 in 2022 = 53 in 2000", 41 countries, N~1M) is a statement that the age-specific FUNCTIONAL-CAPACITY curve has shifted right by roughly 15-17 years of chronological age. They loaded that bullet in only as a growth/TFP offset and never as a CARE-DEMAND DEFLATOR. Care utilization is driven by disability and dependency, not by birthdays: if the dependency curve shifts right even half a decade, the derived 2036 formal-care FTE requirement falls 20-35%, and the "weakest link" shadow price Panelist 2 puts at +60-90% real falls to +25-40% — which is inside what observed wages can deliver without the fiscal transfer 2A says is strained. That is asymmetric prior-framing use (a drag/pull asymmetry one level down from the one the brief names): the locked prior's own healthy-aging term was spent once on growth and never on the quantity it mechanically reduces.

SECOND ATTACK, and this one is an INTERNAL CONTRADICTION in Wave 1 rather than a disagreement. Panelists 2 and 3 both kill CQ1's wage conjunct using a composition artifact: a surge of low-wage entrants into ISIC Q pulls Q's MEDIAN down (-3 to -5pp per Panelist 2; "-10 to -20pp" jointly per Panelist 3). But Panelist 2 simultaneously asserts that entry is throughput-blocked — "OECD-wide care-sector entry capacity 400-700k/yr against a ~2M/yr requirement", "elasticity of actual ENTRIES to wage is only ~0.1", gated by credential recognition, licensure exams, clinical bridging and visa caps. You cannot have both. If the licensing queue binds, the low-wage entrant flood that dilutes Q's median does not arrive; the gap closes on PRICE for incumbents, which is exactly what the median measures. Panelist 3 reproduces the same joint claim without flagging it. The two arguments are substitutes, not complements, and Wave 1 banked both.

MY DECOMPOSITION. Conjunct 1 (OECD-38 harmonized unemployment 5-yr avg <=5.5%, 2032-36). Wave 1: 0.45 / 0.55 / 0.58. All three over-weight the recession channel relative to the denominator channel. Observed: starting level ~4.9-5.0%, the series' record low; locked 2A has 20-64 headcount shrinking while 65+/20-64 goes 31% -> 39-41%, which removes people from the labour-force denominator rather than adding them to the unemployment numerator. Reference class for a SHRINKING-labour-force advanced economy through repeated recessions: Japan 1991-2010 ran 2.1-5.4% across three recessions and two banking crises and never averaged above ~5.4% over any five years; Germany's rate FELL through 2008-09; Korea's never exceeded 4%. Panelist 1's "~40% base rate of an OECD-wide recession year" is right but his translation (+1.5-2.5pp for 2-3 years) is a pre-2008 elasticity estimated on growing labour forces. Marginal 0.62.
Conjunct 2 (F+Q real median hourly growth exceeds J+K+M by >=10.0pp cumulative, 2025-2036). Wave 1: 0.14 / 0.25 / 0.20. Required: ~0.87pp/yr for 11 years. Against Wave 1: (i) the dilution argument is forfeit per the contradiction above, worth +6 to +9pp; (ii) the J/K/M side does not need a median COLLAPSE, only flatness, and 2B AI-Q5 already carries 38.2% for a >=3.5pp labour-share fall in exactly these sectors — a falling labour share with roughly flat sectoral employment is a falling real median by arithmetic; (iii) the observed 2021-2025 sign is already correct and already running at roughly the required rate in the largest weight (US healthcare-support and construction real wage growth above information/finance/professional by ~1-2pp/yr), so the required path is a CONTINUATION, not a sign flip — Panelist 1's framing of it as "the sign FLIPPING" anchors on a 1980-2019 window that the data left five years ago; (iv) Panelist 1's "~70% of Q is publicly financed and administratively wage-set" is true and is the strongest point against, but administratively set wages in a binding shortage move in steps and have moved (UK Agenda for Change, German Pflegemindestlohn, multiple US state Medicaid wage floors 2022-2025). Against me: the credentialing-gated migration inflow is real and does dilute at the margin; K (finance) medians are rent-protected and rising; Panelist 3's point that no harmonized OECD-38 sectoral real MEDIAN hourly series exists at the required endpoints (Eurostat SES quadrennial 2022/2026/2030/2034, ~2.5yr lag, non-EU members absent) is correct and an unmeasurable conjunct resolves NO by convention. Marginal 0.33 on economics, 0.30 after a measurement-convention haircut.
CORRELATION: positive and LARGER than Wave 1 allowed. Wave 1 used rho +0.15 to +0.3 on the theory that the displacement big enough to flatten J/K/M also raises unemployment. That offset is weak, because the displacement is concentrated in a sector group that is ~15-18% of employment while the absorbing sectors (F+Q) are ~18-20% and growing. P(conjunct 2 | conjunct 1) = 0.40 against 0.30 unconditional.
JOINT = 0.62 x 0.40 = 0.248. ANSWER 23, versus Wave 1's 9/16/13. I am not splitting the difference: the gap is the dilution contradiction plus the denominator mechanism.
wave2.cq2_reasoning:
Wave 1 spread 20 / 38 / 49 — the widest in the panel, which tells you the panel knows it has not identified the binding leg. It has not. Panelists 1 and 2 both silently computed a G7-ish core and MISSED the single strongest piece of analysis any Wave-1 panelist produced: Panelist 3's observation that a PPP-GDP-weighted "OECD-38" core aggregate carries Türkiye at ~5% of the weight (versus ~1.3% at market rates) with core CPI ~30% in 2025, plus Mexico, Colombia, Chile, Costa Rica, Poland and Hungary. That is pure anchoring on the phrase "OECD-38" as if it meant "rich countries". The Section lock mandates constant 2025 USD PPP, so the weighting is not a judgment call. I ADOPT Panelist 3's leg and raise it slightly.

Conjunct A (OECD-38 GDP-weighted core CPI/PCE >= 2.50%/yr avg 2027-2036). Observed/mechanical: an underlying G7-ish core of ~2.1-2.3% plus +0.5 to +0.9pp from Türkiye alone on any Türkiye 2027-36 average of 12-18%, plus +0.10-0.20pp from the LatAm/CEE members, lands the stated measure at ~2.7-3.1%. Partially offsetting and correctly identified by Panelist 3: "core CPI/PCE" is an OR, and US core PCE runs 25-40bp below US core CPI at the largest single weight (-0.10 to -0.15pp). Inferred: Türkiye disinflates through the 2030s but a 10-year average needs only the early years to carry it, and the window OPENS with 2026 core elevated. MARGINAL A = 0.84.

Conjunct B (China headline CPI < 1.50%/yr avg 2027-2036). Wave 1: 0.65 / 0.78 / 0.62. THIS is the leg nobody attacked, and it is where I break hardest. All three treat Japanification as near-automatic off an N=1 reference class (Japan's 3-of-3 decade windows). Against: (i) China's own 2000-2019 average was ~2.6%, and a sub-1.5% TEN-YEAR average requires essentially the entire decade at Japan levels with no reflationary interval; (ii) food is ~18-20% of the NBS basket and supplies almost all the variance — Panelist 3 names the arithmetic ("one bad food year at +5% headline adds +0.5pp to a 10-year average") and then under-weights it; over ten years you expect roughly two pork-cycle peaks, so the food channel alone is worth ~+0.5 to +0.8pp on the decade average relative to a no-cycle path; (iii) the 2A fiscal block is misread as deflationary — state pension/social-security subsidies at ~2.9T RMB and rising toward a worker/retiree ratio of 2.8 is a transfer-financed consumption floor under a retiree cohort with a care- and service-heavy basket, i.e. a services-price support, not a drag; (iv) the explicit 2025-26 capacity-cut and anti-price-war policy push is a stated intention to end goods deflation, and the NBS basket is reweighted in 2026 and 2031 inside the window, both of which bias prints up; (v) RMB depreciation under a widening (r-g) gap passes through to a food- and energy-importing basket. MARGINAL B = 0.50.

CORRELATION: mildly NEGATIVE, as all three Wave-1 panelists correctly note — the channel making China sub-1.5% likely (excess capacity exported as tradables disinflation) pushes OECD core down. The offset is weak because my conjunct A is carried by a WEIGHTING ARTEFACT and by services, both orthogonal to Chinese goods prices. rho ~ -0.08, so P(A|B) ~ 0.80.
JOINT = 0.50 x 0.80 = 0.40. ANSWER 40. Note the decomposition is nearly orthogonal to Wave 1's despite landing between Panelists 2 and 3: I am far ABOVE all three on the OECD leg (0.84 vs an implied 0.35-0.53 for Panelists 1-2) and far BELOW all three on the China leg (0.50 vs 0.62-0.78). Anyone reading the ensemble spread as agreement about mechanism is reading noise.
wave2.cq3_reasoning:
Wave 1 produced 1.8 / 1.9 / 1.9 for P50 and 1.0-1.1 / 2.8 for the tails — three independent lenses landing inside 0.1pp. That is not triangulation, it is a shared input. The shared input is the OECD leg at 1.1-1.2% and the China leg at 2.8-3.0%, and both are wrong in the same direction.

THE STRONGEST COHERENT WORLD IN WHICH THE WAVE-1 MODAL VIEW IS SIMPLY WRONG, probability ~35%: "Care-Demand Deflation + Reported-Growth Floor + Scarcity Mechanization." Morbidity compression (2A's own 41-country, N~1M capacity result) cuts the 2036 care-FTE requirement 20-35% below Panelist 2's headcount derivation; the labour-scarcity wage signal induces genuine capital deepening rather than rationing (the Habakkuk mechanism, and Acemoglu-Restrepo 2017 find NO negative cross-country relation between aging and GDP-per-capita growth 1990-2015, if anything positive, with aging countries adopting MORE robots — a result none of the three panelists cites and which is the single best available falsification of the 2A counterfactual's propagation into a FORECAST); the healthy-aging capacity gain lands in the Solow residual and prints as TFP; and reported Chinese growth holds its institutional floor. In that world combined growth is 2.5-2.9%, CQ6-A resolves, and Wave 1's 11-13 for A is a factor-of-two error.

MY BUILD-UP. Weights: OECD-38 ~ $78-80T 2025 PPP, China ~ $40T, combined ~ $118-120T, so China ~ 0.34 / OECD ~ 0.66. Panelist 1 used 0.30/0.70, which biased his composite down ~7bp on his own figures; Panelists 2-3 used 0.35-0.36.
CHINA LEG. All three take 2.8-3.0%. But the question resolves on NBS-REPORTED real GDP as reprinted by the IMF. Panelist 3 identified the reported-versus-deflator-consistent wedge (+1 to +1.5pp, +0.35 to +0.55pp on the composite) and then used 3.0% anyway, applying the wedge to a "true growth" baseline he never wrote down — an unresolved double standard that silently discards his own largest swing factor. Reference class for REPORTED Chinese growth: no sub-4% print in 35 years except 2020 and 2022, and 15th/16th Five-Year-Plan targets will be set around 4.5-5% and then ~4%. The institutional floor is a property of the resolving series, not of the economy. China 2032-36 reported: P50 3.6%, P10 2.0%, P90 4.8%.
OECD LEG. 2A gives per-capita 1.0 -> 0.6%/yr "absent productivity offsets". Population: OECD-38 includes the US, Canada, Australia and the UK; aggregate population growth has run ~0.4-0.5%/yr on migration and tightens from here — use +0.25%. Productivity offset: Wave 1 used +0.15 to +0.28pp. I use +0.35pp, for two reasons Wave 1 itself supplied and then refused to propagate. First, Panelist 3's attribution point: growth accounting measures labour as bodies and hours with at best an education adjustment, so the "70 in 2022 = 53 in 2000" capacity gain is an unmeasured labour-quality improvement that lands in the residual and is PUBLISHED as TFP — he flagged this as a coupling tension and then left it out of his own CQ3. Second, Panelist 1 established the labour-scarcity adoption pull (and would raise AI-Q2 to 38-45%) and then declared, without argument, that "this upward revision does NOT propagate to AI-Q1 or to my CQ3." That is the drag/pull asymmetry in its purest form: aging is allowed to raise the QUANTITY of adoption and forbidden from raising its measured PRODUCT. Retirement-age extension adds ~+0.10pp of hours. Net against Panelist 2's Baumol reallocation drag of -0.15 to -0.20pp/yr, which I halve because the hours shift into Q is itself endogenous to the care-demand deflation above. OECD-38 P50 = 1.30%.
COMPOSITE P50 = 0.66(1.30) + 0.34(3.60) = 0.858 + 1.224 = 2.08 -> 2.1%.
P10 = 1.2%: an OECD recession year inside the window plus a Chinese property/fiscal hard landing, but the left tail is FATTER-TAILED-BUT-SHORTER than Wave 1's because a sub-1.5% composite requires a break in the reported-growth regime, not merely a bad economy.
P90 = 3.1%: OECD 1.9% with the residual carrying the capacity gain, reported China 4.6%, and a 2032-36 migration surge relieving the care constraint.
I accept the locked 2A healthy-aging identity on Panelist 3's NET reading (-1.1pp/yr is net of the +0.4pp) and do not double-count it; my upward revision comes from the measurement and reported-series channels, not from re-adding that term.
wave2.cq4_reasoning:
Wave 1: P50 1.9 / 2.0 / 1.9. All three reconstruct a ~1.68-1.70% GDP-weighted starting level and then land a 2032-36 average within 20-35bp of it, which Panelist 1 explicitly argued is the LOW-base-rate outcome (decade-to-decade G7 shifts of 1.7-5.0pp; only ~30% chance a forward 5-year average sits within +/-50bp of today) and then did anyway. That is anchoring dressed as a base rate.

The shared starting-point reconstruction also embeds a non-US drag that is the fastest-eroding component in the set. Panelist 2's justification is the sharpest error in the panel: "the 50-64 pre-retirement bulge keeps desired saving high through the early 2030s (the dissaving cohort is not yet dominant in the OECD)". The locked 2A arithmetic says the opposite — the old-age ratio reaches 39-41% BY 2036, i.e. the 2032-36 window IS the arrival of the dissaving phase, not its antechamber. He has demography as a saving glut and never as a dissaver, which is the drag/pull asymmetry applied to r* instead of to g.

MY RECONSTRUCTION, 2032-36 averages, PPP-GDP weights per the Section lock (renormalized: US .483, Japan .132, Germany .110, France .077, UK .077, Italy .066, Canada .055): US 2.6 (unchanged from the DFII10 2.60% anchor — my CQ3 P50 of 2.1% does not require r* to fall), Japan 1.3 (BoJ normalization plus a thin JGBi/swap market printing a LOW breakeven against a rising nominal, which Panelist 3 correctly notes prints Japan HIGH on this measure), Germany 1.4, France 1.8, UK 2.6 (Panelist 3's Feb-2030 RPI->CPIH alignment collapses UK breakevens and mechanically RAISES the measured UK real yield ~80-100bp, a dated step INSIDE the window — he identified it and then moved the aggregate only 6-7bp because he kept the pre-alignment UK level), Italy 2.3 (BTP€i references euro-area HICP ex-tobacco, overstating the Italian real yield whenever Italian inflation exceeds the area average), Canada 2.0 (proxied; Real Return Bond issuance ended 2022).
Weighted: 1.256 + 0.172 + 0.154 + 0.139 + 0.200 + 0.152 + 0.110 = 2.18 -> P50 = 2.2%.
Direction of the supporting block, both ways. UP: gross public debt >100% of GDP by 2029 (~142% US, ~127% China by 2031), net interest 2 -> 3% of GDP, 3-yr P95 Debt-at-Risk ~117% (+2.4pp under a 20% AI-led equity shock), eroding sovereign convenience yields, levered basis-trade absorption replacing price-insensitive official and bank demand, IMF's (r-g) worsening ~+1.0pp, and the dissaving cohort arriving in-window. DOWN: the 1945-1970s advanced-economy precedent of resolving high debt through sustained negative real yields, and Japan 1995-2025 as proof that 200%+ debt/GDP can coexist with ~0-1% real yields.
P10 = 1.0%: financial repression plus a post-impairment demand shortfall. I keep this tail tighter than Panelist 1's 0.4% and Panelist 3's 0.9% because a 5-year G7 average near zero now requires the US leg — 48% of the weight, currently at +2.60% — to fall ~250bp, which is a larger move than the repression precedents delivered from a comparable start.
P90 = 3.4%: fiscal dominance with the pension/care claim repriced at the long end, Debt-at-Risk realization, plus the UK alignment step.
wave2.cq5_reasoning:
Wave 1: 23 / 28 / 24, with conjunct A (MOVE 10-yr average >= 105) at 0.33 / 0.42 / 0.48. This is the clearest case in the panel of a correct observation made and then not priced. Panelist 3 states it exactly: "MOVE is NORMALISED (basis-point) implied vol ... so its LEVEL scales with the level of yields. A persistent 4%+ nominal regime floors MOVE around 85-100 without any stress" — and then concludes "a 105 decade-average then requires 2022-23 conditions roughly a third of the time" and sets A = 0.48. If the unstressed FLOOR is 85-100, a 105 average needs stress episodes lifting the mean ~10-20 points above floor, which is one or two 2022-style years plus ordinary 2024-style churn, not a third of the decade at 120-140. Panelist 1's reconstruction compounds the error by averaging historical MOVE levels across yield REGIMES without rescaling: his "1988-1997 and 1990-1999 likely >=105" windows sat on 6-8% nominal yields and his "2010-2019 ~70" sat on 1.5-2.5% — those are not comparable observations of the same quantity, and treating them as one reference class is the base-rate equivalent of adding nominal and real series. My CQ4 P50 of 2.2% real plus ~2.5% OECD inflation implies a US 10y nominal averaging ~4.5-5.0% through 2027-2036. In that regime the bp-vol floor alone is ~90-100. MARGINAL A = 0.60.

Conjunct B. Sub-step 1, at least one MSCI World >=25% peak-to-trough drawdown in 2027-2036: I accept Wave 1's 0.78-0.85 and use 0.80 — 2B AI-Q4 at 66% already posits an impairment or revenue-coverage failure, index concentration in AI-levered names is extreme, the $1.4T commitment stack rests on ~$300B equity and ~$650B debt, the IMF scenario is explicit at 20%, and USD denomination plus a price (not total-return) basis each make the 25% threshold easier.
Sub-step 2, conditional "no-rally" (G7 GDP-weighted 10y nominals fail to fall >=50bp, or rise >=25bp, inside the drawdown window). Wave 1: 0.39 / 0.55 / 0.40. Panelist 1's regime-sorting is the right frame and his own evidence supports a HIGHER conditional than he used: five of eight historical episodes failed, and he discounts to 0.39 by assigning only ~30% weight to the inflation-salient regime — a weight contradicted by his own CQ2 OECD-core marginal and flatly contradicted by my 0.84. Add two structural points Panelist 3 raised and under-priced: under the Section-locked PPP weights Japan is ~13% and Italy ~7% of the aggregate, Japan cannot contribute a 50bp rally from a ~2% nominal, and Italian yields typically RISE in risk-off as spreads widen — so a PPP-weighted G7 aggregate is mechanically less able to rally 50bp than the US alone. Plus the undefined "drawdown window": the equity trough coincides with the yield PEAK in inflation- or supply-driven selloffs, which favours YES. Conditional = 0.55 for at least one qualifying episode given ~1.5-2 expected drawdowns. MARGINAL B = 0.80 x 0.55 = 0.44.
CORRELATION: strongly positive, rho ~ +0.6 — a high-bp-vol decade is definitionally the regime in which the equity-bond hedge fails; both legs are one bet on inflation salience and duration-supply plumbing. P(B|A) = 0.70.
JOINT = 0.60 x 0.70 = 0.42, trimmed to 40 for residual conjunction humility and for the fact that ICE can reconstitute or discontinue the index. ANSWER 40, versus Wave 1's 23-28. This is my largest single break from the Wave-1 centre and it rests on one technical fact about the resolving series that a Wave-1 panelist wrote down and declined to use.
wave2.cq6_reasoning:
Applied the lexical-priority lock strictly, using MY CQ3 (P10 1.2 / P50 2.1 / P90 3.1; implied upper sigma ~0.78pp, lower sigma ~0.70pp, mildly left-skewed) and MY CQ2 inflation legs.

STEP 1, A (growth >= 2.6%): z = (2.6 - 2.1)/0.78 = 0.64 -> P = 0.26, trimmed to 22 for the weight-arithmetic conjunction (A needs reported China ~4.4% with OECD 1.5%, or ~4.0% with OECD 1.9% — the upper-middle of BOTH legs, not either alone). A = 22, versus Wave 1's 11/12/13. The doubling is the direct and intended consequence of the two propagations Wave 1 refused: reported-Chinese-growth institutional floor, and healthy-aging capacity landing in the published Solow residual.
STEP 2, C (OECD-38 core >= 2.7% over 2032-36 AND growth < 2.0%): P(growth < 2.0) = Phi((2.0-2.1)/0.70) = Phi(-0.14) = 0.445. P(core >= 2.7 | growth < 2.0): my CQ2 conjunct A marginal is 0.84 for >=2.50% over 2027-36; the stricter >=2.70% on the later 2032-36 sub-window is ~0.55 unconditionally (the Türkiye/LatAm weighting floor erodes but does not vanish, and the care/Baumol channel builds LATE while capex-digestion disinflation is front-loaded), shaded to 0.52 conditional because part of the low-growth mass is the deflationary-bust branch where the artefact itself fades. C = 0.445 x 0.52 = 0.231 -> 23.
STEP 3, D (growth < 1.7% AND core < 2.0%): P(growth < 1.7) = Phi((1.7-2.1)/0.70) = Phi(-0.57) = 0.285. P(core < 2.0 | growth < 1.7) = 0.25. I ADOPT Panelist 3's largest MECE finding here and Panelists 1-2 missed it entirely: rule 3 requires core < 2.0 on the SAME PPP-GDP-weighted OECD-38 measure CQ2 uses, which carries a ~+0.4 to +0.5pp composition floor, so a genuine BIS-style demand-shortfall world with underlying G7 core at ~1.5% still PRINTS ~2.0-2.1% and fails rule 3, draining D into B. D = 0.285 x 0.25 = 0.071 -> 7, versus Wave 1's 24/18/8. Panelist 1's 24 is the panel's worst number: he marked D UP from 21 to 24 citing AI-Q4's 66% impairment marginal, while Panelist 3 had already shown (correctly, and then under-used) that impairment is a BALANCE-SHEET event with near-zero flow GDP content, and while using an inflation measure he never weighted for Türkiye.
STEP 4, B = 100 - 22 - 23 - 7 = 48 (residual). SUM = 22 + 48 + 23 + 7 = 100 exactly.

CONSISTENCY CHECKS PERFORMED. (i) Against my CQ3: P50 = 2.1% sits inside B's literal 1.7-2.5% band, so B must and does carry the plurality; the mass I give growth >= 2.6% (22) is slightly BELOW the 26 my own sigma implies, justified by the two-leg weight conjunction, so the deviation is in the conservative direction. With a P50 of 2.1% I am permitted far more A-mass than Wave 1's 11-13, and the lock's prohibition ("if your CQ3 P50 is 2.1% you cannot put most mass on A") is respected: 22 < 48. (ii) Against my CQ2: C requires core >= 2.70% on the shorter, later 2032-36 window, strictly tighter than CQ2's >= 2.50% on 2027-36. My CQ2 ANSWER is 40, but the relevant comparison is CQ2's OECD CONJUNCT marginal of 0.84, not the joint — C = 23 is far below 84 and below my 55 marginal for >=2.70% on 2032-36, as required, with the gap being the growth<2.0 condition. Note that CQ6-C is NOT bounded by CQ2's joint of 40, because CQ2's joint is pulled down by the China leg (0.50), which is irrelevant to C. Wave 1 Panelists 1 and 2 both benchmarked C against their CQ2 JOINT rather than the OECD conjunct and thereby mis-stated their own check. (iii) C and D are disjoint by construction (core >= 2.7 vs core < 2.0) and both evaluated after A. (iv) A + B = 70 against P(growth >= 1.7) = 0.715 from my CQ3 — the ~1.5pp wedge is the low-growth/moderate-inflation leftover cell (growth < 1.7 with core 2.0-2.69) that rule 4 assigns to B, net of the growth-2.0-to-2.59 mass also in B. Consistent. (v) I do not accept C's "grid supply wall" leg: Panelist 3's arithmetic on AI-Q3 (365 -> 998 TWh is ~72 GW average load, ~$35-75B/yr against OECD-38+China power capex of ~$600-800B/yr) is correct and the binding constraint is interconnection QUEUE TIME, not capital. My C = 23 rests on the inflation-measurement floor plus the late-building care Baumol channel.

hypothesis_critique.a: "SMOOTHLY" carries the failure, and I agree with Wave 1's near-floor scores (4/4/4) — this is the one plank the panel got right. But the panel's reason is only half the reason. Wave 1 kills it on the supply side (reservation-wage gap ~-55% at the aide tier, 18-42 month credential-recognition queues, modal displaced age 42-55 against a 10-20 year retraining amortization, a care workforce 77-88% female against a male-skewed displaced pool in K and IT, among the highest MSD rates of any occupation, aide turnover 40-60%/yr proving the tier is WAGE- not vacancy-rationed). All true. The second failure is that the plank also presupposes "THE WORKERS NEEDED" as a fixed exogenous quantity, which is the premise I attack: required care FTE is endogenous to morbidity compression, family substitution, utilization policy and the shadow wage. The plank is wrong twice — the transfer does not happen smoothly, AND the quantity it claims to supply is not a constant. 5.
hypothesis_critique.b: TWO words fail. "BLOCKS" is wrong on sign-structure: AI compresses the VIRTUAL leg (Philippines voice-BPO ~1.7M workers, India IT-BPM ~$280B) while OECD demography expands the PHYSICAL leg (nursing, aged care, skilled trades), and the physical leg carries the larger wage premium per worker and the GCC remittance channel is physical-labour-based and structurally insulated. The two legs move in OPPOSITE directions, so "blocks their ability to export labour" misdescribes the mechanism rather than merely over-stating it. "SEVERELY" fails on scope: India IT-BPM exports are ~7% of India's nominal GDP and a far smaller share of PPP GDP; Philippine BPO is ~1.7M of ~50M employed, ~3.5%; remittances (~$125B India, ~$40B Philippines) grow with OECD care demand. A 30% compression of the virtual leg is a 2pp GDP event for India spread over a decade — painful and regionally concentrated (Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Metro Manila), not severe at the national macro level. Wave 1 at 13-15 under-corrected for scope; the net sign for the Philippines over 2025-2036 is plausibly POSITIVE once nursing and seafaring migration and remittances are netted. 11.
hypothesis_critique.c: "THEN FALLS" carries the failure — the SHAPE is wrong, not just the level, and Wave 1's spread (55/17/30) shows the panel never settled it. Three reasons the 2030s are the MORE inflationary half on the measure that resolves: (i) the PPP-GDP-weighted OECD-38 aggregate carries a ~+0.4 to +0.5pp Türkiye/LatAm/CEE composition floor that erodes only slowly; (ii) the care/Baumol channel builds LATE — the 80+ cohort compounds at ~3.5%/yr and the old-age ratio reaches 39-41% BY 2036, so the care shadow price peaks in the 2032-36 window, while the capex-digestion disinflation Wave 1 relies on is front-loaded into 2027-31; (iii) the fiscal claim (net interest 2 -> 3% of GDP, pension and care obligations that cannot be deferred) tightens through the decade. Panelist 1's 55 is the panel's most generous and rests on central-bank reaction functions as a structural feature — which is a reason to expect a LEVEL near target, not a FALL from the 2020s to the 2030s. 20.
hypothesis_critique.d: "EXPONENTIAL" and "EVENTUALLY" both fail, and "WINS" is undefined. "Exponential" is the wrong functional form: diffusion of a general-purpose business input is logistic (Panelist 1's own broadband and cloud reference class), and the Hulten ceiling plus Baumol-exposed sectors cap the measured residual regardless of capability. "Eventually" is unfalsifiable at a Dec-2036 horizon and is doing the plank's real work — strip it and the claim becomes a dated one that the base rate of dated technology-offsets-demography claims resolving true inside their own decade (~1-2 of 6-8 episodes) argues against. I score this HIGHER than Wave 1 (18/12/17) because my CQ3 P50 of 2.1% and CQ6-A at 22 say growth plausibly does hold up — but NOT through the plank's mechanism. What delivers it in my world is the reported-Chinese-growth floor, healthy-aging capacity printing as TFP, labour-scarcity-induced mechanization and migration-driven OECD population growth. The plank is directionally lucky and causally wrong, and "substantially correct AS STATED" grades the causal claim. 22.

key_drivers: ENDOGENOUS CARE DEMAND (the shared assumption I destroy). All three Wave-1 panelists derive required formal care FTE from headcount demography with fixed age-specific utilization (Panelist 2 explicitly: e_caredemand|65+ = 1.25, +22-25M FTE, ~2M/yr requirement). The same 2A bullet they cite for growth says the functional-capacity curve has shifted right by ~15-17 years of chronological age (41 countries, N~1M). Spending that term on growth and never on the care quantity it mechanically deflates cuts the derived 2036 FTE gap 20-35% and the shadow wage from +60-90% to +25-40% real. This is the load-bearing driver of my CQ1 (23), my CQ3 P50 (2.1), and my CQ6-A (22).

THE DILUTION / THROUGHPUT CONTRADICTION. Panelists 2 and 3 kill CQ1's wage conjunct with a low-wage-entrant surge diluting the ISIC Q median, while Panelist 2 simultaneously asserts entry is licence-throttled at 400-700k/yr against a ~2M/yr requirement with an entry-to-wage elasticity of ~0.1. The arguments are substitutes, not complements. If the licensing queue binds, the dilution does not arrive and the gap closes on price for incumbents — which is exactly what a sector MEDIAN measures. Worth +6 to +9pp on CQ1's second conjunct.

REPORTED-SERIES INSTITUTIONAL FLOOR ON CHINESE GROWTH. CQ3 resolves on NBS-reported real GDP as reprinted by the IMF, not on true growth. No sub-4% print in 35 years outside 2020 and 2022; 15th/16th Five-Year-Plan targets will anchor ~4.5-5% then ~4%. Panelist 3 identified the reported-versus-deflator-consistent wedge (+1 to +1.5pp, +0.35-0.55pp on the composite) and then used 3.0% anyway against a true-growth baseline he never wrote down. Correcting that double standard moves the composite +0.24pp at a 0.34 weight and is the largest single contributor to my CQ3 P50 sitting 0.2-0.3pp above the whole Wave-1 panel.

BASIS-POINT NORMALIZATION OF THE MOVE INDEX. MOVE is bp-normalized implied vol, so its unstressed floor scales with the level of yields: ~85-100 in the 4-5% nominal regime my CQ4 implies, versus 50-70 in 2010-2019. Panelist 3 wrote this down and then set the MOVE conjunct at 0.48; Panelist 1 built a reference class by averaging MOVE levels across incommensurable yield regimes. Rescaling takes conjunct A to 0.60 and CQ5 from the Wave-1 centre of 25 to 40.

PPP-WEIGHTING COMPOSITION FLOOR IN THE 'OECD-38' INFLATION AGGREGATE. Under the Section-locked constant-2025-PPP basis, Türkiye is ~5% of OECD-38 GDP (core CPI ~30% in 2025) plus Mexico, Colombia, Chile, Costa Rica, Poland, Hungary — a ~+0.4 to +0.9pp pure-composition addition that Panelists 1 and 2 missed entirely. It carries my CQ2 OECD conjunct to 0.84, supports CQ6-C at 23, and makes CQ6-D nearly unreachable (7) even in a genuine BIS-style demand-shortfall world.

THE DRAG/PULL ASYMMETRY, APPLIED TWICE BY WAVE 1 AT ONE LEVEL UP. Panelist 1 establishes the labour-scarcity adoption pull (would lift AI-Q2 to 38-45%) and then states without argument that it does not propagate to AI-Q1 or his CQ3 — aging raises the QUANTITY of adoption and is forbidden from raising its measured PRODUCT. Panelist 2 claims the OECD dissaving cohort 'is not yet dominant' through the early 2030s when the locked 2A arithmetic puts the old-age ratio at 39-41% BY 2036 — demography as a saving glut and never as a dissaver. Against both: Acemoglu-Restrepo (2017) find no negative cross-country relation between aging and GDP-per-capita growth 1990-2015, with aging countries adopting MORE robots — the best available falsification of propagating 2A's counterfactual accounting into a forecast, and cited by none of the three.

wave2.coupling_tension:
PRIMARY TENSION: 2B's AI-Q1 (2032-36 PPP-weighted TFP lift >= +0.50pp/yr, locked at 23.0% raw) is too LOW once demographics are endogenous, and should sit at ~33-38%. DIRECTION: UP, and by more than any Wave-1 panelist allowed. Three coupling channels, two of which Wave 1 identified and then declined to propagate.
(1) ATTRIBUTION ARTEFACT (Panelist 3's point, which he filed as a tension and then omitted from his own CQ3). Growth accounting measures labour input as bodies and hours with at best an education-share quality adjustment; it has no cognitive- or physical-capacity adjustment. The 2A healthy-aging result ("70 in 2022 = 53 in 2000", 41 countries, N~1M) is precisely an unmeasured labour-quality improvement, so whatever share escapes the education adjustment lands in the Solow residual and is PUBLISHED AS TFP. A conservative quarter-attribution puts +0.10pp/yr of pure demographic health gain into measured TFP — 20% of the 0.50pp bar, with no AI causation. The threshold is defined on measured TFP, so this is not a technology forecast but an accounting fact about the resolving series.
(2) SCARCITY-INDUCED MECHANIZATION (Panelist 1's adoption pull, which he explicitly refused to propagate: "this upward revision does NOT propagate to AI-Q1 or to my CQ3"). The locked 2A labour-scarcity arithmetic is a demand pull, and the reference class for forced factor substitution under labour scarcity (Habakkuk's American manufacturing, post-1964 Bracero-termination agricultural mechanization, Japanese robot density after its 1995 workforce peak, 1950s-60s guest-worker-constrained European manufacturing) shows scarcity raising adoption AND measured labour productivity, not adoption alone. Decisively, Acemoglu and Restrepo (2017) find NO negative cross-country relation between aging and GDP-per-capita growth over 1990-2015 — if anything positive — with aging countries adopting MORE robots. Not one of the three Wave-1 panelists cites it. 2A's "-1.1pp/yr" is a counterfactual accounting decomposition, which is given fact and which I do not re-litigate; what is NOT given is that the counterfactual's magnitude propagates one-for-one into a forecast of the OBSERVED path, and the one direct cross-country test of that propagation returns approximately zero.
(3) THE BAUMOL REALLOCATION DRAG IS PARTLY ENDOGENOUS AWAY. Panelist 2 subtracts 0.15-0.20pp/yr of measured TFP for a forced 3.5-4pp shift of hours into a ~0%-productivity-growth sector, and calls AI-Q1 too HIGH by 5-7pp on that basis. That drag is real but is sized off his own exogenous care-FTE requirement. Deflate the requirement by morbidity compression (20-35%) and the hours shift falls to 2.3-3.0pp, cutting the drag to 0.08-0.13pp/yr. So Panelist 2's tension points the right way and is roughly half the size he gives it, leaving channels (1) and (2) dominant.
NET: endogenizing demographics should move AI-Q1 from 23.0% to ~33-38%, and correspondingly AI-Q6's Transformative Breakout from 16.2% to ~22% with the Hulten-Ceiling cell falling from 36.5% to ~29%. This is the direct source of my CQ3 P50 of 2.1% (vs the Wave-1 panel's 1.8-1.9) and my CQ6-A of 22 (vs 11-13).
SECONDARY, OPPOSITE-SIGN TENSION I ACCEPT: 2B's AI-Q4 at 66.0% is too low on its own reference class (announced capex supercycles ending >=20% impaired: roughly 5 of 6 named episodes — 1840s railway mania, 1870s-90s US rail, 1999-2002 telecom/fibre, 2014-2020 US shale, 1975-85 US nuclear — so ~80%), and coupling with 2A's plumbing block (~$1.4T circular commitments on ~$300B equity and ~$650B debt, +2.4pp Debt-at-Risk under a 20% AI-led equity shock) pushes it higher still. DIRECTION: UP to ~78-82. CRITICALLY, this does NOT contradict my higher growth numbers, and Wave 1 mishandled exactly this: Panelist 3 correctly notes impairments are balance-sheet, not flow, so a 66-80% impairment marginal subtracts almost nothing from measured real GDP — and then Panelist 1 marked CQ6-D UP from 21 to 24 citing that same 66% as evidence for a flow-GDP demand shortfall. A high-impairment, high-growth world is fully coherent: the compute gets written down and keeps running.
THIRD TENSION, where I DISAGREE with Panelist 2's direction: he argues AI-Q5 (J/K/M labour compensation share falling >=3.5pp) should rise +10 to +14pp because sector-specific scarcity is non-arbitrable at e_cross = 0.07. The mechanism is right but its magnitude is hostage to the same exogenous care requirement; deflate that and the care market is less tight, the shadow wage lower, and the J/K/M worker's outside option less catastrophically bad. I would move AI-Q5 UP only modestly, to ~43-46%, and note that this cuts against CQ1's wage conjunct in a way that Panelist 2's own write-up concedes ("the labour SHARE can collapse while the measured MEDIAN rises") — which is why I report CQ1 at 23 rather than higher.

wave2.lens_self_description: I answered purely as an arithmetic decomposer: every number below is the output of an explicit sum, product or weighted average built from the three Wave-1 panelists' own stated coefficients plus the locked Section 2A/2B quantities, and I forbade myself any claim I could not write as a line of arithmetic — no narrative judgment, no appeal to plausibility, and no number carried over from a panelist without re-deriving it and reporting where their own figures fail to multiply.
wave2.cq1_reasoning: CONJUNCT A: OECD-38 harmonized unemployment 5-yr average <=5.5% over 2032-36. Build the level: start 4.90% (2023-25 series low). Mechanical denominator effect from a shrinking 20-64 headcount at -0.3%/yr plus rising 65+ participation (a cohort with sub-3% measured unemployment): -0.30pp. Structural white-collar long-duration friction from e_cross=0.07 (Mechanism panelist's coefficient, which I accept): +0.40pp. No-recession central path = 4.90 - 0.30 + 0.40 = 5.00%, sd of a 5-yr average ~0.40pp -> P(<=5.5 | no recession) = 1-Phi((5.5-5.0)/0.40) complement = Phi(1.25) = 0.89. Recession arithmetic: one OECD-wide recession year inside a 5-year window has base rate ~0.45 (6 episodes/65yr, rising for a window following a 66%-probability capex impairment). A standard recession adds +2.0,+2.0,+1.0,+0.5,+0.0 across the five years = +5.5/5 = +1.10pp -> 6.10%, fails. A mild recession adds +1.0,+1.0,+0.5 = +2.5/5 = +0.50pp -> 5.50%, resolves ~40% of the time. So P(A) = 0.55(0.89) + 0.45(0.30)(0.40 extra) rearranged as 0.55x0.89 + 0.45x0.12 = 0.490 + 0.054 = 0.544. Round A = 0.58 after crediting the migration-driven care/construction low-skill sink (Mechanism panelist's 400-700k/yr entry flow is an employment sink of ~0.1pp). CONJUNCT B: F+Q median real hourly growth minus J+K+M >= +10.0pp cumulative. Two-term decomposition, both terms taken from Wave-1 coefficients: (i) within-job scarcity wedge = +12 to +19pp, midpoint +15.5pp (derived from a 20-25% care FTE gap divided by long-run supply elasticity 0.6 = ~40% shadow wage rise, fiscally throttled to an observed +15-25%, against J+K+M at +3-9%); (ii) composition wedge = -7 to -9pp, midpoint -8.0pp (Q's median diluted by 30-35% growth in aide/migrant employment at ~45% of sector median = -3 to -5pp; J/K/M's median mechanically lifted ~+3 to +4pp by culling the bottom quintile). Net = 15.5 - 8.0 = +7.5pp, sd ~5.0pp (deflator choice alone is +/-2-4pp). P(>=10.0) = 1 - Phi((10.0-7.5)/5.0) = 1 - Phi(0.50) = 0.31. Measurement haircut: no OECD-38 sectoral real MEDIAN hourly series exists (Eurostat SES quadrennial 2022/2026/2030/2034, ~2.5yr lag, neither 2025 nor 2036 endpoint, non-EU members absent); on an unmeasurable conjunct the resolution convention is NO, worth a multiplicative 0.68 -> B = 0.31 x 0.68 = 0.21. CORRELATION: +0.15. Scarcity is a positive common factor, but the displacement large enough to flatten J+K+M real medians is the displacement that lifts unemployment, so the two couplings partly cancel. P(B|A) = 0.21 x 1.15 = 0.24. JOINT = 0.58 x 0.24 = 0.139 -> 13. Independence product would be 0.58 x 0.21 = 0.122; the +0.15 correlation adds 1.7pp.
wave2.cq2_reasoning: CONJUNCT A: OECD-38 GDP-weighted core CPI/PCE >= 2.50%/yr avg 2027-36. This is an INDEX-COMPOSITION sum, not a macro call, and the two Wave-1 panelists who treated it as a macro call are arithmetically wrong (see hypothesis_critique and coupling_tension). Weights on the Section-locked PPP basis: Turkiye ~5.0% of OECD-38 PPP GDP, Mexico ~4.7%, plus Chile/Colombia/Costa Rica/Poland/Hungary ~2.5% = a high-inflation bloc of ~12% of the index versus ~4% at market exchange rates. Set the bloc at 6.0%/yr average 2027-36 (Turkiye disinflating from ~30% toward 8-12%, Mexico ~4%) and the remaining 88% at 2.10%: aggregate = 0.12(6.0) + 0.88(2.10) = 0.72 + 1.85 = 2.57%. Add the Mechanism panelist's Baumol pass-through of +0.28pp/yr (care at 13-14% of core x 70% labour share x ~0% productivity, plus the construction/shelter leg) to the non-bloc term: 0.12(6.0) + 0.88(2.38) = 0.72 + 2.09 = 2.81%. Subtract the US core-PCE option (-0.12pp at a 0.30 US weight in the index) -> 2.69%. So the central value is 2.57-2.81% with sd ~0.35pp -> P(>=2.50 | PPP construction) = 0.82. Under a market-weighted or G7-ish construction: 0.04(6.0) + 0.96(2.25) = 0.24 + 2.16 = 2.40% -> P = 0.35. Resolver weights 0.70 PPP (the Section lock says constant 2025 USD PPP and OECD.Stat's own OECD-total aggregate is PPP-GDP-weighted) / 0.30 market: A = 0.70(0.82) + 0.30(0.35) = 0.574 + 0.105 = 0.68. CONJUNCT B: China headline CPI < 1.50%/yr avg 2027-36. Path arithmetic from a ~0.0-0.2% 2025 base: 2027-29 at 0.3%, 2030-32 at 1.2%, 2033-36 at 1.8% -> (3x0.3 + 3x1.2 + 4x1.8)/10 = (0.9 + 3.6 + 7.2)/10 = 1.17%. sd of the decade average ~0.60pp, dominated by the pork cycle (food ~19% weight; one +5% headline food year adds +0.5pp to a 10-year average). P(<1.50) = Phi((1.50-1.17)/0.60) = Phi(0.55) = 0.71. Shade -0.01 for the 2026 and 2031 basket rebases and official reluctance to print sustained deflation: B = 0.70. CORRELATION: negative but WEAKER than the Reference-Class and Mechanism panelists assumed. Chinese excess capacity exports goods disinflation to the OECD, but 0.72pp of my conjunct-A central value is the emerging-OECD composition term, which is orthogonal to Chinese goods prices, and ~70-75% of the remainder is services. Effective rho = -0.08 -> P(A|B) = 0.68 x 0.94 = 0.64. JOINT = 0.64 x 0.70 = 0.448 -> 46. Independence product would be 0.68 x 0.70 = 0.476; the negative coupling costs 1.6pp. Note this answer is roughly double the Reference-Class panelist's 20 and the gap is entirely the index-weight arithmetic, not a difference of macro view.
wave2.cq3_reasoning: PPP WEIGHT RECONCILIATION FIRST. China 2025 PPP GDP ~$41T; OECD-38 ~$78T (US 30.5, Japan 6.7, Germany 6.1, UK 4.4, France 4.4, Italy 3.5, Turkiye 3.5, Korea 3.3, Mexico 3.3, Canada 2.6, Spain 2.7, Poland 1.9, Australia 1.9, rest ~3.7). Combined $119T -> China 0.345, OECD-38 0.655. I use 0.66/0.34 and the weights are FROZEN at 2025 per the accounting lock, which lowers the composite ~5-10bp versus the IMF's own chain-weighted current-PPP practice. The Reference-Class panelist's 0.30 China weight is 4pp too low and the Auditor's 0.36 is 1.5pp too high. OECD-38 GROWTH-ACCOUNTING SUM, 2032-36: labour input = employment -0.10%/yr (20-64 headcount -0.35, migration +0.20, retirement-age extension +0.15, participation +0.10 -> net ~ -0.10) x labour share 0.62 = -0.06pp; labour quality (education share) +0.15 x 0.62 = +0.09pp; subtotal labour +0.03pp. Capital deepening = capital services +1.80%/yr x capital share 0.38 = +0.68pp, marked to +0.65pp because 2032-36 sits AFTER the AI/grid buildout peak (the AI-Q3 implied capex is only $35-75B/yr against OECD-38+China power capex of $600-800B/yr, 5-10%, so the AI capex stock is not a large enough term to lift the contribution in the measurement window and the AI-Q4 66% impairment marginal implies flow retrenchment). wave2.cq5_reasoning: CONJUNCT A: ICE BofA MOVE 10-year average >= 105 over 2027-36. MOVE is normalized basis-point implied vol, so its LEVEL scales with the yield level; a persistent 4%+ nominal regime floors it near 90-100 with no stress. Explicit arithmetic for a decade average of 105: with a floor of 95 and two stress episodes totalling two years at 150, the average is 0.8(95) + 0.2(150) = 76 + 30 = 106 — just clears. With a floor of 85 and the same spikes, 0.8(85) + 0.2(150) = 68 + 30 = 98 — fails. So the conjunct is exactly a bet on whether the structural floor shifts from ~85 to ~95, and the 2A plumbing facts (eroding convenience yields, levered basis-trade absorption, $1.4T of circular commitments on ~$650B of debt issuance) plus my own +80bp term-premium term support that shift roughly half the time. A = 0.45. CONJUNCT B, two sub-steps. (i) P(at least one MSCI World >= 25% peak-to-trough drawdown in a 10-year window): base rate ~0.80 (9 of 10 decade windows since 1970 contained one; ~7-8 episodes in 55 years), raised by the USD and price-index basis making 25% easier and by the AI-Q4 66% impairment marginal already positing the trigger -> 0.82. (ii) P(the no-rally type | a drawdown occurs): the historical split is 5 of 8 fails but it is entirely regime-sorted — every fail (1973-74, 1980-81, 1987, 1990, 2022) sits in an inflation-salient regime and every pass (2000-02, 2007-09, 2020) in the 1998-2021 disinflation regime. Conditional on an inflation-salient regime 0.80; conditional on disinflation 0.22. My own inflation-salient regime weight from CQ2 and CQ6-C is 0.35: 0.35(0.80) + 0.65(0.22) = 0.280 + 0.143 = 0.423. Add +0.06 for the index-construction artefact — on a PPP-GDP-weighted G7 aggregate Japan carries 0.12 at a yield floor that cannot contribute 50bp of rally and Italy carries 0.06 with spreads that WIDEN in risk-off, so the remaining 0.82 of the index must fall ~65bp for the aggregate to fall 50bp -> 0.48. Episode multiplicity does not compound much because the regime is common across episodes within a decade, so B = 0.82 x 0.52 = 0.43 after regime-correlation shrinkage, call 0.42. CORRELATION: strongly positive, rho ~ +0.57 — a high-MOVE decade IS definitionally the regime in which the equity-bond hedge fails, and in my CQ4 decomposition the same +80bp term-premium term generates both. P(A|B) = 0.72. JOINT = 0.42 x 0.72 = 0.302 -> 28 after a 2pp haircut for the demanding nature of a full-decade volatility average (vol is multiplicative and mean-reverts hard, so the average is hostage to a few spike years). Independence product would be 0.45 x 0.42 = 0.19; regime co-movement adds 9pp, so this is the one CQ where the conjunction discount is more than offset.

hypothesis_critique.a: The failing word is SMOOTHLY, and it fails by a factor of about ten. Required OECD-38 formal care FTE grows 2.6%/yr, about +22-25M FTE by 2036. Gross cognitive displacement is 6-12M, modal age 42-55. At a cross-elasticity of 0.07 the arrow delivers 0.07 x 9M = ~0.6M entrants against a ~23M requirement, i.e. 2.7% of the gap. Each gate is independently multiplicative and each one is near-binding: a -55% reservation-wage step at the aide tier, an 18-42 month credential queue (3-4 years for RN or a trades apprenticeship) against a 10-20 year retraining amortization at that age, a 77-88% female care workforce against a male-skewed displaced pool in K and IT, among the highest MSD/injury rates of any occupation, and geographic immobility (care demand is suburban and rural, displaced cognitive workers sit in high-housing-cost metros). The decisive arithmetic is that 40-60%/yr aide turnover proves the aide tier is WAGE-rationed, not vacancy-rationed, so adding applicants at the prevailing wage adds approximately nothing. 3.
hypothesis_critique.b: Two words fail in opposite directions, which is why the plank nets out near its own floor. BLOCKS is simply the wrong verb: AI compresses the VIRTUAL leg while OECD aging expands the PHYSICAL leg, so the mechanism redirects rather than blocks. SEVERELY is the quantitative failure, and only for India. Legs: the commoditized slice of India's $280B IT-BPM exports is ~35% = ~$98B of gross exposure, of which perhaps 30-50% is actually compressed net of AI-enabled volume scale-up = -$30 to -50B by 2036, about 1.0-1.5% of India's GDP level, i.e. roughly 0.10-0.14pp/yr of growth — material, not severe. The Philippines is genuinely exposed: BPO at ~1.7M workers and ~7-8% of GDP with voice-heavy task composition, so a -25 to -40% task-hour compression is a -2 to -3% GDP-level hit, five to ten times India's in relative terms. Against both: OECD care-sector entry capacity of 400-700k/yr by the early 2030s, of which India plus the Philippines plausibly take 30-40% = 150-250k/yr, each entrant remitting roughly $8-15k/yr, cumulating to $8-20B/yr of incremental remittances by 2036 plus the GCC channel. The plank is therefore roughly right for the Philippines on one leg and wrong for India on both. 14.
hypothesis_critique.c: THEN carries the failure — the plank has the sequence inverted. My decomposition puts the DISINFLATIONARY interval in 2027-31, because that is where the capex-digestion branch sits (AI-Q4 at 66%, impairments and the investment-flow retrenchment) and where Chinese excess capacity is most aggressively exported, while the INFLATIONARY interval is 2032-36, because the 65+ and 80+ waves compound into the care shadow price exactly then, the Baumol pass-through of +0.28pp/yr on core peaks late, and my own CQ6-C derivation puts 2032-36 core AT 2.70% against a 2027-36 average of 2.57-2.81%. 'Hot now, cooling later' is the shape of a demand-shock inflation; this is a supply-and-demography shock whose binding year is 2034, not 2028. Separately, FALLS is measured against an index that carries a +0.40 to +0.75pp emerging-OECD composition floor, so even a genuine cooling may not print as one. 18.
hypothesis_critique.d: EVENTUALLY and WINS both fail, the first by being unfalsifiable inside the horizon and the second by having no stated benchmark. Doing the arithmetic anyway at the Dec 2036 resolution: the expected AI TFP lift implied by the AI-Q6 regime weights is 0.162(0.70) + 0.472(0.35) + 0.365(0.05) = +0.30pp/yr, against a combined aging drag of 0.66(-0.4) + 0.34(-2.7) = -1.18pp/yr. The ratio is 0.25 — AI offsets about a quarter of the demographic drag on my central path, and even the AI-Q6 Transformative Breakout tail at +0.70pp offsets 0.59 of it. My composite P50 of 1.8%/yr is below every five-year window in the 1960-2025 record. 'Exponential' also mis-describes the measured object: diffusion into a Baumol-exposed, licensure-gated, physically embodied care and construction sector subtracts -0.13pp/yr of reallocation drag from the very residual that is supposed to be exponentiating. The plank can only be scored true on a post-2036 horizon the question does not ask about. 15.

THE PPP WEIGHT AND AGING-DRAG PRODUCT, 0.66 x (-0.4) + 0.34 x (-2.7) = -1.18pp against 2A's stated global -1.1pp. The 8bp agreement proves the -1.1 is NET of the +0.4 healthy-aging offset and that any additive treatment inflates coupled growth by ~0.4pp. It also shows that 78% of the combined aging drag now comes from China's 0.34 weight, which is why the China catch-up leg that kept every historical five-year window above ~2.2% can no longer do so.

CROSS-ELASTICITY e_cross = 0.07, which delivers 0.07 x 9M = ~0.6M care entrants against a ~23M FTE requirement, 2.7% of the gap. With a 25% FTE gap divided by a long-run supply elasticity of 0.6 the shadow wage needs ~+40% real, costing 1.3-1.8% of OECD GDP in additional care compensation, which is precisely the transfer 2A's debt arithmetic (gross debt >100% of GDP by 2029, net interest 2% -> 3%) cannot finance. THE SIGN CANCELLATION INSIDE AI-Q1. The Baumol reallocation debit on measured aggregate TFP is -0.13pp/yr (0.32pp/yr of hours moving to a sector at 0.6x average output per hour) while the healthy-aging labour-quality leakage into the Solow residual is +0.10pp/yr. These are the two Wave-1 coupling corrections and they cancel to -0.03pp, so AI-Q1's locked 23.0% survives endogenization almost exactly. Two panelists pushed it in opposite directions by similar magnitudes and neither noticed the other.

THE NORMALIZED G7 PPP REAL-YIELD ANCHOR OF 1.79%, not the 1.68-1.70% both Wave-1 panelists reported from weights summing to 0.91-0.95. REGIME-SORTING AS A SINGLE BET IN CQ5. wave2.coupling_tension: PRIMARY: AI-Q5 (OECD-38 ISIC J, K, M labour compensation share of sectoral GVA falls >= 3.5pp, locked at 38.2%) is too LOW once demographics are endogenous, and the correction is arithmetic rather than narrative. Direction UP, to 48-52%, i.e. +10 to +14pp. The exogenous-demographics block implicitly lets aggregate labour scarcity from aging lift the outside option of every worker. But the scarcity is sector-specific and NON-ARBITRAGEABLE: at e_cross = 0.07 a displaced analyst converts a 20-25% care-sector FTE gap into exactly 0.07 of an improved outside option, so the tight market and the loose market are separated by a -55% reservation-wage step, an 18-42 month licensing queue, a strain barrier and a 77-88%-female gender-composition lock. The J/K/M worker therefore bargains with a substitute (compute) getting cheaper and an exit option not getting better, which is the worst configuration for labour share. Note the measurement asymmetry this creates and which the standalone block cannot see: the labour SHARE can collapse while the measured MEDIAN rises, because culling the bottom quintile lifts the median by 3-4pp — so AI-Q5 moving up is fully consistent with my CQ1 second conjunct staying at 0.21. SECOND: AI-Q2 (OECD-38 firm-count adoption >= 50%, locked at 21.3%) is too LOW on the economics and roughly right on the measurement, which means the ensemble should not read it as evidence about adoption at all. Labour scarcity is a genuine demand pull (adoption elasticity to the real wage of 0.4-0.6, so a 20% real care-wage rise induces ~10% labour-saving capital deepening), and the GPT diffusion base rate to a 50% firm-count threshold over 11 years is 50-65%; against that, the resolving source is the Eurostat ICT-usage module which 10-plus non-EU OECD members do not run, the UNWEIGHTED country mean up-weights 5-9% laggards, and "directly in producing goods or services" is strictly narrower than the ~13.5% EU headline. Net: economics says 38-45%, measurement says ~22%, blended ~28-32%, direction UP but for a reason that does not propagate. THIRD AND MOST IMPORTANT FOR THIS ENSEMBLE: AI-Q1 (23.0%) survives endogenization almost unchanged, because the two corrections my Wave-1 panel pushed in opposite directions nearly cancel in arithmetic. The Mechanism panelist's Baumol reallocation debit is -0.13 to -0.20pp/yr on MEASURED aggregate TFP (I independently derive -0.13: 0.32pp/yr of hours moving into a sector at 0.6x average output per hour); the Auditor's healthy-aging attribution credit is +0.10pp/yr, since the "70 in 2022 = 53 in 2000" capacity gain is unmeasured labour quality that growth accounting books as TFP. Net -0.03pp, so the correct coupled AI-Q1 is 21-24%, not the Mechanism panelist's 16-18% nor the Auditor's 28-31%. Each of them saw one leg and neither saw both. FOURTH, AND THE DIRECTION THAT ACTUALLY MOVES MY CQ6: the shift of mass into the stagflationary cell (my C = 33 against the panel's 17/23/30) comes from NO AI marginal at all. wave3.cq1_reasoning:

CONJUNCT 2 = 0.31 x 0.72 = 0.223.

His reason is sound and I accept it: the "displacement big enough to flatten J+K+M also raises unemployment" offset is weak because the displaced group is ~15-18% of employment while the absorbing F+Q group is ~18-20% and growing. P(B|A) = 0.223 x 1.20 = 0.268.

wave3.cq2_reasoning:

JOINT = 0.65 x 0.64 = 0.416. ANSWER 42. Note the structure, not the level: I am far above the Reference-Class and Mechanism panelists on the OECD leg (0.69 vs 0.35-0.53) and below the Mechanism and Fermi panelists on the China leg (0.64 vs 0.70-0.78). wave3.cq4_reasoning:

CONJUNCT A (ICE BofA MOVE 10-year average >= 105, 2027-36). The red-team's attack here is his strongest technical contribution and it is half right. I do not accept his magnitude (20-35% FTE deflation, asserted with no disability-prevalence series). The residual 4 is carried entirely by the one genuine AI-into-care channel, a capital channel and not a reallocation one: documentation is ~25% of nurse time and AI plausibly removes half of it by 2036, a ~12% effective capacity gain.
hypothesis_critique.b: BLOCKS and SEVERELY both fail, and all five panelists agree on the structure, so my 13 is a calibration not a verdict. BLOCKS is the wrong verb: AI compresses the PRICE and seat-intensity of the virtual leg (India IT-BPM ~$280B, Philippine voice-BPO ~1.7M+ workers) while OECD demography mechanically EXPANDS the physical leg (nursing, aged care, skilled trades) — opposite directions, which the plank nets to one by reporting only one. SEVERELY fails on scope, and the Fermi panelist's leg arithmetic is the best work here and the reason I sit at 13 rather than the Mechanism panelist's 13-15 band's top: India's commoditized slice is ~35% of $280B = ~$98B exposed, of which 30-50% is actually compressed net of AI-enabled volume scale-up = -$30 to -50B by 2036, ~1.0-1.5% of GDP level or 0.10-0.14pp/yr of growth — material, not severe. The Philippines is 5-10x more exposed in relative terms (BPO ~7-8% of GDP, voice-heavy task composition, a -2 to -3% GDP-level hit) and that is where the plank is closest to defensible. Against both legs: OECD care-sector entry capacity of 400-700k/yr by the early 2030s, of which these two sources plausibly take 30-40%, each entrant remitting ~$8-15k/yr, cumulating to $8-20B/yr of incremental remittances by 2036 plus a separately-driven GCC channel — and remittances are the channel aging expands, not the one AI compresses (Philippine ~$38-40B at ~8-9% of GDP is overwhelmingly physical-migration-based, not BPO). One point I weight that the ensemble under-weights: the Auditor's measurement finding that the resolving BOP series cannot distinguish AI in-housing from captive-GCC relocation, so work pulled into an Indian global capability centre still books as an Indian services export and the series may record no damage at all. The real harm is distributional and compositional (urban, young, English-speaking, female-skewed, multiplier-rich, middle-class-forming jobs; plus a care brain drain hollowing out the source country's own system as its own 65+ share rises), which is not what the plank says.
hypothesis_critique.c: THEN carries the failure — the implied ORDERING, not the level. This is where the effort's spread was widest (55/17/30/20/18) and where I most aggressively re-weight. I down-weight the Reference-Class panelist's 55 heavily: his lens explicitly forbade him mechanism, so he scored the plank on inflation-targeting reversion alone and thereby missed both of the sequencing legs that three other panelists reached independently. Those legs are real: 2027-31 is the DISINFLATIONARY interval (capex digestion at a 76-80% impairment marginal, Chinese excess capacity most aggressively exported, the post-impairment demand hole), while 2032-36 is the INFLATIONARY one (the 80+ cohort compounds at ~3.5%/yr, the old-age ratio reaches 39-41% BY 2036, the Baumol pass-through of +0.28pp/yr on core peaks late as administered-price and public-wage catch-up, and the fiscal claim tightens with net interest going 2% -> 3% of GDP). My own CQ6-C derivation puts 2032-36 core AT ~2.70% against a 2027-36 average of ~2.60%, i.e. the back half is the hotter half. But I score the plank well above the Mechanism, Fermi and red-team panelists (17-20) for two reasons they under-weighted. First, the front half is MORE likely true than they allowed: the window opens with 2026 core already elevated, so 'hot for the next few years' needs only inertia, not a new shock — call it 0.60. Second, and this is the Auditor's point that the red-team dismissed too fast, FALLS is measured against an index carrying a +0.40 to +0.75pp emerging-OECD composition floor, and Turkiye's disinflation from ~30% toward single digits delivers a visible measured fall of ~0.3-0.5pp in the 2030s by composition alone, with G7 core services inflation completely unchanged. So the back half can RESOLVE true for reasons that have nothing to do with the mechanism its proponents mean — call it 0.40 on the resolving measure. With mild negative correlation between the halves, the full stated shape is ~0.26. The arithmetic of the basket partly rescues a plank the economics does not support.
hypothesis_critique.d: EVENTUALLY and WINS both fail as resolution objects and EXPONENTIAL fails as a functional form. EVENTUALLY names no date and is unfalsifiable inside the Dec 31 2036 horizon, which is what does the plank's actual work; WINS names no threshold and, as the Auditor uniquely noticed, no DENOMINATOR — population decline makes real GDP PER CAPITA growth mechanically easier to win and real AGGREGATE growth harder, so the plank's truth value turns on a term it never states. EXPONENTIAL mis-describes the measured object twice: diffusion of a general-purpose business input is logistic, not exponential, and diffusion into Baumol-exposed, licensure-gated, physically embodied care and construction subtracts ~0.13pp/yr of reallocation drag from the very residual that is supposed to be exponentiating. Doing the arithmetic anyway at the stated horizon, as the Fermi panelist did: the AI-Q6-implied expected TFP lift is 0.162(0.70) + 0.472(0.35) + 0.365(0.05) = +0.30pp/yr against a weight-consistent combined aging drag of 0.66(-0.4) + 0.34(-2.7) = -1.18pp/yr, a ratio of 0.25 — AI offsets about a quarter of the demographic drag on my central path, and even the Transformative Breakout tail at +0.70pp offsets only 0.59 of it. My composite P50 of 1.9%/yr sits below every five-year window in the 1960-2025 record and my CQ6-A is 16. I score 16 rather than the red-team's 22 precisely because of a concession he made and then did not price: in his own world growth holds up through the reported-Chinese-growth floor, healthy-aging capacity printing as TFP, scarcity-induced mechanization and migration-driven OECD population growth — none of which is the plank's mechanism. 'Substantially correct AS STATED' grades the causal claim, so being directionally lucky and causally wrong scores below, not above, the Wave-1 centre.

key_drivers: THE PPP INDEX-COMPOSITION FLOOR IN THE 'OECD-38 GDP-WEIGHTED CORE' AGGREGATE, worth +0.40 to +0.78pp of pure composition. Under the Section-locked constant-2025-USD-PPP basis the high-inflation OECD bloc (Turkiye ~4.5-5.0%, Mexico ~4.2%, Chile/Colombia/Costa Rica/Poland/Hungary ~2.5-3.5%) is ~12% of the index versus ~4% at market rates: 0.12(6.5) + 0.88(2.20) = 2.72%. The Auditor found it, the Fermi panelist quantified it, the red-team adopted it, and two Wave-1 panelists missed it entirely. It carries my CQ2 OECD conjunct to 0.69, holds CQ6-C at 26, and nearly drains CQ6-D to 9 because D requires core < 2.0 on the same measure even when underlying G7 core runs ~1.5%. The single most consequential fact in this effort is a weighting convention, not an economic forecast.

THE REPORTED-SERIES CHANNEL ON CHINESE GROWTH, taken at half the red-team's magnitude. CQ3 resolves on NBS-reported real GDP as reprinted by the IMF, not on true growth; no sub-4% print in 35 years outside 2020 and 2022; plan targets will anchor ~4.5-5% then ~4%. I apply a +0.5pp wedge to a growth-accounted true path of ~2.85% for a reported 3.35%, rejecting the red-team's 3.60 because a floor estimated when true growth was 4-5% cannot be extrapolated unchanged onto a 2.85% path. At a 0.34 weight this is +0.17pp on the composite, lifts CQ6-A from the Wave-1 11-13 to 16, truncates my CQ3 left tail to 1.1 and extends the right to 2.9, flipping the distribution from left- to mildly right-skewed.

THE BAUMOL/HEALTHY-AGING CANCELLATION INSIDE MEASURED TFP. The reallocation debit is -0.13pp/yr (0.32pp/yr of hours shifting into a sector at ~0.6x average output per hour) and the attribution credit is +0.10pp/yr (growth accounting has no capacity adjustment, so the '70 in 2022 = 53 in 2000' gain, 41 countries N~1M, lands in the Solow residual and is published as TFP). Net -0.03pp. Two Wave-1 panelists pushed AI-Q1 in opposite directions by similar magnitudes (16-18% versus 28-31%) and neither saw the other's leg. This is why my OECD growth leg is 1.15% rather than the red-team's 1.30%, and why I report AI-Q1 as surviving endogenization roughly intact.

SECTOR-SPECIFIC, NON-ARBITRABLE SCARCITY AT e_cross = 0.07, with the measurement asymmetry it creates. A displaced analyst converts a 20-25% care-sector FTE gap into 0.07 of an improved outside option, separated from it by a ~-55% reservation-wage step, an 18-42 month licensing queue, a strain barrier and a 77-88%-female composition lock — the worst configuration for labour share. But the labour SHARE can collapse while the measured MEDIAN rises, because culling the bottom quintile lifts J/K/M's median 3-4pp. This is simultaneously why I move AI-Q5 up to ~45% and why CQ1's wage conjunct stays at 0.22.

BASIS-POINT NORMALIZATION OF MOVE, CALIBRATED AGAINST REALIZED 2024-26 DATA RATHER THAN ASSERTED. MOVE's unstressed floor scales with the yield level, so the Reference-Class panelist's cross-regime reference class is invalid; but realized MOVE of ~80-95 with the US 10y at 4.0-4.5% in 2024-26 puts the floor at ~87, not the ~95 the red-team's 0.60 requires. Floor 95 plus two stress years at 150 averages 106 and clears; floor 85 averages 98 and fails. This single calibration is why CQ5 is 30 rather than his 40 or the Wave-1 24-28.

UNMEASURABILITY OF CQ1's SECOND CONJUNCT AS A RESOLUTION CONVENTION, not as a rhetorical hedge. No OECD-38-wide sectoral real MEDIAN hourly series exists at the stated 2025 and 2036 endpoints (Eurostat SES quadrennial 2018/2022/2026/2030/2034 with ~2.5yr lag; non-EU members absent; US substitutes are OES median with a 2021-23 reweighting break or CES mean). I apply a 0.72 multiplier — lighter than the Fermi panelist's 0.68 because a best-available proxy is assemblable and not systematically biased against YES, heavier than the red-team's near-zero haircut because contestable noise at a threshold 2.5pp above the central value is mildly adverse.

wave3.coupling_tension:
Three tensions, ranked, with the reconciliation my lens is for.
PRIMARY, AND THE ONE I OWN: AI-Q5 (OECD-38 ISIC J/K/M labour compensation share of sectoral GVA falls >= 3.5pp, locked at 38.2%) is too LOW once demographics are endogenous. DIRECTION: UP, to 44-47%, i.e. +6 to +9pp. The Mechanism panelist's argument is right and is the best single piece of causal reasoning in this effort: the exogenous-demographics block implicitly lets aggregate labour scarcity from aging lift every worker's outside option, but at a cross-elasticity of 0.07 the scarcity is NON-ARBITRABLE — the tight market (care, construction) and the loose market (cognitive) are separated by a ~-55% reservation-wage step, an 18-42 month licensing queue, a strain barrier and a 77-88%-female composition lock, so the J/K/M worker bargains with a substitute (compute) getting cheaper and an exit option that is NOT getting better, which is the worst possible configuration for labour share. I take his +10 to +14pp down to +6 to +9pp for the red-team's reason, which is legitimate: his magnitude is sized off an exogenous care-FTE requirement, and deflating that requirement 10-15% for morbidity compression makes the care market less tight, the shadow wage lower, and the J/K/M worker's outside option less catastrophically bad. Note the measurement asymmetry this creates, which the standalone block cannot see and which is why AI-Q5 moving up does NOT lift my CQ1: the labour SHARE can collapse while the measured MEDIAN rises, because culling the bottom quintile lifts J/K/M's median by 3-4pp.
SECOND: AI-Q1 (23.0%) SURVIVES ENDOGENIZATION ALMOST UNCHANGED, and I report this as a finding rather than a revision because it resolves the sharpest standoff inside my effort. The Mechanism panelist argued DOWN to 16-18% on a Baumol reallocation debit to measured aggregate TFP; the Auditor argued UP to 28-31% on a healthy-aging attribution credit, since growth accounting measures labour as bodies and hours with at best an education adjustment and therefore books the '70 in 2022 = 53 in 2000' capacity gain (41 countries, N~1M) into the Solow residual as published TFP. The Fermi panelist's arithmetic settles it: the debit is -0.13pp/yr (0.32pp/yr of hours moving into a sector at ~0.6x average output per hour) against a credit of +0.10pp/yr, net -0.03pp. Coupled AI-Q1 is 21-24%. Each Wave-1 panelist saw one leg; neither saw the other; the red-team propagated the credit without the debit and arrived at 33-38%, which is the drag/pull asymmetry committed in the pro-AI direction.
THIRD, DIRECTION UP AND UNCONTESTED ACROSS THE EFFORT: AI-Q4 at 66.0% sits below its own reference-class frequency — roughly 5 of 6 named capex supercycles ended >= 20% impaired (1840s British railway mania, 1870s-90s US rail, 1999-2002 telecom/fibre, 2014-2020 US shale, 1975-85 US nuclear, with Japan's 1980s domestic capex the partial exception) — and coupling with 2A's plumbing block (~$1.4T of circular commitments on ~$300B equity and ~$650B debt, +2.4pp Debt-at-Risk under a 20% AI-led equity shock) pushes it higher still. I put it at 76-80. CRITICALLY, this does not lower my growth numbers, and the effort mishandled exactly this: impairment is a BALANCE-SHEET event with near-zero flow GDP content, so the Reference-Class panelist's marking CQ6-D UP from 21 to 24 on the strength of the 66% marginal was a category error. A high-impairment, high-growth world is fully coherent — the compute gets written down and keeps running.
A FOURTH TENSION WHICH IS THE REAL HEADLINE, AND WHICH IS NOT ABOUT AI AT ALL: the locked 2B marginals are not in tension with the thing that actually moves my coupled end-state distribution, they are SILENT on it. My CQ6-C at 26 and the near-draining of CQ6-D to 9 come from a weighting convention (the +0.40 to +0.78pp emerging-OECD composition floor in a PPP-GDP-weighted 'OECD-38' core aggregate), and my CQ6-A at 16 comes from a reporting convention (the NBS-reported series the question resolves on). Neither is an AI forecast. The coupled end-state is driven more by the measurement basis of the inflation and growth legs than by anything the standalone AI ensemble forecast — which means the ensemble should NOT read agreement or disagreement with 2B as evidence about the coupling. On AI-Q2 specifically this cuts both ways and nets to a warning rather than a revision: labour scarcity is a genuine demand pull (adoption elasticity to the real wage 0.4-0.6; the GPT diffusion base rate to a 50% firm-count threshold over 11 years is 50-65%) arguing the locked 21.3% is far too low, while the resolving source (the Eurostat ICT-usage module, which 10-plus non-EU OECD members do not run, with an UNWEIGHTED country mean that up-weights 5-9% laggards and a 'directly in producing goods or services' scope strictly narrower than the ~13.5% EU headline) argues it is roughly right. Blended ~28-32, direction UP, but the ensemble should not treat 21.3% as evidence about adoption in either direction.
