wave_audit.wave1_spread: Widest on CQ2 (20 / 38 / 49) and on CQ6-D (24 / 18 / 8), and both gaps trace to ONE fact rather than to any disagreement about the real economy: whether 'GDP-weighted OECD-38' means PPP-GDP weights under the Section lock, which puts Turkiye at ~4.5-5.0% of the index with core CPI ~30% in 2025 plus Mexico, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Poland and Hungary. The Auditor identified it and carried his OECD conjunct to 0.86; the Reference-Class and Mechanism panelists computed a G7-ish core and got 0.35-0.53. The same artefact decided CQ6-D, because D requires core < 2.0 on the same measure. Second-widest: hypothesis plank (c) (55 / 17 / 30), where the Reference-Class panelist's lens forbade him mechanism and he therefore scored inflation-targeting reversion while the other two scored a time-reversed sequencing claim. The CQ3/CQ4 agreement (1.8-1.9 and 1.9-2.0) was NOT triangulation: all three used the same OECD leg of 1.1-1.2% and the same reconstructed ~1.68-1.70% real-yield anchor, and two of those shared inputs were wrong (the anchor's weights summed to 0.91-0.95; the China leg applied a reported-series wedge to a baseline nobody wrote down).
wave_audit.what_wave2_changed: KILLED. (i) The Mechanism panelist's r* justification that 'the dissaving cohort is not yet dominant through the early 2030s' — the red-team is right that locked 2A puts the old-age ratio at 39-41% BY 2036, so 2032-36 IS the dissaving arrival; I moved that term from +10bp to +25bp, lifting CQ4 P50 to 2.1%. (ii) The Reference-Class panelist's CQ6-D = 24, which he marked UP from 21 citing AI-Q4's 66% impairment marginal after the Auditor had already shown impairment is a balance-sheet event with near-zero flow GDP content; a high-impairment, high-growth world is coherent and D is 9 in my payload. (iii) The Reference-Class panelist's MOVE reference class, which averaged levels across incommensurable yield regimes (1990s windows on 6-8% nominals against 2010-2019 on 1.5-2.5%). RESCUED. The Fermi panelist rescued two Auditor findings from their author's own under-use: the MOVE bp-normalization fact (the Auditor wrote it and then set the conjunct at 0.48 anyway) and the PPP composition floor, which he turned into an explicit sum. He also produced the single result that settled an intra-effort standoff: the Baumol reallocation debit (-0.13pp/yr) and the healthy-aging attribution credit (+0.10pp/yr) nearly cancel, so coupled AI-Q1 is 21-24% rather than the Mechanism panelist's 16-18% or the Auditor's 28-31%. PARTIAL HIT ACCEPTED. The red-team's dilution-versus-throughput contradiction in CQ1 — the Mechanism and Auditor panelists both banked a low-wage-entrant surge diluting ISIC Q's median AND licence-throttled entry at 400-700k/yr. They are substitutes at full magnitude but not mutually exclusive: 400-700k/yr over 11 years is 5-7.7M against ~38-42M of OECD-38 ISIC Q employment, ~14-18% growth in the low-wage tail, not the 30-35% used, so the composition wedge is -6.0pp not -8.0pp and CQ1 moves 13 -> 16, not to his 23. MERELY CONTRARIAN-POSED, DID NOT MOVE ME. (a) The morbidity-compression deflator at 20-35% of the care-FTE requirement: the direction is a real and original catch (the 2A capacity bullet was spent once on growth and never on the quantity it deflates), but he produced no disability- or dependency-prevalence series, and formal LTC utilisation in Japan and Germany has tracked 80+ headcount despite measured healthy aging; I took 10-15%. (b) MOVE conjunct A at 0.60, contradicted by realized 2024-26 MOVE of ~80-95 with the US 10y at 4.0-4.5%, which puts the floor at ~87 not ~95; I used 0.48 and CQ5 = 30, not 40. (c) His CQ3 OECD leg of 1.30%, which propagated the attribution credit without the Baumol debit — the same asymmetry he accused Wave 1 of, in the opposite direction. (d) His near-zero haircut on CQ1's unmeasurable conjunct: he conceded the Auditor's finding and then priced it at ~0.90; I used 0.72.
wave_audit.unresolved: FOUR things, honestly. (1) Whether the care-FTE requirement is exogenous to morbidity. The red-team is right that the locked 2A capacity result bears on it and that nobody spent it there, but nobody in this effort produced an age-specific disability or dependency-prevalence series, so the 10-35% range I compressed to 10-15% is a judgment and not an estimate. It is the largest single lever on CQ1, on the Baumol drag inside CQ3, and on hypothesis plank (a). (2) Whether a resolver constructs the CQ1-b proxy at all, and if so from what. The series does not exist at the stated endpoints; my 0.72 multiplier stands for a resolution convention nobody can verify in advance, and the honest spread across the effort was 0.68 to ~0.90. (3) The forward size of the reported-China wedge. The effort spanned +0.3 to +1.5pp with no way to adjudicate, and the +0.5pp I used moves my CQ3 P50 by 0.17pp and CQ6-A by ~5pp. (4) Whether the PPP composition floor persists past Turkiye's disinflation into the 2032-36 window. I shrank it from ~0.78 to ~0.42pp on judgment; that single number is the difference between CQ6-C at 26 and at 16, and between D at 9 and at 14. Also unresolved and explicitly noted: my C = 26 rests entirely on the inflation-measurement leg, because the Auditor's capex arithmetic on CQ6-C's 'grid supply wall' (~$35-75B/yr against $600-800B/yr of OECD-38 + China power capex) is correct and the real constraint is interconnection queue time, which no capex series will ever show.
wave_audit.biggest_update: CQ5: 24 (Wave-1 modal) -> 30, a +6pp move, the largest single numeric update in my payload. Cause: the MOVE basis-point-normalization fact. MOVE is normalized bp implied vol, so its unstressed floor scales with the yield level; my CQ4 P50 of 2.1% real plus ~2.5-2.7% OECD core implies a US 10y nominal averaging 4.5-5.0%, in which regime the floor is ~87-90 rather than the 50-70 of 2010-2019, taking conjunct A from the Wave-1 0.33-0.48 to 0.48 and the joint from 0.23-0.28 to 0.28-0.30. The Auditor wrote the fact down and declined to use it; the red-team used it and over-calibrated to 0.60; I calibrated it against realized 2024-26 MOVE at today's yields and landed between them. A structurally larger move sits underneath a smaller headline number: CQ2's OECD-core conjunct went from the Reference-Class and Mechanism panelists' implied 0.35-0.53 to 0.69 (+16 to +34pp on the conjunct) purely on the PPP index-weight arithmetic, but because I simultaneously cut the China leg from 0.70-0.78 to 0.64 on the red-team's food-cycle and policy-reflation attack, the joint moved only 38 -> 42. Two large offsetting revisions reported as a 4pp change is exactly the kind of thing a reconciler should say out loud.

wave1.lens_self_description: Outside-view reference-class scout: I answered every CQ from the frequency of the widest defensible historical class (overlapping multi-year windows, 1960-2025 where available), adjusting only for the arithmetic content of the locked priors (headcount, debt accounting, basket weights) — I forbade myself from any reasoning about AI capability trajectories, model scaling, adoption S-curves, or any mechanism specific to this episode, and I used no 2036-forecast literature.
wave1.cq1_reasoning:
Reference classes. (i) OECD harmonized unemployment 5-yr averages <=5.5%: of ~61 overlapping windows 1960-2025, roughly 20 qualify (~33%), but the distribution is bimodal by era — nearly all qualifying windows are pre-1980 (1960-74 OECD unemployment ~3-4%); 1980-2019 produced essentially zero qualifying windows (trough 5.3% in 2019 only), and the only post-1980 qualifiers are 2021-2025 (~5.3%, a record-low level). (ii) Base rate of a 5-yr window containing a G7-synchronized recession: ~6 episodes in 65 years (1974-75, 1980-82, 1991, 2001, 2008-09, 2020) implies ~45%; OECD unemployment rises 2-3pp in one, adding ~1.0-1.5pp to a 5-yr average. Arithmetic adjustment UP: a shrinking OECD working-age denominator is near-deterministic and mechanically suppresses the measured rate — Japan held 2.4-2.8% unemployment through a ~1%-growth decade. Conjunct-1 marginal: 0.55*0.85 + 0.45*0.15 ~= 0.55.
Conjunct 2 (F+Q real median hourly beats J+K+M by >=10pp over 11 years). Magnitude is common; the DIRECTION is not. Base rate of a >=10pp divergence between two broad sector groups over 11 years: ~35-45% of windows since 1960. But every large post-1980 OECD instance ran the OTHER way (US information + finance real wages vs construction, 1990-2001 and 2010-2021, each comfortably >15pp in favour of cognitive/info). Reversals of that sign and size have no 11-year precedent in 45 years; the closest is the 1970s compression and the brief 2021-23 US low-wage catch-up (~3-5pp over 2 years, since partly unwound). Two further mechanical cuts: (a) composition — if displacement removes junior/mid cognitive roles, the surviving J+K+M MEDIAN rises, biasing the measure against the plank; (b) monopsony — Q pay is set by governments and insurers, and locked prior 2A has pension/health claims crowding budgets (China subsidies already ~10.1% of fiscal expenditure; OECD net interest 2%->3% of GDP), so the care-wage channel is fiscally rationed exactly when scarcity peaks. Conjunct-2 marginal: 0.17.
Conjunction: positively correlated (both are the tight-labour-scarcity world); assumed correlation lifts the naive product ~1.3x. 0.55 * 0.17 = 0.094 -> ~0.12. Answer 12.
wave1.cq2_reasoning:
Conjunct A: OECD-38 GDP-weighted core >=2.50%/yr avg 2027-2036. Reference class: 10-yr core averages. 1970s ~9%, 1980s ~6%, 1990s ~3.3%, 2000-2009 ~2.0%, 2010-2019 ~1.5%, 2015-2024 ~2.3%. Unconditional over all windows since 1960: ~45-50% clear 2.5%; restricted to the inflation-targeting era (post-1993, the only regime-relevant class): ~1 in 4, and only windows straddling 2021-23. Weight arithmetic (the level/skew separation my effort requires): US core CPI is ~33% shelter, ~40% other services (medical ~7-8%, insurance, education, care), ~25% core goods; core EXCLUDES electricity by construction, so the power/grid-capex impulse enters core only as second-round business-cost pass-through (~+0.1-0.3pp), not directly. Conversely the AI-disinflation side lands mostly in B2B/intermediate prices and GVA deflators — consumer-basket weight on software, media and professional services is only ~3-5% of core. That asymmetry biases the core LEVEL up relative to naive "AI is deflationary" reasoning even under a large relative-price skew. Fermi: shelter 30% @3.2 = 0.96; other services 40% @3.2 = 1.28; core goods 25% @0.3 = 0.08; residual 5% @2.0 = 0.10 -> ~2.4% for the US-like case. GDP-weighting drags it down: 0.37*2.7 (US) + 0.25*2.1 (EA) + 0.08*1.7 (JP) + 0.30*3.0 (rest) = 2.56%. A 2027-30 hot phase (~2.9%) plus a 2031-36 cooler phase (~2.3%) also averages ~2.5%. Sits on the threshold. Marginal: 0.52 (base rate says lower, weight arithmetic says higher).
Conjunct B: China headline CPI <1.50% avg 2027-2036. Semi-independent object. China CPI 10-yr averages: 1996-2005 ~0.9%, 2005-2014 ~3.0%, 2010-2019 ~2.3%, 2015-2024 ~1.4%, 2020-2025 ~0.6%; 2023/2024/2025 run-rate ~0.2%/0.2%/~0%. Reference class for persistence once a large aging economy enters sub-1% CPI: Japan 1995-2025 averaged ~0.3% across three decades — conditional persistence is high. Drivers are structural, not cyclical: property adjustment, household income ~44% of GDP, deliberate supply-side industrial policy, and the locked -2.7pp/yr aging drag with a 60M population fall. For the average to clear 1.5% you need a sustained reflation to ~1.8-2%; a few 0-0.5% years early make that arithmetically hard. Upside risks: pork/food shocks, RMB depreciation import costs, anti-involution supply discipline, eventual services unit-labour-cost pressure from aging. Marginal: 0.72.
Correlation: mixed sign. NEGATIVE through the tradables channel (Chinese overcapacity deflation lowers OECD core goods, the 25% slice I already set at 0.3%, so conditioning costs little extra); POSITIVE through the common "OECD-side capex and care/shelter scarcity vs China-side demographic demand deficit" bifurcation. Net treated as near-independent with a small negative tilt: 0.52*0.72 = 0.374 -> 36.
wave1.cq3_reasoning:
Reference class: 5-yr averages of PPP-weighted OECD+China real growth since 1960, reconstructed with time-varying China PPP weight (China ~33-35% of the combined aggregate today, ~5% in the 1960s, ~12% in the 1990s, ~25-30% in the 2010s). Approximate window averages: 1960s ~5.0%, 1970s ~3.7%, 1980s ~3.6%, 1990s ~3.5%, 2000s ~3.3%, 2010-2019 ~3.5% (0.72*2.0 + 0.28*7.7), 2015-2019 ~3.55%, 2020-2024 ~2.6%, 2022-2024 ~2.7%. Unconditional distribution: mean ~3.4%, sd ~0.8-0.9%, minimum ~2.3-2.6% (2020-24 and 2008-12), maximum ~5.5%. OBSERVED: no 5-year window in 65 years averaged below ~2.3%.
This is the one place where the outside view must yield to arithmetic, and I say so explicitly: the reference class is non-stationary in exactly the dimension the locked priors make near-deterministic. Bottom-up from 2A alone — OECD per-capita trend 0.6%/yr plus OECD-38 population ~+0.2-0.3%/yr gives ~0.8-1.1% headline; China at ~2.0-3.0% with a shrinking population and worker/retiree ratio 4.4->2.8. Combined: 0.66*1.0 + 0.34*2.5 = 1.51%. Adding a modest productivity offset of the historically ordinary size (+0.2-0.4pp to OECD) gives 0.66*1.3 + 0.34*2.6 = 1.74%. P50 set at 1.85%, i.e. structurally BELOW the entire historical support of the reference class, because the headcount is not forecastable away.
Dispersion from the reference class rather than from mechanism: the historical sd of realized 5-yr growth averages around a 6-year-ahead central estimate is ~0.8-1.0pp, and ~45% of 5-yr windows contain a G7-synchronized recession costing ~0.5-0.8pp off the average. P10 0.95% (recession window with no offset), P90 2.80% (no recession plus an offset at the upper end of historical technology episodes; note even P90 falls short of the 1960-2019 reference-class MEAN).
wave1.cq4_reasoning:
Reference class 1: G7 GDP-weighted 10y real yield by decade. 1970s ~-1 to -2% (nominal ~8% vs inflation ~9%); 1980s ~+4.5-5%; 1990s ~+4% (US TIPS debut 1997 at 3.4-3.8%); 2000s ~+2% (US TIPS avg ~2.0-2.2%); 2010s ~+0.4% (US ~0.5%, JP ~0, DE negative); 2020-2025 ~+0.3% (deeply negative 2020-21, +1.5-2.2% 2023-25). GDP weighting matters: US ~50% of G7, Japan ~10%, Germany ~10%, with JP ~-0.3 to +0.5% and DE ~0.3-0.6% real, so the G7 aggregate sits well below the US print. With US 10y TIPS at ~2.60% (locked, Oct 30 2026), the G7 GDP-weighted level today is ~1.7-1.9%.
Reference class 2 (base rate of staying near the starting level): consecutive decade changes were +6.0, -1.0, -2.0, -1.6, -0.1pp — mean absolute change ~2.1pp, and only 2 of 5 transitions stayed within +/-100bp. So "decade-average real yield near its starting level" has a base rate of only ~40%, yet it remains the modal single cell.
Reference class 3 (high-debt resolution, the class the locked debt arithmetic selects): US/UK post-1945 with debt >100% of GDP resolved through financial repression, with G7 real yields ~0 to negative for ~25 years. Against it, the 1980s-90s high-term-premium class gives +3-5%. These two classes bracket the distribution and are why it is wide and right-skewed rather than tight.
Arithmetic adjustments from 2A, all accounting rather than mechanism: gross public debt >100% of GDP by 2029 (~142% US, ~127% China by 2031), net interest 2%->3% of GDP, P95 3-yr Debt-at-Risk ~117%, eroding convenience yields and levered basis-trade absorption — all raise duration supply and term premia. Offsetting: aging raises accumulation-phase saving and lowers g, and repression is the historically common policy response at these debt levels. P50 1.80% (current level, which is also the midpoint of the two bracketing classes); P10 0.55% (repression/post-bust-disinflation class); P90 3.15% (term-premium-spike class). Note this is a REAL yield, so the inflation path largely nets out of the level but drives the width: a hot-and-sticky regime delivers the 2022-style high-real-yield tail, a capex-digestion regime the low tail — bimodality, not noise.
wave1.cq5_reasoning:
Conjunct A: MOVE 10-yr average >=105 over 2027-2036. MOVE history from 1988: long-run mean ~95; roughly 100-130 in 1988-1994, ~90-110 in 1995-2000, ~105-120 in 2001-2003, ~60-80 in 2004-2007, ~100-180 in 2008-2011, ~60-80 in 2012-2019, ~125 in 2022, ~130 in 2023, ~100 in 2024, and sharply lower in 2025 (searched source reports a 2025 close of 63.96, a ~34% annual decline). Of ~28 overlapping 10-yr windows, perhaps 6-9 averaged >=105 (the 1988-1997 and 2000-2009 vintages) -> base rate ~25-30%. 105 is ABOVE the full-sample mean, and the window must start from a currently-normalized ~64-90 level, which is the binding arithmetic. Adjusted up modestly for the locked duration-supply facts (net interest to 3% of GDP, basis-trade absorption, convenience-yield erosion): marginal 0.33.
Conjunct B: an MSCI World >=25% peak-to-trough drawdown in which G7 10y nominals fail to rally >=50bp (or rise >=25bp). Step 1 — base rate of a >=25% MSCI World drawdown in a 10-yr window: episodes 1973-74, 1980-82, 1987, 1990, 2000-02, 2007-09 (-57.82% USD, Oct 2007-Mar 2009, per searched source), 2020 (~-34%), 2022 (~-26%) = ~8 in 55 years; 5 of 6 decades contain one, and 2010-2019 contains NONE at >=25% (2011 ~-22%, 2018 ~-18%) -> ~0.85. Step 2 — CONDITIONAL on such a drawdown, frequency bonds failed to rally: clear failures 1973-74 (yields rose) and 2022 (yields rose sharply); arguable failures in the 1981 leg and the 1990 oil shock; clear flight-to-quality rallies in 1987, 2000-02, 2007-09, 2020. So 2 clear of 8, 4 of 8 at the generous reading -> 0.33. Conjunct B = 0.85 * 0.33 = 0.28.
Conjunction: strongly positively correlated, since both historical failure episodes (1973-74, 2022) were high-rate-vol inflation-correlated regimes. P(MOVE>=105 | correlated-regime drawdown) ~ 0.65 rather than the unconditional 0.33. Joint = 0.28 * 0.65 = 0.182 -> 18. The conjunction discount is what keeps this well under the ~28% single-conjunct figure most forecasters will anchor on.
wave1.cq6_reasoning:
Unconditional reference-class answer first, because it is the most important finding and it is WRONG for this window. Applying the lexical lock to historical 5-yr windows of OECD+China PPP growth since 1960: A (>=2.6%) captures roughly 85-90% of all windows 1960-2019; C requires combined growth <2.0% with OECD core >=2.7%, which occurred only around 1979-1984 (OECD growth ~1.3%, China ~8% at an ~8% weight -> ~1.84% combined, OECD inflation ~9%) -> ~5% of windows; D (growth <1.7% AND core <2.0%) has essentially ZERO historical instances for this combined aggregate (it is a Japan-only cell); B as residual ~5-8%. The unconditional base rate therefore screams A at ~87% — and must be overridden, because A's 2.6% threshold is arithmetically out of reach once the near-deterministic headcount is imposed: it would need China at ~4.5%+ AND OECD at ~1.6%+ simultaneously, against a locked -2.7pp/yr China aging drag and a 0.6%/yr OECD per-capita baseline.
Construction from my own answers, using the lock's measures (CQ3 growth; OECD-38 GDP-weighted core over 2032-2036 — note this is the BACK HALF, not CQ2's 2027-2036 window, so it is the disinflationary half of my effort's tug-of-war; I therefore shade the core distribution down relative to CQ2's 0.52 at >=2.5%).
Marginals used: P(core_32-36 >= 2.7%) = 0.27; P(2.0 <= core_32-36 < 2.7%) = 0.39; P(core_32-36 < 2.0%) = 0.34. From CQ3 (P10 0.95 / P50 1.85 / P90 2.80): P(growth >= 2.6%) = 0.12; P(growth < 2.0%) = 0.57; P(growth < 1.7%) = 0.42.
Step 1, A = P(growth >= 2.6%) = 12.
Step 2, C = P(core >= 2.7%) * P(growth < 2.0% | core >= 2.7%) = 0.27 * 0.68 (conditional lifted from 0.57 for the supply-constrained stagflation correlation) = 0.18 -> 18.
Step 3, D = P(core < 2.0%) * P(growth < 1.7% | core < 2.0%) = 0.34 * 0.55 (conditional lifted from 0.42 for the demand-shortfall correlation) = 0.19 -> 19.
Step 4, B = residual = 100 - 12 - 18 - 19 = 51.
CONSISTENCY CHECK PERFORMED. (i) My CQ3 P50 of 1.85% sits inside B's literal 1.7-2.5% band, and B is my modal cell at 51% — consistent, and B additionally absorbs the low-growth/moderate-inflation leftover cell the lock assigns to it, which is why it exceeds the sum of C and D. (ii) A at 12 equals P(growth >= 2.6%) read off my own CQ3 distribution exactly, so A cannot be inflated by the historical 87% base rate. (iii) C at 18 is strictly below the 0.27 core->=2.7% marginal and below CQ2's 0.52 for the 10-year >=2.5% test, as the lock's narrower back-half window and the added growth condition both require. (iv) C + D = 37, close to twice the 18-19 each, reflecting genuine two-sided inflation risk rather than a one-directional stagflation lean — which is the honest reading of a tug-of-war with an early inflationary phase and a late disinflationary phase. (v) A + B = 63 and C + D = 37; P(growth < 2.0%) = 0.57 is reconciled because much of that mass lands in B's leftover cell (growth 1.7-2.0% with core 2.0-2.7%), not in C or D.

hypothesis_critique.a: "SMOOTHLY" carries the whole failure. Reference class: displaced-worker reallocation across broad occupational families. Jacobson-LaLonde-Sullivan and the 2000-2015 US manufacturing episode put cross-family re-employment at ~20-30% with 15-20% permanent earnings losses; the coal, steel and 1980s UK episodes are worse. The arithmetic also refuses: J+K+M is ~20-25% of OECD employment while Q needs ~+30-40% headcount, and the transfer runs uphill against licensing, credentialing, physical-presence requirements, and a pay gradient that points the wrong way (care pays less than the displaced role). Even a correct net-numbers claim fails on "smoothly": the historical mechanism is a decade of unemployment, early retirement and non-participation, not reallocation. 6.
hypothesis_critique.b: TWO failure words. "BLOCKS" is wrong for the physical channel and "SEVERELY" is wrong at the macro level for the virtual one. Philippine remittances (~$38-40B) are dominated by PHYSICAL land- and sea-based workers — nurses, caregivers, seafarers, domestic workers — a channel that OECD aging is a demand PULL for, not a block; the locked 39-41% old-age ratio mechanically expands it. On the virtual side, BPO is ~7-8% of Philippine GDP and ~1.3-1.7M of a ~49M labour force, and Indian IT services ~7% of GDP, so even a severe sectoral hit is a few points of GDP, not a severe macro outcome. Reference class for technology fully foreclosing a services-export channel (ATMs and tellers, the 2000s offshoring-reversal predictions, telephony): near-zero full-block outcomes. 14.
hypothesis_critique.c: "THEN FALLS" carries the failure — the confident two-phase SEQUENCING, not the direction. This is close to my own modal path, so it scores highest of the four, but the base rate for correctly timing an inflation regime transition is poor in both directions: 1982-83 and 2023 fell much faster than consensus expected, the 1970s persisted far longer, and 2010-2019 undershot for a decade. The claim is also underspecified on magnitude ("hot" relative to what, "falls" to what) — my own CQ6 puts 19% on the late window running BELOW 2.0% and 18% on it running at or above 2.7%, i.e. ~37% on the sequencing being wrong in one direction or the other. A near-miss on timing resolves this plank false even where the shape is right. 55.
hypothesis_critique.d: "EVENTUALLY" and "WINS". "Eventually" is unfalsifiable at a Dec 2036 horizon — most of my credence here is parked on reading it as post-2036, which makes the plank not-yet-resolvable rather than correct. "Wins" names no counterfactual: wins against zero, against the 1960-2019 reference-class mean of ~3.4%, or against per-capita stagnation? The cleanest national tests of "technology offsets demography" all resolved FALSE inside 25-30 years: Japan led the world in robot density and IT investment and still averaged ~0.8%/yr real GDP growth 1995-2025; Germany, Korea and Italy repeat it. 0 for ~4. Hulten/Baumol arithmetic caps the offset at the unautomated share, and "exponential" is doing rhetorical work my lens forbids me from crediting. 15.

key_drivers: Reference-class non-stationarity: for CQ3/CQ6 the 1960-2025 class has NO 5-year window below ~2.3% and puts ~87% of windows in CQ6-A, yet the near-deterministic headcount (OECD old-age ratio 39-41%, China -60M, worker/retiree 4.4->2.8) places the 2032-36 window below the entire historical support. The size of that override is the single largest driver of every number here.

Core-basket weight arithmetic, not inflation mechanism: electricity is EXCLUDED from core by construction, so the grid/power impulse enters only as second-round pass-through (~+0.1-0.3pp), while shelter (~33%) and other services incl. medical/care/insurance (~40%) carry the level. The AI-disinflation side lands in B2B and GVA deflators; software, media and professional services are only ~3-5% of consumer core. The relative-price skew is therefore large but ASYMMETRICALLY weighted toward the inflating side of core.

Conditional persistence of a sub-1% CPI regime in a large aging economy: Japan 1995-2025 averaged ~0.3% over three decades. This, plus a ~0.2% current China run-rate and a property/household-income-share starting point, is what puts CQ2's China conjunct at 0.72 and makes it the stronger of the two conjuncts.

Era-split in the OECD unemployment base rate: 5-yr averages <=5.5% are ~33% unconditionally but ~0% for 1980-2019 and only reappear at 2021-2025 record lows; the mechanical denominator effect (Japan at 2.4-2.8% through a ~1%-growth decade) is the only thing holding conjunct 1 above 50%.

Directional absence of precedent for CQ1's second conjunct: a >=10pp broad-sector real-wage divergence over 11 years is common in MAGNITUDE (~35-45% of windows) but every large post-1980 instance ran in favour of cognitive/information, and the Q-sector monopsony payer is fiscally constrained in exactly the locked scenario.

Bracketing high-debt reference classes for CQ4: post-1945 repression (G7 real yields ~0 to negative for ~25 years) versus the 1980s-90s term-premium class (+3-5%), with only a ~40% base rate of a decade-average staying within +/-100bp of its starting level. This bimodality, not point uncertainty, sets the CQ4 width.

falsification_signposts.signpost: ICE BofA MOVE Index trailing 24-month average published above 110 at any month-end (after a 2025 close near 64 and a currently-normalized level), sustained for three consecutive month-ends.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: My CQ5 conjunct-A marginal of 0.33 was too low against the ~25-30% 10-yr-window base rate; CQ5 moves up from 18 to roughly 30-33. Also pushes CQ4 P50 up ~30-40bp toward the term-premium reference class and shifts ~4-5 points of CQ6 mass from B into C.

falsification_signposts.signpost: China headline CPI annual print at or above 2.0% in two consecutive calendar years, with the household final-consumption share of GDP rising above 42% in the same period.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: Breaks the Japan-persistence class my 0.72 China-deflation conjunct rests on; CQ2 falls from 36 to roughly 14-18 (0.52 x ~0.30). Raises CQ3 P50 by ~0.15-0.25pp via Chinese nominal demand, and moves ~3 points from CQ6-D toward B.

falsification_signposts.signpost: OECD-38 GDP-weighted core CPI/PCE annual average below 2.0% in three of the four years 2027-2030 — i.e. the early inflationary phase my effort posits simply does not materialize.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: Falsifies my weight-arithmetic claim that shelter + care + services dominate core over the goods-deflation and B2B-disinflation channels; CQ2 conjunct A falls from 0.52 to ~0.25 and CQ2 drops from 36 to ~18. CQ6 reallocates ~8-10 points from C into D, and plank (c) drops from 55 to ~25.

falsification_signposts.signpost: OECD harmonized unemployment rate monthly print at or above 6.5% for six consecutive months, while OECD-38 working-age population is simultaneously falling year-over-year.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: Kills the Japan-style denominator adjustment that holds my CQ1 conjunct-1 marginal at 0.55; CQ1 falls from 12 to ~5. Pulls CQ3 P50 down ~0.2-0.3pp and shifts ~6-8 points of CQ6 mass into D, since a rising unemployment rate against a shrinking labour force is the BIS Box C demand-deficit signature rather than the scarcity signature.

falsification_signposts.signpost: Official OECD or Eurostat sectoral data showing cumulative real median hourly wage growth in ISIC F+Q exceeding ISIC J+K+M by >=5.0pp over 2025-2031 (i.e. halfway to CQ1's threshold at the halfway point).
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: Overturns the 45-year directional absence of precedent that sets my conjunct-2 marginal at 0.17; CQ1 rises from 12 to ~30-35. Also implies the care-wage monopsony constraint is not binding, which raises CQ2 conjunct A toward 0.62 and lifts CQ6-C by ~5 points.

wave1.coupling_tension: The sharpest inconsistency is between AI-Q3 and AI-Q4, and it is arithmetic rather than mechanistic, so my lens can speak to it. AI-Q4 puts 66% on the 2027-2032 capex cycle being >=20% impaired or revenue-starved; AI-Q3 puts a P50 of 998 TWh on 2036 STRICT OPERATIONAL data-centre electricity, a ~2.7x multiple of the 365 TWh 2024 base. The base rate for announced capex supercycles says these cannot both stand. Telecom/fibre 1999-2002: a large majority of laid fibre stayed dark for years and ~$100B+ of capitalized value was written off. US nuclear 1974-1984: roughly 100-120 cancellations out of ~250 orders, ~50% impairment, with the OPERATING fleet ending near half the announced plan. Shale 2015-2020: ~$400-450B of impairments. 19th-century railway manias and Japan 1980s property/plant: same shape. In every case the physically-operating asset base settled 30-50% below announcement, and the impairment and the shortfall in operating capacity were the SAME event. Once demographics are endogenous the tension widens further rather than narrowing, because the locked 2A block supplies three additional, purely mechanical brakes that 2B's exogeneity assumption suppresses: aging-driven pension and health claims competing for the same fiscal space that grid interconnection and transmission build needs (China's subsidies already ~10.1% of fiscal expenditure; OECD net interest 2%->3% of GDP); retail electricity-price pass-through becoming politically binding precisely in electorates with 39-41% old-age ratios and fixed incomes; and the locked +1.0pp deterioration in global (r - g) raising the discount rate on long-lived, 15-25-year-payback power and data-centre assets. DIRECTION: AI-Q3's P50 of ~998 TWh is too HIGH by roughly 15-25% conditional on AI-Q4 resolving yes (I would put the coupled strict-operational P50 nearer 800-850 TWh), or equivalently AI-Q4 at 66% is too LOW if AI-Q3's P50 is to be believed — the joint distribution they imply has far more mass on "impaired AND fully built out" than any capex-supercycle reference class supports. Two secondary tensions, same mechanism, opposite signs: AI-Q5 (cognitive labour-compensation share falling >=3.5pp) at 38.2% is biased HIGH because a shrinking OECD working-age denominator pushes the aggregate labour share UP through scarcity, and because the J+K+M median is flattered by the same survivor-composition effect that undermines CQ1's second conjunct; while AI-Q1 (TFP >= +0.50pp) at 23.0% is biased slightly LOW, since aging is a demand pull for capital deepening and measured TFP rises mechanically when hours contract faster than output — the Japanese robot-density episode delivered respectable measured TFP alongside 0.8%/yr growth. Both corrections are small (a few points) relative to the Q3/Q4 arithmetic conflict, and neither rescues CQ6-A: the headcount binds regardless of which side of the Q3/Q4 tension resolves.

wave1.lens_self_description: Inside-view causal-mechanism modeler: I built an explicit transmission chain from aging demographics and AI capex through sectoral supply elasticities, core-basket weights, and administered-price institutions to the level and skew of inflation, and let the mechanism set every number — which forbade me from using any historical base rate (decadal inflation averages, equity drawdown frequencies, MOVE history, OECD unemployment persistence) as evidence, and forbade reversion-to-mean anchoring; where a mechanism output sits far from historical frequency (CQ3 P50 1.6%, CQ6-D 34) I reported the mechanism.
wave1.cq1_reasoning:
MECHANISM. Conjunct 1 (OECD-38 harmonized U ≤5.5% avg 2032-2036). Chain: working-age population -0.3%/yr (2A) -> labour-force denominator shrinks [-, mechanically holds U down ~-0.15 pp/yr cumulative] ; AI displacement in ISIC J/K/M -> displaced cognitive workers whose nearest vacancy is in F+Q at 45-60% of prior wage and behind 6-24mo licensure -> frictional U up [+0.4 to +0.8 pp]; AI-Q4 (locked 66%) capex bust lands 2031-2033 -> cyclical U spike [+1.5 to +2.5 pp for ~8 quarters] INSIDE the measurement window. Two years at 6.6% plus three at 4.9% averages 5.6% — fails by a hair; two years at 6.2% plus three at 4.8% averages 5.4% — passes. Marginal 0.50.
Conjunct 2 (F+Q minus J+K+M real median hourly wage ≥ +10.0 pp cumulative 2025-2036, i.e. ≥0.87 pp/yr). Underlying relative-price mechanism favours YES: 80+ population grows ~3.7%/yr -> ADL care-hour demand elasticity to 80+ ≈ 1.0 -> care labour demand +3%/yr against supply +1%/yr; datacentre/grid/housing construction competes for the electrical trades (incremental DC+grid construction employment ~4-6% of the construction pool but ~15-20% of the electrician/lineman pool) -> F wage +1.5-2.0%/yr real relative. Raw differential 1.0-1.7 pp/yr = 11-19 pp. THREE counter-mechanisms kill it: (i) ISIC Q is 60-80% publicly funded across OECD-38 and net interest goes 2%->3% of GDP (2A), so the monopsony payer settles pay below clearing — the gap becomes waitlists, not wages; (ii) composition: measured F+Q MEDIAN is dragged -0.3 to -0.5 pp/yr by low-wage migrant/low-credential care entrants (the same migration channel aging opens); (iii) inverse composition in J+K+M — AI displaces the BOTTOM of the cognitive distribution (junior analyst, paralegal, BPO, first-line support), so the surviving MEDIAN rises even as AI-Q5's labour share falls. (iii) is a measurement perversity that makes the locked AI-Q5 marginal and CQ1 conjunct 2 point in OPPOSITE directions on the same underlying event. Marginal 0.33.
Correlation: positive — the tight-labour-market state is the same state that delivers the F+Q premium; rho = +0.30. 0.50 x 0.33 = 0.165; cov = 0.30 x sqrt(.25 x .2211) = +0.070; joint = 0.235, shaded to 0.22 for the compositional wedge which is independent of the cycle.
wave1.cq2_reasoning:
ARROW DIAGRAM (sign, rough magnitude on each arrow).
2027-2030 IMPULSE:
AI capex + reshoring -> datacentre load (+635 TWh by 2036 per locked AI-Q3 = +3.2% of OECD+China ~19,800 TWh, but 5-8x the 0.5%/yr baseline load growth rate) -> [+] reserve margin falls below 15% -> residual-demand price semi-elasticity 2.5 -> wholesale power +25-50% -> [x0.45 regulated pass-through over 2-3 yr, plus T&D capex -> rate base -> allowed return, a slower durable channel] -> real retail electricity +1.5-2.5%/yr -> [x0.10 core pass-through ONLY] -> core +0.10 to 0.20 pp.
Grid/DC construction -> [+] electrical-trade scarcity -> construction cost +4%/yr -> [x0.25 over 5yr] -> shelter rents +0.3 pp.

China leg: labour force -1%/yr by then; property-driven capital deepening exhausted (ICOR rising); TFP 1.5-2.0% with the world's deepest robot installed base; 2A's -2.7 pp/yr aging drag applied to a ~5% start. 2032-2036 P50 = 2.9%/yr.
Combined P50 = 0.70(1.0) + 0.30(2.9) = 1.57 -> 1.6%/yr.
WEAKEST LINK (Chad Jones / Baumol). The non-substitutable input capping the system is DIRECT PERSONAL CARE HOURS for the 80+ cohort — hands-on ADL work (lifting, toileting, feeding, bathing, night supervision) that no 2027-2036 model or robot performs at scale and that is credential-gated and immigration-throttled; the close second is grid interconnection and firm dispatchable capacity 2027-2031. In a Jones task-weighted production function, output growth is bounded by the growth of the task you cannot automate times its share, so cheap cognition cannot lift the aggregate past the care/physical wall; this is exactly why a +0.6 pp TFP breakout can be true in J/K/M and still not show up in the CQ3 aggregate. Shadow price by 2036: the TRUE willingness-to-pay for a marginal care hour roughly doubles in real terms (+70% to +110% vs 2025), but the OBSERVED administered price rises only ~25-35% real because the public payer is the monopsonist. The wedge is realised as a QUANTITY: unmet-need hours, waitlists, and informal substitution. That is the mechanism by which the care bottleneck shows up in GDP (down) rather than CPI (up) — the single most load-bearing claim in my model, and the reason my CQ3 P50 is below the 2015-2024 realised rate while my CQ2 is also low.
P10 0.7% = deep bust + care rationing + BIS demand deficit + China under 2%. P90 2.7% = no bust, Transformative Breakout, China 4%, and the physical bottleneck eased by migration liberalisation. Distribution is left-skewed because the weakest link is a cap, not a symmetric shock.

wave1.cq5_reasoning:
Conjunct 1 (MOVE avg ≥105 over 2027-2036). Mechanism: rate vol is the product of (a) dispersion of beliefs about which institutional response to the fiscal arithmetic wins — repression vs term-premium spiral, which my CQ4 says is genuinely bimodal [strong +]; (b) Treasury/JGB/gilt net supply against dealer balance-sheet capacity, with marginal duration absorbed by levered basis trades (2A) that de-risk procyclically [+]; (c) policy-regime instability where the inflation target and the debt path conflict [+]. Against: the back half of the window is, on my mechanism, the post-bust disinflation half, where a credible low-inflation equilibrium compresses vol to 75-90. Front half 100-125, back half 75-100, 10-yr average ~95-105 — this sits almost exactly on the threshold, which is why I will not go above ~0.45. Marginal 0.45.
Conjunct 2 (a coupled shock: MSCI World -25% peak-to-trough while G7 10y nominal FAILS to fall ≥50 bps, or rises ≥25 bps). This requires the shock's SOURCE to be the discount rate or fiscal/inflation credibility, not growth. Mechanism-by-source: (i) the AI capex bust itself is a growth-and-credit shock -> policy cuts, bonds rally -> FAILS the test; (ii) a fiscal/term-premium event (the gilt-2022 transmission: duration supply meets a leveraged holder base) -> equity down, yields up -> PASSES; (iii) a 20% AI valuation shock (2A names it explicitly) propagating through $650B of AI-linked debt into basis-trade unwind and Treasury market dysfunction -> yields rise on the way down -> PASSES if the drawdown extends to 25%. P(at least one ≥25% MSCI World drawdown somewhere in the window) ≈ 0.75 on mechanism: the 2A setup contains both a scheduled valuation reset and a 66%-likely capex bust, either of which reaches 25% once leverage is in the chain. Conditional P(yields fail to rally | ≥25% drawdown) ≈ 0.42 — a 25% equity fall normally buys a cut cycle and a bond rally UNLESS core is above target or the sovereign market is itself the stress; my CQ2 path has core above target precisely in 2027-2030, which is when the capex-cycle shock is most likely. Expected number of qualifying drawdowns ~1.3 -> P = 1 - 0.58^1.3 = 0.51. Marginal 0.50.
Correlation: STRONGLY positive — the same institutional state (fiscal dominance risk, leveraged duration absorption, unanchored term premium) produces both high MOVE and the no-rally drawdown; they are not two draws, they are two readings of one regime. rho = +0.45. 0.45 x 0.50 = 0.225; cov = 0.45 x sqrt(.2475 x .25) = +0.112; joint = 0.337 -> 34. Note this is the one conjunction where I do NOT take the full discount, because the mechanism makes the conjuncts near-co-determined.
wave1.cq6_reasoning:
Applied the lexical lock to my own CQ3 distribution (P10 0.7 / P50 1.6 / P90 2.7, implied sigma ~0.78 pp) and my own 2032-2036 OECD core path (~1.9% central, i.e. LOWER than my 2027-2036 average of 2.08% because the back half is the post-bust disinflation half).
Step 1, A requires growth ≥2.6%: P = 1 - Phi((2.6-1.6)/0.78) = 1 - Phi(1.28) = 0.10; raised slightly to 0.11 for the right-tail case where no bust occurs and the migration channel relieves the care wall. A = 11.
Step 2, C requires core ≥2.7% AND growth <2.0%: P(growth<2.0) = Phi(0.51) = 0.70. P(core ≥2.7 | growth<2.0) = 0.16 — conditional on low growth, high core must be SUPPLY-side, which in my mechanism means the care bottleneck clearing through prices instead of administered rationing, or a grid wall that survives the capex digestion, or outright fiscal dominance. My monopsony arrow is what holds this to 0.16 rather than 0.35. C = 0.70 x 0.16 = 0.11 -> 11.
Step 3, D requires growth <1.7% AND core <2.0%: P(growth<1.7) = Phi(0.128) = 0.55. Within that cell: P(core≥2.7) = 0.17, P(core 2.0-2.7) = 0.21, P(core<2.0) = 0.62. D = 0.55 x 0.62 = 0.34.
Step 4, B residual = 100 - 11 - 11 - 34 = 44.
CONSISTENCY CHECK PERFORMED. (i) My CQ3 P50 of 1.6% sits just inside D's growth band, so D could not be small — but D also needs core <2.0%, which costs it 38% of that mass, so D lands at 34 and not ~55. (ii) B exceeds D (44 > 34) because B is the residual that absorbs BOTH the 1.7-2.5% growth band (~29% of mass) and the low-growth / 2.0-2.7% core leftover cell (~12%); it is not a "muddle through" judgement, it is an accounting residual of my own CQ3/core joint. If I had assumed a flat path these two numbers would conflict, and that front-loading is the single thing a reader should check me on. (iv) A = 11 cannot exceed my P(growth≥2.6) = 0.10-0.11, satisfied. (v) D + C = 45, i.e. I put slightly less than half the mass on the two "something is broken" regimes and the modal single regime on the bifurcated residual — the distinguishable claim is that D at 34 is roughly 3x the 2B standalone ensemble's implied stagnation weight, because endogenous demographics add the care-rationing GDP leak and the BIS Box C demand deficit that the exogenous-demographics run cannot see.

hypothesis_critique.a: The failure word is SMOOTHLY, and it fails twice over — on gradient and on magnitude. Gradient: the reallocation elasticity of labour across occupation-skill distance is ~0.1-0.2 over five years; the displaced J/K/M worker is 40-50, credentialed, urban, and the nearest care vacancy pays 45-60% of prior wage behind 6-24 months of licensure plus physical and emotional labour, so the wage signal needed to move them is the signal the state monopsony is fiscally unable to pay. Magnitude: OECD-38 J+K+M employment is ~15% of total; a 3.5 pp labour-share fall corresponds to perhaps 5-8M displaced-equivalents against ~13-15M additional LTC workers needed by 2036 — even 100% frictionless transfer undersupplies the gap, and realistic transfer is under 15% of it. Also the two flows are mistimed: the cognitive displacement is concentrated 2029-2034 while the 80+ surge runs through 2045. 4.
hypothesis_critique.b: Two failure words, SEVERELY and BLOCKS. BLOCKS is wrong on channel composition: AI exposes the VIRTUAL export channel (Philippine BPO ~1.7M workers, India IT-BPM ~5.5M), but the PHYSICAL migration channel is the one aging widens — nurses, carers, seafarers, construction trades — and for the Philippines physical-worker remittances (~8-9% of GDP) exceed BPO's GDP contribution. My care weakest-link mechanism says OECD willingness-to-pay for a marginal care hour roughly doubles by 2036 while domestic supply elasticity is 0.35, which makes the migration channel the binding relief valve; the only thing that blocks it is OECD politics, not AI. SEVERELY is wrong on the virtual channel too: cost-to-price pass-through of 0.45 in the services these firms sell means falling task cost expands volume (BPO Jevons) before it destroys the sector, and the near-term observable is margin and headcount-per-revenue compression, not export collapse. Net: real distributional damage to Indian and Philippine entry-level cognitive labour, offset at the national-accounts level by the care and construction pull. 12.
hypothesis_critique.c: Closest to my mechanism's own shape — a 2027-2030 impulse from power/grid capex crowding, electricity rate-base pass-through, tariffs and physical/care scarcity, then 2031-2036 disinflation from capex digestion, cognitive automation, Chinese overcapacity and the BIS Box C labour-income deficit. The failure word is HOT (amplitude, not sign). My weights say the 2027-2030 impulse lands overwhelmingly in HEADLINE and in RELATIVE PRICES — electricity, construction, administered-then-rationed care — while core, which excludes electricity by construction and is 18% shelter and 12% care, runs 2.6-2.9%: warm, not hot, and inside most central banks' tolerated overshoot. The second clause, the fall in the 2030s, is where the plank is actually strongest, since it is carried by the locked 66% AI-Q4 capex bust. Residual 38% of doubt is the fiscal-dominance branch where the fall never arrives. 62.
hypothesis_critique.d: Two failure words, EVENTUALLY and WINS. EVENTUALLY is the tell that the plank is unfalsifiable on a dated horizon: an unbounded horizon lets any growth rate be a waystation, while the panel's question is the 2032-2036 path, where my mechanism gives 1.6%/yr — BELOW the 2015-2024 realised rate — so AI does not outrun. WINS conflates aggregate GDP with per-capita GDP and conflates cognitive-task productivity with output: in a Chad Jones task-weighted function, output growth is capped by the growth of the input you cannot automate times its share, and that input is direct personal care hours plus grid interconnection, neither of which gets exponentially cheaper by 2036. Exponential improvement in a substitutable factor against a fixed non-substitutable one yields an ASYMPTOTE, not a win; cheap cognition raises the shadow price of the bottleneck rather than relaxing it. 22, with the 22 reserved for the branch where migration liberalisation or genuine embodied robotics moves the care wall inside the window.

key_drivers: CORE-BASKET WEIGHTS ARE THE WHOLE LEVEL ANSWER: electricity is excluded from US core CPI/PCE and HICP core by construction, so the 2027-2031 power/grid impulse reaches core only through the ~2% energy cost share of service gross output at ~0.5 pass-through (core pass-through elasticity 0.10). A regime of 4-6% electricity/construction/care against -1 to +1% software/goods/tradables yields ~2.0-2.1% core, because ~40% of the core basket sits in the deflating buckets. Huge skew, modest level.

STATE MONOPSONY CONVERTS THE CARE BOTTLENECK FROM A PRICE INTO A QUANTITY: ISIC Q is 60-80% publicly funded across OECD-38 and net interest rises 2%->3% of GDP (2A), so the administered price rises ~25-35% real while true willingness-to-pay for a marginal care hour roughly doubles. The wedge is realised as unmet-need hours, waitlists and 4-7M additional informal family carers. This pushes measured core inflation DOWN and real GDP DOWN simultaneously — the opposite of the naive Baumol-stagflation reading, and the reason my CQ2 and CQ3 are both low.

THE LOCKED 66% AI-Q4 CAPEX BUST LANDS INSIDE THE 2032-2036 MEASUREMENT WINDOW, so CQ3, CQ4 and CQ6 are all read off the post-bust half: gas turbines, transformers and datacentre shells arrive 2030-2033 into stalled load growth, giving excess capacity, flat-to-falling real electricity prices, a -0.8 pp GDP drag for ~2 years, and a cyclical r* depression of ~-0.4 pp.

CHINESE CPI IS A SEMI-INDEPENDENT DEFLATIONARY OBJECT, not an OECD mirror: household income share stuck ~44% of GDP (semi-elasticity +0.08 pp CPI per +1 pp share), residence category (~18-20% of CPI) flat-to-negative after a permanent -55/-60% property adjustment, pension subsidy already 10.1% of fiscal expenditure so the safety net cannot be bought big enough to unlock precautionary saving, and deliberate supply-side policy running capacity +5-7%/yr against domestic demand +3-4%/yr. Offset only late in the window by a -1%/yr working-age contraction pressuring services wages.

TERM PREMIUM VERSUS r* NEARLY CANCEL IN THE REAL-YIELD LEVEL BUT NOT IN VOLATILITY: retiree dissaving (+0.3/+0.5) and a +0.75/+1.25 fiscal term premium offset weaker g (-0.4/-0.6) and post-bust investment collapse (-0.4), leaving the G7 weighted real yield near its 1.80% starting point while the DISPERSION widens, because repression and term-premium spiral are two opposite institutional answers to one fiscal arithmetic.

MEASUREMENT PERVERSITY IN MEDIAN WAGES: composition pushes measured F+Q medians DOWN (low-wage migrant and low-credential care entrants, -0.3 to -0.5 pp/yr) and measured J+K+M medians UP (AI displaces the bottom of the cognitive distribution — junior analyst, paralegal, BPO, first-line support — lifting the survivors' median). The same event therefore raises the locked AI-Q5 labour-share probability and LOWERS CQ1's wage-differential conjunct.
