wave1.coupling_tension:
PRIMARY TENSION — AI-Q3 (2036 OECD-38 + China strict operational datacentre electricity, ensemble mean P10/P50/P90 = 596.8 / 998.2 / 1,573.8 TWh) is INCONSISTENT ONCE DEMOGRAPHICS ARE ENDOGENOUS, and the inconsistency is DOWNWARD on the P50 with a fatter LEFT tail. 2B holds demographics exogenous, which lets AI-Q3 be forecast as a demand-for-compute question: willingness-to-pay times falling cost per token. Endogenise 2A and the SAME demographic block moves both sides of that market in opposite directions. On the demand side aging is a pull: labour scarcity raises automation ROI, so desired inference and robotics load rises [+]. On the SUPPLY side, the inputs that convert desired load into strict operational megawatt-hours are electricians, linemen, substation and HVAC crews, transformer and switchgear manufacturing labour, and interconnection engineering — precisely the physical trades that aging drains. Roughly a quarter of the US electrician workforce reaches retirement eligibility by 2033; the OECD construction workforce median age is 43 and rising; and those same crews are simultaneously bid for by the housing supply response, grid hardening, and the care-facility buildout the 80+ surge requires. My own mechanism makes this the binding arrow: a short-run (3-year) supply elasticity of firm dispatchable capacity plus interconnection of 0.25 is itself conditional on trade labour, so endogenous demographics push that elasticity toward 0.15-0.20. Net: endogenous demographics RAISE desired datacentre load by perhaps +8% and LOWER buildable load by -18 to -25%, and the supply side binds harder because it is a physical, non-substitutable, long-lead input. AI-Q3 should therefore shift to roughly P10 520 / P50 880-900 / P90 1,380 — about -10% on the median with materially more left skew, since the distribution's shape should inherit the convex scarcity of the bottleneck rather than stay near-symmetric. This matters beyond AI-Q3: a lower buildable load reduces the 2027-2031 power-price impulse (-0.04 pp core) AND reduces the AI TFP contribution (-0.08 pp on CQ3), i.e. it is disinflationary and growth-negative together, which is exactly the D-regime pairing and part of why my CQ6-D is 34.
SECONDARY TENSION, OPPOSITE DIRECTION — AI-Q5 (OECD-38 J/K/M labour compensation share of sectoral GVA falls ≥3.5 pp by 2036, 38.2%) is TOO LOW once demographics are endogenous. With a shrinking working-age population, the cognitive labour share can fall by ATTRITION WITHOUT REPLACEMENT: no layoffs, no litigation, no political backlash, no severance — the cheapest possible path, and the one a firm facing a rising wage bill and an unfillable req will actually take. Exogenous demographics force the forecaster to imagine active displacement, which is institutionally hard; endogenous demographics hand firms a free pass. AI-Q5 should be ~46-50%. But that revision generates its OWN tension with AI-Q1 (TFP lift ≥+0.50 pp/yr, 23.0%): a labour share falling via non-replacement at roughly flat sectoral output IS measured TFP growth in those sectors, so AI-Q5 up and AI-Q1 flat is not a coherent joint. One of the two must move; my mechanism says AI-Q5 up and AI-Q1 up only modestly (to ~27%), because the J/K/M TFP gain is diluted at the aggregate by the Baumol composition shift of labour INTO ISIC F and Q, which the exogenous-demographics run has no way to represent. That dilution term — sectoral TFP gains real, aggregate TFP gains much smaller because aging reallocates workers into measured-zero-productivity sectors — is the general form of every tension above.

wave1.lens_self_description: I forecast the resolution process rather than the world: for each CQ I ask which published series would actually resolve it, how it is constructed, revised and composition-biased, and I let definitional artefacts set the probability — which forbade me from using any structural macro-theoretic conviction (AI capability priors, geopolitics, policy-reaction functions) except as a weak prior on the underlying quantity once the measurement audit was done.
wave1.cq1_reasoning:
RESOLVING SERIES. Conjunct A: OECD Short-Term Labour Market Statistics "harmonised unemployment rate", OECD-total aggregate, labour-force-weighted ILO-definition LFS, age band NOT uniform (15-74 EU, 16+ US, 15+ JP); lightly revised (seasonal-factor and LFS-reweighting revisions ~0.1-0.2pp, occasionally larger after census rebasing, e.g. US 2025-26 population-control jumps). Conjunct B: there is NO published "OECD-38 real median hourly wage by ISIC F / Q / J / K / M". The resolver must stitch: Eurostat Structure of Earnings Survey (median gross hourly earnings by NACE section, QUADRENNIAL — 2022, 2026, 2030, 2034, with 2034 published ~2036-37, i.e. AFTER resolution, so the observable endpoints are 2022 and 2030, not 2025 and 2036); UK ASHE (annual, median gross hourly ex-overtime by SIC — the only clean series); US BLS OES (median hourly by NAICS, employer-reported, NAICS≠ISIC, known establishment-weighting breaks); Japan BSWS; Korea/Canada partial. OECD.Stat's earnings holdings are AVERAGE annual wages and decile ratios, not sectoral medians.
MARGINAL A: level today ~4.9-5.1%; 2015-19 OECD average ~5.8%, 2018-19 ~5.3-5.4%. A clean 5-year average ≤5.5% requires essentially no recession inside 2032-36 plus no elevated hangover from the 2A/AI-Q4 capex bust (66% prior on impairments by 2032). Recession-free 5-year windows are ~35-40% of history; a 2-year +2pp episode adds ~0.8pp to the window average. Unadjusted: ~40%. Measurement adjustments, all one-way UP on YES: (i) rising 65+ participation injects workers whose unemployment rate is ~2-3%, diluting the aggregate by ~0.1-0.25pp over 11 years (+4pp prob); (ii) AI-displaced white-collar workers who exit rather than search are recorded as participation decline, not unemployment (+3pp); (iii) composition shift of the labour force toward 55-74 (low measured unemployment) (+2pp). Offsetting: membership drift — several accession candidates (Brazil, Peru, Argentina, Bulgaria, Romania, Croatia, Indonesia) could make the LIVE OECD aggregate ≠ a fixed OECD-38 basket; if the resolver uses the published live aggregate and a high-unemployment member accedes, YES gets harder (-3pp). Net A = 45%.
MARGINAL B: substance first — a 10.0pp cumulative gap over 11 years is 0.87pp/yr differential; plausible for a FIXED-COMPOSITION wage index (care/construction scarcity vs cognitive compression) at ~25%. Then composition, which is decisive and runs AGAINST the gap on BOTH legs: (1) Q (health/social care) is the OECD's largest low-wage-entrant sink — elder-care expansion hires migrants, part-timers and re-entrants near the bottom decile; +15-25% Q headcount with entrants at 70-80% of the incumbent median drags the MEASURED median down 2-5pp while every incumbent gets a raise (-5pp prob). (2) F (construction) gets the same entrant dilution from grid/data-centre/housing buildout plus a cyclical 2031-33 post-capex-bust hit (-2pp). (3) J+K+M goes the other way: AI truncates the BOTTOM of the cognitive distribution first (junior analysts, paralegals, entry coders, K back-office), and removing the lower tail MECHANICALLY RAISES the measured median by 3-6pp with no incumbent raise at all (-6pp). So roughly 6-10pp of the 10.0pp threshold is consumed by composition artefact pointing the wrong way. Deflator note: using the same national CPI for both sector baskets cancels in the differential, so "real" adds noise, not bias — unless the resolver mixes HICP and national CPI across members. Post-artefact substance ~11%; multiply by P(resolver can even demonstrate ≥10.0pp from the available vintages) ~0.75 (the 2034 SES lands too late; a strict resolver defaults NO or annuls). B = 9%.
CORRELATION & JOIN: positive — a tight labour market is the state that generates F+Q scarcity premia, and white-collar compression coexisting with ≤5.5% unemployment requires exactly that re-absorption. Assume rho ≈ +0.3, i.e. P(B|A) ≈ 0.09 x 1.35 ≈ 0.12. Joint = 0.45 x 0.12 = 5.4%. REFERENCE CLASS: tightly-worded two-conjunct questions where one conjunct depends on a series that is not published at the stated frequency/aggregation — these resolve NO far more often than their narrative plausibility suggests. ANSWER 6.
wave1.cq2_reasoning:
RESOLVING SERIES. Conjunct A: "GDP-weighted OECD-38 core CPI/PCE". No such series is published. OECD publishes an OECD-total CPI and CPI-excluding-food-and-energy weighted by PRIVATE CONSUMPTION PPP, not GDP. The "/PCE" latitude alone is worth +0.1-0.3pp on the US leg (US core CPI has run ~30-40bp above core PCE on shelter weight and formula/scope) and the US is ~40% of OECD-38 PPP GDP. Euro-area "core" (HICP ex energy, food, alcohol, tobacco) uses a different exclusion set from US core AND excludes owner-occupied housing entirely; if OOH enters HICP during the window (long-standing Eurostat workstream) euro core steps up +0.1-0.3pp with no change in the world. EM-OECD weight is the biggest single artefact: Turkey, Mexico, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica are inside OECD-38 and carry structurally higher core inflation; at 2025 PPP GDP weights Turkey alone (~2.3%) at 12-18% core adds ~0.25-0.35pp to the aggregate, and the five together put a floor of roughly +0.30pp under any OECD-38 GDP-weighted core print. Direction: strongly YES. Revisions: CPI is not revised (seasonal factors aside); PCE is revised annually and in benchmark years, by up to 0.2-0.3pp on an annual rate — so a PCE-based resolution is vintage-dependent.
LEVEL vs SKEW (the effort's core requirement, carried with weights). 2027-2030 impulse: tariff/fragmentation goods pass-through; shelter (33% of US core CPI, ~15% of euro core) running 2.5-3.5% as construction costs compete with grid/data-centre trades; medical+social care services (~7-9% of US core) at 3-5% on care wage scarcity. CRITICAL ARTEFACT: the single most AI-specific inflationary channel — data-centre electricity pass-through — is ENERGY and therefore EXCLUDED from core on both the US and euro definitions. +635 TWh (AI-Q3 P50 ~1,000 vs 365 in 2024) implies ~130-160 GW firm capacity plus transmission, ~$1.3-2.0T over 12 years, i.e. ~20% on top of current OECD+China grid/generation capex — large, zonally violent (PJM, Virginia, Ireland, Osaka), but diluted to perhaps +0.1-0.3pp on OECD-38 HEADLINE and only +0.1-0.2pp on core via second-round business costs. A naive reader double-counts this into core; I do not (-4pp vs naive). 2031-2036 disinflation: the mirror-image artefact runs the other way. ISIC J, K, M are PRODUCER-heavy; AI's output-price deflation lands overwhelmingly in intermediate/B2B services that barely enter a CONSUMER basket. Consumer-facing AI-deflatables are telecom/internet (~1.5-2%), audio-video/media (~1%), education (~2.5%), household legal/accounting (<1%), plus imputed financial services (2-7% of PCE, measured by a method AI will not touch cleanly). Even a total collapse of J/K/M prices moves core CPI by only -0.2 to -0.4pp. So "AI disinflation" is structurally under-weighted in the index that resolves this (+6pp on YES vs the narrative reading).
ARITHMETIC OF THE 10-YEAR AVERAGE: the window is FRONT-LOADED. 2027-30 at ~2.8% and 2031-36 at ~2.35% gives a 10-year average of ~2.53% — it clears. The hurdle is met largely by the first four years plus the EM-OECD floor, not by a 2030s stagflation. Conjunct A = 62%.
Conjunct B (China headline CPI < 1.50%/yr, 2027-36). SERIES: NBS monthly CPI, basket weights rebased on a 5-year cycle (2026 is a rebase year — a services-weight increase would nudge prints UP), housing captured as RENT with a crude imputation so the property adjustment barely registers, pork cycle dominating the volatility. Starting point ~0.0-0.3% (2024 +0.2%, 2025 ~0%, repeated negative prints); PPI negative for most of 2022-26. Drivers per the brief, treated semi-independently: property-balance-sheet adjustment, household income share of GDP ~44%, deliberate supply-side industrial policy manufacturing persistent goods overcapacity, and (coupled from 2A) a -60M population with ~4.4->2.8 worker/retiree ratio and strained pension subsidies (~2.9T RMB, 10.1% of expenditure) that cap the transfer-financed consumption rebalancing. Japan 1995-2005 analogue averaged ~-0.1%. Against: 10 years is long; one pork/food spike at +5% adds 0.5pp to the decade average, an RMB devaluation imports food/energy inflation, and NBS has mild upward measurement/political bias against printing deflation. B = 72%.
CORRELATION: mildly NEGATIVE in the standard channel (Chinese goods deflation exports into OECD core goods) but the tariff/fragmentation wall is precisely the mechanism that severs it, and both legs are driven by the same asymmetry (OECD builds physical capacity under labour scarcity; China has excess capacity and deficient demand). Net rho ≈ -0.12, so P(B|A) ≈ 0.72 x 0.90 ≈ 0.65. JOINT = 0.62 x 0.65 = 0.40, minus a ~1pp haircut for construction ambiguity that could be adjudicated against YES (a consumption-weighted rather than GDP-weighted OECD core, or a core-PCE-only reading, both of which lower the OECD leg). ANSWER 39.
wave1.cq3_reasoning:
RESOLVING CONSTRUCTION: chain-linked national real GDP (OECD Quarterly National Accounts for 38 members, NBS for China), aggregated at FIXED 2025 USD PPP weights as the question locks. Three measurement findings. (1) The constant-2025-PPP lock is a genuine help — it removes the moving-weight problem — but the 2025 PPP LEVEL is itself a published estimate that ICP rounds revise retroactively (ICP 2021 raised China's PPP GDP materially; ICP 2026 results land ~2029-30 and ICP 2030 ~2033). If the resolver uses the then-current vintage of 2025 PPPs, a China weight revision of +2-3pp raises the measured aggregate by ~0.05-0.15pp given China grows faster. (2) China's official real growth is widely argued to be overstated by 0.5-2pp (deflator construction, provincial aggregation); the resolver will use NBS, so the MEASURED answer is ~0.3-0.6pp above any "true" measure. I am forecasting the measured number and therefore do NOT shade down for this — but it is the largest single wedge between this question and the economics. (3) AI capex deflators: quality-adjusted price indices for accelerators/servers convert flat nominal capex into large positive real investment volumes. This has materially supported measured US real growth in 2024-26 and will subtract symmetrically in a digestion phase; for a 2032-36 window following an AI-Q4-style impairment event it is more likely a measured drag than a support. Offsetting and unmeasured: free/AI-provided digital services are the classic missing-output problem — real GDP UNDERSTATES welfare but that does not move this series.
FERMI. Weights: 2025 PPP GDP ~ OECD-38 $76T, China $40T, so China ~34% at t0, drifting to ~37-38% of the combined by 2032 under constant-2025-price accumulation if China outgrows the OECD. OECD-38 leg: 2A gives 0.6%/yr per capita absent productivity offsets; OECD population growth 0.2-0.3%/yr (migration-dependent, and in a labour-scarcity regime migration policy is the swing variable) → 0.8-0.9% aggregate baseline; add an AI TFP lift whose expectation from 2B is ~+0.30pp (AI-Q1 only 23% on >=+0.50pp; AI-Q6 central band +0.15-0.59 at 47.2%) → OECD-38 ~1.1-1.3%. China leg 2032-36: 2A's -2.7pp/yr aging drag on an economy already decelerating, population -0.4%/yr and workforce faster, property adjustment largely digested by 2032 → official 2.0-3.0%, P50 2.6%. Aggregate = 0.62 x 1.2 + 0.38 x 2.6 = 0.74 + 0.99 = 1.73%. P50 = 1.8% (rounding up slightly for the ICP/NBS upward measurement wedge).
DISPERSION: a 5-year annualized average compresses tails versus annual growth. P10 1.0% = one recession inside the window plus a China step-down to ~1.5% (post-capex-bust excess capacity, BIS Box C demand deficit, labour-income shortfall). P90 2.7% = broad AI diffusion (the 16.2% Transformative Breakout tail) plus a genuine Chinese consumption rebalancing. Mild right truncation because 2.6%+ requires BOTH legs to beat, which is why I keep CQ6-A at 12. REFERENCE CLASS: realized 5-year annualized OECD+China PPP growth, 2010-14 ~3.2%, 2015-19 ~2.9%, 2020-24 ~2.2%, with the China weight rising but its growth halving — the series has declined ~0.4pp per quinquennium for three consecutive windows, which lands 2032-36 near 1.7-1.9% on pure extrapolation.
wave1.cq4_reasoning:
RESOLUTION MECHANICS FIRST — this is the CQ where the definition does the most work. The stated measure is "10y nominal benchmark minus 10y inflation swap / TIPS breakeven", GDP-weighted across G7. Five audit findings:
(1) TWO G7 MEMBERS CANNOT BE MEASURED AS STATED. Canada discontinued Real Return Bonds in Nov 2022 and has no liquid 10y CAD inflation swap market; Japan's JGBi breakevens are thin and BOJ-distorted. So ~16% of G7 GDP requires a proxy the question does not specify. Any resolver's proxy choice moves the aggregate 5-15bp.
(2) BREAKEVEN IS NOT EXPECTED INFLATION. It embeds a positive inflation risk premium (10-30bp when inflation uncertainty is high, exactly the CQ5 regime) and a positive TIPS liquidity premium. Nominal-minus-breakeven therefore OVERSTATES the ex-ante real rate by roughly 10-40bp in the states of the world this panel is forecasting. Direction: the measured CQ4 prints HIGH relative to any structural r*.
(3) UK RPI REFORM IS A STEP DISCONTINUITY INSIDE THE WINDOW. UK breakevens are RPI-linked and carry an RPI-CPI wedge of ~80-100bp; the 2030 alignment of RPI to CPIH collapses that wedge, mechanically RAISING the UK measured real yield by ~0.6-1.0pp from 2030 with no change in the economics. At ~8% of G7 PPP GDP that is +5-8bp on the aggregate and a visible break in the series.
(4) WEIGHTING BASIS. The scope lock says constant 2025 PPP; PPP weights raise Japan and Italy relative to market-rate weights. Japan is the low-real-yield member and Italy the high one, so the two partly offset, but the net PPP-vs-market difference is ~5-15bp and the question does not say which.
(5) THE US ANCHOR IS NOT THE SAME OBJECT AS THE US TERM IN CQ4. The locked prior quotes DFII10 (a fitted par TIPS yield) at 2.60%; nominal-minus-breakeven differs from it by indexation-lag, carry and seasonality effects of ~5bp. A minor identity that does not close exactly, but it matters that the panel's anchor and the resolution formula are different series.
FERMI AT TODAY'S LEVELS. G7-internal 2025 PPP GDP shares: US 51.5%, Japan 11.7%, Germany 10.5%, UK 7.9%, France 7.6%, Italy 6.2%, Canada 4.6%. Plugging plausible 2032-36 member averages (US 2.6, JP 0.6, DE 1.2, UK 2.0 post-RPI-reform, FR 1.8, IT 2.6, CA 2.2) gives 1.34+0.07+0.13+0.16+0.14+0.16+0.10 ≈ 2.09%. So simply freezing the current configuration yields ~2.1%, with Japan the only material drag.
STRUCTURE. Up: 2A's +1.0pp worsening in global (r-g); gross public debt >100% of GDP by 2029 (US ~142%, China ~127% by 2031); net interest 2%->3% of GDP; P95 Debt-at-Risk 117% (+2.4pp under a 20% AI equity shock); eroding sovereign convenience yields; levered basis-trade absorption replacing price-insensitive official demand; retiree dissaving shrinking the saver pool while AI capex and grid buildout bid for it. Down: post-bust excess capacity, BIS Box C labour-income demand shortfall, flight-to-quality episodes inside the window, and the possibility of explicit financial repression (which would compress the measured real yield while the fiscal problem worsens — a regime where CQ4 prints LOW precisely because the stress is severe).
IMPORTANT CROSS-REFERENCE TRAP: the IMF's (r-g) uses the EFFECTIVE interest rate on the outstanding debt stock — a backward-looking weighted average coupon — which lags the 10y marginal real yield by 100-150bp during a rate-rise phase because of the maturity roll. A reader who equates CQ4 with the IMF's r in 2A will double-count. P50 = 2.00%; P10 = 1.00% (secular-stagnation/repression state); P90 = 3.10% (term-premium/fiscal-dominance state), with the measure's own upward biases (2) and (3) keeping the distribution right-of-centre relative to a true ex-ante real rate.
wave1.cq5_reasoning:
RESOLUTION MECHANICS. Conjunct A: ICE BofA MOVE Index — yield-curve-weighted NORMALIZED (basis-point) 1-month implied vol on 2/5/10/30y Treasuries. Decisive artefact: because it is bp-normalized rather than log/relative, the LEVEL scales with the yield level. MOVE averaged ~60 in 2017-19 at ~2% yields, ~120-130 in 2022-23, ~100-110 in 2024, ~85-90 in 2025. At 4-5% nominal yields the vol-neutral level of MOVE is ~90-110, not ~60 — so a 105 hurdle is closer to "rates stay where they are and nothing calms down" than to "a decade of crisis". Direction: materially UP on conjunct A versus a naive reading of 105 as a stress threshold (+8pp). Counter-risk: ICE has revised MOVE's constituent/weighting conventions before; a methodology change, re-basing or discontinuation inside a 10-year window is a real annul/ambiguity risk, call it 10-15%, and it is one-way against a clean YES.
Conjunct A marginal: starting ~85-95, needs a 10-year average >=105, i.e. roughly 2022-23 conditions half the time. With 2A's fiscal regime (Debt-at-Risk, eroding convenience yields, basis-trade absorption, QT/issuance-duration risk) and the bp-normalization tailwind: 42%.
Conjunct B, two sub-mechanics. (i) MSCI World >=25% peak-to-trough. Index choices worth >3pp each: USD vs local currency (a dollar rally in the drawdown deepens the USD fall 5-10pp — UP on YES; the index is conventionally read in USD); price index vs net-return (price is deeper by ~1-2pp of accumulated dividends — UP); daily close vs intraday (closing basis is 1-3pp SHALLOWER — DOWN, and the resolver will almost certainly use closes). Structural: MSCI World is now ~72-75% US with top-10 ~25% of float, heavily the AI complex — the index's own concentration makes a 25% drawdown conditional on an AI repricing much likelier than a diversified reading implies (+8-12pp). Reference class: >=25% MSCI World peak-to-trough drawdowns since 1970 — 1973-74, 1980-82, 1987, 2000-02, 2007-09, 2020, 2022 (USD price basis) = ~7 in 55 years, ~0.13/yr, so ~75% for at least one in 10 years; lifted to ~85% by the $1.4T circular vendor/cloud/chip commitments on ~$300B equity and ~$650B debt and the 66% AI-Q4 prior.
(ii) THE YIELD CONDITION IS LOOSER THAN IT READS. "FAIL to fall by >=50bps (or rise by >=25bps)" — rising >=25bp is a strict SUBSET of failing to fall >=50bp, so the OR adds nothing and the operative test is simply "G7 GDP-weighted 10y nominal does not fall 50bp during the drawdown window". Anything from -49bp upward qualifies. A naive forecaster scans history for "equities crashed AND yields rose" and finds only 1973-74 and 2022; the actual test also admits every muted-bond-rally episode. Worth +5-8pp. Second ambiguity: "during the equity drawdown window" is undefined — peak-date-to-trough-date change (the natural reading) versus any-point-within-window. On the loose within-window reading, long drawdowns (2000-02, 24 months) almost always contain a >=50bp fall somewhere, which flips 1987 and 2000-02 to NO; on the peak-to-trough reading the condition is easier. I weight 70/30 toward endpoint-to-endpoint.
JOIN. P(yield condition | a >=25% drawdown) historically ~2 of 7 cleanly = 29%, lifted to ~45-50% because the 2A plumbing (convenience-yield erosion, levered basis-trade absorption, supply-driven term premium) makes the 2020-style flight-to-quality less reliable, and because 10 years affords multiple independent attempts. P(B) ≈ 0.85 x 0.50 ≈ 0.43. Correlation with A is strongly positive — both conjuncts ARE the fiscal-dominance/rate-volatility regime, so P(A|B) ≈ 0.67 rather than 0.42. Joint = 0.43 x 0.67 ≈ 0.29, less a ~2pp haircut for MOVE index-continuity/annul risk. ANSWER 27.
wave1.cq6_reasoning:
LOCK CONFIRMED AND AUDITED. The lexical priority (A if growth>=2.6; else C if core>=2.7 AND growth<2.0; else D if growth<1.7 AND core<2.0; else B) is well-formed and exhaustive, and I apply it exactly. Two audit findings about the lock itself.
FINDING 1 — WINDOW MISMATCH BETWEEN CQ2 AND THE C TRIGGER. CQ2's inflation conjunct is a 2027-2036 ten-year average; the lock's C trigger is GDP-weighted OECD-38 core over 2032-2036 only. My inflation path is explicitly front-loaded (2027-30 ~2.8% on tariff pass-through, zonal electricity costs, shelter and care scarcity; 2031-36 ~2.35% on capex digestion, J/K/M automation, Chinese overcapacity export deflation and the BIS Box C labour-income demand drag). So my 62% on "2027-36 core >=2.50%" implies only ~24% on "2032-36 core >=2.70%". A naive reader would map my CQ2 straight onto C and over-weight it by 10-15pp. This is the single most important consistency statement I can make.
FINDING 2 — THE EM-OECD INFLATION FLOOR SUPPRESSES REGIME D. D requires 2032-36 OECD-38 core BELOW 2.0% on a GDP-weighted basis that INCLUDES Turkey, Mexico, Chile, Colombia and Costa Rica. Those members put a floor of roughly +0.30pp (Turkey alone ~0.25-0.35pp at 2025 PPP weights) under the aggregate, so a sub-2.0% print requires G7 core at ~1.6-1.7% — a deeper Japanification than the narrative "D" implies. A naive reader imagining post-bust Japanification assigns D 20-25%; the index construction moves ~5pp of that mass into B. Direction: D down, B up.
CONSTRUCTION FROM MY OWN CQ3/CQ2.
A: P(growth >= 2.6) from my CQ3 (P50 1.8, P90 2.7) ≈ 12%. Both legs must beat: OECD-38 ~1.1-1.3 and China ~2.6 produce 1.73; A needs roughly OECD 1.8+ and China 3.5+, i.e. the AI-Q1/AI-Q6 Transformative Breakout tail (16.2% standalone) AND a Chinese consumption rebalancing. 12.
C: P(growth<2.0) ≈ 0.60 given P50 1.8. P(2032-36 core >= 2.70 | growth<2.0) ≈ 0.28 — above the unconditional 0.24 because the bottleneck channel (grid, construction trades, care wages) is the shared cause of both low growth and high core; capped below by the audited fact that the data-centre electricity shock lands in the ENERGY exclusion, not in core, and that the +635 TWh grid build is a ~20% capex increment rather than a regime-breaking one, so it cannot by itself produce a 2.7% core aggregate. 0.60 x 0.28 = 17%.
D: P(growth<1.7) ≈ 0.44. P(core<2.0 | growth<1.7) ≈ 0.34 after the EM-OECD floor haircut (would be ~0.42 on a G7-only basket). 0.44 x 0.34 = 15%. No overlap with C (core>=2.7 excluded) or A (growth<1.7).
B: residual = 100 - 12 - 17 - 15 = 56.
RESIDUAL-B ABSORPTION QUANTIFIED, as my lens requires. Of the 56, roughly 16pp sits in cells a naive reader would have assigned elsewhere: (i) the low-growth/moderate-inflation leftover, growth<1.7 with core 2.0-2.69 — 0.44 x 0.28 ≈ 12pp, which reads as "stagnation" and would naively go to D; (ii) growth 2.0-2.5 with core >=2.7 — ~4pp, which reads as "stagflation" and would naively go to C. Only ~40pp of my B is the literal "1.7-2.5% growth barbell" a reader pictures. So B is favoured by my central path AND inflated by the catch-all; both effects are real and I report them separately rather than netting them.
CONSISTENCY CHECK PERFORMED: CQ3 P50 = 1.8% < 2.6%, so A is confined to upper-tail mass and is set at 12, not at the regime's narrative appeal; CQ2 = 39 is a JOINT (OECD core >=2.50 over 2027-36 at 62% x China <1.50 at 72% x rho adjustment) and its OECD leg is a different window from the C trigger, so C is built from P(2032-36 core >=2.70 | growth<2.0) = 0.28 and NOT from 0.62; D is built from P(growth<1.7)=0.44 x 0.34; residual B = 56. Sums to exactly 100.

hypothesis_critique.a: "SMOOTHLY" carries the failure, and a quantity identity carries it further. Measurement view: the flows do not match in size or in classification. OECD J+K+M employment is ~12-15% of total employment and AI's near-term displacement is concentrated in its junior tail, so even a severe compression frees a few million workers against elder-care vacancy needs an order of magnitude larger over the same period. The freed workers are 35-55, credentialed in ISIC J/K/M, located in metros, and would take a 40-60% hourly pay cut; care work is licensure-gated (RN/LPN/care certificates, 1-3 years), non-tradable, and physically located where the old people are. Observed occupational transition matrices put mid-career cross-sector moves of this specific type in the low single digits annually. Also a resolution point: if the transition DOES happen, it shows up as exactly the composition artefact that defeats CQ1 — low-wage entrants pulling the Q median down. So the plank is self-undermining on the only series that would evidence it. 7.
hypothesis_critique.b: TWO words fail: "BLOCKS" and "SEVERELY". The scope lock itself distinguishes VIRTUAL services exports from PHYSICAL labour migration, and AI touches only the first. For the Philippines the physical leg is the larger remittance channel (nurses, caregivers, seafarers, domestic workers; remittances ~$38-40B) and OECD+China aging is a demand PULL for it — the Philippines is a demographic beneficiary on that leg even as IT-BPM (~$38B revenue, ~1.7M workers, voice and back-office heaviest) is genuinely exposed. India's ~$200B+ IT services export base is exposed on price per seat but Indian firms also SELL AI integration, so the effect is repricing and mix-shift, not blockage. "Blocks" is categorically wrong; "severely" over-claims for India and mis-locates the harm for the Philippines. Measurement caveat on any resolution: remittances are BOP-compiled with large informal-channel gaps, and "IT-BPM revenue" is NASSCOM/IBPAP industry self-reporting with no published confidence interval or sampling frame — so even a true severe hit would be hard to date and size. 22.
hypothesis_critique.c: "FALLS" carries the failure, and it is ambiguous in three ways the plank never resolves: falls in RATE or in LEVEL; falls TO target or BELOW it; falls in which index. Directionally this plank IS my effort's central path — a 2026-2030 impulse (tariff and fragmentation pass-through, zonal electricity costs, shelter, care wage scarcity) giving way to 2031-36 disinflation (capex digestion and post-bust excess capacity, J/K/M automation, Chinese overcapacity export deflation, BIS Box C labour-income demand drag) — which is why this is the plank I score highest. Where it still fails: the magnitude of the fall is much smaller than the narrative implies, because (i) AI's price deflation lands in producer-heavy J/K/M that barely enter consumer baskets, (ii) shelter at ~33% of US core and care services at ~7-9% keep a 2.3-2.6% floor, and (iii) the OECD-38 GDP-weighted aggregate carries a ~+0.30pp EM-OECD floor. "Falls" to ~2.3-2.4%, not to 1.5%. 61.
hypothesis_critique.d: "EVENTUALLY" is the fatal word and it is a resolution dodge: it places the claim outside the Dec 31 2036 horizon and makes the plank unfalsifiable by the resolution date, which in a scored ensemble must count against it. "WINS" is the second failure — undefined over aggregate versus per-capita versus measured-versus-true GDP, and silent on distribution (the BIS Box C point is that output can grow while labour income lags, so "growth wins" and "demand fails" are simultaneously satisfiable). "EXPONENTIAL" is a claim about compute and capability, not about measured output: the binding quantity is the measured TFP lift, and 2B puts only 23.0% on >=+0.50pp/yr for 2032-36 with 36.5% on a Hulten-ceiling outcome below +0.15pp. Against a 2A demographic drag of -1.1pp/yr globally and -2.7pp in China, a +0.30pp expected lift does not outrun population decline inside this horizon — my CQ3 P50 of 1.8% is the arithmetic statement of that. As stated and scored at 2036: 18.

key_drivers: WINDOW ASYMMETRY BETWEEN THE INFLATION TESTS. CQ2 scores a front-loaded 2027-2036 average (cleared largely by 2027-30 plus the EM-OECD floor) while the CQ6-C trigger scores 2032-2036 only. Same inflation path, 62% on one and ~24% on the other. This single accounting distinction moves ~12pp of CQ6 mass out of C and into B.

CORE EXCLUDES ENERGY, SO THE MOST AI-SPECIFIC INFLATION CHANNEL IS UNMEASURED. The +635 TWh data-centre build (AI-Q3 P50 ~1,000 vs 365 TWh in 2024) and its zonal electricity price spikes land in HEADLINE, not in the core CPI/PCE aggregate CQ2 and CQ6 resolve on; it enters core only as second-round business cost, ~+0.1-0.2pp. Caps the stagflation regime.

AI'S DEFLATION IS IN PRODUCER PRICES, NOT CONSUMER BASKETS. ISIC J, K, M are B2B-heavy; consumer-facing AI-deflatables (telecom ~1.5-2%, media ~1%, education ~2.5%, household professional services <1%) total under 8% of core, so even total J/K/M price collapse moves core by -0.2 to -0.4pp. Shelter (~33% of US core) and care services (~7-9%) hold a 2.3-2.6% floor. Keeps the level sticky while the SKEW is violent.

TWO-SIDED COMPOSITION BIAS DESTROYS CQ1's WAGE CONJUNCT. Low-wage entrant surge into ISIC Q (and F) pulls those MEDIANS down 2-5pp while incumbents get raises; AI truncating the bottom of the J/K/M distribution pushes that median UP 3-6pp with no raises at all. Both run against the +10.0pp gap, consuming 6-10pp of a 10pp threshold. Compounded by the fact that quadrennial Eurostat SES means the 2034 vintage publishes after resolution.

THE EM-OECD INFLATION FLOOR. Turkey, Mexico, Chile, Colombia and Costa Rica inside a GDP-weighted OECD-38 core put ~+0.30pp under the aggregate (Turkey alone 0.25-0.35pp at 2025 PPP weights). Raises P(core>=2.50) and suppresses regime D, which requires G7 core at ~1.6-1.7% rather than the ~1.9% a naive reader pictures.

MEASURE-SPECIFIC UPWARD BIAS IN THE CQ4 REAL YIELD, PLUS A UK STEP BREAK. Nominal-minus-breakeven embeds inflation-risk and TIPS-liquidity premia (+10-40bp over a true ex-ante real rate) exactly in the high-uncertainty states being forecast; the 2030 RPI-to-CPIH alignment mechanically lifts the UK leg 0.6-1.0pp with no change in the world; Canada has no 10y linker or liquid inflation swap at all, so ~5% of G7 GDP needs an unspecified proxy.

wave1.coupling_tension:
THREE TENSIONS, EACH AN ACCOUNTING FINDING, WITH DIRECTIONS.
(1) AI-Q3 (data-centre TWh) and AI-Q4 (impairments) are jointly inconsistent at their stated values once demographics are endogenous. AI-Q3's P50 of ~1,000 TWh implies ~130-160 GW of net firm capacity plus transmission, ~$1.3-2.0T of OECD+China grid and generation capex over 12 years, i.e. a ~20% increment on current annual grid/generation spend. In dollars that is absorbable; in LABOUR it is not independent of 2A. The same electricians, linemen, welders and HV technicians are claimed simultaneously by the grid build, housing, and the care-sector physical build-out (hospitals, long-term-care capacity), out of a trades pool that 2A's old-age ratio moving from ~31% to ~39-41% is actively shrinking. So either the TWh is delivered at much higher construction and electricity prices — which raises my CQ2 OECD leg and pushes CQ6 mass toward C, AND raises the impairment probability further — or the TWh under-delivers, which lowers the AI-Q1 TFP lift and pushes mass toward D. Direction of the correction: AI-Q4 should be ABOVE 66.0% once demographics are endogenous (I would put it ~72%), AI-Q3's P50 should be BELOW 998 TWh (~900), and AI-Q3's P10-P90 should be WIDER, because the dominant variance source becomes physical trades and interconnection lead times rather than chip supply.
(2) AI-Q5 (38.2%) is marginally inconsistent with my own effort's premise through a nominal-denominator identity, and in the direction of being TOO HIGH. AI-Q5 asks whether labour compensation share of ISIC J+K+M sectoral GVA falls >=3.5pp. That share is (wage x headcount) / NOMINAL sectoral GVA. My effort's central mechanism is that AI DEFLATES J/K/M output prices. Falling output prices shrink the DENOMINATOR, which mechanically supports the compensation share even as headcount falls — the standard result that labour-share declines require output prices to hold up while labour input falls. Add the endogenous-demographics effect: labour scarcity raises the wage of the retained senior J/K/M workers, supporting the numerator. Both work against the 3.5pp fall. Direction: AI-Q5 should fall to ~30% once demographics are endogenous and the price channel is taken seriously. Note this is the ONE place where my relative-price-skew effort and the labour-share question point opposite ways from the naive reading, and the resolution would also be vintage-sensitive: nominal GVA by ISIC section is revised in benchmark national-accounts years by more than 3.5pp in some members, so the threshold is near the noise floor of the series.
(3) SECTION 2A's OWN ARITHMETIC DOES NOT CLOSE ON A COMMON BASIS, though it can be reconciled. The -1.1pp/yr figure is GLOBAL AGGREGATE GDP over 2025-2050 (with China at -2.7pp) and is stated as NET of the +0.4pp healthy-aging offset ("adds ~+0.4 pp/yr ... YET aging still slows ... by ~-1.1 pp/yr"), so the gross drag is ~-1.5pp and the +0.4pp must NOT be added back. The OECD 1.0% -> 0.6% figure is PER CAPITA, OECD-only, over 2025-2036, i.e. -0.4pp. These are different geographies, different horizons and different per-capita-versus-aggregate bases; they reconcile only if the -1.1pp is read as inclusive of labour-INPUT decline (OECD -0.4pp productivity plus ~-0.4 to -0.5pp labour-force growth gives an OECD aggregate drag of ~-0.8 to -0.9pp, which with China's -2.7pp weighted in and a near-zero India/Africa drag yields the global -1.1pp). Stated as written, the identity does not close; read that way, it does. SEPARATELY, 2A's "+1.0pp worsening in global (r-g)" cannot be mapped onto CQ4: the IMF's r is the EFFECTIVE interest rate on the outstanding debt stock, a backward-looking average coupon, which lags the 10y marginal real yield by 100-150bp during a rate-rise phase because of the roll-over structure. Any panelist who anchors CQ4 to 2A's (r-g) will over-state it by roughly that lag.

wave2.lens_self_description: Adversarial red-team falsifier on the inflation-path/relative-price-skew effort: I attacked the Wave-1 panel's shared premise that core-basket weight arithmetic caps the inflation LEVEL near 2.0-2.1%, and I forbade myself from using the weighted-sum-of-exogenous-component-rates identity as if it constrained the aggregate, from treating the 2% nominal anchor as exogenous, and from splitting the difference with Wave 1 anywhere I had an argument.
wave2.cq1_reasoning:
SHARED WAVE-1 ERROR I EXPLOIT: all three computed the F+Q minus J+K+M REAL median differential inside their own ~2.0-2.1% core world, where a nominal cognitive wage freeze still prints roughly 0% real. At my core path (front half ~3.1%, back half ~2.6%, 10yr ~2.78%) the arithmetic changes qualitatively: a J+K+M nominal median path of +2.0%/yr -- entirely plausible under the 2B panel's own 47.2% "Jagged Diffusion & Hyperscaler Rent Concentration" regime, where the AI surplus accrues to capital and not to surviving cognitive labour -- is -0.8%/yr REAL, i.e. -8.8 pp cumulative. F+Q at +3.6% nominal is +0.8% real, +9.2 pp. Differential 18 pp, clearing the 10.0 pp bar with room for the composition artefacts Wave 1 correctly identified. Wave 1 never coupled the differential to its own price level; that is conjunction neglect in reverse -- they discounted the wage conjunct on composition grounds while assuming away the deflator that does most of the work.
CONJUNCT 2 MARGINAL = 0.34. I accept both composition cuts (entrant dilution drags the measured F+Q median 2-5 pp; truncating the bottom of the J+K+M distribution lifts that median 3-6 pp, together consuming 6-10 pp of a 10 pp threshold) but reject Panelist 2's monopsony-suppression arrow as the dominant care-wage mechanism -- see key drivers: at a 39-41% old-age ratio the elderly ARE the median voter, and administered care prices are set by that electorate, not against it. Then multiply by ~0.85 for resolution hazard: there is no published OECD-38 sectoral real median hourly series, Eurostat SES is quadrennial with the 2034 vintage landing after resolution, and a strict resolver stitching ASHE/OES/BSWS defaults NO on ambiguity. 0.40 x 0.85 = 0.34.
CONJUNCT 1 MARGINAL (OECD-38 harmonized U <= 5.5% avg 2032-2036) = 0.52. Shrinking working-age denominator is near-deterministic and mechanically suppresses the rate (~-0.15 pp), rising 65+ and 55-74 participation dilutes further, and AI-displaced workers who exit are recorded as participation decline not unemployment. Against: the locked 66% AI-Q4 capex bust lands 2031-2033, inside the window. My distinguishing addition: a hot-nominal-demand regime (my CQ2 world) runs LOW unemployment -- high nominal GDP growth is the historical friend of the measured unemployment rate -- which is why I sit at 0.52 rather than Wave 1's 0.45-0.50.
CORRELATION: strongly positive, rho ~ +0.35, since in my world both conjuncts are readings of one state (tight labour + negative real cognitive wages + strong nominal demand). P(B|A) = 0.34 x 1.4 = 0.476, capped at 0.42 because the composition wedge is cycle-independent. JOINT = 0.52 x 0.42 = 0.218 -> 21. Still a real conjunction discount (21 vs a 0.52/0.34 naive-independent 18 lifted by correlation), but above Panelists 1 and 3 for a mechanism neither used.
wave2.cq2_reasoning:
THIS IS WHERE WAVE 1 IS WRONG AND I AM FAR FROM THEM (36/18/39; OECD-leg marginals 0.52/0.30/0.62).
THE SINGLE STRONGEST SHARED ASSUMPTION, ATTACKED: all three write the core aggregate as a weighted sum of EXOGENOUS sectoral rates and conclude the level is capped because electricity is excluded from core by construction and consumer-facing AI-deflatables are only 3-8% of the basket. The identity is true and constrains nothing. Three failures. (i) DOWNWARD NOMINAL RIGIDITY: all three plug core goods at 0.3-0.5% and communication/digital at -1.0%. Those are hyper-globalization numbers (US core goods averaged ~0% 1995-2019 under maximum China supply, zero tariffs, no mineral constraint). In a tariff/fragmentation/reshoring/copper-constrained decade, sectors that "want" to deflate print 0 to +1.5% instead, because nominal wages and prices do not fall -- so a large relative-price skew raises the MEAN. (ii) PASS-THROUGH IN CONCENTRATED SECTORS: Panelist 2 applies a 0.45 cost-to-price pass-through to professional/financial services while simultaneously describing them as concentrated; rent concentration is a price-RAISING mechanism. The 2B panel's own modal regime (47.2%) is literally named hyperscaler rent concentration. You cannot hold both. (iii) ENDOGENOUS ANCHOR: all three assert gross debt >100% of GDP by 2029, net interest 2->3% of GDP, P95 Debt-at-Risk 117%, +1.0 pp worse (r-g), and then quietly assume the 2% target survives the window and the back half reverts. No OECD polity with a 40% old-age ratio has delivered the primary consolidation that requires. The reference class for high-debt aging democracies is partial inflation of the debt: a de facto 3% anchor.
MY OECD-38 GDP-WEIGHTED CORE FERMI, weights carried explicitly: shelter/OOH 0.22 (raised from Panelist 2's 0.18 for the US weight and for prospective HICP owner-occupied-housing inclusion, which Panelist 3 correctly flags as mechanically +0.1-0.3 pp with no change in the world) @ 3.6% = 0.79; health + social care services 0.11 @ 4.2% = 0.46; other labour-intensive services 0.28 @ 3.1% = 0.87; household-consumed financial/professional 0.09 @ 2.0% = 0.18; core goods 0.25 @ 1.2% = 0.30; communication/digital 0.05 @ -0.3% = -0.02. Sum = 2.58%. Add +0.20 pp for the EM-OECD excess (Turkey, Mexico, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica inside a GDP-weighted OECD-38; Panelist 3's audited floor is +0.30, haircut to avoid double counting). TOTAL ~2.78%, path 2027-30 ~3.1% and 2031-36 ~2.6%. The 2.50% hurdle is cleared by 0.28 pp. With ~0.45 pp sd on a ten-year average: CONJUNCT A MARGINAL = 0.70.
CHINA CONJUNCT, red-teamed in the opposite direction from Wave 1 (who used 0.70/0.70/0.72 by anchoring on the Japan 1995-2025 analogue -- a reference class with no wage-floor policy, no hukou/rural-pension expansion, and no pork cycle): ten years is long and the policy reaction function is active. Against sub-1.5%: explicit anti-involution capacity discipline; a -1%/yr working-age contraction that is ultimately a SUPPLY contraction; food at ~18-20% of the basket with 1-2 pork cycles per decade and a single +5% food year adding ~0.5 pp to the decade average; disorderly RMB depreciation importing food/energy; NBS basket rebases in 2026 and 2031 shifting weight toward services, which lifts prints; and NBS's mild institutional reluctance to publish deflation. For: ~0.0-0.2% starting run rate, a permanent -55/-60% property adjustment with residence ~18-20% of CPI, household income share stuck ~44% of GDP, and pension subsidies already ~10.1% of fiscal expenditure capping transfer-financed rebalancing. CONJUNCT B MARGINAL = 0.63, deliberately below all three Wave-1 panelists.
CORRELATION: Wave 1 assumed mildly NEGATIVE via Chinese goods deflation entering OECD core goods. I assume mildly POSITIVE, rho ~ +0.10: the tariff/fragmentation wall is precisely the mechanism that severs that transmission (it is why my core-goods term is 1.2% and not 0.4%), and both legs are readings of one asymmetry -- OECD builds physical capacity into labour scarcity with a drifting anchor while China has excess capacity and deficient demand. P(B|A) = 0.63 x 1.08 = 0.68. JOINT = 0.70 x 0.68 = 0.476 -> 47.
wave2.cq3_reasoning:
Wave 1 converged on 1.6-1.85 and all three built it the same way: OECD per-capita 0.6% (locked) + ~0.2% population + a small AI term, times ~0.65, plus China at 2.6-2.9% times ~0.35. Two attacks.
(1) THE CHINA LEG IS A MEASURED OBJECT WITH A POLICY FLOOR. Panelist 3 established the correct principle -- the resolver uses NBS, so forecast the measured number and do not shade for the widely-argued 0.5-2 pp overstatement -- and then declined to apply it, using 2.6%. NBS real growth has met its "around" target every year by construction. A 2032-2036 NBS print of 3.3% with a -1%/yr workforce is a political object before it is an economic one. I use 3.3%.
(2) BAUMOL-AT-ZERO IS A DEFLATOR CONVENTION, NOT AN ECONOMIC FACT, AND IT CUTS BOTH WAYS. Panelist 2's -0.15 to -0.20 pp Baumol drag plus a care-rationing GDP leak is his most load-bearing claim and it rests on measured care output being real output. Public health and social-care output is deflated largely by input costs with essentially no quality adjustment, so in my higher-care-inflation world measured real care output is biased DOWN and his drag is partly a measurement artefact already embedded in the locked 0.6%/yr per-capita baseline -- counting it again double-counts. Separately, Wave 1 under-uses the DRAG/PULL asymmetry correction: aging is an automation demand-pull that raises capital deepening, and measured TFP rises mechanically when hours contract faster than output.
MY FERMI: OECD-38 leg = 0.6% per capita + 0.25% population + 0.30 pp net AI/automation-pull (0.45 gross pull less 0.15 for genuine non-automatable ADL-hour and interconnection bottlenecks) = 1.15%. China leg 3.3% measured. Constant-2025-PPP weights ~0.64 OECD / 0.36 China: 0.64(1.15) + 0.36(3.3) = 0.74 + 1.19 = 1.92%. P50 = 1.95%.
DISPERSION: P10 1.00% -- the 66%-likely capex bust lands inside the window, China steps to ~2.0%, BIS Box C labour-income demand deficit bites. P90 3.00% -- no bust, the 16.2% Transformative Breakout tail, China printing 4.2%. My right tail is fatter than all three Wave-1 panelists because (i) the China measurement floor, (ii) I reject the size of the care-rationing leak, (iii) a strong-nominal-demand regime does not produce the left-skewed cap Panelist 2's weakest-link model imposes. Reference class used only as a cross-check and overridden: no 5-year window in 65 years averaged below ~2.3%, and I sit well below that because the headcount is not forecastable away -- but Wave 1 took that override further than the arithmetic licenses.
wave2.cq4_reasoning:
Wave 1 landed P50 at 1.80 / 1.80 / 2.00, i.e. essentially at the current GDP-weighted level of ~1.8-2.1%, by letting r* arrows and term-premium arrows cancel. That is ANCHORING ON THE STARTING LEVEL, and Panelist 1 documented the base rate that refutes it himself: consecutive G7 decade changes were +6.0, -1.0, -2.0, -1.6, -0.1 pp, mean absolute change ~2.1 pp, with only 2 of 5 transitions inside +/-100 bp. A ~40% modal cell was then treated as a P50 by all three.
THE DECISIVE STRUCTURAL ERROR: all three put their left tail on FINANCIAL REPRESSION (P10 0.55 / 0.80 / 1.00). Repression and inflation are SUBSTITUTE institutional responses to one fiscal arithmetic, not complements. If the anchor drifts to ~3% -- my CQ2 world -- the debt is partially inflated away and explicit yield caps are politically unnecessary, so the real yield clears in the market. Conceding drift therefore THINS the left tail rather than fattening it. Wave 1 wants the high-inflation front half and the repression tail simultaneously.
THE RIGHT TAIL IS ALSO UNDERWEIGHTED, for the same reason: the 1980-85 reference class shows that once the anchor is questioned, REAL yields go UP, not down, because credibility must be re-earned -- G7 real yields averaged +4.5-5% in that decade. Add the locked plumbing: gross debt >100% of GDP by 2029 (142% US, 127% China by 2031), net interest 2->3% of GDP, P95 Debt-at-Risk 117% (+2.4 pp under a 20% AI equity shock), eroding sovereign convenience yields, marginal duration absorbed by levered basis trades that de-risk procyclically rather than by price-insensitive real money, shrinking DB plans turning from duration buyers into net sellers, and BoJ normalization lifting the JGB real yield. Offsetting down: post-bust investment collapse 2032-2034 (cyclical, inside the window) and retiree dissaving's ambiguous net on r*.
MEASURE AUDIT ACCEPTED BUT NOT LOAD-BEARING: nominal-minus-breakeven is not a clean ex-ante real rate (inflation risk premium pushes the measure down, TIPS liquidity premium pushes it up; net contested, Panelist 3 puts it +10-40 bp high); the 2030 RPI-to-CPIH alignment mechanically lifts the UK leg 0.6-1.0 pp, ~+5-8 bp on the aggregate; Canada has no 10y linker or liquid CAD inflation swap, so ~5% of G7 GDP needs an unspecified proxy. Also accepted: 2A's +1.0 pp (r-g) uses the EFFECTIVE rate on the outstanding stock and lags the 10y marginal by 100-150 bp in a rate-rise phase -- anchoring CQ4 to it over-states.
MY MEMBER PATH, G7 2025-PPP weights (US 0.515, JP 0.117, DE 0.105, UK 0.079, FR 0.076, IT 0.062, CA 0.046): US 2.90, JP 1.10, DE 1.50, UK 2.40 (post-RPI-reform), FR 2.10, IT 3.10, CA 2.50 -> 1.49 + 0.13 + 0.16 + 0.19 + 0.16 + 0.19 + 0.12 = 2.44; shaded to P50 2.35 for the 2032-2034 post-bust r* depression. P10 1.25 (genuine post-bust disinflation with flight to quality, or a repression branch I give much less weight than Wave 1). P90 3.60 (Debt-at-Risk tail realizes, term premium spirals, anchor-repair real yields). Distribution right-skewed, not bimodal-symmetric.
wave2.cq5_reasoning:
I adopt Panelist 3's best piece of analysis and extend it past where he stopped, and I attack Panelist 2's back-half assumption.
CONJUNCT A (MOVE 10yr average >= 105 over 2027-2036) = 0.55. MOVE is basis-point-NORMALIZED, not log/relative, so its level scales with the yield level: ~60 in 2017-19 at ~2% yields, 120-130 in 2022-23, and a vol-neutral level of roughly 95-115 at 4-5% nominals. A 105 hurdle is therefore not a stress threshold -- it is close to "yields stay here and nothing calms down." Panelist 3 got this and still only reached 0.42; Panelist 2 reached 0.45 by assuming the BACK half delivers a credible low-inflation equilibrium compressing vol to 75-90. That assumption is exactly the one my lens destroys: at a drifted ~2.6-3.1% back-half core with an unresolved debt path, the belief dispersion between repression and term-premium spiral persists through 2036 rather than collapsing. Front half 105-130, back half 95-115, average ~110. Marginal 0.60 less 0.05 one-way for MOVE methodology/re-basing/discontinuation annul risk over a ten-year window = 0.55.
CONJUNCT B = 0.47. Sub-mechanic (i): P(at least one >= 25% MSCI World peak-to-trough drawdown in 10 years) = 0.85. Base rate ~7 episodes in 55 years gives ~0.75; lifted by the index now being ~72-75% US with top-10 ~25% of float and heavily the AI complex, the ~$1.4T circular vendor/cloud/chip commitments on ~$300B equity and ~$650B debt, and the locked 66% AI-Q4 prior. Sub-mechanic (ii): Panelist 3's reading is correct and decisive -- "rise >= 25 bps" is a strict SUBSET of "fail to fall >= 50 bps", so the OR clause is vacuous and the operative test is merely that G7 GDP-weighted 10y nominals do not rally 50 bp during the window; anything from -49 bp upward qualifies. Naive forecasters scan for "stocks crashed AND yields rose" (1973-74, 2022 only) and badly under-count, because every muted-rally episode also qualifies. P(no 50 bp rally | drawdown) = 0.55 in my regime, above all three Wave-1 panelists (0.33/0.42/0.50): with core at 2.6-3.1% the policy cut is slow and small, the sovereign market is itself a candidate stress source, convenience yields are eroding, and the marginal duration holder is a levered basis trade that de-risks into the drawdown. 0.85 x 0.55 = 0.47.
CORRELATION: strongly positive -- these are two readings of one institutional state, not two draws. P(A|B) = 0.78 rather than the unconditional 0.55. wave2.cq6_reasoning:
Lexical lock applied mechanically to MY OWN CQ3 and MY OWN GDP-weighted OECD-38 core over 2032-2036 ONLY.
INPUT DISTRIBUTIONS. CQ3: P10 1.00 / P50 1.95 / P90 3.00, implied sigma ~0.80 pp. Core 2032-2036: central 2.60% (my 10yr average is 2.78% with a front half of ~3.1% and a back half of ~2.6%), sd ~0.55 pp. Hence P(core_32-36 >= 2.7%) = 1 - Phi(0.18) = 0.43; P(2.0 <= core < 2.7) = 0.43; P(core < 2.0%) = Phi(-1.09) = 0.14. Growth: P(>= 2.6%) = 1 - Phi(0.81) = 0.21; P(< 2.0%) = Phi(0.06) = 0.525; P(< 1.7%) = Phi(-0.31) = 0.38.
STEP 1, A = P(growth >= 2.6%) = 0.21 -> 20. This is my largest single departure from Wave 1 (12/11/12) and it comes entirely from my CQ3, not from narrative appeal: the measured-NBS China floor at 3.3% plus aging-as-capital-deepening. LOCK ARTEFACT I AM OBLIGED TO REPORT: the lexical rule assigns A on growth alone, so a nominal-reflation cell with 2.7% growth and 2.9% core lands in "AI-Solvent Broad Productivity Renaissance" despite failing the label's "broad wage gains" and "debt/GDP stabilizes via growth" clauses. Perhaps 5 of my 20 points in A are that cell. I follow the lock as instructed rather than the label.
STEP 2, C = P(core >= 2.7%) x P(growth < 2.0% | core >= 2.7%) = 0.43 x 0.58 = 0.249 -> 25. The conditional is only slightly above the 0.525 unconditional, not the 0.68 Panelist 1 used, because in my world high core is part supply-bottleneck (growth-negative) and part strong nominal demand plus a drifted anchor (growth-neutral to positive). STEP 3, D = P(core < 2.0%) x P(growth < 1.7% | core < 2.0%) = 0.14 x 0.65 = 0.091 -> 9. THIS IS MY SHARPEST DISAGREEMENT WITH WAVE 1 (15/34/15, and Panelist 2 made D his second cell at 34). D requires a GDP-weighted OECD-38 core below 2.0% INCLUDING Turkey, Mexico, Chile, Colombia and Costa Rica -- Panelist 3's audited +0.30 pp EM floor means D needs G7 core at ~1.6-1.7%, a deeper Japanification than the narrative implies, and it must survive tariffs, a trades-constrained grid and housing build, care-wage politics, and a debt path that makes the 2% target itself the adjusting variable. Panelist 2 reached 34 only by pairing a post-bust excess-capacity story with his own coupling finding that the grid UNDER-builds on trades scarcity -- you cannot have both excess electrical capacity and a labour-constrained under-build. Resolving that contradiction toward under-build makes the back half energy- and shelter-INFLATIONARY while still growth-poor, which moves mass from D to C. That single internal contradiction is worth roughly 15 pp of CQ6 mass.
STEP 4, B = residual = 100 - 20 - 25 - 9 = 46. Of that, ~29 pp is the literal 1.7-2.5% barbell and ~17 pp is leftover cells (growth < 1.7% with core 2.0-2.69, and growth 2.0-2.5% with core >= 2.7%). Reported separately rather than netted.
CONSISTENCY CHECK PERFORMED. (i) My CQ3 P50 of 1.95% sits inside B's literal band and B is modal at 46 -- consistent; I do not put most mass on A despite A being 20. (ii) A = 20 equals P(growth >= 2.6%) read off my own CQ3 exactly, cross-checked against my own P90 of 3.00 (P(>=3.00) = 0.10, so P(>=2.6) ~ 0.21 is coherent). hypothesis_critique.a: "SMOOTHLY" carries the failure, and "supply" carries a second one. The mismatch is total on four axes at once -- skill, licensure (6-24 months of credentialing), geography, and a 45-60% wage haircut -- so a displaced paralegal does not become an ADL aide. But the deeper defect is that the only mechanism that WOULD move them is the one the plank's adverb denies: in my 2.8%-core regime the displaced cognitive worker's reservation wage falls in REAL terms year after year until care work clears, and that process is slow, involuntary and politically explosive, i.e. the exact opposite of smooth. Headcount scale also fails: the 11-year white-collar displacement flow is small relative to the 80+ cohort growing 3.7%/yr. 5.
hypothesis_critique.b: "BLOCKS" is false and "SEVERELY" has the sign wrong on the larger channel. The scope lock itself separates cross-border VIRTUAL services exports from PHYSICAL labour migration, and the plank silently merges them. AI compresses one slice of the virtual channel -- voice BPO, first-line support, entry coding -- while raising the productivity and the billable scope of the Indian GCC worker, which is why Indian services exports accelerated through the AI period rather than stalling. It does nothing whatsoever to physical migration, and physical migration is where a 39-41% OECD old-age ratio plus an unfillable care and construction req creates the strongest labour demand pull in the Philippines' and India's history: Filipino nurses and Indian care and construction workers face the best decade on record, with remittances plausibly rising in real terms. The honest statement is a composition shift inside the export mix, not severe suffering. 11.
hypothesis_critique.c: "FALLS" carries the failure, and the plank's implicit destination -- back to the pre-2021 regime -- is what makes it scoreable and wrong. This is the plank all three Wave-1 panelists endorsed at 55-62 because all three built front-loaded paths, and it is the direct target of my lens. My own path does decline (3.1% front half to 2.6% back half), so the SHAPE is right and the plank gets partial credit; the LEVEL is wrong, since on my distribution P(2032-2036 OECD core < 2.0%) is only 0.14. Worse, roughly a quarter of my mass has no decline at all: fiscal dominance compounds, the grid under-builds on trades scarcity so energy and construction costs keep rising into the 2030s, and statutory care-wage settlements land LATE in the window, so the back half can run hotter than the front. A reader scoring this plank as the consensus does is scoring a 2% anchor they have not defended. 38.
hypothesis_critique.d: "EVENTUALLY" makes it unfalsifiable at the Dec 31 2036 horizon and "WINS" is undefined -- growth of aggregate or per-capita, measured or true, against what counterfactual. The plank is not so much wrong as unscoreable as written, and when forced into a scoreable form -- 2032-2036 coupled real growth above the 2015-2024 realized rate -- my own CQ3 P50 of 1.95% FAILS it against ~2.9% for 2015-2019. "Exponential" is also doing illegitimate work: compute scaling is exponential, output is not, because the binding inputs are ADL care hours, interconnection queues and high-voltage trades, and the 2B panel's own mass sits at 47.2% on jagged diffusion, not on breakout. I score it above Panelist 1 and near Panelists 2-3 only because my measured-China floor and my rejection of the care-rationing GDP leak give the growth side more room than Wave 1 allows. 16.

key_drivers: DOWNWARD NOMINAL RIGIDITY CONVERTS THE SKEW INTO THE LEVEL -- the attack on Wave 1's single shared assumption. All three wrote core as a weighted sum of exogenous sectoral rates and plugged core goods at 0.3-0.5% and digital at -1.0%, which are hyper-globalization numbers measured under maximum China supply and zero tariffs. Sectors that 'want' to deflate print 0 to +1.5% instead, because nominal prices and wages do not fall. Core goods at 1.2% rather than 0.4% on a 0.25 weight is worth +0.20 pp on the aggregate by itself and is the difference between a 2.1% and a 2.8% core.

THE NOMINAL ANCHOR IS ENDOGENOUS TO THE LOCKED FISCAL BLOCK, which Wave 1 used as an input to growth and real yields but never to the price level. Gross debt >100% of GDP by 2029, net interest 2->3% of GDP, P95 Debt-at-Risk 117%, +1.0 pp worse (r-g), and a 39-41% old-age-ratio electorate together imply a primary consolidation no aging OECD democracy has delivered. The reference class is partial inflation of the debt: a de facto ~3% target. This is anchoring on the locked priors' FRAMING -- treating 2A as a real-side constraint only.

AGING AS POLITICAL DEMAND-PULL ON ADMINISTERED CARE PRICES, against Panelist 2's monopsony-rationing arrow (his own self-declared most load-bearing claim) and Panelist 1's fiscal-rationing version. Both treat the elderly as passive price-takers at the precise moment a 39-41% old-age ratio makes them the median voter. Care-worker wage floors, sectoral awards and CPI-indexed pensions are the actual observed policy response under fiscal stress, and OECD medical and social-care CPI has outpaced core through every austerity episode. Care at 4.2% on an 0.11 weight, not 3.2%, and the fiscal consequence shows up in CQ4's term premium rather than in suppressed care wages.

WAVE 1'S INTERNAL CONTRADICTION ON THE BACK HALF: Panelist 2 produces the disinflationary 2031-2036 from 'turbines, transformers and datacentre shells arrive into stalled load,' which requires the capacity to HAVE BEEN BUILT, while his own coupling section argues buildable load is -18 to -25% because the electricians, linemen and HV technicians are being drained by aging and bid for by housing and the care-facility build. You cannot have excess electrical capacity and a trades-constrained under-build. Resolving toward under-build makes the back half energy- and shelter-inflationary while still growth-poor: that is regime C, not D, and it is worth roughly 15 pp of CQ6 mass.

REPRESSION AND INFLATION ARE SUBSTITUTES, NOT COMPLEMENTS -- which thins the CQ4 left tail that all three Wave-1 panelists lean on (P10 0.55/0.80/1.00). If the anchor drifts, the debt is partly inflated away and explicit yield caps become politically unnecessary. Conversely the 1980-85 analogue says that once credibility must be re-earned, REAL yields go up, so the right tail fattens. CQ4 P50 2.35 with P10 1.25 and P90 3.60.

MEASURED-NBS CHINA HAS A POLICY FLOOR. Panelist 3 established the right principle -- the resolver uses NBS, so forecast the measured series and do not shade for the 0.5-2 pp overstatement -- and then used 2.6% anyway. A 3.3% NBS print for 2032-2036 with a -1%/yr workforce is a political object before an economic one, and at a ~0.36 PPP weight it carries ~1.19 pp of my 1.95% CQ3 P50 and nearly all of my CQ6-A at 20 versus Wave 1's 11-12.

wave2.coupling_tension:
AI-Q5 IS THE MARGINAL MY LENS BREAKS, AND IT IS BIASED LOW BY ROUGHLY 20 pp -- the opposite of Panelist 3's revision and well beyond Panelist 2's. AI-Q5 asks whether OECD-38 ISIC J+K+M labour compensation share of sectoral GVA falls >= 3.5 pp by 2036; the standalone is 38.2%. Panelist 3 argued it should fall to ~30% because AI DEFLATES J/K/M output prices, shrinking the nominal denominator and mechanically supporting the share. Panelist 2 argued it should rise to ~46-50% because endogenous demographics let the share fall by attrition without replacement. Both reason from the price side in opposite directions and NEITHER coupled the aggregate price level, which is the actual resolving variable: a labour share is a wage bill over NOMINAL GVA. In my coupled world J/K/M nominal GVA grows at roughly 5.5-6%/yr -- a ~2.8% economy-wide deflator plus 2.5-3% real, with the 2B panel's own modal regime (Jagged Diffusion and Hyperscaler RENT CONCENTRATION, 47.2%) meaning the sector captures a RISING markup rather than passing cost savings through at Panelist 2's assumed 0.45. The wage bill meanwhile grows at ~3%: flat-to-falling heads via non-replacement, with nominal wages of +2.0-2.5% that are NEGATIVE in real terms. That is a share declining roughly 2 pp per year of nominal divergence, which clears a 3.5 pp fall over eleven years with enormous room. DIRECTION: AI-Q5 should be ~58-62%, not 38.2% and not Panelist 3's 30%. The exogenous-demographics run cannot see this because it implicitly carries a 2% anchor and a competitive pass-through assumption, and Panelist 3's own deflation-of-the-denominator argument is self-refuting once you grant the rent concentration his effort's own regime weights assert. Note the resolution hazard he correctly flags survives: nominal GVA by ISIC section is revised in benchmark national-accounts years by more than 3.5 pp in some members, so the threshold sits near the series noise floor -- which argues for a wider, not a lower, number.
SECOND TENSION, SAME MECHANISM, OPPOSITE SIGN TO PANELIST 1: AI-Q1 (PPP-weighted TFP lift >= +0.50 pp/yr, 23.0%) is biased slightly HIGH once demographics are endogenous AND the price level is allowed to drift, not low. Panelist 1 argued up (aging as capital-deepening pull plus hours contracting faster than output). The countervailing coupling neither he nor the others carried: public health, social care and much of government output are deflated by INPUT COSTS with essentially no quality adjustment, so a care-wage surge of the size my political-demand-pull channel implies mechanically produces zero measured real output growth and negative measured TFP in a sector whose employment share aging is actively growing. Higher care inflation therefore LOWERS measured aggregate TFP with nothing real changing. Netted against Panelist 1's genuine capital-deepening pull, AI-Q1 lands at ~19-21%. This also means Panelist 2's Baumol drag is partly double-counted: it is already inside 2A's locked 0.6%/yr per-capita baseline as a deflator convention, which is why my CQ3 P50 (1.95%) sits above all three Wave-1 panelists despite my accepting a real care bottleneck.
THIRD, BRIEFLY, ON AI-Q3: all three Wave-1 panelists found the same arithmetic conflict between AI-Q4 at 66% and AI-Q3's P50 of 998 TWh, and all three resolved it by taking the inconsistency out of the TWh (to 880-900) while KEEPING a low or falling real electricity price. That resolution is incoherent. Trades scarcity, interconnection queues and an aging HV workforce deliver LESS load at HIGHER cost -- under-build and price impulse are the same event, exactly as impairment and operating-capacity shortfall were the same event in fibre 1999-2002, US nuclear 1974-1984 and shale 2015-2020. DIRECTION: AI-Q3 P50 to ~880 with a materially fatter LEFT tail (P10 ~500) AND front-half real retail electricity growth revised UP, not down. That joint -- less compute delivered, at higher power cost, with the TFP lift diluted by Baumol reallocation -- is inflationary and growth-negative together in the SUPPLY sense, which is the C-regime pairing and the whole source of my CQ6-C at 25 against Wave 1's 11-18 and my CQ6-D at 9 against their 15-34.

wave2.lens_self_description: I answered purely as an arithmetic decomposer: every number below is the output of an explicit identity, weighted sum, growth-accounting ledger or conjunction multiplication that I show in full — which forbade me from using narrative plausibility, regime storytelling, AI-capability priors, or any appeal to "the modal world" as evidence, and obliged me to keep a figure that the arithmetic produced even where it sits outside all three Wave-1 panelists' ranges.
wave2.cq1_reasoning:
CONJUNCT A (OECD-38 harmonized U <= 5.5% avg 2032-2036). Ledger on the 5-yr average: structural level 5.0% (current print ~4.9-5.1) + frictional reallocation from J/K/M displacement into F+Q behind licensure gates (+0.30) - denominator effect from a working-age contraction of -0.3%/yr with rising 55-74 and 65+ participation, whose own unemployment rate is 2-3% (-0.20) = 5.10 no-recession central. Recession inside a 5-year window: 6 G7-synchronized episodes in 65 years = 45% hazard; a 2-year +2.0pp episode adds 0.80pp to a 5-yr average -> 5.90 in that branch. Branch arithmetic with sd 0.40 on the window average: P(<=5.5 | no recession) = Phi((5.5-5.10)/0.40) = Phi(1.00) = 0.84, shaded to 0.75 for the AI-Q4 (locked 66%) capex-bust hangover arriving 2031-33 even without an NBER-style recession; P(<=5.5 | recession) = Phi((5.5-5.90)/0.40) = 0.16, shaded to 0.10 because a bust-driven spike is wider than 2pp. P(A) = 0.55(0.75) + 0.45(0.10) = 0.4125 + 0.045 = 0.4575 -> 0.47.
CONJUNCT B (F+Q minus J+K+M cumulative real median hourly >= +10.0pp over 11 yrs = 0.87pp/yr). Decomposed as a per-year differential ledger. Gross scarcity differential: 80+ cohort +3.7%/yr with ADL-hour elasticity ~1.0 gives care labour demand +3%/yr against supply +1%/yr, and incremental DC/grid/housing construction takes ~15-20% of the electrician/lineman pool -> +1.15pp/yr gross. Deductions: (i) monopsony suppression, ISIC Q is 60-80% publicly funded and Q is ~2/3 of F+Q employment weight (Q ~13% vs F ~7%), administered pay settles ~0.50pp/yr below clearing -> -0.33pp/yr weighted; (ii) entrant dilution of the F+Q MEDIAN by migrant/part-time/low-credential care hires, -0.40pp/yr; (iii) inverse composition in the subtrahend — AI truncates the BOTTOM of the J/K/M distribution, lifting the surviving median by ~0.40pp/yr with no incumbent raise, which subtracts 0.40 from the differential. Net = 1.15 - 0.33 - 0.40 - 0.40 = +0.02pp/yr against a 0.87pp/yr threshold. With sd 0.60pp/yr on the differential: z = (0.87-0.02)/0.60 = 1.42 -> P = 0.078. Measurement mixture: P(resolver uses a composition-controlled fixed-weight proxy such as an ECI-by-industry stitch) = 0.20, in which world the three composition deductions mostly vanish and P = 0.25. Mixture = 0.80(0.078) + 0.20(0.25) = 0.062 + 0.050 = 0.112 -> 0.12.
CORRELATION AND MULTIPLICATION. Positive: the tight-labour state that holds unemployment under 5.5% is the same state that generates the F+Q premium; but deductions (ii) and (iii) are composition artefacts independent of the cycle, so the lift is modest. rho = +0.30, implemented as P(B|A) = 0.12 x 1.30 = 0.156. JOINT = 0.47 x 0.156 = 0.0733 -> 8. The conjunction discount is doing most of the work: the naive reader multiplies 0.50 x 0.33 and gets 17; my conjunct B is 2.7x lower than that because three of the four terms in the differential ledger point the wrong way.
wave2.cq2_reasoning:
CONJUNCT A (OECD-38 GDP-weighted core CPI/PCE >= 2.50%/yr avg 2027-2036). I carry BOTH weight layers explicitly, because the question is a threshold question on a quantity whose uncertainty is dominated by weights, not by inflation mechanism.
Layer 1, within-country basket (US-like core): shelter 0.33 @ 3.2 = 1.056; medical + social care services 0.09 @ 3.3 = 0.297; other labour-intensive core services 0.30 @ 2.7 = 0.810; core goods 0.23 @ 0.4 = 0.092; communication/digital 0.05 @ -0.8 = -0.040. Sum 2.215, plus electricity entering ONLY as second-round business cost (~2% energy share of service gross output x ~0.5 pass-through) +0.12 = 2.335. ACCOUNTING LOCK: electricity is excluded from US core CPI/PCE and from HICP core by construction, so a 4-6% power/construction/care skew against 0 to -1% software/media/tradables yields ~2.3% core, not ~3%. The skew is violent; the level is not.
Layer 2, GDP weights across OECD-38 (2025 PPP shares): US 0.38 x 2.35 = 0.893; Japan 0.07 x 1.6 = 0.112; Germany 0.055 x 2.0 = 0.110; UK 0.043 x 2.5 = 0.108; France 0.040 x 1.9 = 0.076; Italy 0.033 x 2.0 = 0.066; Canada 0.025 x 2.2 = 0.055; Korea 0.035 x 2.0 = 0.070; Spain 0.027 x 2.2 = 0.059; Mexico 0.034 x 3.8 = 0.129; Turkey 0.035 x 10.0 = 0.350; Poland 0.020 x 3.2 = 0.064; Australia 0.020 x 2.5 = 0.050; remainder 0.18 x 2.3 = 0.414. SUM = 2.556%.
THE SWING TERM IS TURKEY, AND IT IS ARITHMETIC, NOT MACRO. Drop Turkey and renormalize: (2.556 - 0.350)/0.965 = 2.286%. So one member at a 3.5% PPP weight contributes +0.27pp to the aggregate and is the difference between clearing and missing the threshold. Sensitivity: Turkey at 6% avg -> aggregate 2.42 (FAILS); at 10% -> 2.56 (clears); at 14% -> 2.70. Path check: 2027-2030 at ~2.85 and 2031-2036 at ~2.37 averages (4 x 2.85 + 6 x 2.37)/10 = 2.56, matching the weighted build, so the hurdle is cleared by the front half plus the EM-OECD floor, not by 2030s stagflation. With sd 0.35 on a 10-year average and central 2.56: P = 1 - Phi((2.50-2.56)/0.35) = 0.57; haircut to 0.52 for resolver latitude that runs one-way DOWN (core-PCE-only reading -0.25pp on the US leg; consumption-PPP rather than GDP weighting lowers the EM contribution). P(A) = 0.52.
CONJUNCT B (China headline CPI < 1.50%/yr avg 2027-2036), treated as a semi-independent object with its own basket. Food 0.19 @ 1.5 (pork cycles mean-revert, not trend) = 0.285; residence 0.21 @ 0.3 (rent-imputed, so a -55/-60% property adjustment barely registers but delivers no rent growth) = 0.063; other goods 0.25 @ -0.2 (capacity +5-7%/yr vs domestic demand +3-4%/yr, PPI leakage) = -0.050; services ex-residence 0.35 @ 1.6 (late-window working-age -1%/yr wage pressure, held down by a household income share stuck ~44% of GDP and pension subsidies already 10.1% of fiscal expenditure that cannot buy down precautionary saving) = 0.560. SUM = 0.858, call central 1.05 after allowing for the 2026 basket rebase raising the services weight. Distance to threshold 0.45pp; sd on a 10-yr average 0.60pp (tails: deliberate reflation, RMB depreciation import pass-through, one +5% food year adds 0.5pp to the decade average). P = Phi(0.45/0.60) = Phi(0.75) = 0.77 -> 0.75.
CORRELATION AND MULTIPLICATION. Mixed sign, netting slightly negative: Chinese goods deflation is itself the force holding my OECD core-goods term at 0.4%, so conditioning on A buys little extra on B through the tradables channel (negative), while the common "OECD physical/care scarcity vs China demand deficit" bifurcation is positive, and tariff/fragmentation walls partly sever the negative channel. rho = -0.10 -> P(B|A) = 0.75 x 0.93 = 0.698. JOINT = 0.52 x 0.698 = 0.363 -> 36.
wave2.cq3_reasoning:
PPP WEIGHT RECONCILIATION FIRST. 2025 constant-PPP levels: OECD-38 ~$76T, China ~$40T -> 65.5%/34.5% at t0. Accumulating at OECD 1.5%/yr and China 3.5%/yr to 2032: OECD 76 x 1.110 = 84.4, China 40 x 1.272 = 50.9 -> 62.4%/37.6%. I use 0.63 OECD-38 / 0.37 China for the 2032-2036 window.
OECD-38 LEG, growth accounting. Labour input: working-age -0.3%/yr; participation +0.15 (65+ and 55-74 entry); population +0.15 (migration-dependent); hours per worker -0.1 -> labour input -0.20%/yr x labour share 0.62 = -0.12pp. Capital deepening: capital services +1.8%/yr pre-bust and +1.0%/yr post-bust, and 2032-36 is the post-bust half at the locked AI-Q4 66%, so expected +1.25%/yr x capital share 0.38 = +0.48pp (the AI/grid capex stock is inside this term, not additional to it). wave2.cq5_reasoning:
CONJUNCT A (MOVE 10-yr average >= 105, 2027-2036). The decisive arithmetic is that MOVE is basis-point-normalized, so its level scales with the yield level: at a 4.0-4.5% 10y nominal the vol-neutral MOVE is ~95-105, versus ~60 at 2% yields in 2017-19. So 105 is roughly "rates stay here and nothing calms down", not "a decade of crisis". But the window must START from ~70-90 (2025 close reported at 63.96, 2024 ~100-110). Two-phase build: 2027-2031 ~105 (fiscal/AI-capex/inflation-impulse phase, duration supply against dealer balance sheets, repression-vs-spiral belief dispersion), 2032-2036 ~90 (post-bust disinflation phase in my own CQ2 path). 10-yr average = (5 x 105 + 5 x 90)/10 = 97.5. To clear 105 the back half must stay stressed at ~105+ as well, i.e. fiscal dominance persisting through the digestion phase. With sd ~12 on the decade average: P = 1 - Phi((105-97.5)/12) = 1 - Phi(0.625) = 0.266; lifted to 0.36 for the bp-normalization tailwind if nominals sit at 4.5-5%, then cut 0.02 for ICE methodology-change/discontinuation annul risk, which is one-way against a clean YES. P(A) = 0.34.
CONJUNCT B (an MSCI World >= 25% peak-to-trough drawdown in which G7 GDP-weighted 10y nominal fails to fall >= 50bp, or rises >= 25bp). Note the OR adds nothing: "rises >= 25bp" is a strict subset of "fails to fall >= 50bp", so the operative test is only that yields do not rally 50bp — anything from -49bp upward qualifies, which is far looser than the "stocks down AND yields up" scan most forecasters run. Step 1: base rate of >= 25% MSCI World drawdowns, ~7-8 episodes in 55 years = 0.135/yr -> P(>=1 in 10 yrs) = 0.75, lifted to 0.82 for index concentration (~73% US, top-10 ~25% of float, heavily the AI complex) plus $1.4T circular vendor/cloud/chip commitments on ~$300B equity and ~$650B debt and the locked 66% AI-Q4. Step 2: conditional on a drawdown, P(no 50bp rally) = 2 clear failures of 8 historically = 0.25, lifted to 0.42 because (a) the test is the loose one just noted, (b) my CQ2 path has OECD core above target precisely in 2027-2030 when the capex-cycle shock is most likely, (c) convenience-yield erosion and levered basis-trade absorption make the 2020-style flight-to-quality less reliable. Step 3: multiple attempts — expected drawdown count 1.25 -> P(at least one qualifying) = 1 - (1-0.42)^1.25 = 1 - e^(1.25 x ln 0.58) = 1 - e^(-0.681) = 0.494; haircut 0.04 for the undefined "during the equity drawdown window" (on a loose within-window reading long drawdowns almost always contain a 50bp fall somewhere, flipping 1987 and 2000-02 to NO; I weight 70/30 toward endpoint-to-endpoint). P(B) = 0.45.
CORRELATION AND MULTIPLICATION. Strongly positive — both conjuncts are readings of one institutional state (fiscal dominance risk, leveraged duration absorption, unanchored term premium), not two independent draws. rho = +0.40, implemented as P(A|B) = 0.60 rather than the unconditional 0.34. JOINT = 0.45 x 0.60 = 0.270, less 0.02 for MOVE index-continuity risk = 0.25 -> 25. I take a partial rather than a full conjunction discount here: the naive independent product is 0.34 x 0.45 = 0.153, and the near-co-determination of the conjuncts is worth 1.6x of that.

Step 2, C = P(core >= 2.70) x P(growth < 2.0 | core >= 2.70) = 0.19 x 0.78 (conditional lifted from the unconditional 0.68 because a high back-half core at low growth must be supply-side — the care bottleneck clearing through prices instead of administered rationing, a surviving grid wall, or outright fiscal dominance) = 0.148 -> 15.

CONSISTENCY CHECK PERFORMED, EXPLICITLY AGAINST MY OWN CQ3 AND CQ2. (i) A = 10 is numerically identical to P(growth >= 2.6) read off my CQ3 distribution — it is not a judgement about the appeal of a productivity renaissance, and it cannot be inflated by the historical base rate (which puts ~85-90% of 1960-2019 five-year windows above 2.6% for this aggregate). Mapping 0.52 straight onto C would over-weight it by ~15pp. (iii) C + D = 32, i.e. I put under a third of the mass on the two "something is broken" regimes, with genuine two-sided inflation risk (0.19 up-tail vs 0.25 down-tail) rather than a one-directional stagflation lean — the honest reading of a tug-of-war whose inflationary phase is 2027-2030 and whose disinflationary phase is 2031-2036.
