hypothesis_critique.a: "SMOOTHLY" carries the failure, and the flow arithmetic is an order of magnitude short. Required: the 80+ cohort grows ~3.7%/yr, so OECD care demand rises ~40-45% by 2036; against a care-specific workforce of roughly 12M FTE that is +4.5 to 6M FTE needed. Supplied: J+K+M employment is ~15% of OECD employment, ~55M; even a 10% displacement releases 5.5M people, but the realized occupational transition rate into F+Q across a wage cut to 45-60% of prior pay, a 6-24 month licensure gate, and a geographic mismatch is 5-10% -> 0.3-0.6M actual flow, i.e. ~10% of the requirement, and arriving as low-credential entrants who depress the measured Q median. Worse, the two flows are not even contemporaneous: displacement peaks with the capex cycle, care demand compounds monotonically. The plank also presumes the care post is FUNDED; ISIC Q is 60-80% publicly funded while OECD net interest goes 2% -> 3% of GDP, so the binding constraint is a budget line, not a labour pool. Replace "smoothly" with "at roughly a tenth of the required rate, financed by a payer that is simultaneously being squeezed" and the plank is near-dead.
hypothesis_critique.b: TWO words fail, in OPPOSITE directions. "BLOCKS" is simply wrong on the physical channel: aging is a demand PULL for imported hands-on labour — nursing, LTC aides, construction trades — and 2A's 39-41% old-age ratio makes that pull stronger, not weaker, so AI cannot block the migration leg; if anything the Gulf/OECD nursing corridor expands. "SEVERELY" is asymmetric between the two countries and the plank conflates them: the Philippines carries ~1.7M BPO jobs and ~7-8% of GDP in exactly the voice/first-line/back-office tasks AI automates first, so a severe VIRTUAL-exports hit is a live arithmetic risk; India's ~5.5M-direct IT services sector is ~7% of GDP but moves up-stack and retains a large domestic-demand base, so "severely" is a stretch there. Scored as written — one country, one channel, one verb all have to hold — it is 18, with most of the surviving mass being the Philippines-only, virtual-only reading.
hypothesis_critique.c: "FALLS" carries the failure, because it is a verb about a DIRECTION applied to a quantity whose LEVEL is what the questions resolve on. My own decomposition agrees with the shape — 2027-2030 at ~2.85% then 2031-2036 at ~2.37% — so the plank's timing is the one thing in this hypothesis set that my arithmetic endorses, hence 62. What it gets wrong is the magnitude and the destination: the fall is ~0.5pp, to ~2.3-2.4%, not to or below target, because (i) electricity is excluded from core by construction so the disinflation of the power glut barely registers in the resolving index just as its inflation barely did, (ii) shelter (~33% of US core) and medical/social care (~9%) carry ~2.3% on their own, (iii) consumer-facing AI-deflatables are under 8% of core so even a total J/K/M price collapse moves core only -0.2 to -0.4pp, and (iv) the EM-OECD members put a ~+0.30pp floor under any GDP-weighted OECD-38 aggregate. "Falls" implies a regime change; the arithmetic delivers a step down of half a point onto a sticky plateau.
hypothesis_critique.d: "EVENTUALLY" and "WINS" both fail, and "EVENTUALLY" is disqualifying on a Dec 31 2036 horizon — a plank whose truth condition lies outside the resolution window cannot be substantially correct as stated. "WINS" fails on arithmetic: P(coupled growth >= 2.6%/yr) = 0.10 on my own CQ3, and the headcount term is near-deterministic — China's 0.37 PPP weight times its locked -2.7pp drag is -1.00pp on the combined aggregate by itself, plus ~-0.54pp from the OECD leg, for a total aging drag of ~-1.54pp that no plausible AI TFP contribution (my coupled expectation is +0.305pp) offsets. "EXPONENTIAL" also smuggles in a false inference that my lens can kill precisely: measured TFP rising because hours contract faster than output is an accounting artefact that adds nothing to GDP growth, so AI-Q1 can resolve YES in a world with 1.65% coupled growth. High measured TFP and "growth wins" are different events, and the plank assumes they are the same one.

key_drivers: CORE-BASKET WEIGHT ASYMMETRY IS THE WHOLE LEVEL ANSWER, AND IT IS ARITHMETIC. Electricity is excluded from US core CPI/PCE and HICP core by construction, so the 2027-2031 power/grid impulse reaches core only via the ~2% energy cost share of service gross output at ~0.5 pass-through (+0.12pp), while AI's deflation lands in B2B/intermediate prices and GVA deflators and the consumer-facing AI-deflatables are under 8% of core. A regime of 4-6% electricity/construction/care against 0 to -1% software/media/tradables yields ~2.3% core: violent skew, modest level, and the skew is weighted toward the INFLATING side of core because shelter (0.33) plus care and other labour-intensive services (0.39) dominate.

THE EM-OECD WEIGHT IS THE SINGLE LARGEST TERM IN CQ2 AND CQ6-D, AND IT IS NOT A MACRO JUDGEMENT. Turkey at a ~3.5% 2025 PPP weight contributes +0.27pp to the GDP-weighted OECD-38 core aggregate on its own; with Turkey removed and renormalized my aggregate falls from 2.556% to 2.286%. That one term decides whether CQ2's OECD conjunct clears 2.50, and it forces regime D to require G7 core at ~1.65-1.70 rather than ~1.9, moving ~6pp of mass from D to B.

CHINA'S PPP WEIGHT TIMES CHINA'S DRAG. At a 0.37 weight the locked -2.7pp/yr China aging drag subtracts -1.00pp from the combined aggregate by itself; the OECD leg's own ~-0.85pp drag at 0.63 adds -0.54pp, for ~-1.54pp total — about 40% larger than 2A's global -1.1pp figure, purely because the OECD-38 + China geography excludes India and Africa. Importing the global number into CQ3 understates the drag by ~0.44pp, which is the difference between a 1.65% and a 2.1% P50.

THE MEASURED-TFP DENOMINATOR IS AN ACCOUNTING ARTEFACT, NOT GROWTH. With OECD hours at -0.2%/yr instead of 2015-2022's +0.4%/yr, the same output path mechanically lifts measured TFP by 0.62 x 0.6 = +0.37pp; in China, hours at -1.1%/yr against a +0.2% baseline lift it by 0.52 x 1.3 = +0.68pp; PPP-weighted that is 0.63(0.37) + 0.37(0.68) = +0.485pp handed over by the denominator with no AI at all. This raises AI-Q1 and leaves CQ3 and CQ6-A untouched — the separation my lens exists to make.

CONJUNCTION DISCOUNTS WITH EXPLICITLY SIGNED CORRELATIONS. CQ1: 0.47 x 0.12 with rho +0.30 = 8 (three of four terms in the wage-differential ledger point against the threshold, netting +0.02pp/yr against a required 0.87pp/yr). CQ2: 0.52 x 0.75 with rho -0.10 = 36. CQ5: 0.45 x 0.34 with rho +0.40 taken as P(A|B) = 0.60 = 25 — a partial, not full, discount because the conjuncts are two readings of one regime.

WINDOW PLACEMENT OF THE LOCKED 66% AI-Q4 BUST. It lands inside 2031-2033, so CQ3, CQ4 and CQ6 are all read off the post-bust half: capital-services growth 1.8 -> 1.0%/yr (-0.30pp on the OECD leg), r* cyclically depressed (my AI/grid savings-demand term flips to -0.05pp expected), MOVE's back half at ~90, and the back-half core at 2.37 rather than 2.85 — which is exactly why C (15) is smaller than CQ2's OECD marginal would naively imply.

wave2.coupling_tension:
PRIMARY: AI-Q1 (TFP lift >= +0.50pp/yr, 23.0%) IS TOO LOW, AND THE REASON IS A DENOMINATOR IDENTITY, NOT AN AI JUDGEMENT. Measured TFP = output growth minus share-weighted input growth. 2B holds demographics exogenous, so the forecaster implicitly carries the 2015-2022 labour-input path. Endogenize 2A: OECD hours go from +0.4%/yr to -0.2%/yr, a 0.6pp swing at a 0.62 labour share = +0.37pp of measured TFP for the SAME output path; China's hours go from +0.2%/yr to -1.1%/yr, a 1.3pp swing at a 0.52 share = +0.68pp. PPP-weighted at my CQ3 weights: 0.63(0.37) + 0.37(0.68) = 0.233 + 0.252 = +0.485pp/yr, handed over by arithmetic with no AI contribution whatsoever, against a +0.50pp threshold. DIRECTION: AI-Q1 should sit at ~38-45%, not 23.0%. CRITICALLY, THIS DOES NOT RAISE MY CQ3 BY ONE BASIS POINT — measured TFP that rises because hours contract faster than output adds nothing to GDP growth — so the usual inference "AI-Q1 up therefore CQ6-A up" is invalid once demographics are endogenous. That breaks the AI-Q6 regime labels too: the 16.2% Transformative Breakout band is defined in TFP pp/yr and can resolve YES in a world of 1.65% coupled growth and CQ6-B or D. Any downstream aggregation that reads AI-Q6's bands as growth regimes will double-count the demographic drag's own TFP artefact as if it were output.
SECOND: AI-Q3 AND AI-Q4 ARE JOINTLY INCONSISTENT AT THEIR STATED VALUES. AI-Q3's P50 of 998 TWh in 2036 against 365 TWh in 2024 is +633 TWh, an 8.7%/yr CAGR. Endogenizing 2A widens rather than narrows the gap, because the inputs that convert desired load into STRICT OPERATIONAL megawatt-hours are electricians, linemen, substation and HVAC crews and interconnection engineers — the trades aging drains (roughly a quarter of the US electrician workforce reaches retirement eligibility by 2033), bid for simultaneously by housing, grid hardening and the 80+ care-facility build. AUDITOR'S FIRST READING, ADOPTED BY EVERYONE AFTER HIM: the OR clause is VACUOUS. "Rises >= 25 bps" is a strict subset of "fails to fall by >= 50 bps," so the operative test is only that G7 GDP-weighted 10y nominals do not rally 50 bp during the drawdown window — anything from -49 bp upward qualifies. This is far looser than the scan most forecasters run and it admits every muted-rally episode, not just 1973-74 and 2022.

AUDITOR'S SECOND READING, ALSO ADOPTED: MOVE is yield-curve-weighted, basis-point-NORMALIZED 1-month implied vol, not log/relative, so its level scales with the yield level. It averaged ~60 in 2017-19 at ~2% yields, 120-130 in 2022-23, ~100-110 in 2024, and a 2025 close reported at 63.96. At 4-4.5% nominals the vol-neutral level is ~95-105, so a 105 hurdle is closer to "rates stay here and nothing calms down" than to "a decade of crisis."

CONJUNCT A (MOVE 10-yr average >= 105, 2027-2036) = 0.42. Fermi's two-phase build: 2027-2031 ~105 (fiscal/AI-capex/inflation-impulse phase, duration supply against dealer balance sheets, repression-versus-spiral belief dispersion), 2032-2036 ~90, average 97.5, sd ~12 on the decade average -> 1 - Phi(0.625) = 0.27, lifted to 0.34 for the bp-normalization tailwind at 4.5-5% nominals, less ~0.02 one-way for ICE methodology-change, re-basing or discontinuation risk over a ten-year window. CONJUNCT B = 0.43. P(at least one >= 25% MSCI World peak-to-trough drawdown in 10 years) = 0.83: base rate ~7-8 episodes in 55 years = ~0.135/yr gives 0.75, lifted for index concentration (~73% US, top-10 ~25% of float, heavily the AI complex), the ~$1.4T circular vendor/cloud/chip commitments on ~$300B equity and ~$650B debt, and the locked 66% AI-Q4. P(no 50 bp rally | drawdown) = 0.45: historically 2 clear failures of ~8 = 0.25, lifted because the test is the loose one above, because my CQ2 path has OECD core above target precisely in 2027-2030 when the capex-cycle shock is most likely, and because convenience-yield erosion plus levered basis-trade absorption make the 2020-style flight-to-quality less reliable — but NOT to the Red-Team's 0.55, which again rides his anchor. Expected qualifying attempts ~1.25 -> 1 - (0.55)^1.25 = 0.47, less 0.04 for the undefined "during the equity drawdown window" (on a loose within-window reading, long drawdowns such as 2000-02 almost always contain a 50 bp fall somewhere, flipping 1987 and 2000-02 to NO; I weight 70/30 toward endpoint-to-endpoint, per the Auditor). 0.43.

CONJUNCTION: strongly positive — both conjuncts are readings of ONE institutional state (fiscal-dominance risk, leveraged duration absorption, unanchored term premium), not two independent draws. P(A|B) = 0.65 against an unconditional 0.42. JOINT = 0.43 x 0.65 = 0.280, less 0.02 for MOVE index-continuity and annul risk = 0.26 -> 27. I will not go to the Inside-View's or Red-Team's 34-38, which require conditionals of 0.50-0.55 on the yield leg.

COHERENCE CHECKS, STATED AS REQUIRED. (i) Against CQ4's variance: my interdecile span is 2.30 pp (1.05 to 3.35) around a 2.00 P50, i.e. high and bimodal-leaning rate uncertainty, which is what supports conjunct A at 0.42 against a ~0.27 unconditional base rate — a narrow CQ4 would have forced CQ5 toward 18. wave3.cq6_reasoning:
INPUTS, read off MY OWN answers, not off any panelist's. Growth, from my CQ3 (P10 0.90 / P50 1.75 / P90 2.75, sd ~0.72): P(growth >= 2.6) = 0.12; P(growth < 2.0) = 0.64; P(growth < 1.7) = 0.47. This central ALREADY contains the ~+0.30 pp EM-OECD floor (Turkey ~+0.27 pp of it). Hence P(core_32-36 >= 2.70) = 1 - Phi(0.729) = 0.233; P(core_32-36 < 2.00) = Phi(-0.729) = 0.233; P(2.00-2.70) = 0.534.

LEXICAL APPLICATION, FIRST MATCH WINS.
Step 1, A = P(growth >= 2.6) = 0.12 -> 12.
Step 2, C = P(core >= 2.70) x P(growth < 2.0 | core >= 2.70) = 0.233 x 0.72 = 0.168 -> 17. The conditional is lifted from the 0.64 unconditional because a high back-half core at low growth must be substantially supply-side in my world — the care bottleneck clearing partly through prices, a grid wall surviving capex digestion on trades scarcity, or fiscal dominance — but it is well below the Outside-View's 0.68-equivalent and below what a pure stagflation narrative would take, because part of my high-core mass is strong-nominal-demand and growth-neutral.
Step 3, D = P(core < 2.00) x P(growth < 1.7 | core < 2.00) = 0.233 x 0.62 = 0.144 -> 14. Lifted from 0.47 for the demand-shortfall correlation (post-capex-bust excess capacity and the BIS Box C labour-income deficit produce both legs).
Step 4, B = 100 - 12 - 17 - 14 = 57. Sums to exactly 100.

RESIDUAL-B DECOMPOSITION, so B is an accounting residual and not a muddle-through judgement: P(1.7 <= g < 2.6) = 1 - 0.47 - 0.12 = 0.41, less the slice C takes in that band with core >= 2.7 (~0.04) = 0.37; plus the low-growth / moderate-core leftover cell at g < 1.7 with core in [2.00, 2.70) = 0.47 - 0.14 (D) - 0.11 (C's g < 1.7 share) = 0.22. Total 0.59, matching the residual 0.57 to within rounding. So only ~37 of my 57 is the literal 1.7-2.5% barbell; ~20 is the leftover cell a naive reader would have assigned to D.

CONSISTENCY CHECK AGAINST MY OWN CQ3. A = 12 is numerically identical to P(growth >= 2.6) read off my CQ3 distribution. It is not a judgement about the appeal of a productivity renaissance and it is NOT the historical base rate, which puts ~85-90% of 1960-2019 five-year windows for this aggregate above 2.6% — the Outside-View panelist's single most important finding was that this base rate must be overridden because A's threshold is arithmetically out of reach once the near-deterministic headcount is imposed (it needs China at ~4.5%+ AND OECD at ~1.6%+ simultaneously). My CQ3 P50 of 1.75 sits inside B's literal band, and B is modal at 57 — consistent. I reject the Red-Team's A = 20, which comes entirely from his China leg at 3.3% (measurement wedge plus political floor, partly double-counted) and which he himself conceded includes ~5 points of a nominal-reflation cell that fails A's own label clauses on broad wage gains and growth-stabilized debt.

CONSISTENCY CHECK AGAINST MY OWN CQ2. CQ2 = 38 is a JOINT: OECD core >= 2.50 over 2027-2036 at 0.58, times the China leg at 0.68 with rho -0.05. The OECD leg's 0.58 must NOT be mapped onto C, which needs core >= 2.70 over 2032-2036 only, marginal 0.233. The two are consistent ONLY because my path is front-loaded (2.95 then 2.45), and that front-loading is the single assumption a reader should check me on — on a flat path the two numbers would conflict and C would have to rise ~10-14 points. This window mismatch was the Resolution Auditor's best finding and it survived Wave 2 untouched; it is worth roughly 12-15 points of CQ6 mass that a naive reader puts in C.

WHERE I LAND BETWEEN THE PANEL. C at 17 sits between Wave 1's 11-18 and the Red-Team's 25: I accept his core-goods rigidity and half his care-price politics, which raise the core marginal from Fermi's 0.19 to 0.233, but not his anchor drift, which is what would take C to 25. D at 14 is my largest single departure from the Inside-View's 34, and for two stated reasons rather than one. First, the Auditor's audited EM-OECD floor means D requires G7 core at ~1.65-1.70, a deeper Japanification than the narrative pictures — an index-construction constraint, not a macro view, worth ~6 points out of D. Second, the Red-Team landed a real hit on an internal contradiction: the Inside-View derives his disinflationary back half from turbines, transformers and datacentre shells arriving into stalled load, which requires the capacity to have been BUILT, while his own coupling section argues buildable load is -18 to -25% because the trades are drained by aging and bid for by housing and the care-facility build. You cannot have both excess electrical capacity and a labour-constrained under-build. Resolving toward under-build makes the back half energy- and shelter-inflationary while still growth-poor, moving mass from D toward C and B. I price that at ~8-10 points rather than his 15.

hypothesis_critique.a: "SMOOTHLY" carries the whole failure, and "supply" carries a second. All five panelists converged at 4-7 and the convergence is earned by a flow identity, not by a narrative: the 80+ cohort grows ~3.7%/yr so OECD care demand rises ~40-45% by 2036, which against a care workforce near 12M FTE is +4.5 to 6M FTE needed, while J+K+M is ~12-15% of OECD employment and realized cross-family occupational transition rates across a 40-60% pay cut, a 6-24 month licensure gate and a geographic mismatch are 5-10%, giving an actual flow of 0.3-0.6M, roughly a tenth of the requirement. The gradient also points the wrong way on every axis at once (skill, licensure, geography, pay), and the two flows are not contemporaneous: cognitive displacement is concentrated with the capex cycle 2029-2034 while the 80+ surge compounds monotonically through 2045. Two further cuts the panel supplied: the post must be FUNDED, and ISIC Q is 60-80% publicly funded while net interest goes 2% -> 3% of GDP, so the binding constraint is a budget line rather than a labour pool; and the plank is self-undermining on the only series that would evidence it, because a realized transfer arrives as low-credential entrants who depress the measured Q median, which is the same composition artefact that defeats CQ1's second conjunct. The Red-Team's addition is the sharpest statement of why the adverb fails: the only mechanism that WOULD move these workers is the one the adverb denies — a multi-year real-terms erosion of the displaced worker's reservation wage until care work clears, which is slow, involuntary and politically explosive. 5.
hypothesis_critique.b: TWO words fail, and they fail in OPPOSITE directions, which is why the plank cannot be rescued by weakening either one alone. "BLOCKS" is categorically wrong, because the scope lock itself separates cross-border VIRTUAL services exports from PHYSICAL labour migration and AI touches only the first; aging is a demand PULL on the second, and a 39-41% old-age ratio with unfillable care and construction requisitions makes the physical channel stronger, not weaker. For the Philippines the physical leg (nurses, caregivers, seafarers, domestic workers) is the larger remittance channel, ~8-9% of GDP against BPO's contribution, so the country is a net demographic BENEFICIARY on the channel the plank says is blocked; the only thing that can block it is OECD migration politics, not AI. "SEVERELY" then fails asymmetrically and the plank conflates the two countries: the Philippines carries ~1.7M BPO workers and ~7-8% of GDP in exactly the voice, first-line and back-office tasks automated first, so a severe virtual-exports hit is a live arithmetic risk there, while India's ~5.5M-direct IT services sector moves up-stack, sells AI integration and retains a large domestic base, making "severely" a stretch. Two panelists added that even a true severe hit would be hard to date and size, since remittances are BOP-compiled with large informal-channel gaps and IT-BPM revenue is NASSCOM/IBPAP industry self-reporting with no published sampling frame or confidence interval. Scored as written — one verb, both countries, both channels — 15, with most surviving mass on the Philippines-only, virtual-only reading.
hypothesis_critique.c: "FALLS" carries the failure, and it fails on DESTINATION and MAGNITUDE rather than on direction or sequencing. This is the plank my own path endorses in shape: 2027-2030 at ~2.95% then 2031-2036 at ~2.45%, driven down by capex digestion, cognitive automation, Chinese overcapacity export deflation and the BIS Box C labour-income demand drag. It is therefore the highest-scored plank, as it was for all three Wave-1 panelists (55-62). But the fall is ~0.5 pp onto a sticky plateau at ~2.4%, not a regime change: electricity is excluded from core by construction, so the disinflation of a power glut barely registers in the resolving index exactly as its inflation barely did; shelter at ~33% of US core plus medical and social care at ~9% carry ~2.3% on their own; consumer-facing AI-deflatables are under 8% of core, so even a total J/K/M price collapse moves core only -0.2 to -0.4 pp; and the EM-OECD members put a ~+0.30 pp floor under any GDP-weighted OECD-38 aggregate. On my own distribution P(2032-2036 OECD core < 2.00%) is only 0.233, and a further 0.233 has the back half at or above 2.70% with NO fall at all — so ~0.23 of my mass falsifies the second clause outright. The Red-Team's version of this attack (that scoring the plank as consensus is scoring an undefended 2% anchor) is half right and I move partway toward him: 55, down from Wave 1's 55-62, up from his 38. "Hot" is also doing undefended work in the first clause, since my front half is warm (2.95% core) rather than hot and sits inside most central banks' tolerated overshoot — the 2027-2030 impulse lands overwhelmingly in HEADLINE and in RELATIVE PRICES, not in the resolving core aggregate.
hypothesis_critique.d: "EVENTUALLY" is disqualifying and "WINS" is undefined; "EXPONENTIAL" smuggles in the inference that actually fails. "Eventually" places the truth condition outside the Dec 31 2036 resolution horizon, and a plank that cannot be falsified by the resolution date cannot be scored as substantially correct as stated — all five panelists reached this independently. "Wins" names no counterfactual and conflates aggregate with per-capita, measured with true, and output with welfare; the BIS Box C point is precisely that output can grow while labour income lags, so "growth wins" and "demand fails" are simultaneously satisfiable. Forced into a scoreable form — 2032-2036 coupled real growth above the 2015-2024 realized rate — my own CQ3 P50 of 1.75% fails it against ~2.2-2.9% for recent windows, and P(growth >= 2.6%) is 0.12. The headcount term is near-deterministic: China's 0.37 PPP weight times its locked -2.7 pp drag is -1.00 pp on the combined aggregate by itself, plus ~-0.54 pp from the OECD leg, for ~-1.54 pp of aging drag against a coupled AI TFP expectation of ~+0.31 pp. "Exponential" is a claim about compute, not output: in a Jones task-weighted function, growth is bounded by the growth of the input you cannot automate times its share, and that input is direct personal ADL care hours plus grid interconnection and high-voltage trades — exponential improvement in a substitutable factor against a fixed non-substitutable one yields an ASYMPTOTE, and cheap cognition raises the bottleneck's shadow price rather than relaxing it. The cleanest national tests all resolved FALSE inside 25-30 years (Japan led world robot density and IT investment and still averaged ~0.8%/yr real GDP growth 1995-2025; Germany, Korea, Italy repeat it). The Fermi panelist added the decisive separation: measured TFP can rise >= +0.50 pp/yr purely because hours contract faster than output, so AI-Q1 can resolve YES in a 1.75% world — high measured TFP and "growth wins" are different events and the plank assumes they are one. 16, the 16 reserved for reading it as a post-2036 claim or for migration liberalisation and genuine embodied robotics moving the care wall inside the window.

key_drivers: CORE-BASKET WEIGHT ASYMMETRY SETS THE LEVEL, AND IT IS ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN MECHANISM. Electricity is excluded from US core CPI/PCE and HICP core by construction, so the 2027-2031 power and grid impulse reaches core only through the ~2% energy cost share of service gross output at ~0.5 pass-through (+0.12 pp), while AI's deflation lands in B2B/intermediate prices and GVA deflators and consumer-facing AI-deflatables are under 8% of core. A regime of 4-6% electricity, construction and care against 0 to +1% software, media and tradables yields ~2.4-2.5% core: violent skew, modest level, and the skew is weighted toward the INFLATING side because shelter (~0.33) plus care and other labour-intensive services (~0.39) dominate the basket. All five panelists agreed on this; the Red-Team's attempt to convert the skew into the level succeeds only partially, through nominal rigidity in core goods.

THE EM-OECD WEIGHT IS THE SINGLE LARGEST TERM IN CQ2 AND THE BINDING CONSTRAINT ON REGIME D, AND IT IS A WEIGHT-VECTOR FACT, NOT A MACRO VIEW. Turkey at a ~3.5% 2025 PPP weight contributes +0.27 pp to the GDP-weighted OECD-38 core aggregate on its own; with Turkey, Mexico, Chile, Colombia and Costa Rica the floor is ~+0.30 pp. Removing Turkey and renormalizing drops my aggregate from ~2.65 to ~2.38. That one term decides whether CQ2's OECD conjunct clears 2.50, and it forces regime D to require G7 core at ~1.65-1.70 rather than the ~1.9 the narrative pictures, moving ~6 points from D to B. The entire 0.54 pp spread in the three Wave-1 core centrals (2.556 / 2.02 / 2.53) was essentially this omission rather than any disagreement about transmission.

WINDOW PLACEMENT: THE LOCKED 66% AI-Q4 CAPEX BUST LANDS INSIDE 2031-2033, SO CQ3, CQ4 AND CQ6 ARE ALL READ OFF THE POST-BUST HALF. Capital-services growth 1.8 -> 1.0%/yr (-0.30 pp on the OECD leg); the AI/grid savings-demand term in r* flips to -0.05 pp expected; MOVE's back half near 90; and back-half core at ~2.40 rather than the ~2.95 front half. This front-loading is the single assumption that reconciles my CQ2 OECD marginal of 0.58 with my CQ6-C core marginal of 0.233, and it is the thing a reader should check me on — on a flat path the two conflict and C rises 10-14 points.

THE AGING DRAG ON THIS SPECIFIC GEOGRAPHY IS ~40% LARGER THAN 2A'S GLOBAL HEADLINE. China's 0.37 PPP weight times its locked -2.7 pp/yr drag is -1.00 pp on the combined aggregate by itself; the OECD leg's ~-0.85 pp drag at a 0.63 weight adds -0.54 pp; total ~-1.54 pp, versus the global -1.1 pp, purely because OECD-38 + China excludes India and Africa. Importing the global figure understates the drag by ~0.44 pp, the difference between a 1.75% and a 2.2% CQ3 P50 — and the difference between CQ6-A at 12 and at 20.

CARE PRICES VERSUS CARE QUEUES IS THE LIVE UNSETTLED CHANNEL, AND I SPLIT IT. The Inside-View's monopsony-rationing arrow (ISIC Q 60-80% publicly funded, net interest 2% -> 3% of GDP, so the administered price rises ~25-35% real while true willingness-to-pay for a marginal care hour roughly doubles, the wedge realized as unmet-need hours and 4-7M additional informal carers) pushes measured core DOWN and real GDP DOWN together. The Red-Team's political-demand-pull arrow (at a 39-41% old-age ratio the elderly are the median voter; statutory wage floors, sectoral awards and CPI-indexed pensions are the observed response, and OECD medical and social-care CPI has outpaced core through austerity episodes) pushes core UP. Nothing in the locked priors settles it. I take care services at 3.8% rather than 3.2% or 4.2%, worth ~+0.05 pp on core and ~8 points of CQ6 C-versus-D mass.

CONJUNCTION DISCOUNTS WITH EXPLICITLY SIGNED CORRELATIONS, APPLIED CONSISTENTLY ACROSS CQ1, CQ2 AND CQ5. CQ1: 0.49 x 0.145 at rho +0.30 = 10, with three of four terms in the wage-differential ledger pointing against the threshold and the real-versus-nominal deflator cancelling exactly in a differential of two real series. CQ2: 0.58 x 0.68 at rho -0.05 = 38. CQ5: 0.43 x 0.42 at rho +0.40 implemented as P(A|B) = 0.65 = 27 — a partial rather than full discount, because the conjuncts are two readings of one institutional regime, and because the Auditor showed the OR clause in the yield test is vacuous, making that conjunct materially looser than the naive 'stocks crashed AND yields rose' scan implies.

falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: Falsifies the one Red-Team hit I partially adopted — downward nominal rigidity converting the relative-price skew into the level. My core-goods term reverts from 0.8% to the Wave-1 plug of ~0.4% (-0.09 pp on the US leg, ~-0.07 pp on the aggregate), and with it the whole claim that tariffs and fragmentation have changed the regime in sectors that 'want' to deflate. CQ2 falls from 38 to ~32; CQ6-C from 17 to ~13 with the mass to B; CQ5 conjunct A falls ~0.03, taking CQ5 from 27 to ~25. It would also mean the Red-Team contrarian-posed on his single largest departure from Wave 1 and I should not have moved at all.

falsification_signposts.signpost: China headline CPI (NBS monthly series, any basket vintage) prints 2.0% year-on-year or higher for four consecutive quarters at any point between 2027 and 2031, with the non-food, non-residence component contributing at least 1.0 pp of it (i.e. not a pork or energy spike).
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: Kills CQ2's stronger conjunct and the China-as-semi-independent-deflationary-object premise my effort brief required me to carry. P(China CPI < 1.50% over 2027-2036) falls from 0.68 to ~0.38 and CQ2 drops from 38 to ~22 even with my OECD leg fully intact — which is the cleanest available test of whether my CQ2 comes from the OECD leg (my claim) or from the correlation assumption. It also lifts my China real leg from 3.05% toward 3.4%, raising CQ3 P50 from 1.75 to ~1.88 and shifting ~4 points of CQ6 mass out of D into B and C.

falsification_signposts.signpost: Cumulative publicly disclosed AI-related capex impairments and cancellations stay below 10% of announced hyperscaler buildouts AND net external AI software/API revenue exceeds 1.0x annualized AI compute D&A for four consecutive quarters, with at least 70 GW of net firm capacity serving data centres reaching commercial operation across OECD-38 + China (EIA / ENTSO-E / CEC commissioning data) by end-2031.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: The highest-leverage signpost for my payload, because it removes the locked AI-Q4 bust from the middle of every 2032-2036 measurement window and simultaneously refutes my coupled claim that trades labour and interconnection bind harder than the dollars. Capital-services growth stays at ~1.8%/yr (+0.30 pp on the OECD leg) and the AI savings-demand term returns to +0.25 pp on r*. CQ3 P50 moves from 1.75 to ~2.05 and P90 from 2.75 to ~3.00; CQ4 P50 from 2.00 to ~2.30 with a thinner left tail; CQ6-A from 12 to ~19, D from 14 to ~9, B to ~57, C ~15; CQ5 falls from 27 to ~21 as the back-half MOVE path drops toward 85 and the leveraged-unwind shock source thins. It would also retire my AI-Q3 coupling correction.

falsification_signposts.signpost: An equity drawdown of >= 20% (MSCI World, USD, closing basis) occurs in which the G7 GDP-weighted 10y nominal sovereign yield FALLS by >= 100 bp between the equity peak date and the trough date — the classic flight-to-quality reasserting itself despite convenience-yield erosion, basis-trade absorption and >100% debt/GDP.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: Falsifies the fiscal-dominance correlation structure behind both CQ5 and CQ4's right tail. P(no 50 bp rally | drawdown) falls from 0.45 to ~0.28 and the A|B conditional from 0.65 to ~0.52, taking CQ5 from 27 to ~16. CQ4 P90 falls from 3.35 to ~2.95 and the distribution loses its right skew. ~3 points of CQ6 mass move from C to D, because bond-market tolerance means repression is unnecessary and accommodation of inflation is less likely.

wave3.lens_self_description: I am the effort-level posterior for the inflation-path and relative-price-skew effort: I reweighted the five prior panelists question by question on the quality of each specific argument, moved only where the Wave-2 red-team landed a checkable hit and said so where it merely posed, and then enforced arithmetic coherence across my own six answers — which forbade me from introducing any new mechanism, reference class or private view of my own that no panelist in my effort had put on the table, and from averaging where one panelist's construction was demonstrably wrong.

wave_audit.wave1_spread: The three Wave-1 lenses disagreed most on the OECD-38 GDP-weighted core LEVEL, and almost all of that disagreement turned out not to be about inflation at all. Their conjunct-A marginals were 0.52 (Outside-View), 0.30 (Inside-View) and 0.62 (Auditor) on central paths of 2.556, 2.02 and 2.53 — a 0.54 pp spread in the level producing a 2.1x spread in the probability, on a threshold question. The Fermi panelist diagnosed the cause: the Inside-View's basket is a G7-style basket with no EM-OECD members, worth ~+0.30 pp (Turkey alone ~+0.27 pp) on a GDP-weighted OECD-38 aggregate. A weight-vector omission was doing more work than every transmission channel the three of them argued about combined. The second-largest spread was CQ6-D (15 / 34 / 15): the Inside-View made D his second cell at 34 on a care-rationing GDP leak plus the BIS Box C demand deficit, while the other two held D down on the EM floor requiring G7 core at ~1.65-1.70. Third was CQ3 (P50 1.85 / 1.60 / 1.80), a narrow spread that concealed a wide disagreement about the China leg (2.6 to 2.9) and whether the Baumol drag is already inside 2A's locked 0.6%/yr per-capita baseline. The three CQ4 P50s (1.80 / 1.80 / 2.00) and the CQ1 answers (12 / 22 / 6) were the other visible splits; CQ5 (18 / 34 / 27) split entirely on whether the yield-failure test is read strictly or loosely.
wave_audit.what_wave2_changed: KILLED, by the Fermi Decomposer: the Inside-View's CQ2 conjunct-A marginal of 0.30, which is ~2.3x what his own mechanism implies (his path averages 2.135, his weighted build 2.023; at the sd appropriate to a ten-year average, ~0.35, that is P = 0.13, and recovering 0.30 needs sd ~0.6 pp, which is implausible). Also killed: the Outside-View's unexplained +0.29 pp upgrade of the US leg he had computed one sentence earlier at 2.42, which was the sole thing carrying his 0.52 over the threshold and the sole basis for a 2x override of his own stated post-1993 base rate of ~1 in 4. Also corrected: BOTH of the Inside-View's CQ4 weighted averages were computed on a G7 weight vector summing to 0.96, biasing his level down ~0.07 pp. RESCUED, by Fermi: the Outside-View's low CQ1, via an explicit per-year differential ledger (+0.02 pp/yr net against a required 0.87 pp/yr) that made the claim checkable rather than asserted. KILLED, by the Auditor and ratified by both Wave-2 panelists: the premise that CQ5's yield test is 'stocks crashed AND yields rose' — 'rises >= 25 bps' is a strict subset of 'fails to fall >= 50 bps', so the OR clause is vacuous and every muted-rally episode qualifies. RED-TEAM HITS I ACCEPTED: (i) downward nominal rigidity — core goods at 0.3-0.5% is a hyper-globalization number and Wave 1 plugged it unexamined; I moved to 0.8%, half his 1.2%. (ii) Repression and inflation are SUBSTITUTE answers to one fiscal arithmetic, not complements, so all three Wave-1 left tails (P10 0.55 / 0.80 / 1.00) are incoherent with their own hot front halves; I cut P(repression binding) from 0.25 to 0.18 and thinned the CQ4 left tail to 1.05. (iii) The Inside-View's back half cannot be both 'turbines and shells arrive into stalled load' (requires the capacity to have been built) and 'buildable load -18 to -25%' on trades scarcity — resolving toward under-build moves mass from D to C, which I priced at ~8-10 points rather than his 15. (iv) The measured-NBS China floor: the Auditor stated the principle and then did not apply it. RED-TEAM POSES I REFUSED TO MOVE ON: (a) his CQ1 deflator argument — the resolution measure is a difference of two REAL series deflated by the same national index, so the deflator cancels exactly and his 18 pp gap is identical to his nominal assumption of 3.6 - 2.0 = 1.6 pp/yr; he dressed a wage-setting claim as a price-level claim and the Outside-View had already stated the cancellation. (b) his CQ4 anchoring charge — mean ABSOLUTE decade change of ~2.1 pp licenses a wide distribution, which I have, but says nothing about direction, so it cannot move a P50. (c) his de facto 3% anchor — asserted from the locked fiscal block with no transmission that moves a measured ten-year core average by 2036. (d) his AI-Q5 at 58-62%, which rides entirely on (c).
wave_audit.unresolved: THREE things remain genuinely unresolved inside this effort. FIRST and largest: whether the care bottleneck clears through administered PRICES (the Red-Team's median-voter channel — at a 39-41% old-age ratio the elderly are the median voter, and statutory wage floors, sectoral awards and indexed pensions are the observed response under fiscal stress) or through QUEUES (the Inside-View's monopsony channel — ISIC Q is 60-80% publicly funded, net interest goes 2% -> 3% of GDP, so the administered price rises ~25-35% real against a roughly doubled true willingness-to-pay, the wedge realized as unmet-need hours and millions of additional informal carers). The two have OPPOSITE signs on both core inflation and measured GDP, nothing in the locked 2A block adjudicates between them, and the gap is worth ~0.10-0.15 pp on back-half core and ~8 points of CQ6 C-versus-D mass. I split it rather than resolved it. SECOND: the level of the nominal anchor. Granting the Red-Team's core-goods rigidity without his target drift is a defensible but uncomfortable halfway house — the two arguments share a premise about nominal behaviour under fiscal stress, and if he is right about the second I am ~8 points low on CQ2 and ~6 low on CQ6-C. THIRD: CQ1's second conjunct has no published resolving series. Eurostat SES is quadrennial with the 2034 vintage landing after resolution, OECD.Stat holds average annual wages and decile ratios rather than sectoral medians, and the panel could not agree whether a strict resolver defaults NO (Auditor) or whether a composition-controlled proxy stitch is likely (Fermi, at 0.20). That 0.20-versus-0 disagreement alone spans CQ1 from 6 to 12, and no amount of macro reasoning narrows it.
wave_audit.biggest_update: The largest single numeric update from a Wave-1 modal position to my reconciled number is CQ6-D: 20 points down, from the Inside-View panelist's 34 to my 14. Two causes, both named and sized. The Auditor's audited EM-OECD floor accounts for ~6 points — D requires 2032-2036 GDP-weighted OECD-38 core BELOW 2.00% on a basket containing Turkey, Mexico, Chile, Colombia and Costa Rica, which with a ~+0.30 pp floor means G7 core at ~1.65-1.70, a deeper Japanification than the narrative pictures; this is index construction, not macro. The Red-Team's demonstration of an internal contradiction in the Inside-View's back half accounts for ~8-10 points: excess electrical capacity and a trades-constrained under-build cannot both hold, and resolving toward under-build makes the back half energy- and shelter-inflationary while still growth-poor, which is regime C rather than D. The remainder is my own core-central revision from the Inside-View's ~1.9 to 2.35 for the 2032-2036 window. Runner-up updates, for scale: CQ6-C up 6 from Wave 1's modal ~11 to 17 (core-goods rigidity plus half the care-price politics); CQ4's P10 up 50 bp from the Wave-1 modal 0.55-0.80 to 1.05 (repression and inflation as substitutes); and CQ3's P50 up 0.15 pp from the Inside-View's 1.60 to 1.75 (measured-NBS China leg plus the Baumol double-count correction). CQ2 moved barely at all — 36/39 modal to 38 — but for entirely rebuilt reasons on both legs, which is the kind of movement a reconciler should flag rather than hide.

efforts.effort_name: Equilibrium Real Rates r*, Fiscal Dominance & Term Premia

wave1.lens_self_description: I answered only from the widest defensible historical reference classes and their frequencies — decade and rolling-window distributions of OECD+China growth, G7 real yields, MOVE, equity drawdowns and bond co-movement, OECD unemployment, sectoral wage divergence and impaired capex supercycles — adjusting solely for the mechanical arithmetic in the locked priors (headcount, weights, debt accounting), and I forbade myself any reasoning about AI capability trajectories, model progress, diffusion mechanics, or any episode-specific causal story.
wave1.cq1_reasoning: Reference class 1 (unemployment): OECD-total harmonised rate, annual series 1970-2025. Rolling 5-yr averages <=5.5% occur in roughly 7-9 of ~52 windows (the early-1970s cluster, OECD total ~3.2-4.3%, then nothing until the 2021-2026 cluster) = unconditional ~15%. Conditioning is legitimate and large: current prints are 5.0% (2022) and ~4.8-4.9% (2023-25) with the FRED 15+ quarterly series in a 4.7-5.3% band (series discontinued/respliced, caveat preserved), and the 2A headcount decline is near-deterministic arithmetic that lowers the trend rate ~0.3-0.5pp by the mid-2030s. Binding constraint is recessions, not trend: base rate of >=1 OECD-wide recession in a 5-yr window is ~55-65%, and a typical one adds 0.8-1.5pp to a 5-yr average, pushing 4.9% to ~6.0-6.3%. So P(conjunct 1) = P(no OECD recession 2032-36) ~0.35 + P(recession mild enough given lower trend) ~0.10 x 0.65 => 0.42. Reference class 2 (wage divergence): base rate of a sustained >=10pp cumulative real-median-hourly divergence between two broad sector groups over 11 years (0.87pp/yr) is not rare in the abstract, but the REQUIRED DIRECTION is physical/care over cognitive, against 40+ years of a widening cognitive skill premium in nearly every OECD member. Observed episodes in that direction: the 1970s compressed-wage-structure years in several members, and partially 2020-2024 in the US (hospitality/construction over professional services, ~5-8pp over 4 yrs) — but health/social care specifically did NOT keep pace because Q is fiscally administered, and 2A's arithmetic (OECD net interest 2%->3% of GDP, China pension subsidies ~10.1% of fiscal expenditure) tightens that funding, not loosens it. Additional mechanical drag: median-wage composition bias — attrition concentrated at the junior/low end of J+K+M mechanically RAISES the measured cognitive median, working against the required gap. P(conjunct 2) = 0.14. Correlation: positive, both legs ride labour tightness; latent rho ~ +0.30, lifting P(C2|C1) from 0.14 to ~0.21. Joint = 0.42 x 0.21 = 0.088 -> 9.
wave1.cq2_reasoning: Conjunct A (OECD-38 GDP-weighted core >=2.50%/yr, 2027-2036). Reference class: rolling 10-yr averages of OECD GDP-weighted core since 1970. Decade approximations: 1970s ~8-9%, 1980s ~6%, 1990s ~3.0-3.5%, 2000s ~1.9-2.1%, 2010s ~1.5%, 2016-2025 ~2.6-2.8%. Within the inflation-targeting era (~30 windows from 1996) only ~8 clear 2.5%, and every one of those contains 2021-2023 — which is OUT of the 2027-2036 window. Base rate of a G7-wide 10-yr target overshoot of >=50bp since targets began: one episode, driven by a single shock. Mechanical upward adjustments I allow: fiscal arithmetic (net interest 2%->3% of GDP, 3-yr P95 Debt-at-Risk ~117%) and near-deterministic labour-force shrinkage; repression, if chosen, works precisely by running inflation above nominal yields. P(A) = 0.33. Conjunct B (China headline CPI <1.50%/yr, 2027-2036). Reference class: Japan post-1995 as the only clean large-economy analogue for a post-working-age-peak, post-property-bust Asian economy — 10-yr CPI averages of 0.0% (1995-2005), ~0.3% (2005-2015), ~0.5% (2010-2020). China's own 2020-2025 run is already ~0.8% (2023 +0.2%, 2024 +0.2%, 2025 ~0.0%), and 2A gives -60M population 2026-2035 with worker/retiree 4.4->2.8. Discounts for reflation attempts, RMB pass-through, food/energy shocks, methodology, and the 10-yr length. P(B) = 0.66. Correlation: NEGATIVE. Chinese goods deflation is a direct mechanical drag on OECD core goods (core CPI/PCE includes core goods), so B pushes against A. Latent rho ~ -0.25, so P(A|B) falls from 0.33 to ~0.27. Joint = 0.66 x 0.27 = 0.178 -> 18. The joint is not tiny only because a services/goods bifurcation (OECD care+construction services hot, Chinese tradables deflating) is the one historically observed configuration that satisfies both.
wave1.cq3_reasoning: Reference class A (unconditional): 5-yr windows of OECD+China PPP-weighted real growth since 1960. The combined measure has essentially never averaged below 2%/yr over any 5-yr window because China carried it through every OECD downturn (2007-2011: OECD ~0.5%, China ~9.9%, combined at then-weights ~2.4%). Monotonically declining OECD component: ~4.5% (1960s), ~3.2% (1970s), ~3.0% (1980s), ~2.6% (1990s), ~2.0% (2000s), ~1.9% (2010s), ~1.7% (2015-2024). Mapped to CQ6 bands at 2032-36 weights, the unconditional history puts most historical windows in A or B. Reference class B (the convergence analogue, which dominates): China at ~$28-30k PPP/capita in 2032 is roughly Japan 1985 / Korea 2005. Post-demographic-peak large-economy 5-yr windows: Japan 4.5% (1980s) -> 1.4% (1990s) -> 0.9% (2000s); Korea 7% -> 4% -> 2.9% -> ~2%. That class gives China 2032-36 at 2-4%/yr, P50 ~3.0%. Mechanical arithmetic (the only adjustment my lens permits, and it is decisive): PPP weights 2032-36 approximately OECD-38 0.63 / China 0.37 (OECD-38 ~$75T PPP, China ~$40T PPP in 2025, China's share rising). OECD-38 = per-capita + population: 2A's locked 0.6%/yr per capita baseline plus ~+0.1 to +0.2%/yr population gives ~0.7-0.8% baseline, ~1.0-1.4% with a partial productivity offset. Combined P50 = 0.63 x 1.2 + 0.37 x 3.0 = 0.76 + 1.11 = 1.87%; at the optimistic corner of each (1.4 / 3.2) = 2.06%. Set P50 = 1.95%. Dispersion: historical 5-yr-window SD of this combined series is ~0.8-1.0pp; a 5-yr average damps but does not remove recessions (>=1 OECD-wide recession in a 5-yr window has a ~55-65% base rate), and at 2032 weights an OECD-zero/China-1% bust prints ~0.4%. P10 = 0.95, P90 = 2.85 (sigma ~0.74 with a slight left skew). The 2A claim that aging slows global growth ~-1.1pp/yr (-2.7pp in China) against a +0.4pp healthy-aging offset is consistent with this central value; I treat the net as already inside the convergence base rate rather than additive to it.
wave1.cq4_reasoning: FIRST, a mechanical restatement of the anchor, which the brief's framing invites getting wrong: US 10y TIPS ~2.60% (FRED DFII10, Oct 30 2026) is NOT the G7 GDP-weighted level. At approximate market-FX GDP weights (US ~0.55, Japan ~0.10, Germany ~0.09, UK ~0.07, France ~0.06, Italy ~0.05, Canada ~0.05) and plausible current component real 10y yields (US 2.6, JP ~0.6, DE ~1.1, UK ~1.6, FR ~1.4, IT ~2.0, CA ~1.9), the GDP-weighted starting level is ~1.95-2.00%. Reference class (decade averages of G7 real 10y yields): 1970s negative to ~0% (real rates negative for much of the decade per RBA Bulletin Oct 1991); 1980s ~+4 to +5% (Macrobond: US real 10y ~5% post-inflation, best decade in its series); 1990s ~+3 to +3.5%; 2000s ~+2.0%; 2010s ~+0.1 to +0.3% GDP-weighted (US 10y TIPS ~0.2% average 2009-2021 per QIC; US median real yield 2.7% for 1962-2007 vs 0.4% post-2008 per Renaissance — figures not independently verified); 2020-2025 ~+0.4% (negative 2020-21, +1.8-2.2% 2023-25). Unconditional range across six decades: roughly -1% to +5%. Base rate of a decade-average real yield staying near its starting level: LOW — 4 of 5 decade transitions moved >=100bp, mean absolute decade-over-decade change ~200bp. But the long-run 1960-2025 G7 GDP-weighted mean is ~1.8-2.2%, so the starting level ~2.0% already SITS on the reversion target. Mean reversion therefore implies near-zero central drift with very wide bands — the opposite of what the 2.60% framing suggests. Decomposition r* + real term premium - repression wedge: (i) r*: G7 GDP-weighted ~0.8-1.0% on HLW-style estimates (US 0.7-1.5, euro area/Japan 0.2-0.8). Boomer dissaving and physical/grid capex demand push up; precautionary saving under labour-income uncertainty, cognitive-compression income loss, and the Chinese/OECD savings gluts push down. 2A itself concedes a frictionless r* may EASE. Central contribution +1.0, 1-sigma ~0.45. (ii) Real term premium: ~+0.5 to +1.0pp pre-2008, ~-0.5pp under QE 2012-2020, +0.5 to +1.0 in 2023-26. Rising rollover volumes, eroding sovereign convenience yields, and levered basis-trade absorption as a fragile marginal buyer push up; the historical debt-to-real-yield elasticity is weak (Japan 1990-2020: debt 65%->250% of GDP while real yields FELL; US 1945-1980: debt falling while real yields negative), so I allow only ~1-3bp per pp of debt/GDP: +25pp x 2bp = +50bp. Central contribution +0.9, 1-sigma ~0.60. (iii) Repression wedge: a genuine policy branch, not a tail. Base rate of at least one G7 sovereign under de facto yield management in a post-1945 5-yr window is very high (1945-1980 sustained G7 repression; Japan YCC 2016-2024; ECB PEPP/TPI spread management). GDP-weighted magnitude is what matters: ~45% x ~100bp (materially binding) + ~30% x ~25bp (mild) => expected -0.55pp, central -0.5, 1-sigma ~0.45. Central = 1.0 + 0.9 - 0.5 = 1.4%; I weight this 40% against the 60%-weighted base-rate/mean-reversion anchor of ~2.0-2.1% to land P50 = 1.95%. VARIANCE ATTRIBUTION: real term premium ~55%, r* ~25%, repression wedge ~20%. The term premium carries most of it, which is exactly what the 2A (r - g) claim is about: that claim is fiscal arithmetic and premium, not an r* claim, and my decomposition keeps r* nearly flat while letting the premium and the wedge fight. Bands respect the decade base rate: ~33% of historical decades were below +1.0% (1970s, 2010s) and ~33% above +3.0% (1980s, 1990s), so P10 = 0.65, P90 = 3.35.
wave1.cq5_reasoning: Conjunct A (MOVE 10-yr average >=105, 2027-2036). Reference class: MOVE since inception 1988 (Bloomberg dates the data to 1988). Reported long-run averages conflict and neither is an official series statistic: ~103 since inception (TS Academy) vs ~85 (an informal TradingView chart idea); I weight the ~103 figure more. Decade approximations: 1988-1999 ~100-110 (1994, 1998), 2000-2009 ~100-105, 2010-2019 ~70-75 (QE suppression), 2020-2025 ~95-105 (2022-23 spikes to 140-190; 2025 opened 96.67, closed 63.96 per Convextrade, with Bloomberg reporting ~59 at end-2025, lowest since Oct 2021 and the steepest annual drop since 2009). Fraction of overlapping 10-yr windows averaging >=105: roughly 12-16 of ~27 => ~45-55% unconditional. Conditioning cuts this hard: the window STARTS from a volatility trough near 60, and the arithmetic of a 10-yr average is unforgiving — a 2-yr spike at 150 plus 8 years at 75 averages 90, not 105. Clearing 105 requires ~4-5 years above 130 or a durably higher baseline, i.e. a persistent regime shift, not one episode. P(A) = 0.25. Conjunct B: (i) base rate of an MSCI World >=25% peak-to-trough drawdown within a 10-yr window — episodes since 1970: 1973-74 (-43%), 1980-82 (-27%), 1987 (~-22 to -24%, borderline), 1990 (-26%), 2000-02 (-49%), 2007-09 (-57%), 2020 (-34%), 2022 (-26%) => ~7-8 in 55 years, one per ~7-8 years, so ~88% of 10-yr windows contain one. (ii) CONDITIONAL on a drawdown, the historical frequency that G7 10y nominals failed to fall >=50bp (or rose >=25bp) during the drawdown window: yes in 1973-74 (yields rose on the inflation shock), 1990 (US 10y ~8.5%->9.0% in the Aug-Oct oil shock), 2022 (yields rose sharply) = 3; no in 1980-82, Oct 1987 (US 10y fell ~90bp post-crash), 2000-02, 2007-09, 2020 = 5. Frequency 3/8 = ~37%, and critically all three "yes" cases were inflationary/supply-shock regimes rather than flight-to-quality regimes. Take 0.36. P(B) = 0.88 x 0.36 = 0.32. Correlation: strongly POSITIVE — a >=105 decade-average MOVE and a correlated equity-bond selloff are the same inflation-volatility regime. Latent rho ~ +0.55, so P(B|A) rises from 0.32 to ~0.65. Joint = 0.25 x 0.65 = 0.163; I round up to 17 for the 2A mechanical pressures that raise both legs (rollover volumes, eroding convenience yields, basis-trade fragility as the marginal buyer, Debt-at-Risk P95 117% rising 2.4pp more under a 20% AI-led valuation shock).
wave1.cq6_reasoning: Built mechanically from my own CQ3 distribution and a CQ2-consistent inflation distribution, under the lexical priority lock. Step 1 — growth bands from CQ3 (P10 0.95 / P50 1.95 / P90 2.85, sigma ~0.74, slight left skew): P(g>=2.6) = 0.16, P(2.0<=g<2.6) = 0.29, P(1.7<=g<2.0) = 0.16, P(g<1.7) = 0.39. Step 2 — inflation: P(OECD-38 GDP-weighted core 2032-36 >= 2.7%) = 0.25 (base rate: only the 2019-23 and 2021-25 windows clear 2.7% as 5-yr averages in the whole inflation-targeting era, ~5 of 30 = 17%, adjusted up for 2A's fiscal arithmetic); P(core < 2.0%) = 0.38. Step 3 — lexical allocation, first match wins: band g>=2.6 -> A entirely = 0.16. Band 2.0-2.6 -> always B (rule 2 needs g<2.0, rule 3 needs g<1.7) = 0.29. Band 1.7-2.0 -> C if core>=2.7 (conditional 0.33, supply-constraint stories elevated at low growth) = 0.053, else B = 0.107. Band g<1.7 -> conditional split 0.30 core>=2.7 / 0.45 core<2.0 / 0.25 in between: C += 0.117, D = 0.176, B += 0.098. Totals A 0.16, B 0.495, C 0.170, D 0.176 -> 16 / 49 / 17 / 18, summing to exactly 100. CONSISTENCY CHECK vs my CQ3: A is identically P(g>=2.6) = 16 by construction; my P50 of 1.95% sits in the residual-B cell, and B is the plurality precisely because the lock makes it the residual that absorbs both the 1.7-2.5% band and the low-growth/moderate-inflation leftover cell. CONSISTENCY CHECK vs my CQ2: this table implies P(core 2032-36 >= 2.7%) = C mass 0.17 plus the core>=2.7 cells that lexically land in A or B (0.29 x 0.15 + 0.16 x 0.20 = 0.075) = ~0.245, matching the 0.25 I assumed, and coherent with the 0.33 I gave CQ2's conjunct A at the lower 2.50% threshold over the longer 2027-2036 window. Note B's 49 is NOT a hedge toward the centre: it is the arithmetic consequence of a left-of-2.0% modal growth number colliding with a lock that routes low-growth/moderate-inflation outcomes into B rather than C or D.

hypothesis_critique.a: "SMOOTHLY" carries the failure. The base rate of frictionless cross-occupational reallocation is effectively zero: the China-shock literature finds displaced manufacturing workers' earnings never fully recovered and local labour markets adjusted over 15+ years, not 5; UK coal 1984-2000 and the US Rust Belt are the same story. Add two pieces of pure arithmetic: the care deficit is denominated in millions of FTEs in wage-regulated, fiscally funded Q, while 2A's fiscal block is tightening (net interest 2%->3% of GDP), and care credentialing runs 1-3 years. Base rate of reallocating >2% of employment across broad sectors within a decade with no measurable wage or unemployment friction: no clean historical instance. The plank could be right on DIRECTION and still fail entirely on "smoothly".
hypothesis_critique.b: "BLOCKS" and "SEVERELY" both fail, and they fail for different reasons. "Blocks" is a total-substitution claim; the base rate of a technology ending an offshoring corridor within a decade is zero observed cases — corridors historically move up-market instead. "Severely" ignores both scale and channel: Philippine BPO is ~1.3-1.7M workers and India IT-BPM ~5.4M, each ~7-8% of GDP in receipts, large but not the growth engine (India's growth is domestically driven), and PHYSICAL labour migration (nurses, carers, seafarers) is the channel 2A's aging OPENS. Remittances to the Philippines run ~8-9% of GDP and have never declined for a sustained period — they rose through 2008-09 and through 2020. The plank also conflates the virtual and physical channels that the scope lock deliberately separates.
hypothesis_critique.c: "THEN" carries the failure — the sequencing is asserted, not derived, and the first clause may already be false at the starting line. Inflation IS strongly mean-reverting under credible targets (post-Volcker, post-1990 G7), so "falls in the 2030s" is close to a restatement of the base rate and deserves credit: my own numbers give 38% to 2032-36 core below 2.0% and only 25% to >=2.7%, so the modal path is indeed reversion. But "runs hot for the next few years" is the weak leg given the locked starting point: OECD core is near target entering 2027 and China is outright deflating, so the plank's own premise is doubtful. Scored 44 because the second clause tracks a strong base rate while the first clause is probably already wrong — a half-correct plank, not a correct one.
hypothesis_critique.d: "EVENTUALLY" and "WINS" both fail, and "eventually" is the worse offender because an unbounded horizon makes the claim unfalsifiable while the resolution date is Dec 31 2036. "Wins" names no threshold. The cleanest historical test is Japan 1995-2025: the world's robotics-leading economy, per-capita growth ~0.8%/yr and aggregate ~0.5%/yr — technology did not outrun demography in AGGREGATE output. Germany, Italy and Korea repeat it. Base rate of "technology will offset demography" claims resolving true within ~10 years of the claim: roughly 1 in 5-8 historically, and never inside a decade — electricity took 30-40 years to show in TFP, IT gave the Solow paradox 1973-1995 then one 1995-2004 burst, and Hulten/Baumol ceilings bind the aggregate even when a sector booms. My own arithmetic agrees: coupled growth >=2.6%/yr gets 16%, and the locked AI-Q1 marginal for >=+0.50pp/yr TFP is 23%.

key_drivers: Conjunction arithmetic. Three of six CQs are conjunctions, and two of them (CQ2, implicitly CQ1 via composition bias) have legs that pull against each other. Multiplying named marginals rather than scoring the narrative is what drives CQ1 to 9, CQ2 to 18 and CQ5 to 17 — all far below what the component stories read like.

Mechanical headcount, which cuts both ways in CQ1. OECD-38 labour-force shrinkage is near-deterministic and lowers the unemployment TREND by ~0.3-0.5pp (helping conjunct 1) while lowering aggregate growth (hurting CQ3 and CQ6-A). The 2A demand-pull for automation does not raise measured unemployment.

Weight-times-rate arithmetic for CQ3. OECD-38 at ~0.63 PPP weight x ~1.2%/yr plus China at ~0.37 x ~3.0%/yr mechanically caps coupled growth near 1.9-2.0%, which forces CQ6-A to ~16 and makes B the lexical residual regardless of any AI story.

Recomposition of the CQ4 anchor. The US TIPS 2.60% starting point maps to a G7 GDP-weighted ~1.95-2.00%, which happens to sit on the 1960-2025 long-run mean — so mean reversion over a 6-10 year horizon implies near-zero central drift, and the honest answer is a wide band around the current level, not a decline from 2.60%.

Term-premium dominance of CQ4 variance (~55% premium, ~25% r*, ~20% repression wedge). Decade-to-decade G7 real-yield shifts average ~200bp and are driven by regime and premium, not by r*; the historical debt-to-real-yield elasticity is weak (Japan 1990-2020), so fiscal arithmetic enters through the premium exactly as 2A's (r - g) claim implies, and financial repression is a ~45% materially-binding policy branch rather than a tail.

Direction-of-divergence base rate for CQ1's second leg. Forty-plus years of a widening cognitive skill premium, plus median-wage composition bias (junior-end attrition in J+K+M mechanically raises the measured cognitive median), plus fiscally administered Q wages, make the required F+Q > J+K+M by 10pp a low-frequency event specifically in the direction asked.

It also pushes CQ4's P90 up ~40bp via the real term premium and adds ~4pp to CQ6-C at B's expense.

It raises CQ5 conjunct A, adds ~4pp to CQ6-C and removes ~5pp from CQ6-D (high real yields are inconsistent with a savings-glut demand shortfall).

It lowers CQ5 conjunct A (managed curves suppress MOVE) taking CQ5 to ~11, and shifts ~4pp of CQ6 mass from C into B and D, since repression trades a term-premium spike for a slower-growth, administered-rate equilibrium.

wave1.coupling_tension: Two 2B marginals cannot survive endogenous demographics at their locked values, and both fail through the COST OF CAPITAL — the channel 2B necessarily held fixed when it held demographics exogenous. (1) AI-Q3 (data-centre TWh, P50 998) and AI-Q4 (66% impairment/revenue-shortfall) are jointly too optimistic on capital cost and must move in OPPOSITE directions. The 2A block — rising public-debt rollover volumes, eroding sovereign convenience yields, levered hedge-fund basis-trade absorption as the fragile marginal buyer, 3-yr P95 Debt-at-Risk ~117% rising a further 2.4pp under a 20% AI-led valuation shock, and ~$1.4T of circular vendor/cloud/chip commitments backed by only ~$300B equity and ~$650B debt — raises the real term premium that any physical AI and grid buildout must clear. A higher hurdle rate mechanically LOWERS equilibrium data-centre deployment (Q3 P50 should fall from 998 toward ~900 TWh) and RAISES the impairment probability (Q4 should rise from 66% toward ~72%), because Q4's threshold is defined against ANNOUNCED buildouts underwritten at a lower cost of capital, and because its second limb compares external revenue to compute D&A, which is a function of capitalized capex priced at the old discount rate. The partial offset is self-referential: a lower Q3 shrinks the installed base whose D&A the revenue test measures against, so Q4 cannot rise by the full amount the hurdle-rate shift implies. Direction: Q3 down, Q4 up, with Q4's move damped. (2) AI-Q1 (23% for >=+0.50pp/yr TFP) and AI-Q5 (38% for >=3.5pp cognitive labour-share compression) are priced too close to independent. With demographics endogenous, 2A's fiscal arithmetic means that compressing J/K/M labour compensation erodes the income-tax base funding the very transfers the old-age ratio is inflating (OECD net interest 2%->3% of GDP; China pension subsidies ~10.1% of fiscal expenditure), forcing either a higher tax wedge or financial repression — both of which lower MEASURED TFP through misallocation. So a high-Q5 world should carry a LOWER Q1 than independent marginals imply. The locked pair therefore over-states the joint "white-collar compression WITH broad productivity" cell, which is precisely the cell CQ6-A needs, and is one reason my A is 16 rather than near the standalone 2B Transformative Breakout figure of 16.2% plus a coupling bonus. Net direction across both tensions: the coupled world is more capital-cost-constrained and less productivity-solvent than 2B's exogenous-demographics marginals read, which pushes mass from CQ6-A into B and D rather than into C.

wave1.lens_self_description: Inside-view causal-mechanism modeler: I built an explicit transmission chain for loanable funds, fiscal arithmetic and term premia with numeric elasticities on each arrow and let the mechanism set the numbers; I forbade myself any appeal to historical base rates, frequency of recessions/drawdowns, or "yields have averaged X" anchoring, using the Oct-2026 level only as a starting condition for a mean-reversion mechanism.
wave1.cq1_reasoning: CHAIN: [65+/20-64 +9pp 2024->2036] --(+, care-hours demand +2.2%/yr)--> [Q-sector labour demand] --(+)--> [care shadow price +45-70% real] --BUT--(payer is fiscally constrained state; net interest 2%->3% of GDP, debt>100%)--> [measured Q median real wage only +8-15%]; the excess is cleared as RATIONING (vacancies, waiting lists, patient:staff ratios, informal family care), not as price. Second chain: [AI-Q5 cognitive compensation-share fall] --(+)--> [J/K/M compensation share down] --(composition, -)--> [J/K/M MEDIAN wage UP, because the lowest-paid junior/entry rungs are cut first]. Share-down and median-up are fully compatible; the question asks about the median, so the compression story does NOT deliver conjunct 2. CONJUNCT A (OECD-38 harmonized unemployment avg <=5.5%, 2032-36): mechanism is denominator-driven - OECD working-age population falls ~0.3%/yr, so a given level of labour demand clears at lower measured unemployment; offset by white-collar re-matching frictions (+0.3-0.5pp structural) and the post-capex-digestion demand shortfall. Marginal = 0.62. CONJUNCT B (F+Q minus J+K+M real median hourly wage differential >= +10.0pp cumulative 2025-2036, i.e. >=0.90pp/yr): requires the care shadow price to pass through to the measured median against a fiscally constrained payer, AND requires J/K/M median not to be lifted by composition. Both must fail-to-fail. Marginal = 0.26. CORRELATION: both live in the labour-scarcity branch, rho = +0.25. Joint = 0.62*0.26 = 0.161, correlation lift to ~0.19. Answer 18 (shaded a point for the 11-year cumulative measurement risk in F, where construction is cyclical and a capex bust hits F median hard mid-window).
wave1.cq2_reasoning: CONJUNCT A (GDP-weighted OECD-38 core >= 2.50%/yr avg 2027-2036): build it by weight, not by base rate. US ~45% of OECD-38 GDP, euro area ~30%, Japan ~9%, rest ~16%. Mechanism per bloc: US core PCE 2.6-2.8 (care/construction Baumol + tariff/fragmentation + fiscal dominance), euro 2.1-2.3 (grid+defence capex into a shrinking workforce, but weak demand), Japan 1.7-1.9, rest ~2.3. Weighted central = 0.45*2.70 + 0.30*2.20 + 0.09*1.80 + 0.16*2.30 = 1.215+0.660+0.162+0.368 = 2.41%/yr. So the threshold sits ~0.1pp ABOVE my mechanical center, and a 10-year average has little variance (sigma ~0.25pp). P(A) = 0.40. CONJUNCT B (China headline CPI avg < 1.50%/yr, 2027-2036): mechanism - population -60M, household income share low, savings rate high and PRECAUTIONARY precisely because pension promises are underfunded, property-collateral deflation hangover, and excess tradable capacity exported. The only reflation channel is the fiscal one: pension/social-security subsidies already 2.9T RMB (10.1% of fiscal expenditure) rising toward 15%+, which is a transfer to high-MPC retirees. P(B) = 0.72. CORRELATION: negative - China's tradable glut is the disinflationary impulse INTO OECD goods prices, so the OECD-hot branch is slightly less likely when China is cold; but the bifurcation driver (OECD non-tradable bottleneck vs China tradable glut) is common and positive. Net rho = -0.10. Joint = 0.40*0.72 = 0.288, shade to 0.27. Answer 27.
wave1.cq3_reasoning: Growth-accounting mechanism, not a base rate. WEIGHTS at 2032 (PPP, constant 2025 USD): within the OECD-38+China bloc, OECD ~0.68, China ~0.32. OECD-38 2032-36: per-capita 0.6%/yr (Section 2A, aging-adjusted, taken as given) + population +0.25%/yr (migration-driven; the physical-migration channel is a DEMAND pull, not blocked) = 0.85%; plus expected AI TFP lift, taken from the 2B regime mix as an expectation (0.162*0.70 + 0.472*0.35 + 0.365*0.05 = +0.30pp) ; minus post-capex digestion drag in the 2032-36 window, which is exactly when a 2027-2032 impairment event (AI-Q4 66%) shows up as a lower investment contribution: -0.15pp. OECD P50 = 0.85+0.30-0.15 = 1.15%/yr. CHINA 2032-36: labour -0.80pp (working-age -1.3%/yr x labour share 0.45, net of +0.2pp from retirement-age/participation reform); capital +1.75pp (investment share 38%->33%, ICOR deteriorating as the marginal project is grid/DC rather than housing); TFP +1.30pp (China is the strongest automation-demand-pull case in the world: worker/retiree 4.4->2.8 forces robot and AI substitution, and the wage signal is domestic); fiscal pension drag -0.45pp (subsidy 10.1%->15%+ of expenditure crowds public investment). China P50 = 2.80%/yr. COMBINED P50 = 0.68*1.15 + 0.32*2.80 = 0.78+0.90 = 1.68 -> report 1.75 (small upward nudge for the labour-scarcity acceleration of diffusion, below). P10 = 0.95: capex bust is deep, repression binds, OECD at 0.5 and China at 1.9. P90 = 2.65: Transformative Breakout plus China holding 3.6% and OECD at 2.1. This P50 is far below the 2015-2024 realized bloc path (~2.7%/yr) and I am deliberately not pulling it back toward that frequency - the mechanism says the China capital/labour engine decelerates structurally and the OECD per-capita base is halved by the age structure.
wave1.cq4_reasoning:
DECOMPOSITION: real yield = r* + real term premium - repression wedge. Measured today, G7 GDP-weighted (US 0.52, Japan 0.12, Germany 0.12, UK 0.08, France 0.08, Italy 0.06, Canada 0.05): 0.52*2.60 + 0.12*0.60 + 0.12*1.00 + 0.08*1.50 + 0.08*1.30 + 0.06*1.90 + 0.05*1.60 = 1.96%. The US 2.60% TIPS lock is NOT the G7 number; the G7 aggregate is ~0.65pp below it, and most of the 2032-36 change is Japanese and euro-area convergence UP, not US mean reversion.
ARROW DIAGRAM (sign, magnitude on r* or TP in bp, 2036 vs 2025):
[65+ share +9pp] --(-, desired-wealth/longer-retirement-horizon channel, Auclert-Malmberg-Martenet-Rognlie direction)--> [r*: -20]
[65+ share +9pp] --(+, life-cycle decumulation flow)--> [r*: +35]  // 65+ hold ~40% of OECD net worth, net worth/GDP ~4.5x, so 1.8x GDP drawn down at ~1.5%/yr = -2.7% of GDP saving flow, offset by the 45-64 cohort's +2.2% of GDP: net desired saving -0.5 to -1.0% of GDP
[public debt/GDP +15pp G7-weighted] --(+, supply)--> [TP: +38]
[convenience-yield erosion + levered basis-trade as fragile marginal buyer] --(+)--> [TP: +25, and +60 conditional on stress]
[AI/grid physical capex, +1.0-1.5pp of GDP investment demand 2027-2031] --(+)--> [r*: +40 in 2027-31, then -25 in 2032-36 if AI-Q4 resolves YES] --> net 2032-36: [r*: -10]
