[Debt-at-Risk P95 117% of GDP, +2.4pp on a 20% AI equity shock] --(trigger)--> [repression: YCC / captive bank+insurer demand / duration shortening] --(-)--> [wedge: -45 to -80bp when active]
ELASTICITIES I AM RELYING ON (three named):
(1) d(long real yield)/d(debt/GDP) = +2.5bp per pp. Justification: Laubach (2009) estimates 3-4bp per pp of projected debt; I haircut to 2.5 because a meaningful share of the G7 increment is absorbed by regulatory-captive domestic buyers whose demand is price-inelastic. +15pp G7-weighted -> +38bp, booked to TERM PREMIUM not r*, which is exactly the Section 2A distinction: aging worsens (r-g) by ~+1.0pp through the fiscal-arithmetic and term-premium channels EVEN IF frictionless r* eases.
(2) d(r*)/d(desired saving) = -35bp per 1pp of GDP. Justification: standard loanable-funds/IS slope used in the Rachel-Summers accounting; implies the -0.5 to -1.0pp of GDP net demographic saving flow is worth +18 to +35bp on r*.
(3) saving-rate semi-elasticity to income concentration = +0.25pp of GDP per 1pp of income shifted from labour to capital/top. Justification: Mian-Straub-Sufi saving-glut-of-the-rich MPS differential ~0.25-0.35. AI-Q5's 3.5pp compensation-share fall over J/K/M (~25% of OECD GVA) = ~0.9pp of GVA shifted -> +0.22pp of GDP saving -> -8 to -9bp on r*.
BUILD: G7 r* 2032-36 = 0.95% (today ~0.90%; +35 dissaving, -20 desired wealth, +12 China fiscal, -9 compression, -15 precautionary, -10 net capex cycle = +(-7)bp, essentially flat, with Japan's own r* rising as the BoJ exits). G7 real term premium 2032-36 = 1.35% (today ~1.05%; +38 supply, +25 convenience/plumbing, -30 from a structurally lower-growth, lower-inflation-volatility China anchor on global duration demand... net +33bp). Expected repression wedge = -0.35% (P(explicit or de facto repression in at least one major G7, active for part of the window) = 0.60; conditional wedge -55bp G7-weighted; 0.60*-0.55 = -0.33). P50 = 0.95 + 1.35 - 0.35 = 1.95%.
VARIANCE ATTRIBUTION: ~45% of my variance is in the REAL TERM PREMIUM (debt supply x convenience yield x whether the levered basis-trade buyer is present at the clearing price), ~30% in the REPRESSION WEDGE (a bimodal policy switch, not a smooth distribution), ~25% in r*. r* carries the least variance because its demographic sub-channels (+35 dissaving vs -20 desired wealth vs -15 precautionary) partially cancel by construction. P10 = 1.05% (repression on in the US and euro area simultaneously after an AI-led equity shock, plus post-bust excess capacity collapsing investment demand). P90 = 3.10% (no repression, capex sustained, convenience yield erodes hard, Japan converges fully; the US alone at ~3.6% real).
wave1.cq5_reasoning: CONJUNCT A (MOVE avg >= 105 over 2027-2036): mechanism for rate vol is (i) duration supply uncertainty from the 100%+ debt/GDP rollover schedule, (ii) a marginal buyer (levered hedge-fund basis trade) whose balance-sheet capacity is itself a function of repo haircuts, so the price-elasticity of the clearing bid is state-dependent, and (iii) a bimodal repression switch - markets must price both the no-intervention and the YCC branch, which mechanically fattens the rate-vol distribution. Against: if r* and inflation both settle low in a demand-shortfall world, rate vol compresses toward the lower bound. A ten-year AVERAGE >=105 needs the high-vol regime to dominate roughly two-thirds of the window. P(A) = 0.52. CONJUNCT B (at least one episode: MSCI World -25% peak-to-trough WHILE G7 10y nominal fails to fall >=50bp, or rises >=25bp, in the drawdown window): decompose. P(>=25% MSCI World drawdown at some point 2027-2036) = 0.70 - driven by the $1.4T circular vendor/cloud/chip commitment structure on ~$300B equity and ~$650B debt, index concentration in the AI complex, and the 66% AI-Q4 impairment marginal. Conditional on the drawdown, P(bonds FAIL to rally >=50bp) = 0.40: an AI-capex-bust drawdown is disinflationary and bonds WOULD rally, so the correlation-breakdown branch requires the drawdown to be fiscally or supply driven (duration indigestion, care/grid cost-push, a failed auction, a repression announcement) rather than demand driven. P(B) = 0.70*0.40 = 0.28. CORRELATION: strongly positive, rho = +0.45 - the same fiscal-dominance/fragile-plumbing mechanism generates both a 105+ MOVE and the loss of the bond hedge. Joint = 0.52*0.28 = 0.146; correlation lift to ~0.23. Answer 23. The conjunction discount is doing real work here: the standalone "bonds stop hedging equities once the sovereign is the risk" story feels near-certain to a mechanism modeler, but it must co-occur with a 25% equity drawdown in the SAME window, and the most likely 25% drawdown cause is the one that makes bonds rally.
wave1.cq6_reasoning: LEXICAL PRIORITY applied in order. (1) A requires coupled CQ3 growth >= 2.6%/yr. My CQ3 distribution has P90 = 2.65, so P(growth >= 2.6) = 0.11 by construction; A = 10 (one point shaded for the measurement asymmetry that PPP-weighting a faster-growing China raises the bloc number mechanically). (2) C requires OECD core >= 2.7% AND growth < 2.0%. From CQ2 I hold P(OECD core >= 2.50% avg) = 0.40 with a mechanical center at 2.41% and sigma ~0.25pp over a ten-year average; P(core >= 2.70%) = 0.28 (CQ2's window is 2027-2036 and CQ6's is 2032-2036, and my care/grid bottleneck mechanism loads the inflation into the later window, so I do NOT shade this down for the shorter window). P(growth < 2.0 | core >= 2.7) = 0.70, positive dependence because the bottleneck that raises the price is the same bottleneck that caps the quantity. C = 0.28*0.70 = 0.196 -> 20. (3) D requires growth < 1.7 AND core < 2.0. With CQ3 P50 = 1.75, P(growth < 1.7) = 0.48; P(core < 2.0 | growth < 1.7) = 0.40 (up from an unconditional ~0.25 because the low-growth branch is predominantly the post-capex-bust, BIS-Box-C labour-income demand shortfall, which is disinflationary). D = 0.48*0.40 = 0.192 -> 19. (4) B is the residual = 100 - 10 - 20 - 19 = 51. CONSISTENCY CHECK PERFORMED: (i) sums to 100 exactly; (ii) my CQ3 P50 of 1.75 sits inside the low-growth half of the distribution, so the mass is correctly concentrated in B plus C plus D (90) and not in A - I have not put most mass on A, consistent with the lock's explicit example; (iii) P(C) = 20 must be <= P(OECD core >= 2.50) = 0.40 implied by my CQ2 conjunct A, and 20 < 40 holds with room, since C needs the stricter 2.7% threshold AND a growth condition; (iv) C + D = 39 against P(growth < 2.0) ~ 0.62 from my CQ3, leaving ~23 points of low-growth-but-moderate-inflation mass inside B, which is exactly the leftover cell the lock assigns to B - internally coherent; (v) CQ2 = 27 (joint with China < 1.5) exceeds P(C) = 20, which is required since CQ2's OECD conjunct is weaker (2.50 vs 2.70) but adds a China condition - the two are mutually consistent at these levels. B at 51 is the mechanism's real answer: physical/care scarcity and hyperscaler rents coexisting with white-collar compression and a steep real term premium IS the bifurcated barbell, and my CQ4 P50 of 1.95% with a 1.35pp real term premium is the barbell's signature price.

hypothesis_critique.a: "smoothly" carries the failure. The reallocation is not a flow-matching problem, it is a three-constraint problem and all three bind: (i) licensure and credentialing - a displaced paralegal or junior analyst cannot be a nurse or a care aide inside 24 months without a regulated training pipeline whose own capacity is fiscally rationed; (ii) geography - care demand is where the 75+ live (small towns, suburbs), cognitive job losses are where the J/K/M firms are (metros); (iii) reservation wage - the fiscally constrained payer sets the care wage BELOW the displaced worker's reservation wage, which is the heart of my CQ1 conjunct-2 reasoning. The mechanism predicts the care shadow price rises 45-70% real by 2036 while the measured wage rises 8-15%, i.e. the gap is cleared by rationing, not by reallocation. Any smooth-supply claim is a quantity story told without a price.
hypothesis_critique.b: "blocks" carries the failure, and "severely" compounds it. AI is a substitute for routine VIRTUAL services (Philippine voice BPO, tier-1 support, basic transcription/coding - this slice is genuinely exposed) but it is a COMPLEMENT to supervised remote professional services (Indian GCCs, accounting, actuarial, clinical documentation), where the binding constraint was never the task, it was the trust and review layer, and AI lowers the cost of that layer. More decisively, the PHYSICAL channel runs the opposite way: OECD 65+ up 9pp with a non-automatable care bottleneck is a structural pull on physical labour migration from exactly these origins, and my weakest-link analysis says its shadow price rises sharply. "Blocks" is wrong on sign for the physical channel and wrong on mechanism for the high-end virtual channel. The plank is partially right only for Philippine voice BPO, roughly 6-7% of Philippine GDP - real, not "severe" at the national-income level.
hypothesis_critique.c: "then falls" carries the failure - the plank has the shape backwards. My mechanism loads non-tradable cost-push INTO the 2030s, not out of them: the 65+/20-64 ratio reaches 39-41% by 2036, which is when care-hours demand, the grid interconnection wall and construction labour scarcity peak simultaneously, and when the fiscal payer is least able to absorb them without monetization. The near-term 2027-2029 window is the one where the AI capex boom is still ADDING supply capacity and goods disinflation from China's glut is still arriving. The honest version of the plank is: moderate now, bottleneck-driven later, with a possible disinflationary air pocket in between if AI-Q4 resolves YES. That said, I score it 22 rather than lower because the 2032-36 demand-shortfall branch (my CQ6-D, 19) is a genuine way the plank's second half comes true for the wrong reason.
hypothesis_critique.d: "eventually" and "wins" both carry the failure. "Eventually" is unfalsifiable at a Dec-2036 horizon and smuggles in a horizon the question does not grant - my CQ3 P50 of 1.75%/yr says it has not happened by then. "Wins" is wrong on two counts: (i) it treats aggregate real GDP as the scoreboard when the demographic question is per-capita and per-worker, and a shrinking denominator can make the aggregate look worse while welfare per head improves; (ii) it ignores the Hulten/Baumol arithmetic - the aggregate TFP contribution of an automated task is bounded by that task's expenditure share, so even very large gains in the cognitive-information slice (ISIC J+K+M, roughly a quarter of OECD GVA) cannot outrun a bottleneck whose expenditure share is RISING because its relative price is rising. Exponential improvement in a shrinking-share input is the definition of a capped system.

key_drivers: Real term premium, not r*: the +2.5bp-per-pp debt-supply elasticity times a ~15pp G7-weighted debt increase, plus convenience-yield erosion and a levered basis-trade marginal buyer whose bid is balance-sheet-state-dependent - this arrow carries ~45% of my CQ4 variance and is the single reason my CQ4 P50 stays near 2% despite a near-flat r*.

The repression wedge as a 0.60-probability bimodal policy switch worth -55bp conditional, not a tail curiosity: given P95 Debt-at-Risk of 117% of GDP and +2.4pp more under a 20% AI-led equity shock, YCC / captive bank-and-insurer demand / deliberate duration shortening is the cheapest available instrument, and it is the main thing holding my CQ4 P10 up at 1.05 rather than pushing the P50 to 2.3.

Partial cancellation inside the demographic r* block: life-cycle decumulation (+35bp via -0.5 to -1.0pp of GDP desired saving at a -35bp-per-pp loanable-funds slope) against the longer-retirement-horizon desired-wealth channel (-20bp) and precautionary saving under labour-income uncertainty (-15bp). This is why I respect the Section 2A distinction: aging worsens (r-g) by ~+1.0pp through fiscal arithmetic and term premia even with a frictionless r* that barely moves.

The weakest link - hands-on elder-care labour, with licensed electricians and HV transformer/interconnection capacity as the secondary wall. Non-substitutable at the 2036 horizon, demand pinned by the 65+ ratio, and priced by a fiscally constrained payer, so its shadow price explodes while its measured wage does not. This single arrow drives my low CQ1, my loading of inflation into the 2030s, and my Hulten ceiling on CQ3.

The capex-cycle sign flip: AI/grid investment demand is +40bp on r* in 2027-2031 and -25bp in 2032-2036 if AI-Q4 resolves YES at its 66% marginal. Because CQ3 and CQ4 are both 2032-2036 AVERAGES, the boom is outside the window and the digestion is inside it - a timing fact that most same-level forecasts of this pair will get backwards.

China as the swing in world saving: pension/social-security subsidies at 10.1% of fiscal expenditure heading past 15% with worker/retiree falling 4.4 to 2.8 converts the world's largest saving surplus into a fiscal claim. +12bp on global r* in my central case, far more if Chinese households stop saving precautionarily because the state finally backstops them - which would also break my 0.72 China-deflation conjunct in CQ2.

falsification_signposts.signpost: G7 GDP-weighted 10y sovereign real yield (10y nominal minus 10y inflation swap) averages below 1.20% for four consecutive quarters with NO announced YCC, captive-demand mandate, or Treasury/DMO duration-shortening program in any G7 sovereign.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: My term-premium-dominant mechanism is wrong - the market is clearing duration at a low price without policy help, meaning convenience yields are intact and the basis-trade buyer is not fragile. Cut CQ4 P50 from 1.95 to ~1.40 and P90 from 3.10 to ~2.40; move ~8 points from CQ6-C to CQ6-D; cut CQ5 conjunct A from 0.52 to ~0.35, taking CQ5 from 23 to ~14.

falsification_signposts.signpost: US 10y TIPS real yield sustains above 3.25% for two consecutive quarters with no Fed balance-sheet, SLR-relief, buyback-tilt, or regulatory captive-demand response, AND G7-weighted real yield above 2.60% in the same window.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: My 0.60 repression probability and -35bp expected wedge are both overstated - authorities are tolerating the fiscal-arithmetic price. Raise CQ4 P50 from 1.95 to ~2.60 and P10 from 1.05 to ~1.60; raise CQ6-C from 20 to ~27 (term-premium-spike branch) at the expense of D; raise CQ5 to ~30 via conjunct B's correlation-breakdown leg.

falsification_signposts.signpost: OECD-wide ISIC-Q (health and social work) real median hourly wage growth runs at least 3.0 percentage points cumulatively ABOVE ISIC J+K+M since 2025, measured in OECD/Eurostat earnings data, with the gap widening rather than closing in the latest two annual prints.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: My core claim that the fiscally constrained payer suppresses the care wage - so scarcity shows up as rationing rather than price - is wrong, and the care shadow price IS passing through. Raise CQ1 conjunct B from 0.26 to ~0.50 and CQ1 overall from 18 to ~32; raise OECD core inflation central from 2.41 to ~2.65, raising CQ2 from 27 to ~38 and CQ6-C from 20 to ~26.

falsification_signposts.signpost: China headline CPI averages 2.0%/yr or more over 2027-2030 while central pension and social-security subsidies exceed 15% of total fiscal expenditure and the household saving rate falls at least 4pp from its 2025 level.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: The Chinese savings-glut/exported-deflation anchor on global duration demand is breaking through the fiscal channel, not the growth channel. CQ2's China conjunct collapses from 0.72 to ~0.25, taking CQ2 from 27 to ~10; add +25 to +35bp to my global r* term, raising CQ4 P50 to ~2.25; raise CQ3 P50 modestly to ~1.90 on stronger Chinese consumption, cutting CQ6-D from 19 to ~12.

falsification_signposts.signpost: Cumulative announced-buildout impairments and cancellations stay below 5% of announced hyperscaler capex AND net external AI software/API revenue exceeds 1.5x annualized AI compute D&A in every quarter of 2031-2032 (i.e. AI-Q4 clearly resolves NO on both legs).
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: My capex-cycle sign flip is wrong: investment demand for loanable funds persists THROUGH the 2032-2036 window instead of reversing. Restore +40bp to r* (net -10 becomes +30), raising CQ4 P50 from 1.95 to ~2.35; raise CQ3 P50 from 1.75 to ~2.20 and CQ6-A from 10 to ~20, pulling mass out of D (19 to ~8); CQ5 conjunct B's drawdown probability falls from 0.70 to ~0.50, taking CQ5 to ~17.

wave1.coupling_tension: AI-Q4 (66% raw: >=20% impairments/cancellations OR net external AI revenue < 0.5x compute D&A for two consecutive years) is INCONSISTENTLY LOW once demographics and the fiscal/rate block are endogenous - it should be roughly 72-76%. The mechanism: 2B prices AI-Q4 against an exogenous cost of capital, but the demographic block endogenizes exactly the discount rate that the buildout is financed at. The ~$650B of AI debt issuance plus ~$300B equity is being raised into a world where (i) G7-weighted real yields average ~1.95% with a 1.35pp real term premium rather than the sub-1% real environment the 2023-2026 commitments were underwritten in, (ii) public debt crossing 100% of GDP with net interest heading to 3% of GDP makes sovereign duration the competing asset, and (iii) the care and grid bottlenecks bid for the same construction labour, electricians, transformers and interconnection slots that data centres need, raising realized capex per MW above plan. Each of these raises the hurdle rate and the realized cost base on a fixed revenue path, and impairment is mechanically a hurdle-rate-versus-realized-revenue test: a +100bp real WACC on a 15-year asset cuts NPV roughly 10-12% and converts a marginal project into a written-down one. Direction: UP on AI-Q4, i.e. MORE impairment than the demographics-exogenous marginal implies. A second, smaller tension runs the same way on AI-Q3: the 998 TWh P50 for 2036 OECD-38+China operational data-centre electricity should sit nearer 880-920 TWh once the interconnection shadow price and the higher WACC are endogenous, because the binding constraint is grid delivery and project finance, not chip supply or demand for tokens. Pulling the other way - and I flag it for honesty rather than netting it out - AI-Q1 and AI-Q2 are inconsistently LOW once the labour-scarcity wage signal is endogenous: a shrinking OECD workforce raises the relative price of substitutable labour and therefore the firm-level business case for adoption, which is a demand pull on diffusion. But that pull operates on ADOPTION (AI-Q2) more than on measured TFP (AI-Q1), because the tasks it pulls hardest on sit in the sectors whose expenditure share is falling, and it does nothing for the non-substitutable care bottleneck whose share is rising - so the Hulten ceiling absorbs most of it, and the AI-Q4 tension dominates on net.

wave1.lens_self_description: I forecast the RESOLUTION PROCESS, not the world: for each CQ I named the specific statistical series, its publication frequency, revision/rebasing behaviour, weighting convention and coverage gaps, and let definitional and composition artefacts — not macroeconomic narrative — carry the probability; this forbade me from using any judgment about AI capability trajectories, geopolitics, or policy intent except where it changes a published index's construction, and it forbade me from treating an unobservable quantity (true incumbent wages, true Chinese real growth, r* itself) as the resolving object.
wave1.cq1_reasoning:
CONJUNCT 1 (OECD-38 harmonized unemployment avg <=5.5%, 2032-36): marginal 62%. Series = OECD labour-force-weighted unemployment rate (the branded "Harmonised Unemployment Rate" database was restructured in 2024-25; a resolver may not find that exact label — ambiguity, not a level problem). Currently ~4.9-5.1%. Artefacts, all >3pp: (i) the aggregate is LABOUR-FORCE weighted, so Mexico (~9% of OECD labour force, measured ~2.7% on informality) and Korea/Japan drag it down ~0.3-0.4pp vs an unweighted read — favours YES; (ii) rising 65+ participation is an unambiguous DOWNWARD bias: discouraged older workers exit to "retired" (out of labour force) rather than registering as unemployed, so the aging-driven denominator shift lowers the printed rate independent of labour-market slack — favours YES by ~0.1-0.2pp; (iii) OECD accession (Indonesia, Brazil, Argentina, Peru, Bulgaria, Croatia, Romania in train) would make the published aggregate OECD-40+ with higher-unemployment members, +0.2-0.4pp — favours NO, and "OECD-38" is locked at 38 while the published series is not; (iv) US CPS decennial population controls off the 2030 census rebase levels in Jan 2032/2033 by tenths. Revisions are small (benchmark, not continuous). 62%.
CONJUNCT 2 (F+Q real median hourly wage cumulative growth beats J+K+M by >=10.0pp, 2025-2036): marginal 13%, and most of that discount is MEASUREMENT not economics. (a) Observability: almost no OECD-38 member publishes a real MEDIAN hourly wage by ISIC/NACE section annually. Eurostat Structure of Earnings Survey does give median gross hourly earnings by NACE section but only every FOUR years (2018/2022/2026/2030/2034) with a ~2.5-year publication lag — the 2034 wave lands ~2037 and there is NO 2036 vintage. UK ASHE (annual, median gross hourly ex-overtime by SIC section) and Canada's LFS (median hourly by industry) are the only clean annual sources; Australia's EEBTUM is biennial; Japan's BSWS is contractual MEAN by industry; the US has no comparable series at all (OES is occupational, nominal, and BLS explicitly warns against time-series use). An OECD-38 aggregate of sectoral real median hourly wages cannot be constructed for this window. A resolver will therefore fall back on national-accounts compensation per hour by ISIC activity (a MEAN), which fails the question as written. (b) COMPOSITION, my specialty, and it runs OPPOSITE to the economic story in BOTH sectors simultaneously: Q's aging-driven hiring boom arrives disproportionately as low-wage, high-part-time, often migrant entrants (care aides), pulling the SECTOR MEDIAN DOWN while every incumbent gets a raise; AI compression in J+K+M destroys ENTRY-LEVEL cognitive jobs first (juniors, paralegals, analysts), and truncating the bottom of a distribution RAISES the measured median. Those two artefacts jointly erode roughly 8-12pp of a 10pp gap, in the wrong direction. (c) If resolved on the mean proxy it gets worse: K (finance) and M (professional services) means are pulled up by superstar-firm and equity compensation, which national-accounts compensation includes in several members. (d) Hourly-measure sensitivity: Q's high and shifting part-time share moves measured hourly pay with zero change in anyone's pay. (e) Deflator choice (local CPI vs harmonized vs a single OECD deflator) is worth 2-4pp on an 11-year cumulative gap. 13%.
CORRELATION: mildly positive (+0.15 effective). Labour scarcity in F+Q both suppresses unemployment and lifts F+Q pay; but the AI-displacement branch that most helps conjunct 2 is the branch that most hurts conjunct 1, so the correlation is capped. JOINT = 0.62 x 0.13 x 1.15 = 9.3%, then -1pp for the standing convention that an unresolvable conjunct grades NO. 8.
wave1.cq2_reasoning:
CONJUNCT 1 (GDP-weighted OECD-38 core CPI/PCE avg >=2.50%/yr, 2027-2036): measured marginal 52% vs an economic view of ~42%; the 10pp gap is pure index construction. Artefacts >3pp: (i) TURKIYE. OECD aggregates are PPP-GDP weighted and DO include Turkiye (~4% of OECD-38 PPP GDP). Turkiye core at 10-15% adds 0.40-0.60pp to the aggregate; even at 8% it adds ~0.25pp. On a 2.50% threshold this single inclusion is worth ~10-15pp of probability, upward. The OECD publishes an ex-Turkiye aggregate precisely because of this — which series resolves is UNSPECIFIED and is the largest single unresolved ambiguity in CQ2. (ii) "core CPI/PCE" mixes instruments. US core PCE runs persistently 25-35bp BELOW core CPI (weights, broader scope, chained formula). With the US ~37-40% of OECD-38 PPP GDP, the CPI-vs-PCE choice moves the aggregate 0.10-0.15pp = ~5-8pp of probability, upward if core CPI is used. (iii) Euro-area HICP excludes owner-occupied housing; the long-delayed phased integration of OOH into HICP (plausibly ~2029-2031, inside the window) would ADD to measured euro core mid-window, a one-way upward artefact worth 3-5pp. (iv) Core excludes food and energy, so the AI-buildout electricity channel reaches the measure only with a lag through services — a DOWNWARD artefact against the "grid costs push inflation" story, worth ~3pp. (v) Core series are essentially unrevised (index reconstitution aside), so a 10-year average is a clean arithmetic object — no revision risk, unlike GDP. 52%.
CONJUNCT 2 (China headline CPI avg <1.50%/yr, 2027-2036): marginal 62%. Series = NBS monthly headline CPI. Resolution-friendly: NBS does not back-revise CPI. Artefacts: (i) basket weights are not fully published and are rebased every five years (2026 rebase due inside the window); pork weight alone has historically swung headline by 0.5-1.0pp. (ii) the series is widely assessed as SMOOTHED — a lower-variance series is mechanically more likely to remain inside a narrow band near its ~0.5-1.0% trend, which favours YES by maybe 4-6pp relative to a same-mean/higher-variance series. (iii) Rent/imputed housing is a small and methodologically contested weight, which has suppressed measured CPI through the property bust. Economically: 2023-26 ran 0.2-0.7%; Section 2A's 60M population contraction and 2.9T RMB pension subsidy burden lock in demand weakness; the Japan 1995-2015 reference class averaged ~0.0-0.3% over twenty years. The risk to NO is a decade-long policy reflation or an RMB-depreciation food/import shock. 62%.
CORRELATION: near zero, with two offsetting channels. Positive: both legs are the same "OECD bottleneck inflation / China deflation" bifurcation narrative. Negative and mechanical: Chinese overcapacity EXPORTS goods disinflation to the OECD, which pushes OECD core down — but core is service-heavy, so the drag is weak. Net +0.10 effective. JOINT = 0.52 x 0.62 x 1.05 = 33.9%. 33.
WINDOW WARNING: CQ2's OECD core window is 2027-2036 (10y) but the CQ6 lexical lock uses OECD core over 2032-2036 (5y). Reusing this number in CQ6 is a window error; I used ~+0.15pp for the back half (near-term capex-digestion disinflation, later care-wage and debt-service pressure).
wave1.cq3_reasoning:
Reference class: bloc-weighted 5-year growth windows for mature-plus-converging aggregates with fixed base-year PPP weights.
MEASUREMENT FIRST. (i) WEIGHTS: the lock ("constant 2025 USD PPP") fixes China at ~34% of the combined bloc ($40T of ~$118T PPP) and removes what would otherwise be a 0.10-0.20pp artefact from ICP rebasing (ICP 2024 round publishing ~2027, ICP 2029 after). But the resolver's choice of IMF WEO VINTAGE reintroduces it: WEO re-weights and back-revises PPP history every October. Flag. (ii) CHINA'S PRINT vs CHINA'S GROWTH: the question resolves on PUBLISHED real GDP. Published Chinese real growth is argued (Nakamura-Steinsson-Liu, satellite-luminosity work) to overstate true growth by ~1-2pp, and the deflator has been negative, which mechanically lifts the real print. On a 34% weight, a +1pp print bias is +0.34pp on the bloc measure. This is the single largest artefact in CQ3 and it is UPWARD. (iii) OECD GDP is revised repeatedly (annual benchmark, 3-5 year vintages); a 2032-36 average read in 2037 differs from the same average read in 2040 by typically 0.1-0.2pp, direction indeterminate but historically upward for the US.
FERMI. OECD-38 aggregate: locked per-capita baseline 0.6%/yr + population ~+0.20%/yr (migration-dependent and tightening) = 0.80%. AI offset: AI-Q1 puts only 23% on >=+0.50pp TFP and AI-Q6's modal regime is +0.15-0.59pp, so expected TFP lift ~+0.30pp -> OECD ~1.10%/yr (range 0.3-2.0). China published: population -0.5%/yr, worker-retiree 4.4->2.8, -2.7pp aging drag; central published print 3.2%/yr (range 1.5-4.5), already inclusive of the print bias. Bloc = 0.66 x 1.10 + 0.34 x 3.20 = 0.73 + 1.09 = 1.82%. P50 = 1.85.
P10 = 1.00: OECD 0.3 + China 1.5 gives 0.71; I lift to 1.00 because a 5-year AVERAGE dilutes any single bust year (AI-Q4 at 66% makes a capex-digestion recession inside the window likely but not decade-defining) and because the China print floor is policy-anchored near 3% in practice.
P90 = 2.80: requires OECD ~2.0 (the AI-Q1 tail) with a China print at 4.5. Note the asymmetry the print bias creates: the bloc can measure 2.6%+ with OECD at only ~1.9%.
wave1.cq4_reasoning:
THE ANCHOR IS WRONG BY ~85bp AND THAT IS MY HEADLINE FINDING. The brief anchors on US 10y TIPS ~2.60% (Oct 30 2026), but the question asks for the GDP-WEIGHTED G7 real yield. Pricing it today on PPP GDP weights (US .52, JP .11, DE .10, UK .07, FR .07, IT .06, CA .05) with current national real yields (US 2.60, JP ~0.35, DE ~0.60, FR ~0.90, IT ~1.40, UK ~1.30, CA ~1.50) gives ~1.76%, not 2.60%. Any panelist who anchors on 2.60 and adjusts will be ~0.8pp too high. Worse, the WEIGHTING BASIS is genuinely unspecified: the locked accounting basis is 2025 USD PPP, but a yield is defined in local nominal terms, so the weights do not inherit the lock. On MARKET-FX GDP weights the US share rises to ~0.64 and the same observation prices at ~2.07% — a +31bp artefact, far above my 3pp flag threshold. I resolve on PPP weights per the lock and report the 31bp as the dominant definitional risk.
OTHER MEASUREMENT ARTEFACTS >3pp. (i) TIPS BREAKEVEN vs INFLATION SWAP: US 10y CPI swaps trade ~20-35bp ABOVE the TIPS breakeven (TIPS liquidity premium plus deflation floor). Using swaps LOWERS the measured US real yield by 20-35bp; at .52 weight that is 10-18bp on the aggregate. The question says "10y inflation swap / TIPS breakeven" as if interchangeable. They are not. (ii) JAPAN: the JGBi market and yen inflation-swap market are thin; the Japanese BEI is biased LOW by illiquidity, so Japan's measured real yield is biased HIGH by 20-40bp (x .11 = +3-4bp). (iii) ITALY/FRANCE/GERMANY all get the SAME euro-area HICP swap, so Italy's measured "real yield" embeds the BTP-Bund credit spread as though it were a real rate (+5bp on the aggregate). (iv) CONCEPTUAL: nominal = r* + real term premium + E[pi] + inflation risk premium. Subtracting a breakeven (= E[pi] + IRP) returns r* + real term premium only if the IRPs match; they do not, and in stress the TIPS-implied real rate overstates the true real rate by 10-25bp. (v) "AVERAGED over 2032-2036": an arithmetic mean over five years of a non-mean-reverting level. This is level-dominated, kills the spike tails, and NARROWS the distribution substantially versus the point-in-time question a naive reader answers. Expected net artefact on the measured aggregate vs the conceptual one: ~+10bp.
REQUIRED DECOMPOSITION: CQ4 = r* + real term premium - repression wedge.
r* (G7 PPP-weighted, ~0.75%, range 0.3-1.3): UP from boomer life-cycle DISSAVING (+20-30bp vs 2015-19) and from physical-AI/grid capex (+10-20bp only — see my Identity-2 audit: AI-Q3's own TWh range implies $20-60B/yr of incremental OECD+China grid capex, ~0.1-0.3% of bloc gross fixed capital formation, an order of magnitude too small to move a global saving-investment balance; the crowding must run through interconnection queues, transformer/turbine supply and electricity PRICES, not loanable funds). DOWN from precautionary saving under labour-income uncertainty, cognitive-labour income compression (CQ5/AI-Q5 channel), and the persistent Chinese household saving surplus with no domestic investment outlet (-20 to -30bp). Japan and euro r* well below US, which is why the G7-weighted r* is low.
REAL TERM PREMIUM (+1.10%, range 0.4-2.0) — THIS CARRIES MOST OF MY VARIANCE, and it is the correct home for Section 2A's "(r-g) worsens by ~+1.0pp EVEN WHERE a frictionless r* eases." That claim is a term-premium-and-fiscal-arithmetic claim, not an r* claim, and I honour the distinction: my r* central is only ~0.75% while my term premium does the work. Drivers: rollover VOLUME at >100% global debt/GDP (142% US, 127% China by 2031) with net interest to ~3% of GDP; eroding sovereign convenience yields; levered hedge-fund basis trade as a fragile marginal buyer whose capacity is balance-sheet- and repo-haircut-contingent; reduced central-bank duration absorption; and an underrated DEMOGRAPHIC channel on the long end — closed DB schemes reaching full funding and buying out REMOVE a price-insensitive long-duration bid (+10-25bp), i.e. aging raises the term premium through the asset side, not just the fiscal side.
REPRESSION WEDGE (-20bp expected, fat left tail): I treat repression as a real policy option, not a curiosity. P(at least one G7 running materially repressive policy for a sustained part of 2032-36) = ~35% (Japan most likely, then Italy/UK via Eurosystem or regulatory mandate; US least likely but largest if it happens). Expected wedge 0.35 x ~60bp = -20bp; conditional on the US adopting it, -100bp or more, which is what builds my left tail.
CENTRAL: 0.75 + 1.10 - 0.20 = 1.65% conceptual, +10bp measurement artefact = 1.75% measured. Path-wise this is roughly FLAT versus today's PPP-weighted 1.76%, because two moves cancel: Japan's real yield rises 40-80bp on BoJ normalization while the US mean-reverts DOWN from 2.60 toward 1.9-2.1 as the 2026 term premium normalizes. P10 0.95 (low r* + repression + post-bust precautionary saving). P90 2.65 (fiscal dominance expressed entirely through the term premium, no repression, strong capex pull); the five-year averaging is what keeps P90 below 3%.
wave1.cq5_reasoning:
CONJUNCT A (ICE BofA MOVE avg >=105, 2027-2036): marginal 48%, driven mostly by INDEX CONSTRUCTION. MOVE is the curve-weighted average of normalized implied vol on 1-month Treasury options (20/20/40/20 across 2y/5y/10y/30y) expressed in BASIS POINTS of annualized yield vol. It is therefore LEVEL-DEPENDENT: bp vol scales roughly with the yield level, so MOVE at 105 with 4.5-5% nominals is the same RELATIVE uncertainty as MOVE at ~60-70 with 2% nominals. If the fiscal-dominance path in my CQ4 holds, MOVE clears 105 with no increase in genuine rate uncertainty at all. That is worth ~10-15pp of probability, upward, and a naive forecaster comparing to the 2010s average (~70-80) will badly under-forecast. Second construction point: a 10-year ARITHMETIC mean of a right-skewed series is pulled up by spikes — one 2023-style year averaging 130 lifts the decade mean ~4-5 points. Third: index continuity. The MOVE has had methodology/ownership changes (Merrill -> ICE, tenor weighting and CMT normalization revisions); a 2027-2036 average spliced across a methodology change is not a single series. Long-run context: ~100 in the 1990s, ~95 in the 2000s, ~70-80 in the 2010s, 200 spike in 2023, ~70-85 in 2025-26. 48%.
CONJUNCT B (a >=25% MSCI World peak-to-trough drawdown in which G7 GDP-weighted 10y NOMINALS fail to fall >=50bp): marginal 33%. Decomposed: P(any >=25% MSCI World drawdown in 10 years) = 78%. Base rate: 1973-74, 1987, 2000-02, 2007-09, 2020, 2022 (~26% in USD) = ~6 in 53 years, i.e. ~65-70% over a decade; lifted to 78% by the $1.4T circular AI vendor/cloud/chip commitments on ~$300B equity and ~$650B debt, and by AI-Q4 at 66%. P(bond hedge fails | drawdown) = 42%, and this is where my effort's logic bites AGAINST the question: the single most likely source of a >=25% drawdown in this window is an AI CAPEX BUST, which is DISINFLATIONARY and reliably produces a Treasury RALLY (2020: 10y 1.9 -> 0.5), so the most probable drawdown is precisely the one that FAILS the second clause. The hedge fails in inflation/fiscal-shock drawdowns (2022 is the clean precedent, 1 of the last 6) and in a convenience-yield/basis-trade unwind. Mix of shock types given AI-Q4: ~42%. 0.78 x 0.42 = 33%.
DRAFTING AUDIT: "(or rise by >=25bp)" is REDUNDANT — any rise of >=25bp already fails to fall by >=50bp. The operative test is the single condition "nominals do not fall >=50bp," so the parenthesis does not loosen the bar and a reader who treats it as a second independent path over-rates the conjunct. Also undefined: the "equity drawdown window" endpoints. Peak-to-trough windows run from 5 weeks (2020) to 30 months (2000-02); over a long window yields almost always move >50bp somewhere, so the natural reading (peak DATE to trough DATE) is the only one that resolves, and it makes long slow bears much likelier to satisfy the clause than sharp crashes.
CORRELATION: strongly positive, +0.45. A world of high bp-denominated rate vol IS the world where the bond hedge fails; both are the same fiscal-dominance/convenience-yield-erosion regime. JOINT = 0.48 x 0.33 = 15.8%, lifted x1.5 for correlation = 23.7%. 23.
wave1.cq6_reasoning:
LOCK CONFIRMED AND APPLIED AS WRITTEN: (1) A if g>=2.6; (2) else C if OECD core>=2.7 AND g<2.0; (3) else D if g<1.7 AND core<2.0; (4) else B. Measures: CQ3's bloc growth and GDP-weighted OECD-38 core over 2032-2036 (NOT CQ2's 2027-2036 window; I added ~+0.15pp for the back half).
A = 11. P(bloc g >= 2.6%) from my CQ3 distribution (P50 1.85, P90 2.80) is ~12-14%, trimmed to 11 on the arithmetic: with China's published print at 4.0%, a 2.6% bloc requires OECD aggregate growth of (2.6 - 0.34x4.0)/0.66 = 1.88%/yr, i.e. ~1.65% per capita against a locked 0.6% baseline — roughly +1.0pp of realized TFP offset, strictly inside the AI-Q1 (23%) tail and needing a favourable China print on top. Note the lock means A is decided on GROWTH ALONE; "broad wage gains" and "debt stabilizes via growth" in A's prose are NON-OPERATIVE under the lexical rule, which transfers mass INTO A from readers who would have withheld it on the wage clause. My CQ1 at 8 says broad wage gains are very unlikely, yet the lock still forces 11 into A. That is a lock artefact and I flag it rather than hedge against it.
C = 22. P(g<2.0) = 57%. P(OECD core 2032-36 >= 2.7%) = 34% INCLUSIVE of Turkiye (~26% ex-Turkiye — the same 8pp artefact audited in CQ2, and it lands entirely on this cell). Mild positive correlation (+0.15) for coherent supply-wall stagflation. 0.57 x 0.34 x 1.15 = 22.3.
D = 12. P(g<1.7) = 45%. P(core<2.0 | weak growth) = 26%: a GDP-weighted OECD-38 core below 2.0% WITH Turkiye in the basket requires the ex-Turkiye core at ~1.6%, which is a hard bar. So the Turkiye inclusion SUPPRESSES D and INFLATES C by roughly 5-7pp of mass each way — the largest single index-construction transfer in CQ6. 0.45 x 0.26 = 11.7.
B = 55 by residual.
CONSISTENCY CHECK PERFORMED (as required). (i) Against CQ3: my P50 is 1.85%, squarely inside B's literal 1.7-2.5% band, and mass is concentrated in B — I have NOT put most mass on A, which would be the violation the brief names. P(g>=2.6) = 11-14% matches A = 11. P(g<2.0) = 57% matches C + D + the low-growth slice of B = 22 + 12 + ~23 = 57. Closes. (ii) Against CQ2: CQ2's OECD core conjunct (>=2.50%, 2027-36) at 52% measured implies substantial but not dominant high-inflation mass; the >=2.7% 2032-36 sub-threshold at 34% and the <2.0% threshold at ~18% unconditional leave ~48% of the inflation distribution in the 2.0-2.7 middle band, which the lock routes to B regardless of growth. C (22) < 34 because it is intersected with g<2.0; D (12) < 18-26 because it is intersected with g<1.7. Closes.
RESIDUAL-B AUDIT (required). Of B's 55: ~37pp comes from the literal 1.7-2.5% growth band after lexical priority strips the growth-1.8/inflation-2.8 cells into C, and ~18pp comes from cells with NO literal home — principally growth <1.7% with core 2.0-2.6% (the "stagnation without disinflation" cell, which a naive reader assigns to D on the growth clause alone) plus growth 2.0-2.5% with core >=2.7% (which a naive reader assigns to C on the inflation clause alone). So the catch-all absorbs ~18pp — about one third of B's mass and ~18% of the whole distribution — drawn mostly from D. Put differently: a naive reader applying the literal definitions would report roughly A 11 / B 37 / C 26 / D 26; the lock moves ~14pp from D and ~4pp from C into B. B is not a forecast, it is a drafting residual, and the ensemble should not read B = 55 as 55% confidence in the Bifurcated Barbell narrative.

hypothesis_critique.a: The failure word is "smoothly". Three accounting objections. (1) No published series could ever show smoothness: occupational-transition matrices (US CPS-based flows, EU LFS retrospective questions) are the only instrument, and they put professional/clerical -> health-associate-professional transitions at ~1-3%/yr, with the care occupations gated by licensure, credential recognition and geography that a displaced J/K/M worker does not clear within the horizon. (2) The binding constraint in Q is the WAGE and the public reimbursement rate, not the supply of bodies — a displaced analyst is not a marginal care worker at the offered price, which is exactly why my CQ1 conjunct-2 composition story has low-wage migrant entrants, not reallocated professionals, filling Q. (3) The identity "labour saved in J = labour supplied to Q" is not an identity at all: AI's measured labour savings show up as lower hours or lower headcount in J, with the displaced flowing to non-employment, early retirement or unrelated services, and no national accounting framework tracks the transition, so the plank is also substantially unfalsifiable. 6.
hypothesis_critique.b: Two failure words, and "blocks" is the categorical one. AI does not touch PHYSICAL labour migration at all — Philippine nurses, seafarers and Gulf/OECD construction labour face rising demand precisely from the Section 2A aging path; what constrains that flow is OECD immigration politics, not AI. On VIRTUAL services exports, "blocks" is contradicted by the direction of travel: India's GCC/GIC headcount and services exports grew THROUGH the 2024-26 adoption wave, with AI substituting for the lowest-value transactional/voice BPO tier while mid- and high-value captive work expanded — substitution at the bottom with expansion in the middle is not a block. "Severely" also fails a measurement test: the resolving series are BSP's OFW remittance data and RBI's services-export data, both reported in nominal USD; PHP/INR depreciation inflates local-currency receipts and masks volume losses, so even a real hit would not read as severe in the published numbers. 14.
hypothesis_critique.c: The failure carrier is "then" — the implied sequencing — with "falls" doing secondary damage. My own CQ2/CQ6 arithmetic has the OECD core risk skewed to the LATE window, not the early one: the near-term "hot" component is substantially a tariff/level-shift effect that washes out of year-on-year prints within 12-18 months, while the 2030s drivers (care-sector wage pressure from the Q hiring boom, electricity costs from the AI buildout reaching core through services with a lag, and net interest at ~3% of GDP pressing on fiscal space) are persistent and arrive later. So the plank may have the SHAPE inverted. The measurement point that rescues part of it: headline falls faster than core on energy and food base effects, and a reader resolving on headline will see the plank "confirmed" while core does the opposite — a vintage/instrument artefact, not a fact about inflation. 27.
hypothesis_critique.d: Two failure words, both fatal to resolvability. "Eventually" places the claim outside any dated horizon and makes it unfalsifiable by construction — the cardinal resolution-criteria sin, and reason enough to score it low regardless of the economics. "Wins" is undefined across three different accounting objects: real GDP LEVEL (trivially wins, since population decline is slow and the level compounds), real GDP GROWTH RATE (the actual question, and AI-Q1 at 23% with the Hulten Ceiling regime at 36.5% says the measured channel is weak), and GDP PER CAPITA (where aging is a tailwind to the per-capita ratio as the denominator shrinks — "winning" per capita while the aggregate shrinks is arithmetic, not a productivity renaissance). Separately: measured TFP is a residual that absorbs unmeasured labour-quality decline in an aging workforce (biasing it DOWN) and depends critically on how BEA/BLS and national statistical offices treat hedonic price indices for AI accelerators — the compute-deflator choice alone moves measured real investment and TFP by several tenths, which is the same order as the entire quantity being forecast. 17.

key_drivers: CQ4's anchor mis-specification: the G7 GDP-weighted real yield prices at ~1.76% today on PPP weights versus the brief's US TIPS anchor of 2.60%, and at ~2.07% on market-FX weights — a ~31bp weighting ambiguity and a ~85bp anchoring trap that dominate any macroeconomic view of r*.

Turkiye's inclusion in the GDP-weighted OECD-38 core aggregate (+0.25 to +0.60pp on the printed number), which single-handedly adds ~10-15pp to CQ2's first conjunct, inflates CQ6-C and suppresses CQ6-D by ~5-7pp each.

Opposed composition effects in CQ1's second conjunct: low-wage entrant surge drags the Q sector median DOWN while AI's destruction of entry-level cognitive jobs pushes the J+K+M median UP, eroding ~8-12pp of the required 10pp gap in the wrong direction — plus the fact that annual sectoral real MEDIAN hourly wages for F and Q simply are not published for an OECD-38 aggregate before ~2038.
MOVE's basis-point normalization makes it mechanically level-dependent: higher nominal yields clear the 105 bar with no increase in genuine rate uncertainty, worth ~10-15pp on CQ5's first conjunct.

The real TERM PREMIUM, not r*, carries my CQ4 variance (central +1.10pp, range 0.4-2.0): rollover volume at >100% debt/GDP, eroding convenience yields, basis-trade fragility, and the underrated aging channel of closed DB schemes buying out and withdrawing a price-insensitive long-duration bid.
China's published-versus-true real growth wedge applied to a locked 34% bloc weight: a +1pp print bias is +0.34pp on CQ3's measured growth, which is the difference between CQ6-B and CQ6-A mass.

falsification_signposts.signpost: OECD switches its headline GDP-weighted OECD-38 core inflation aggregate to an ex-Turkiye basis (or Turkiye core settles below 5%), so that the resolving series no longer carries the +0.25-0.60pp wedge.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: My core-inflation artefact claim is spent: CQ2's first conjunct falls ~8-12pp (CQ2 to ~25), CQ6-C falls ~5-6pp and CQ6-D rises ~5-6pp. The direction of the whole inflation leg of my view reverses from artefact-driven to fundamentals-driven.

falsification_signposts.signpost: Eurostat Structure of Earnings Survey 2026 (publication due ~2029) reports median gross hourly earnings by NACE section for 25+ OECD members with section Q's real median rising FASTER than J+K+M over 2022-2026 — i.e. the entrant-composition drag I claim does not appear in the data.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: My central CQ1 mechanism is falsified: conjunct 2 rises from 13% toward ~28%, CQ1 moves from 8 to ~17. Also weakens hypothesis plank (a)'s critique and lifts CQ6-A by ~2pp via the broad-wage-gains channel.

falsification_signposts.signpost: G7 GDP-weighted 10y real yield (PPP weights, national breakeven basis) prints below 1.00% for four consecutive quarters with NO explicit yield cap, mandated sovereign-holding rule, or central-bank purchase programme sized >3% of GDP announced in any G7 member.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: My "term premium carries the variance, repression is a 35% option" decomposition fails and an easing frictionless r* dominates instead: CQ4 P50 drops ~50bp to ~1.25 with P90 down to ~2.1, CQ6-D rises ~6pp, CQ6-C falls ~4pp, and CQ5's first conjunct falls ~8pp as the level-dependence channel for MOVE disappears.

falsification_signposts.signpost: Any G7 sovereign announces an explicit 10-year yield ceiling, a regulatory minimum sovereign-debt holding for banks or insurers, or a central-bank "market functioning" purchase programme exceeding 3% of GDP.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: The repression wedge is realized rather than probability-weighted: CQ4 P50 down ~35bp and P90 down ~60bp (the top tail is truncated by policy, not by economics); CQ5's MOVE conjunct down ~8pp because capped yields suppress bp-denominated rate vol; CQ6-C rises ~3pp on the financial-repression clause in its own definition.

falsification_signposts.signpost: An MSCI World peak-to-trough drawdown of >=25% occurs AND G7 GDP-weighted 10y nominals fall by >=50bp during that window (i.e. the bond hedge WORKS), while the trailing MOVE average since Jan 2027 is still below 110.
falsification_signposts.if_observed_implies: CQ5's most likely qualifying episode is consumed by a non-qualifying case and the remaining window is short: CQ5 drops from 23 to ~9-11. It also confirms my claim that the modal large drawdown is a disinflationary AI-capex bust, which pulls CQ6 mass from C toward D by ~4pp and lowers CQ4 P50 by ~20bp.

wave1.coupling_tension:
Two 2B marginals go inconsistent once demographics are endogenous, and — this is the finding — they move in OPPOSITE directions, so the ensemble cannot repair 2B with a single sign.
(1) AI-Q2 (21.3%) is too LOW, by ~10-15pp, and the reason is partly measurement. The resolving instrument is the Eurostat "ICT usage and e-commerce in enterprises" survey plus national analogues, read as an UNWEIGHTED OECD-38 country average. That survey's AI question has been re-worded nearly every wave (2021 "AI technologies"; 2023 "at least one of seven listed AI technologies"; 2024-25 adding generative AI explicitly), and each re-wording has produced a 5-15pp level jump with no change in behaviour — a one-way upward drift over a 2025-2036 window containing two or three more revisions. The narrower phrase "directly in producing goods or services" is a sub-question whose level sits well below "uses AI," so the threshold may be measured lower than intended; but the UNWEIGHTED country average is dominated by small, high-wage, high-digital-intensity members (Iceland, Luxembourg, Denmark, Estonia, Finland) rather than by the large economies, and those are exactly the members where endogenous labour scarcity bites hardest and earliest. Aging as a DEMAND PULL for automation therefore loads onto the very countries that carry disproportionate weight in the resolving statistic. Direction: UP.
(2) AI-Q1 (23.0%) is, if anything, too HIGH once demographics are endogenous, because measured TFP is a RESIDUAL. An aging workforce mechanically depresses measured TFP through unmeasured labour-quality and hours-composition decline, which 2B holds exogenous and therefore excludes from the TFP measure it is forecasting. Adding that channel subtracts roughly 0.05-0.15pp from measured 2032-36 TFP growth against a +0.50pp threshold — enough to move AI-Q1 down 3-6pp. Direction: DOWN. The same residual also absorbs the AI-compute deflator choice (hedonic treatment of accelerator prices), whose sign is unresolved and whose magnitude is several tenths, i.e. larger than the threshold's own distance from the baseline.
Third, smaller but relevant to my effort: 2A's claim that aging worsens global (r-g) by ~+1.0pp "even where a frictionless r* eases" is coherent with 2B only if 2B's capex and rate assumptions live in the term premium and the fiscal arithmetic rather than in r*. AI-Q3's own TWh range confirms this: +633 TWh by 2036 implies ~$20-60B/yr of incremental OECD-38+China grid capex, 0.1-0.3% of bloc gross fixed capital formation — an order of magnitude too small to move a global saving-investment balance. Any effort that raises r* materially on "AI grid capex demand for loanable funds" is in direct arithmetic tension with the locked AI-Q3 marginal, and the tension resolves in favour of the term premium, which is where I placed my CQ4 variance.

wave2.lens_self_description: Adversarial red-team falsifier: I attacked my effort's three Wave-1 panelists rather than averaging them, and the attack forbade me from using the one framework all three shared uncritically — the HLW/Rachel-Summers low-and-flat r* prior with all fiscal arithmetic booked into the term premium — so every number below is built from the premise that the equilibrium real rate LEVEL, not the premium, is the open question.
wave2.cq1_reasoning:
CONJUNCT 1 (OECD-38 harmonized unemployment avg <=5.5%, 2032-36) = 0.66. All three Wave-1 panelists put this at 0.62 and all three built it the same way: current ~4.9% minus a trend-rate reduction from headcount, minus recession risk. I go modestly higher because two mechanical biases they named but underweighted both run the same way and both STRENGTHEN over 11 years: (i) the rising-65+-participation exit bias — discouraged older workers reclassify to "retired" (out of labour force), not "unemployed", so the aging denominator shift lowers the PRINTED rate independent of slack, and this grows monotonically as the 65+/20-64 ratio goes 31%->40%; (ii) labour-force-weighted aggregation with Mexico at ~9% of the OECD labour force measuring ~2.7% on informality. Against: OECD accession (Indonesia/Brazil/Argentina/Peru/Bulgaria/Croatia/Romania) would make the published aggregate OECD-40+ with higher-unemployment members, +0.2-0.4pp, and the lock says "OECD-38" while the published series is not frozen at 38. Net 0.66.
CONJUNCT 2 (F+Q real median hourly beats J+K+M by >=10.0pp cumulative, 2025-2036, i.e. >=0.87pp/yr) = 0.19. This is where I attack Wave 1's strongest shared move on this question. All three leaned heavily on a SINGLE composition argument — AI destroys entry-level cognitive jobs first, truncating the bottom of the J+K+M distribution and mechanically RAISING its measured median, which they valued at 5-12pp of the required gap in the wrong direction. That argument is conditional on a mechanism nobody checked against the locked marginal it depends on. AI-Q5 is a labour-COMPENSATION-SHARE question, not a headcount question, and the configuration most consistent with Q5 at 38% alongside Wave 1's own benign unemployment conjunct is incumbent real-wage STAGNATION at roughly flat headcount (margin capture, not mass separation) — in which case the truncation effect is small and the J+K+M median simply stalls, which is exactly what conjunct 2 needs. Wave 1 ran the headcount mechanism for the median and the share mechanism for Q5 simultaneously without noticing they are different worlds. I therefore restore a meaningful slice of the probability they stripped. Separately, panelist 3's "-1pp because an unresolvable conjunct grades NO" is a resolution convention he invented and I reject; the Eurostat SES four-yearly problem and the UK ASHE / Canada LFS annual coverage make an exact OECD-38 sectoral real-median-hourly aggregate unconstructible before ~2038, but unresolvability is resolver risk in both directions, not a one-way discount. What I DO accept and keep is the opposite-direction artifact inside Q: the aging-driven care-hiring boom arrives as low-wage, high-part-time, often migrant entrants, dragging the SECTOR median down while incumbents get raises — that is the single most damaging fact for this conjunct, it is independent of the AI mechanism, and it is why I stay at 0.19 rather than 0.30. Also the fiscally administered payer: 2A locks OECD net interest 2%->3% of GDP and my own CQ4 (real yields averaging 2.45%) makes the Q wage bill HARDER to fund than Wave 1 assumed, because debt service at a higher real rate crowds the transfer budget — my high-rate thesis cuts against this conjunct, and I will not hide that.
CORRELATION: both legs sit in the labour-scarcity branch, but the AI-displacement branch that most helps leg 2 is the branch that most hurts leg 1, so rho is capped: latent rho ~ +0.25, lifting P(C2|C1) from 0.19 to ~0.235. JOINT = 0.66 x 0.235 = 0.155 -> 14. Only modestly above the Wave-1 centre of 12: I found a real error in their composition argument but it is worth ~5pp of probability, not 20, and I am not inflating a conjunction to look contrarian.
wave2.cq2_reasoning:
CONJUNCT A (GDP-weighted OECD-38 core CPI/PCE avg >=2.50%/yr, 2027-2036) = 0.50. The decisive fact here was found by exactly one of three Wave-1 panelists and ignored by the other two, which is itself the finding: panelists 1 and 2 both built the OECD aggregate from US/euro/Japan blocs (P2 explicitly: 0.45xUS + 0.30xeuro + 0.09xJapan + 0.16x"rest") and never asked what is actually IN the published GDP-weighted OECD-38 aggregate. TURKIYE is in it, at ~4% of OECD PPP GDP, with core running 8-15%; that single inclusion adds 0.25-0.60pp to the printed number against a 2.50% threshold. P1's 0.33 and P2's 0.40 are answers to a question about an aggregate that is not the one being forecast. P2's own bloc arithmetic produced a 2.41% centre with sigma ~0.25 over a ten-year average — add 0.30pp of Turkiye and that mechanical centre is 2.71%, i.e. the threshold sits BELOW centre rather than 0.1pp above it, which flips the sign of the whole calculation. Second channel in the same direction: "core CPI/PCE" is left interchangeable, and US core PCE runs 25-35bp below core CPI with the US at ~37-40% of OECD-38 PPP GDP, worth 0.10-0.15pp. Third: euro-area HICP's long-delayed phased integration of owner-occupied housing plausibly lands ~2029-2031, inside the window, one-way upward.
BUT I apply a genuine downward coupling that the panel got backwards, and it is my lens's main substantive move here. Panelists 1 and 2 both let fiscal stress raise inflation AND raise term premia at the same time. Those are substitutes at the margin, not complements: if the sovereign clears its rollover at a higher REAL yield (my CQ4 P50 of 2.45%, against their 1.75-1.95%), the adjustment has already happened in the price of duration and the inflation tax is not required. The world where OECD core averages 2.7%+ is disproportionately the world where repression is chosen and the measured real yield is LOW. So my own CQ4 forces my inflation distribution DOWN relative to a forecaster who reads 2A's fiscal block as straightforwardly inflationary. Net of Turkiye up and rate-expression down: P(A) = 0.50.
CONJUNCT B (China headline CPI avg <1.50%/yr, 2027-2036) = 0.65. NBS headline, no back-revision, resolution-friendly; 2023-26 ran 0.2-0.7%; the Japan 1995-2015 analogue averaged ~0.0-0.3% over twenty years; 2A locks -60M population 2026-2035 and worker/retiree 4.4->2.8. The series is widely assessed as smoothed, and a lower-variance series near a 0.5-1.0% trend is mechanically likelier to stay inside a band. Against: the 2026 basket rebase (pork weight alone has historically swung headline 0.5-1.0pp); and the reflation branch Wave 1 underweighted — 2A's own pension/social-security subsidy path (2.9T RMB, 10.1% of fiscal expenditure, heading past 15%) is a transfer to high-MPC retirees, and a state that finally builds a credible household backstop releases exactly the precautionary saving holding Chinese prices down. That mechanism is INSIDE the locked 2A block rather than exogenous, and this is a ten-year window. Also RMB depreciation with food-import exposure. 0.65, below P2's 0.72.
CORRELATION: two offsetting channels. Positive: both legs are the same OECD-bottleneck / China-glut bifurcation. Negative and mechanical: Chinese overcapacity exports goods disinflation into OECD core, and core does include core goods — but OECD core is service-heavy so the drag is weak. Net +0.05 effective. JOINT = 0.50 x 0.65 x 1.05 = 0.341 -> 34. At the top of the Wave-1 range (18/27/33) and for a reason two of three never priced: the resolving aggregate contains Turkiye.
wave2.cq3_reasoning:
WEIGHTS FIRST, because Wave 1 disagreed with itself and the lock settles it. The accounting basis is CONSTANT 2025 USD PPP, which FIXES the weights at 2025 shares: OECD-38 ~$75T, China ~$40T, so China ~0.34 and OECD ~0.66 for the whole window. Panelist 1 used 0.37 on the grounds that "China's share is rising" — that is a chain-weighted construction and the lock forbids it; it shows an anchoring slip toward the familiar market-share framing. P2's 0.32 and P3's 0.34 are closer; I use 0.34.
THE ATTACK ON WAVE 1'S SHARED BASELINE. All three took 2A's "0.6%/yr OECD real GDP per capita" as a forecast baseline and then added a small AI offset (P1 +0.4-0.6, P2 +0.30 less 0.15 digestion, P3 +0.30). 2A's own words are "absent productivity offsets" — it is a COUNTERFACTUAL constructed to isolate the aging drag, not a conditional forecast, and all three anchored on the locked prior's framing in exactly the way my brief names. What the 0.6% figure holds out is not only AI TFP. It holds out CAPITAL DEEPENING, which in a shrinking-workforce economy is close to arithmetic: labour input falls ~0.3%/yr in the OECD while the capital stock does not fall, so capital per worker rises and measured labour productivity rises with it at alpha ~0.35 — roughly +0.10-0.20pp/yr with no TFP contribution at all. And the deepening is not incidental: a labour-scarce economy with a care and construction wage signal is the strongest automation business case in the historical record, which is why all three Wave-1 coupling notes conclude AI-Q2 (adoption) should be revised UP. Adoption is the cheap, software-priced, wage-driven decision; it is barely touched by my high-hurdle-rate thesis. So OECD-38 = 0.6 per capita + 0.25 population (migration-driven; the PHYSICAL labour-migration channel is pulled by aging, not blocked) + 0.45 realized offset from deepening plus diffusion = 1.30%/yr.
AGAINST MYSELF, HONESTLY: my CQ4 is the highest real-yield number on this panel, and a 2032-36 average real yield of 2.45% is a genuine investment drag and a genuine debt-service claim on GDP. That is the main reason I stop at 1.30 on the OECD leg. The two forces — deepening pulled by labour scarcity, investment rationed by the cost of capital — are the same automation decision seen from the quantity and the price side, and they substantially offset.
CHINA 2032-36 published print = 3.30%/yr. Labour -0.80pp; capital +1.75pp with deteriorating ICOR as the marginal project turns from housing to grid and datacentre; TFP +1.30pp (China is the world's sharpest automation demand-pull: worker/retiree 4.4->2.8 with a domestic wage signal); pension-subsidy crowding -0.45pp. P3's point that the published print is argued to overstate true growth by ~1-2pp (Nakamura-Steinsson-Liu, satellite-luminosity work) is correct and is UPWARD on the resolving measure at a 0.34 weight; the print floor is also policy-anchored near 3% in practice. I keep 3.30 rather than P2's 2.80.
COMBINED P50 = 0.66 x 1.30 + 0.34 x 3.30 = 0.858 + 1.122 = 1.98 -> 2.00%. Above all three Wave-1 panelists (1.75 / 1.85 / 1.95), driven entirely by refusing to treat a counterfactual as a baseline and by the capital-deepening arithmetic they omitted.
DISPERSION, with a deliberately fatter RIGHT tail than Wave 1. P10 = 1.05: deep capex digestion inside the window (AI-Q4 at 66% makes 2032-36 the digestion years — P2's timing point is correct and important), repression binding, OECD ~0.4 and China ~1.9. P90 = 3.05: the fiscally-priced-equilibrium world described below, where high real rates are the price signal that FORCES automation deepening rather than blocking it — OECD ~2.2 with China at 4.2. Sigma ~0.78 with slight left skew. Wave 1's P90s (2.65 / 2.80 / 2.85) all sit below 2.9, which is the signature of three forecasters who priced the drag channel in detail and the pull channel in a sentence.
wave2.cq4_reasoning:
THE SINGLE STRONGEST SHARED ASSUMPTION ACROSS ALL THREE WAVE-1 PANELISTS, AND MY ATTACK ON IT. Strip the three answers to skeletons: P1 = r* 1.00 + TP 0.90 - wedge 0.50 = 1.40, blended to 1.95. P2 = r* 0.95 + TP 1.35 - wedge 0.35 = 1.95. P3 = r* 0.75 + TP 1.10 - wedge 0.20 = 1.65, +10bp artifact = 1.75. Three panelists, three lenses explicitly forbidden from using each other's methods, and all three put r* in a 0.75-1.00% band and all three declared the TERM PREMIUM the dominant variance source (55% / 45% / "most"). That unanimity is not convergent validity. It is one borrowed prior — the HLW/Laubach-Williams filtered r* plus the Rachel-Summers secular-stagnation accounting — that NONE of them interrogated. They then reinforced it with a shared rhetorical move: "the brief's 2.60% anchor is a trap, the real G7-weighted level is 1.76-2.00%", which all three treated as their headline finding and which all three resolved in the SAME downward direction on a genuinely ambiguous weighting basis. Three independent panelists resolving one ambiguity identically downward is anchoring on each other's framing dressed up as independent recomposition.
WHY THE LOW-FLAT r* PRIOR IS THE WEAK JOINT. (i) It is a filter output, not an observation. HLW-class estimates are two-sided Kalman filters on realized data with standard errors around +/-1pp — wider than the entire quantity being forecast — and structurally incapable of detecting a regime break until years after it happens; the authors suspended publication in 2020 when the filter broke. The same filter has already been revising UP (roughly 0.4% in 2019 toward 1.3-1.4% by 2024-25). A lagging estimator currently revising upward is the worst possible anchor for a 2032-2036 average, and all three used its CURRENT read as their central value. (ii) The sample that produced it is the 1990-2019 global-savings-glut window: Chinese and EM reserve accumulation, a disinflating China, central banks absorbing duration. Every one of those reverses inside the locked 2A block. (iii) THE CLEAN CATEGORY ERROR. P2 explicitly cancels +35bp of life-cycle decumulation FLOW against -20bp of longer-retirement-horizon DESIRED-WEALTH effect (the Auclert-Malmberg-Martenet-Rognlie direction), and P1 and P3 do the same qualitatively. But the desired-wealth channel is a steady-state stock effect that was PRICED IN during the 1990-2020 accumulation phase — it is why rates fell then. The drawdown is the part still ahead. Netting a realized stock effect against an unrealized flow effect and reporting "r* roughly flat" double-counts the past. (iv) THE BOOKING ERROR, the structural heart of it. All three insist 2A's "aging worsens global (r-g) by ~+1.0pp even where a frictionless r* eases" licenses putting fiscal arithmetic exclusively in the premium. Read it again: even where a FRICTIONLESS r* eases. A frictionless r* clears desired saving against private investment in a model with no government paper. The equilibrium rate in an economy where the sovereign issues claims at 6-7% of GDP a year, with global gross debt past 100% of GDP and net interest heading to 3%, is the rate that clears saving against private investment PLUS government absorption — a LEVEL shift in r*, not compensation for uncertainty. Booking +25pp of G7 debt/GDP at a Laubach 2.5-4bp elasticity into "term premium" is an accounting convention the panel mistook for a finding about the world. P1 then used that same convention to justify a near-zero debt elasticity by citing Japan 1990-2020 (debt 65%->250%, real yields FELL) — but Japan's counterexample runs through a captive domestic buyer base, a current-account surplus and a deflating price level, i.e. precisely the three conditions 2A removes.
MY DECOMPOSITION (G7 GDP-weighted, 2032-2036 average).
(1) r* = 1.55%. US r* 1.75% (filter revising up; debt absorption booked where it belongs; boomer decumulation as an uncancelled flow). Euro area rises hardest in relative terms: Germany's post-2025 fiscal regime change, a deteriorating French path, Eurosystem QE runoff, taking the bloc from ~0.3 toward ~1.0. Japan from roughly -0.5 to +0.5 as the BoJ completes normalization. China's saving surplus is the single most likely piece to vanish: 2A locks pension subsidies at 10.1% of fiscal expenditure heading past 15%, and the glut was substantially a China/EM-reserve story. Downward channels I do price: precautionary saving under labour-income uncertainty (-15bp), cognitive-compensation compression raising the saving rate via the Mian-Straub-Sufi MPS gap (-9bp), post-bust excess capacity collapsing investment demand (-20bp in the digestion window).
(2) Real term premium = 1.05% — BELOW P2's 1.35 and near P3's 1.10, because once fiscal supply moves into r* the premium is only compensation for real-rate uncertainty: elevated by rollover volume, eroding convenience yields, the levered basis trade as a fragile balance-sheet-contingent marginal buyer, and reduced central-bank absorption, plus P3's genuinely underrated aging channel on the asset side (closed DB schemes reaching funding and buying out, withdrawing a price-insensitive long-duration bid, +10-25bp). Capped because premium estimates rarely sustain above 1.5pp and because 2032-36 sits after the capex boom.
(3) Repression wedge = -0.30%, and here I red-team the panel in the OTHER direction. P1 priced -0.55 expected (45% x 100bp + 30% x 25bp) and P2 -0.35 on a 0.60 probability. Two objections. First, repression operates on NOMINAL yields and CQ4 subtracts a breakeven: Japan under YCC 2016-2024 held 10y nominals at 0-0.25% and still frequently printed a POSITIVE measured real yield, because the yen BEI sat near zero. Repression suppresses the measured REAL yield only when paired with an inflation overshoot the central bank tolerates — the CQ2-conjunct-A world my own answer puts at 0.50, not 1.0. Second, binding US YCC on the 10y by 2032-36 requires the Fed to spend the inflation credibility that is the asset it is defending; P1's own base-rate evidence is 1945-1980 (pre-independence, pre-targeting) plus Japan plus euro-area SPREAD management, which is a different instrument on a different part of the curve. P(materially binding, G7-weighted) ~0.35 x conditional ~85bp = -30bp expected, with a fat left tail rather than a central case.
CENTRAL: 1.55 + 1.05 - 0.30 = 2.30%, plus ~+15bp of measurement artifact (TIPS breakeven vs inflation swap, Italy's BTP-Bund credit spread entering the aggregate as though it were a real rate, Japan's illiquid BEI biasing its measured real yield high) and the weighting basis resolved toward MARKET-FX GDP weights rather than PPP. On weights: the lock fixes the real ACCOUNTING basis, but a sovereign yield is a local nominal market price and inherits nothing from a PPP conversion; the standard construction for a G7 yield aggregate is market-FX nominal GDP, lifting the US to ~0.60-0.64 and the level by ~25-30bp. All three Wave-1 panelists flagged this ambiguity and all three resolved it downward. P50 = 2.45%.
PATH CHECK, WHERE P2 CONTRADICTS HIMSELF. P2 writes that "most of the 2032-36 change is Japanese and euro-area convergence UP, not US mean reversion" — then reports 1.95%, i.e. no change at all. Price his own sentence: Japan 0.5->1.8 (x0.11 = +14bp), Germany 0.8->1.6 (+9bp), France +10bp, Italy +6bp, UK +4bp, Canada +3bp is roughly +45-50bp on the weighted average with the US unchanged. He neutralized it with an assumed US mean reversion to 1.9-2.1 whose only mechanism is "the 2026 term premium normalizes" — while the entire 2A block says the premium's drivers INTENSIFY through 2031 (US debt 142%, net interest to 3% of GDP, convenience-yield erosion, basis-trade fragility, P95 Debt-at-Risk 117% rising 2.4pp on a 20% AI-led equity shock). You cannot hold both.
VARIANCE ATTRIBUTION — MY DISTINGUISHING CLAIM: r* ~45%, real term premium ~30%, repression wedge ~25%. The unanimous Wave-1 verdict was premium-dominant. I say the r* LEVEL carries the most variance precisely because it is unobservable, estimated by a lagging filter with standard errors wider than the forecast quantity, and because the debt-absorption channel belongs there. I still respect 2A's distinction — 2A's +1.0pp (r-g) claim is fiscal arithmetic and premium, not an r* mechanism — and I honour it by NOT inflating the premium: I let the equilibrium rate itself reprice, which is the stronger version of the same claim.
BANDS. P10 = 1.25: the filter was right all along, repression binds in the US and euro area simultaneously after an AI-led equity shock, post-bust precautionary saving swamps the decumulation flow. P90 = 3.80: no repression, convenience yield erodes hard, Japan and Europe converge fully, US real 10y above 4%. Five-year arithmetic averaging kills the spike tails and is why P90 stops at 3.80.
wave2.cq5_reasoning:
CONJUNCT A (ICE BofA MOVE avg >=105, 2027-2036) = 0.58. Panelist 3 found the controlling fact and panelists 1 and 2 both missed it: MOVE is curve-weighted normalized implied vol expressed in BASIS POINTS of annualized yield vol (20/20/40/20 across 2y/5y/10y/30y, 1-month options), so it is mechanically LEVEL-DEPENDENT — 105 with 5% nominals is the same relative uncertainty as ~60-70 with 2% nominals. P1's central argument is that "the window STARTS from a volatility trough near 60" and that clearing 105 needs a persistent regime shift; the level-dependence point destroys that framing, and it is worth 10-15pp. My own CQ4 compounds it: real yields averaging 2.45% with core near 2.4-2.6% puts G7 nominals in a 4.75-5.25% band for most of the window, a level at which MOVE clears 105 with no increase whatsoever in genuine rate uncertainty. Add the right-skew arithmetic of a ten-year ARITHMETIC mean (one 2023-style year averaging 130 lifts the decade mean 4-5 points) and the bimodal repression switch, which forces markets to price both the intervention and no-intervention branches and mechanically fattens the rate-vol distribution. Index-continuity caveat preserved: the MOVE has had ownership and tenor-weighting/CMT-normalization revisions, so a 2027-2036 average is a splice, not a single series. 0.58, above P3's 0.48 because my yield level is ~60bp higher than his.
CONJUNCT B (an episode in which MSCI World falls >=25% peak-to-trough while G7 GDP-weighted 10y NOMINALS fail to fall >=50bp) = 0.39. P(any >=25% MSCI World drawdown 2027-2036) = 0.78: base rate ~6-8 episodes in 53-55 years (1973-74, 1980-82, 1987 borderline, 1990, 2000-02, 2007-09, 2020, 2022) gives ~65-70% per decade, lifted for the ~$1.4T of circular vendor/cloud/chip commitments on ~$300B equity and ~$650B debt, index concentration in the AI complex, and AI-Q4 at 66%. P(hedge fails | drawdown) = 0.50, and THIS is Wave 1's second-strongest shared assumption, held by all three at 0.36-0.42: "the most likely >=25% drawdown is an AI capex bust, a capex bust is disinflationary, therefore bonds rally, therefore the most probable drawdown is precisely the one that fails the second clause." Three attacks. (i) The AI complex is now substantially DEBT-financed — ~$650B of issuance against ~$300B of equity. A 2030-32 AI bust is therefore a credit event, not a 2000-style equity-only event: spreads widen, levered holders deleverage, and the first thing a levered holder sells is the liquid Treasury leg. The 2020 analogue the panel leans on (10y 1.9->0.5) ran through a central bank with 150bp of policy space and no fiscal constraint; neither condition holds in 2032-36. (ii) The marginal buyer of duration in the panel's own description is the levered hedge-fund basis trade, whose bid is repo-haircut and balance-sheet contingent — it withdraws in exactly the states where the equity drawdown happens. A market whose marginal buyer disappears under stress does not reliably rally. (iii) In my CQ4 world the sovereign IS the risk asset: with the measured real yield averaging 2.45% and no repression backstop in the central case, a flight to quality out of equities into duration is far less automatic than the 1987/2000/2007/2020 template on which the panel's 3-of-8 and 1-of-6 frequencies rest. DRAFTING POINTS I accept from P3: "(or rise by >=25bp)" is redundant — any rise of >=25bp already fails to fall by >=50bp — so the parenthesis does not loosen the bar; and the "equity drawdown window" is undefined, with peak-DATE-to-trough-DATE the only reading that resolves, which favours long slow bears over sharp crashes. 0.78 x 0.50 = 0.39.
CORRELATION: strongly positive, rho ~ +0.45 — a high-bp-vol decade and a failed bond hedge are the same fiscal-dominance / eroding-convenience-yield regime, and that is the same regime as my CQ4. P(B|A) rises from 0.39 to ~0.52. JOINT = 0.58 x 0.52 = 0.302 -> 30. Well above the Wave-1 centre of 21, and it is not a narrative lift: it is the arithmetic consequence of my own higher yield LEVEL feeding a basis-point-normalized index, plus the credit-financing of the AI complex breaking their disinflationary-bust premise. I retain the conjunction discount in full — the unconditional product is 0.23, and only the common-regime correlation takes it to 0.30.
wave2.cq6_reasoning:
LEXICAL PRIORITY applied as written, first match wins, on my own CQ3 growth measure and GDP-weighted OECD-38 core over 2032-2036 (NOT CQ2's 2027-2036 window; I add ~+0.15pp for the back half, since the care/grid bottleneck and the debt-service claim both load later).
STEP 1 — growth bands from MY CQ3 (P10 1.05 / P50 2.00 / P90 3.05, sigma ~0.78, slight left skew): P(g>=2.6) = 0.20; P(2.0<=g<2.6) = 0.30; P(1.7<=g<2.0) = 0.15; P(g<1.7) = 0.35.
STEP 2 — inflation. P(OECD-38 GDP-weighted core 2032-36 >= 2.7%) = 0.34, Turkiye-inclusive (~0.25 ex-Turkiye; that ambiguity over which published aggregate resolves lands almost entirely on cell C). WHERE I ACTUALLY DEPART FROM WAVE 1, since B at 51 happens to land on their centre. P3's residual audit is correct and I adopt it: B is a drafting residual, not a forecast, and ~18pp of its mass comes from cells with no literal home (principally g<1.7 with core 2.0-2.6, the stagnation-without-disinflation cell a naive reader assigns to D). The ensemble should not read B = 51 as 51% confidence in the Bifurcated Barbell narrative. My real disagreements are A at 20 against their 10-11, and D at 10 against their 16-19.
