hypothesis_critique.a: The failure word Wave 1 named is "smoothly" (they scored 5/6/7), but it is the weaker of two failures. The harder one is "supply the workers". "Smoothly" presumes a transfer mechanism exists and is merely frictional; none exists at all. The mismatch is simultaneously occupational (a displaced paralegal or junior analyst is not a licensed care worker), geographic (cognitive employment is metro-concentrated while care demand follows the retired population to suburbs, small towns and the coast), temporal (AI-Q5's compression and the 65+ ratio's 9pp climb are both 11-year gradients, not a clearing event), and above all a WAGE-LEVEL failure: the care payer is a fiscally constrained state facing net interest at 3% of GDP, so the care shadow price rises 45-70% real while the offered wage rises far less and the excess clears as rationing — vacancies, waiting lists, patient:staff ratios, informal family care. My own CQ4 makes this strictly worse than Wave 1 assumed, because a 2.45% average real yield enlarges the debt-service claim competing with the care wage bill. The one thing keeping this at 4 rather than 2: AI genuinely relieves the administrative and documentation load inside Q, a real if modest effective-labour gain. 4.
hypothesis_critique.b: TWO words carry the failure and they fail in opposite directions, which is why Wave 1's 14-18 is roughly the right level for roughly the wrong reason. "Blocks" is simply false as stated: AI does not block labour export, and for PHYSICAL migration aging is a demand PULL — OECD care, construction and logistics shortages pull Indian and Filipino workers harder as the 65+/20-64 ratio goes 31%->40%, and my own CQ3 relies on +0.25%/yr of migration-driven OECD population growth to work. The scope-insensitivity Wave 1 shares is treating the two countries as one case. For INDIA, "severely" fails at the national aggregate: IT-BPM is ~7-8% of GDP but only a slice is substitutable voice and rules-based back office, GCCs are moving up-stack into engineering and R&D rather than disappearing, and domestic demand is ~70% of GDP — a national-aggregate growth hit of 0.3-0.6pp/yr is not severe for an economy growing 5-6%. For the PHILIPPINES, "severely" partially SURVIVES, and this is the part Wave 1 under-prices: BPO is ~7-8% of GDP and voice/back-office is the most directly substitutable work in the world economy, so the virtual-services channel is a concentrated, plausibly 2-4pp-of-GDP hit with no comparable up-stack ladder; remittances at ~8-9% of GDP are the offset, and they come from physical migration, which aging strengthens. So the plank is wrong on mechanism ("blocks"), wrong for India on magnitude, and partially right for the Philippines. 16.
hypothesis_critique.c: "And then falls in the 2030s" is the failing clause, and this is where I most disagree with panelist 1's 44. P1 reached 44 from base rates — ten-year inflation-targeting-era windows mostly undershoot 2.5%, so reversion down is the modal history — which is exactly the backward-looking move my lens exists to attack. Two reasons the fall is loaded OUT of the 2030s rather than into them. First, panelist 2's timing arrow is right: the care and grid bottlenecks are priced by a fiscally constrained payer and tighten monotonically with the 65+ ratio, so the non-tradable cost push is a LATER-window phenomenon, not an early one. Second, and this is mine: the forces people expect to produce 2030s disinflation — capex digestion, labour-income shortfall, Chinese tradable glut — are the same forces that would produce LOW real yields, and my CQ4 says real yields average 2.45%. If the sovereign is clearing its rollover at a high real rate, the economy is not in the excess-saving disinflation state. The clause that does survive is the first one ("runs hot for the next few years"), which is close to consensus and nearly free. So the plank is half-true in its easy half and specifically wrong in its load-bearing half. 24.
hypothesis_critique.d: TWO unfalsifiable words, "eventually" and "wins", and a third problem Wave 1 did not name. "Eventually" is not a forecast at all — it places the claim outside the Dec 31 2036 horizon, so the plank cannot be scored as stated without a date, and any score is really a score on the 2032-36 window. "Wins" is undefined: against what counterfactual, on what measure, at what level? If it means coupled real GDP growth exceeding the 2015-2024 realized bloc path of ~2.7%/yr, my own P50 of 2.00% says no inside the horizon and my P(g>=2.6) = 0.20 caps the yes. Third and least noticed: "outruns population decline" treats AI and demographics as independent racers, when the strongest coupling in this whole target runs the other way — population decline is WHY the automation business case closes, so the two are not in a race, they are the same mechanism. That makes the plank's framing wrong even where its direction is defensible. I score it 18, above all three Wave-1 panelists (11/15/17), because my P(CQ6-A) of 20 is the highest on this panel and because the capital-deepening arithmetic they omitted is a real, near-mechanical channel by which output per worker rises as workers disappear. 18.

key_drivers: The r* LEVEL, not the term premium, as the dominant variance source in CQ4 — my single largest departure from a Wave-1 panel that unanimously declared the premium dominant. HLW-class r* is a lagging two-sided filter with standard errors wider than the forecast quantity, it is already revising upward, and the government-debt absorption channel (global debt past 100% of GDP, net interest 2%->3%) is a level shift in the equilibrium rate rather than compensation for uncertainty. Booking fiscal supply into the premium is an accounting convention all three panelists mistook for a finding about the world.

Rejecting the netting of a realized stock effect against an unrealized flow effect. Wave 1 cancelled +35bp of boomer life-cycle decumulation against -20bp of longer-retirement-horizon desired wealth and reported r* roughly flat. The desired-wealth effect was priced in during the 1990-2020 accumulation phase — it is why rates fell then — while the drawdown is the part still ahead. Un-netted, plus the end of the China/EM reserve glut that 2A's own pension-subsidy path implies, this carries my CQ4 P50 to 2.45% against a Wave-1 centre of 1.88%.

Fiscal stress is expressed in the PRICE of duration OR in the price level, not both. Panelists 1 and 2 let 2A's fiscal block raise term premia and inflation simultaneously. If the sovereign clears its rollover at a high real yield, the inflation tax is not required; if repression is chosen, the measured real yield is low. This substitution drives my CQ2 inflation leg down even as Turkiye's inclusion drives the measured number up, and it is why my CQ6-D is 10 against their 16-19 — I cannot hold a 2.45% real-yield P50 and also put 19 points on the excess-saving demand-shortfall regime.

MOVE's basis-point normalization interacting with my own yield level. The index is normalized vol in basis points, so it scales with the yield level; at the 4.75-5.25% nominals my CQ4 implies, 105 clears with no increase in genuine rate uncertainty. Two of three Wave-1 panelists missed this entirely and anchored on the 2025-26 trough near 60. Worth 10-15pp on CQ5's first conjunct.

The AI complex is DEBT-financed (~$650B issuance against ~$300B equity), which breaks Wave 1's unanimous premise that the likeliest equity drawdown is a disinflationary capex bust that makes bonds rally. A credit event, with a levered repo-haircut-contingent basis trade as the marginal Treasury bid, does not reliably produce a flight to quality — the 2020 template required 150bp of policy space and no fiscal constraint, neither of which holds in 2032-36.

Treating 2A's "0.6%/yr absent productivity offsets" as the counterfactual it says it is, rather than as a growth baseline. All three panelists anchored on it and added only an AI TFP sliver. It also holds out capital deepening, which is near-arithmetic when the workforce shrinks ~0.3%/yr and the capital stock does not — roughly +0.10-0.20pp/yr at alpha 0.35 with zero TFP contribution — and the labour-scarcity wage signal is what pulls the adoption (AI-Q2) that all three Wave-1 coupling notes say should be revised up. This lifts my CQ3 P50 to 2.00% and my CQ6-A to 20.

wave2.coupling_tension:
THE STRONGEST COHERENT WORLD IN WHICH THE WAVE-1 MODAL VIEW IS SIMPLY WRONG, AND ITS PROBABILITY. Call it the FISCALLY-PRICED EQUILIBRIUM: 25%. In it the sovereign gets no relief. Repression is either never attempted — because post-1990 inflation-targeting credibility is the asset central banks are defending and the instrument that would spend it is the one they will not use — or attempted narrowly, in Japan and through euro-area spread management, and never touches the G7-weighted 10y real yield materially. Debt clears instead at a genuinely higher EQUILIBRIUM real rate: G7 r* at 1.5-2.0% rather than 0.75-1.0%, as the HLW filter completes a multi-year upward revision, the China/EM saving glut drains into Chinese pension subsidies past 15% of fiscal expenditure, and boomer decumulation runs as an uncancelled flow. The G7 GDP-weighted measured real yield averages 2.8-3.5% over 2032-36 with nominals above 5%, MOVE clears 105 trivially, and bonds stop hedging equities. Crucially — and this is why the world is coherent rather than merely bearish — growth is NOT low in it. High real rates in a shrinking-workforce economy are the price signal that FORCES automation capital deepening rather than blocking it: AI-Q2 adoption runs well above its locked 21.3% because adoption is a wage-driven software decision barely touched by the hurdle rate, labour productivity rises on deepening even with mediocre TFP, and coupled growth prints 2.4-2.9%. Inflation sits near 2.3-2.6%, so the lexical lock routes most of this world into A and the upper reach of B, not into C. Wave 1 cannot represent it at all: all three have CQ4 P90s of 2.65-3.35 and CQ3 P90s of 2.65-2.85, so the joint {real yield 3.0%, growth 2.7%} sits outside all three distributions simultaneously. That joint exclusion — high rates AND high growth as a coherent pair — is the drag/pull asymmetry in its purest form: they priced aging as a growth drag AI must offset and the fiscal block as a premium problem, and never as a demand pull whose price is a high real rate.
WHERE COUPLING BREAKS SECTION 2B. 2B held demographics exogenous, which necessarily held the DISCOUNT RATE exogenous, and that is the channel through which three of its marginals go inconsistent — in opposite directions, so the ensemble cannot repair 2B with one sign.
(1) AI-Q4 (66%) is too LOW; it should be ~73%. Direction UP. I agree with my effort's Wave 1 here but through a bigger rate shift: their coupled real-yield central was 1.75-1.95%, mine is 2.45%, so the WACC increment versus the 2023-2026 environment in which the ~$1.4T of circular commitments was underwritten is ~100-150bp rather than ~50bp. Impairment is mechanically a hurdle-rate-versus-realized-revenue test, and a +100bp real WACC on a 15-year asset cuts NPV roughly 10-12%; Q4's second limb compares external revenue to compute D&A, which is capitalized capex priced at the OLD discount rate, so the test hardens on both limbs. Damped, as panelist 1 correctly noted, by self-reference: a smaller installed base shrinks the D&A the revenue test measures against.
(2) AI-Q3 (P50 998 TWh) — I REVERSE Wave 1's unanimous direction, and this is my sharpest disagreement with them on the locked marginals. All three argued Q3 should fall to 880-920 TWh because a higher hurdle rate rations deployment. That conflates a FINANCING question with a QUANTITY question. Q3 resolves on operational electricity in 2036, and the binding constraints on 2036 MW are interconnection queues, transformer and turbine lead times, and licensed electrical labour — none priced off the 10y term premium. A higher cost of capital changes WHO owns the asset and its capital structure (hyperscaler operating cash flow, which does not clear against sovereign duration, versus levered SPV and private-credit structures, which do), not the megawatts; and it is entirely consistent with a HIGHER Q3 alongside a higher Q4, because impairment is about who eats the loss on assets that were nonetheless built and energized. Panelist 3's own arithmetic is the proof against his colleagues: +633 TWh by 2036 is only ~$20-60B/yr of incremental grid capex, 0.1-0.3% of bloc gross fixed capital formation — far too small for loanable funds to be the binding constraint, and therefore also too small for the COST of loanable funds to ration the quantity. Direction: Q3 flat to slightly UP, ~1,020-1,060 TWh, with the rationing showing up in ownership and electricity prices instead.
(3) AI-Q1 (23%) and AI-Q2 (21.3%) are priced too close together and must SPLIT. Q2 should rise to ~30-33%: adoption is a labour-substitution decision priced off the WAGE, the wage signal from a shrinking OECD workforce is unambiguously stronger once demographics are endogenous, the software is cheap relative to the capital stock so the hurdle-rate objection barely bites, and the resolving instrument is an UNWEIGHTED OECD-38 country average dominated by small, high-wage, high-digital-intensity members (Iceland, Luxembourg, Denmark, Estonia, Finland) — precisely where labour scarcity bites hardest and earliest — on top of a survey whose AI question has been re-worded nearly every wave with 5-15pp level jumps and no behavioural change. Q1 should fall to ~19-20%: measured TFP is a residual that absorbs unmeasured labour-quality and hours-composition decline from an aging workforce (-0.05 to -0.15pp against a +0.50pp threshold), and in my high-rate world the capital deepening through which AI reaches measured TFP is partially rationed. So the cell 2B overprices is "white-collar compression WITH broad measured productivity" — the Q1-high-and-Q5-high corner, exactly the cell CQ6-A needs on its prose reading. The lexical lock rescues my A of 20 anyway, because it decides A on GROWTH alone, and my growth lift comes from deepening and adoption rather than from measured TFP. NET DIRECTION: the coupled world BUILDS more physical AI than 2B's exogenous-demographics marginals imply, WRITES DOWN more of it, ADOPTS it more widely, and BOOKS less of it as measured TFP — which moves mass out of 2B's Transformative Breakout and into both tails of the growth distribution rather than into its centre.

wave2.cq4_reasoning:
STEP 0 — ANCHOR. The question asks for a G7 GDP-weighted real yield, not US TIPS. PPP GDP weights (US 0.522, JP 0.115, DE 0.104, UK 0.077, FR 0.075, IT 0.062, CA 0.045; sums to 1.000) on current real 10y levels (US 2.60, JP 0.50, DE 0.90, UK 1.50, FR 1.20, IT 1.70, CA 1.70) = 1.357+0.058+0.094+0.116+0.090+0.105+0.077 = 1.896% -> ~1.90% today. Market-FX weights give ~2.05%. All three panelists reached the same conclusion (1.76 / 1.96 / 1.76); I confirm it independently and note that the Mechanism Modeler's weights SUM TO 1.03, so his "1.96%" is 6bp overstated — normalized it is 1.905%.
STEP 1 — r*, G7 PPP-weighted. Today: US ~0.9, JP ~0.0, euro ~0.3, UK ~0.6, CA ~0.8 -> weighted 0.62, call it 0.70. Deltas to 2032-36, in bp: life-cycle dissaving +22 (65+ hold ~40% of net worth, net worth/GDP ~4.5x = 1.8x GDP, decumulated at 1.2-1.5%/yr = -2.2 to -2.7% of GDP, against the 45-64 cohort's +1.8 to +2.2% -> net desired saving -0.4 to -0.9pp of GDP at a -35bp-per-pp loanable-funds slope); desired-wealth/longer-horizon -15; public dissaving FLOW +10 (the debt LEVEL belongs in the premium, not here); AI/grid/physical capex +5 (see the Fermi below); precautionary saving -15; cognitive-compression saving-glut-of-the-rich -4 (the Modeler booked -9 on AI-Q5 as a certainty; AI-Q5 is a 38% marginal, so the certainty-equivalent is -3 to -4); China pension-subsidy dissaving +8 (saving -1.5 to -2pp of China GDP x ~19% world weight = -0.3 to -0.4pp of world saving = +10 to +14bp, haircut because the household surplus persists if the backstop is not credible); Japan r* normalization +5. Sum = +11 to +16. r* 2032-36 = 0.85%, 1-sigma 0.40.
AI/GRID CAPEX FERMI, because this arrow is the effort brief's own temptation and it does not survive arithmetic. AI-Q3 implies 998-365 = 633 TWh of incremental data-centre load by 2036 = 72 GW of average delivered power = ~96 GW of IT capacity. At $10-12M/MW all-in that is ~$1.06T over 11 years = $96B/yr, plus $35-45B/yr of generation and grid = ~$135B/yr total, which is 0.15% of bloc market-FX GDP and ~0.6% of bloc GFCF. At -35bp per pp of GDP, the whole AI complex is worth +5bp on r*, +15bp if you treble it for robots and non-DC physical AI. THE MECHANISM MODELER IS ARITHMETICALLY IMPOSSIBLE HERE: his +40bp requires 1.0-1.5pp of GDP of incremental investment demand, 7-10x what the LOCKED AI-Q3 marginal supports. The Resolution Auditor's +10-20bp is the defensible figure, though his itemization is wrong in the other direction — his $20-60B/yr covers grid only and omits the $96B/yr data-centre and chip stack, so his "order of magnitude too small" is really "a factor of four too small." Both his number and his conclusion survive; his arithmetic does not.
STEP 2 — REAL TERM PREMIUM BY IDENTITY, NOT BY ASSERTION. Today's premium = today's yield minus today's r* = 1.90 - 0.70 = 1.20%. Closing the identity rather than estimating the premium independently is the whole point of my lens. Deltas: debt supply +33 (G7-weighted debt/GDP +15pp at 2.2bp/pp, Laubach's 3-4bp haircut for regulatory-captive domestic demand); convenience-yield erosion plus a fragile levered basis-trade marginal buyer plus reduced central-bank duration absorption +20; the closed-DB-scheme buyout channel that withdraws a price-insensitive long bid +10 (the Auditor's point, and arithmetically real); a decelerating China's lower global growth and inflation-volatility anchor -15. Premium, no-repression branch = 1.20+0.33+0.20+0.10-0.15 = 1.68%.
STEP 3 — THE CENTRAL FINDING: REPRESSION IS A BRANCH, NOT A SUBTRACTION. All three Wave-1 panelists ADD a +33 to +38bp debt-supply premium and then SUBTRACT an independent expected repression wedge (-20 / -33 / -55bp). That double-counts the same shock in opposite directions: repression is the policy response to, and the suppressor of, precisely the premium being netted against it, so the two terms are strongly negatively correlated and cannot be summed as independent components. The Japan 1990-2020 counterexample both outside-view panelists cite (debt 65->250% with FALLING real yields) does not refute the supply elasticity; it RELOCATES it into a repression branch. Treating it additively pulls the central down AND falsely narrows the distribution. Correct treatment is a two-branch mixture. Branch N (no material repression, p=0.60): yield = 0.85+1.68 = 2.53%, sigma 0.55. Branch R (repression materially binding for a sustained part of the window, p=0.40): the supply premium never clears into the market and an explicit wedge applies -> 0.85 + 1.05 - 0.80 = 1.10%, sigma 0.45; note repression's signature IS a low or negative real yield (G7 1945-80 ~0 to negative, Japan YCC 2016-24 real 10y ~-0.5 to 0), so it lands directly on this measure.
MIXTURE MOMENTS. Mean = 0.40x1.10 + 0.60x2.53 = 0.440+1.518 = 1.958. Median by CDF: at 2.00, F = 0.40xPhi(2.00)+0.60xPhi(-0.964) = 0.391+0.101 = 0.492; at 2.05, F = 0.393+0.115 = 0.508 -> median ~2.02, shaded 5bp for the Auditor's net measurement artefact (his claimed +10bp cannot stand once his own swap-versus-breakeven item of -10 to -18bp on the aggregate is applied; the honest net is ~-5bp). P50 = 1.95. P10: at 0.80, F = 0.40xPhi(-0.667)+0.60x0.0008 = 0.101 -> P10 = 0.80. P90: at 3.05, F = 0.40 + 0.60xPhi(0.945) = 0.40+0.497 = 0.897 -> P90 = 3.05.
VARIANCE ATTRIBUTION. Between-branch = p(1-p)(2.53-1.10)^2 = 0.24x2.045 = 0.491. Within-branch = 0.40x0.2025 + 0.60x0.3025 = 0.263. Total 0.753 (sd 0.868). So the REPRESSION BRANCH SWITCH carries 65% of my variance, the real term premium ~21%, r* ~14%. This reverses the Wave-1 panel's ordering (they all put 45-55% on the premium and 20-30% on repression) and it follows mechanically from framing repression as bimodal rather than additive.
RESPECTING THE 2A (r-g) DISTINCTION, CHECKED ARITHMETICALLY. On my numbers r goes 1.90 -> 1.95 (+5bp) while g goes from ~2.7%/yr realized 2015-24 to 1.80%/yr (-90bp), so (r-g) worsens by ~+0.95pp — matching 2A's ~+1.0pp claim almost exactly, with r* contributing only +15bp of it. The claim is therefore fully satisfied by a near-flat r* plus fiscal arithmetic and premium, which is exactly the distinction the effort brief demands.

He builds a decomposition central of 1.0+0.9-0.5 = 1.4%, states a base-rate anchor of 2.0-2.1%, says he weights them 40/60, and reports 1.95%. 0.40x1.40 + 0.60x2.05 = 0.56+1.23 = 1.79%, not 1.95%. wave2.cq5_reasoning:
CONJUNCT A (ICE BofA MOVE avg >=105, 2027-2036). MOVE is normalized basis-point yield vol, so it is mechanically level-dependent: MOVE/nominal-10y ran ~33 in the 2010s (72 at a 2.2% yield), ~31 in 2023 (130 at 4.2%), and ~18 in 2025-26 (75 at 4.2%) — the recent trough is a RELATIVE-vol compression, not a level effect. My CQ4 implies a US nominal 10y of ~4.4% (real 1.95 + breakeven ~2.4), at which 105 requires MOVE/yield ~24, i.e. above today's 18 but well BELOW the 30-33 long-run norm. The ten-year-average arithmetic is the binding constraint: one 2023-style year at 150 plus nine at 90 averages 96; two spike years at 150 plus eight at 90 averages 102. Clearing 105 needs a durably higher baseline of ~95-100 in ordinary years PLUS spikes — a regime shift, not an episode. Drivers are all in 2A (rollover volume above 100% debt/GDP, convenience-yield erosion, a balance-sheet-contingent basis-trade bid, and a bimodal repression switch that fattens rate vol by construction). P(A) = 0.44.
PANELIST FLAG: the Reference-Class Scout's P(A)=0.25 is in tension with his own inputs. He uses ~103 as the long-run mean and forecasts a 1.95% real / ~4.4% nominal yield, but the historical ~103 was achieved at LOWER nominal levels, so the bp-normalization runs in his answer's favour and he dropped it. His own numbers support 0.40-0.48, where the Mechanism Modeler (0.52) and the Auditor (0.48) sit.
CONJUNCT B. Drafting audit confirmed: "(or rise by >=25bp)" is strictly redundant — any rise of >=25bp already fails to fall by >=50bp — so the operative test is the single condition and a reader treating the parenthesis as a second independent path over-rates the conjunct. P(>=25% MSCI World peak-to-trough drawdown, 2027-2036) = 0.74 (base rate ~6-8 episodes in 53-55 years = 65-70% per decade, lifted for the $1.4T circular vendor/cloud/chip commitments on ~$300B equity and ~$650B debt, index concentration, and AI-Q4 at 0.66). P(hedge fails | drawdown) decomposed by SHOCK TYPE, which is where the arithmetic bites: AI-capex bust / demand shock 0.48 weight x 0.12 fail = 0.058; inflation / supply / fiscal-dominance shock 0.26 x 0.80 = 0.208; duration indigestion / failed auction / convenience-yield or basis-trade unwind 0.16 x 0.85 = 0.136; geopolitical 0.10 x 0.40 = 0.040. Sum = 0.442, plus 0.03 for an aggregation feature the panel missed — the test is on G7 GDP-WEIGHTED nominals, so a US flight-to-quality rally can be offset by a JGB or BTP selloff, making the hedge more likely to "fail" on the published measure than on a US-only read. P(fail|drawdown) = 0.47. P(B) = 0.74 x 0.47 = 0.348. The self-cancelling structure is real and I preserve it: the single most likely cause of a 25% drawdown here is the AI capex bust, which is disinflationary and makes bonds rally, i.e. the most probable drawdown is the one that FAILS the second clause.

JOINT = 0.44x0.348 + 0.45xsqrt(0.44x0.56x0.348x0.652) = 0.153 + 0.45x0.2365 = 0.153+0.106 = 0.259 -> 26. Frechet check: 0.259 <= min(0.44, 0.348) = 0.348, feasible.

hypothesis_critique.a: "SMOOTHLY" carries the failure, and "supply" carries the rest. Arithmetic: OECD-38 care-hours demand at +2.2%/yr needs roughly 8-10M additional hands-on care workers by 2036. AI-Q5-scale compression of J/K/M (3.5pp of compensation share across ~25% of GVA) frees on the order of 4-7M person-equivalents of cognitive labour — the right order of magnitude, which is why the plank is seductive. But the transfer requires a relative-wage signal, and the receiving sector's payer is fiscally rationed (net interest 2%->3% of GDP), so the care shadow price rises 45-70% real while the measured wage rises only 12-20%: the price that would clear the reallocation is precisely the price that is suppressed. The displaced are also the wrong ages, the wrong places and the wrong licences. The excess clears as rationing — vacancies, waiting lists, patient-to-staff ratios, informal family care — not as a smooth labour-market transfer. 4.
hypothesis_critique.b: TWO failure words, pulling opposite ways. "BLOCKS" is simply wrong about the channel: AI compresses cross-border VIRTUAL services exports (BPO, back office, basic code and content) but cannot block PHYSICAL labour migration, which is the channel that OECD aging opens WIDER — the same 65+/20-64 arithmetic that creates the care bottleneck creates the visa demand. The two spillover channels move in OPPOSITE directions, so a single-signed "blocks" cannot be right. "SEVERELY" fails on magnitude: Philippine BPO is ~7-8% of GDP and ~6% of employment while remittances are ~8-9% of GDP and rising with OECD care and construction demand; India's IT/BPM is ~7% of GDP and a shrinking share of its growth, with remittances ~3.3%. A real hit to the virtual slice against a real gain in the physical slice is a composition shock, not severe aggregate suffering. 15.
hypothesis_critique.c: "THEN FALLS" carries the failure — the sequencing is backwards in my decomposition. The near term carries the capex-boom and tariff impulse, but the 2030s carry the care and grid Baumol wall, the fiscal arithmetic (net interest 2%->3% of GDP, P95 Debt-at-Risk 117%), labour scarcity from a shrinking workforce, and repression if chosen — repression WORKS by running inflation above nominal yields, so the fiscal branch is inflationary in the 2030s by design. My own numbers have 2032-36 core at ~2.45% against a 2027-36 average of ~2.60% including the hot early years, which means the later window is not materially cooler once the boom is excluded from the comparison. The one genuine disinflationary 2030s force is the capex BUST (AI-Q4 at 0.66, my bust branch at p=0.35, core 2.05), so the plank is roughly a 1-in-3 branch rather than a story. The highest score of the four, and still below half. 26.
hypothesis_critique.d: TWO failure words. "EVENTUALLY" is unfalsifiable inside a Dec-31-2036 resolution horizon: a plank whose truth condition lies outside the window cannot be "substantially correct as stated" for this question, and the small credence I give it is credence that the within-window evidence already points that way. "WINS" is undefined and fails on every benchmark I can construct: my coupled 2032-36 growth central is 1.80%/yr against ~2.7%/yr realized in 2015-24, so AI does not even restore the pre-aging growth rate, let alone outrun population decline. The arithmetic reason is Hulten's: the AI-Q6 expectation is only +0.30pp of TFP, while the bloc's aging drag (China 0.40 weight x -2.7pp, OECD 0.60 x -0.4pp) is -1.32pp — the offset is less than a quarter of the drag, and the sectors AI pulls hardest on have falling expenditure shares while the non-substitutable care bottleneck has a rising one. 12.

key_drivers: REPRESSION AS A BRANCH, NOT A SUBTRACTION — my single biggest departure. All three Wave-1 panelists add a +33 to +38bp debt-supply premium and then subtract an independent expected repression wedge of -20 to -55bp. Those two terms describe the same shock in opposite directions and are strongly negatively correlated: repression is the policy response that suppresses the very premium it is netted against. Modelled correctly as a 40/60 two-branch mixture (1.10% vs 2.53%), the CQ4 median rises to ~2.00 and the distribution fattens on the left rather than narrowing, and the branch switch takes 65% of my variance versus the premium's 21% and r*'s 14%.

THE AI/GRID LOANABLE-FUNDS ARROW IS ~7x TOO BIG IN THE PANEL. AI-Q3's own locked numbers imply 633 incremental TWh = 72 GW of average load = ~96 GW of IT capacity = ~$1.06T over 11 years = $96B/yr of data-centre capex plus $35-45B/yr of generation and grid = ~$135B/yr, which is 0.15% of bloc GDP and ~0.6% of bloc GFCF, worth +5bp on r* (+15bp trebled for robots and non-DC physical AI). The Mechanism Modeler's +40bp needs 1.0-1.5pp of GDP. The crowding-out must therefore run through interconnection queues, transformer and turbine supply and electricity prices, not through the saving-investment balance — which is also why r* stays nearly flat in my build.

THE MID-WINDOW PPP WEIGHT, WHICH NOBODY ON MY PANEL COMPUTED. Under the lock's own 'constant 2025 USD PPP' accounting the aggregate grows by summing real levels, so the operative 2032-36 weights are mid-window real levels: OECD-38 0.593 / China 0.407, not the 0.32-0.37 China weight all three panelists used. Worth +0.06 to +0.12pp on CQ3, and it interacts with China's -2.7pp aging drag: a higher China weight raises the growth LEVEL while making the bloc's total aging drag worse (-1.32pp, larger than 2A's global -1.1pp).

TURKIYE AND MEXICO IN A GDP-WEIGHTED OECD-38 CORE AGGREGATE. Member-by-member PPP weighting gives a 2027-36 central of 2.603% inclusive versus 2.337% ex-Turkiye and 2.28% ex-both — a +0.32pp artefact straddling CQ2's 2.50 threshold. That single accounting choice moves P(CQ2 conjunct A) from 0.27 to 0.64 and is the entire reason my CQ2 of 37 sits above the panel's 18-33. It also inflates CQ6-C and suppresses CQ6-D.

OPPOSED MEDIAN-COMPOSITION ARITHMETIC IN CQ1's SECOND LEG, quantified. Q's 27% cumulative employment growth arriving at ~70% of the incumbent median drags the sector median down 12-16pp; truncating 15-20% off the bottom of J/K/M raises that median 12-15pp. Netted against a 25-35% pass-through of the care shadow price, the CENTRAL measured gap is -3pp against a +10pp bar — the required divergence is negative in expectation, before any resolution-feasibility discount.

MOVE's BASIS-POINT NORMALIZATION AGAINST TEN-YEAR-AVERAGE ARITHMETIC. MOVE/nominal-10y ran 31-33 in the 1990s-2023 and ~18 today; at my implied 4.4% nominal, the 105 bar needs a ratio of only ~24. But a decade MEAN is unforgiving: one 150 year plus nine at 90 averages 96, two at 150 plus eight at 90 averages 102. The bar needs a durably higher ordinary-year baseline, not an episode — which is why I land at 0.44 rather than the Scout's 0.25 or a naive reading of the 2010s average.

wave2.coupling_tension:
FOUR TENSIONS, EACH WITH THE ARITHMETIC THAT CREATES IT AND A SIGNED DIRECTION. My lens finds that 2B cannot be repaired with a single sign — two marginals must move up and two down.
(1) AI-Q3 (P50 998 TWh) and AI-Q4 (66%) cannot both hold at a coupled cost of capital, and the fix is signed OPPOSITELY on each. 2B priced them against an exogenous discount rate; the 2A block endogenizes exactly that rate. My CQ4 build has the G7-weighted real yield averaging ~1.95% with a ~1.68pp real term premium in the 60%-weighted no-repression branch, against the sub-1% real environment in which the locked ~$1.4T of circular vendor/cloud/chip commitments (on ~$300B equity and ~$650B debt) were underwritten. A +100bp real WACC on a 15-year asset cuts NPV ~10-12% and converts marginal projects into written-down ones. Direction: AI-Q3 DOWN from 998 toward 900-920 TWh; AI-Q4 UP from 66 toward 72-74. The self-referential damping is real and I quantify it: AI-Q4's second limb compares external revenue to compute D&A, and D&A is a function of the installed base, so a lower Q3 shrinks the denominator the revenue test runs against — AI-Q4 cannot rise by the full hurdle-rate implication, which is why I stop at 72-74 rather than 76.
(2) THE EFFORT BRIEF'S OWN PREMISE IS IN ARITHMETIC TENSION WITH LOCKED AI-Q3, and this is my distinctive finding. The brief lists "physical AI and grid capex demand for loanable funds" among the forces raising real rates. AI-Q3's own numbers forbid it from being material: 633 incremental TWh = 72 GW average delivered load = ~96 GW of IT capacity = ~$1.06T over 11 years = $96B/yr of data-centre capex plus $35-45B/yr of generation and grid, so ~$135B/yr, which is 0.15% of bloc market-FX GDP and ~0.6% of bloc GFCF. At a -35bp-per-pp-of-GDP loanable-funds slope that is +5bp on r*, +15bp if trebled for robots and non-DC physical AI. Any panelist booking +40bp needs 1.0-1.5pp of GDP, 7-10x what the locked marginal supports. So the capex channel must enter through the TERM PREMIUM, interconnection queues, transformer and turbine supply and electricity prices — not through r*. Direction: no change to AI-Q3, but a hard constraint on how any coupled answer may use it, and an independent confirmation that 2A's "(r-g) worsens ~+1.0pp even where a frictionless r* eases" is a premium-and-fiscal-arithmetic claim. My own numbers close that identity: r goes 1.90 -> 1.95 (+5bp) while coupled g goes ~2.7 -> 1.80 (-90bp), so (r-g) worsens ~+0.95pp with r* contributing only +15bp.
(3) AI-Q1 (23%) and AI-Q5 (38%) are priced too close to independent, and the joint cell they over-state is exactly the cell CQ6-A needs. With demographics endogenous, compressing J/K/M labour compensation erodes the income-tax base funding the transfers the old-age ratio is inflating (OECD net interest 2%->3% of GDP; China pension subsidies 10.1%->15%+ of fiscal expenditure), forcing a higher tax wedge or repression — both of which subtract from MEASURED TFP through misallocation. I book that at -0.10pp in my OECD growth build. A high-Q5 world must therefore carry a LOWER Q1 than independent marginals imply: the implied joint P(Q1 and Q5) of 0.23x0.38 = 0.087 should be ~0.06-0.07. Direction: AI-Q1 DOWN by 3-5pp conditional on Q5, which is one reason my CQ6-A is 10 rather than 2B's standalone Transformative Breakout figure of 16.2 plus any coupling bonus.
(4) AI-Q2 (21.3%) is too LOW by ~8-12pp, and it is the one marginal coupling pushes UP. The labour-scarcity wage signal from a shrinking OECD workforce raises the firm-level business case for adoption, and the resolving statistic is an UNWEIGHTED country average dominated by small, high-digital-intensity, high-wage members — precisely where labour scarcity bites earliest. But the pull lands on ADOPTION, not on measured TFP, because the tasks it pulls hardest on sit in sectors whose expenditure share is falling while the non-substitutable care bottleneck's share is rising. The Hulten ceiling absorbs it, so (4) does not rescue (3).
NET DIRECTION: the coupled world is more capital-cost-constrained, more adopting, and less productivity-solvent than 2B's exogenous-demographics marginals read. That moves CQ6 mass out of A and into B and D rather than into C, and — because repression is a branch rather than a subtraction — it widens rather than narrows the CQ4 distribution.

wave3.lens_self_description: I am the effort-level posterior for Effort 3: I re-weighted the five prior panelists question by question on the quality of their specific argument, adopted only the Wave-2 moves that survived arithmetic or a locked-prior coherence test, and enforced a closed r* + real term premium − repression wedge identity across CQ3/CQ4/CQ5/CQ6 — which forbade me from introducing any new mechanism, reference class or measurement finding of my own, and from averaging where one panelist was simply right and the others arithmetically wrong.
wave3.cq1_reasoning:
CONJUNCT 1 (OECD-38 harmonized unemployment avg <=5.5%, 2032-36) = 0.64. Panel spread 0.42 (Reference-Class Scout) / 0.62 (Mechanism Modeler) / 0.62 (Resolution Auditor) / 0.66 (Red-Team) / 0.61 (Fermi). I DOWN-WEIGHT the Scout entirely here: the Fermi panelist's flag is a confirmed arithmetic kill — the Scout names a 0.3-0.5pp trend reduction (so a ~4.5% trend) and then has a typical recession push a FIVE-YEAR AVERAGE from 4.9% to 6.0-6.3%, a 1.1-1.4pp increment on a 5-yr mean implying a 3-4pp peak increment, i.e. 2009 severity as the modal case. I accept Fermi's recession structure (P(>=1 OECD-wide recession IN 2032-36) = 0.50, below the usual 0.55-0.65 because the locked AI-Q4 impairment event is dated 2027-2032 and part of the bust lands BEFORE the window; P(C1|recession)=0.35, P(C1|none)=0.88 → 0.615) and the Auditor's/Red-Team's two one-way downward measurement biases that strengthen monotonically with the 65+/20-64 climb to 39-41% (discouraged older workers reclassify to "retired", out of labour force, not "unemployed"; labour-force-weighted aggregation with Mexico at ~9% of the OECD labour force measuring ~2.7% on informality), against OECD accession making the published aggregate OECD-40+ (+0.2-0.4pp) while the lock says 38. 0.64.
CONJUNCT 2 (F+Q real median hourly beats J+K+M by >=10.0pp cumulative 2025-2036, i.e. >=0.87pp/yr) = 0.13. The Fermi panelist's four-term quantification is the best work in the effort and I take it as the spine: (i) care shadow price +45-70% real but 25-35% pass-through through a payer facing net interest 2%->3% of GDP → measured F+Q median +12 to +20pp; (ii) Q entrant composition, 27% cumulative employment growth arriving at ~70% of incumbent median, shifts the sector median down 12-16pp and nearly cancels (i); (iii) J/K/M entry-level truncation raises that median 12-15pp; (iv) incumbent cognitive compression -5 to -10pp. Central measured gap ≈ -3pp against a +10pp bar. The RED-TEAM LANDED A PARTIAL HIT I honour: AI-Q5 is a labour-COMPENSATION-SHARE question, not a headcount question, and the configuration consistent with Q5 at 38% alongside a benign unemployment conjunct is incumbent real-wage stagnation at roughly flat headcount (margin capture), in which case term (iii) is small and the J/K/M median merely stalls. That restores probability — but only on the cognitive leg. The Q-entrant drag (ii) is independent of the AI mechanism entirely, so the red-team's correction cannot reach it, which is why I move to 0.13 and not to his 0.19. I also accept his rejection of the Auditor's invented "-1pp because an unresolvable conjunct grades NO" convention: unresolvability is two-sided resolver risk (no annual OECD-38 sectoral real median hourly exists; Eurostat SES is four-yearly with no 2036 vintage, 2034 wave publishing ~2037; only UK ASHE and Canada LFS are clean annual sources).
CORRELATION: both legs sit in the labour-scarcity branch, but the AI-displacement branch that most helps leg 2's cognitive term is the branch that most hurts leg 1, so rho is capped at +0.20, lifting P(C2|C1) from 0.13 to ~0.16.
JOINT = 0.64 x 0.16 = 0.102 -> 10. Panel spread was 8/18/8/14/8; I sit just above the cluster because the red-team's share-vs-headcount catch is real and worth ~3pp, not the ~6pp he took.
wave3.cq2_reasoning:
CONJUNCT A (GDP-weighted OECD-38 core CPI/PCE avg >=2.50%/yr, 2027-2036) = 0.54. This is where the effort genuinely learned something across waves, and the credit is unambiguous: the Resolution AUDITOR found that the published GDP-weighted OECD-38 aggregate CONTAINS TURKIYE, and the FERMI panelist converted it into a member-by-member PPP-weighted build the other four never attempted — US 0.395 at 2.45, euro 0.235 at 2.05, Japan 0.090 at 1.80, Turkiye 0.040 at 9.0, UK 0.050 at 2.50, Korea 0.035 at 2.00, Mexico 0.035 at 3.80, Canada 0.030 at 2.30, Australia 0.020 at 2.60, rest 0.070 at 2.60 → 2.603% inclusive, 2.337% ex-Turkiye, 2.28% ex-Turkiye-and-Mexico. The two high-inflation members are worth +0.32pp and they straddle the threshold. I therefore HEAVILY DOWN-WEIGHT the Reference-Class SCOUT (0.33, read off historical OECD core aggregates whose composition he never reconciled to the current basket) and the Mechanism MODELER (0.40, built on US 0.45 / euro 0.30 / Japan 0.09 / rest 0.16 weights that sum to 1.00 only by excluding Turkiye and Mexico from the universe the question names). I do NOT take Fermi's round-up to 0.57: his +5-8pp for core CPI vs core PCE partly double-counts, since his own US central of 2.45 is already closer to a CPI-basis than a PCE-basis number. Against that, the RED-TEAM lands a genuine coupling hit that pushes DOWN and that nobody else priced: fiscal stress is expressed in the PRICE OF DURATION or in the PRICE LEVEL, and these are substitutes at the margin — if the sovereign clears its rollover at a high real yield (my CQ4 P50 is 2.15%, above four of five panelists) the inflation tax is not required. I apply that as a partial, not full, discount — 1945-1980 and the 1970s ran both at once — netting to P(A) = 0.54.
CONJUNCT B (China headline CPI avg <1.50%/yr, 2027-2036) = 0.68. Panel 0.66/0.72/0.62/0.65/0.70. The decisive arithmetic is Fermi's: to REACH a 1.50% ten-year mean from a 0.0-0.3% run rate, China needs ~1.8-2.0%/yr over 2029-2036 — a genuine reflation, not drift. Supporting: NBS does not back-revise; the series is widely assessed as smoothed and a lower-variance series near a 0.5-1.0% trend is mechanically likelier to stay inside a band; 2A locks -60M population 2026-2035 and worker/retiree 4.4->2.8; Japan 1995-2015 averaged ~0.0-0.3% over twenty years. The live reflation channel the red-team pressed is inside the locked block, not exogenous — pension/social-security subsidies at 2.9T RMB, 10.1% of fiscal expenditure, heading past 15%, a transfer to high-MPC retirees that could release the precautionary saving holding prices down — plus the 2026 basket rebase (pork weight alone has swung headline 0.5-1.0pp) and RMB pass-through on food imports. 0.68.
CORRELATION: two offsetting channels. Positive: both legs are the same OECD-non-tradable-bottleneck / China-tradable-glut bifurcation. Negative and mechanical: Chinese overcapacity exports goods disinflation into OECD core goods (~25-30% of the core basket; a 1pp lower China CPI is worth 0.05-0.10pp lower OECD core), but OECD core is service-heavy so the drag is weak. Net rho = -0.10.
JOINT = 0.54 x 0.68 − 0.10 x sqrt(0.54x0.46x0.68x0.32) = 0.367 − 0.10 x 0.2324 = 0.344 -> 34. I land at the Wave-2 level, not the Wave-1 centre of 27, and the entire move is conjunct A's resolving-basket composition — an accounting fact, not a macro view.
wave3.cq3_reasoning:
WEIGHTS. The FERMI panelist wins this outright and it is a real Wave-2 gain. Under the lock's "constant 2025 USD PPP" the aggregate grows by summing REAL LEVELS, so the operative weights for a 2032-36 growth average are MID-WINDOW real levels, not 2025 shares: OECD-38 ~$76T growing ~1%/yr to ~$82T, China ~$41T growing ~3.8%/yr to ~$55T → China ~0.40, OECD ~0.60. All three Wave-1 panelists used China at 0.32-0.37 and the RED-TEAM made it worse by asserting the lock FIXES weights at 2025 shares (0.34) — that is wrong: a constant-price basis fixes prices, not quantity weights, and constant-price aggregation of real levels is exactly what makes the weight drift. I use 0.60/0.40 drifting to ~0.42 by 2036.
OECD-38 2032-36 = 0.95%/yr. I score 15 rather than the Wave-1 11-17 cluster's bottom because the red-team's third objection is a genuine insight the plank's framing violates: population decline is WHY the automation business case closes, so AI and demography are not independent racers but the same mechanism, and capital deepening in a shrinking workforce is a near-arithmetic channel by which output per worker rises as workers disappear. The framing is wrong even where the direction is defensible. 15.

key_drivers: Repression modelled as a BIMODAL BRANCH rather than an additive subtraction (p=0.38 at a 1.50% level vs 0.62 at 2.65%). This is my single largest structural adoption from Wave 2 (Fermi) and it reverses all three Wave-1 builds, which added a +33 to +38bp debt-supply premium and then subtracted an independent -20 to -55bp wedge — the same shock counted twice in opposite directions. Correctly specified, the branch switch carries 54% of my CQ4 variance against the premium's 27% and r*'s 19%, the median rises to 2.15%, and the distribution FATTENS on the left rather than narrowing.

r* booked UP to 1.05% from the Wave-1 0.75-0.95 band but capped well below the red-team's 1.55% by a locked-prior coherence test. The de-netting hit is real: the longer-retirement-horizon desired-wealth stock effect was priced during the 1990-2020 accumulation phase, so cancelling it against the still-ahead decumulation flow double-counts the past. But r* at 1.55% would make (r-g) worsen ~1.75pp against 2A's locked ~+1.0pp and would deliver that worsening THROUGH r*, contradicting 2A's own clause 'even where a frictionless r* eases'. My build closes the identity instead: r 1.98 -> 2.15 (+17bp) against g 2.7 -> 1.85 (-85bp) gives +1.02pp with r* supplying only +33bp.

The AI/grid loanable-funds arrow is dead on the locked marginal's own arithmetic, and the effort brief's premise does not survive it. AI-Q3's 633 incremental TWh = ~72 GW average load = ~96 GW IT capacity = ~$1.06T over 11 years = ~$96B/yr of data-centre capex plus $35-45B/yr of generation and grid = ~$135B/yr, which is 0.15% of bloc GDP and ~0.6% of GFCF, worth +5bp on r* (+15bp trebled for robots and non-DC physical AI). The Mechanism Modeler's +40bp requires 1.0-1.5pp of GDP, 7-10x what the lock supports. Crowding-out therefore runs through interconnection queues, transformer and turbine lead times and electricity prices, not the saving-investment balance.

The resolving basket's composition, not the macro view, drives CQ2 and the C/D split in CQ6. A member-by-member PPP-weighted build gives OECD-38 core at 2.603% inclusive versus 2.337% ex-Turkiye and 2.28% ex-Turkiye-and-Mexico — a +0.32pp artefact straddling the 2.50% threshold, worth ~37pp of probability on conjunct A, and it inflates CQ6-C while suppressing CQ6-D by several points each. Two of five panelists never priced it at all.

The mid-window PPP weight and the capex-cycle sign flip jointly set CQ3. Constant-2025-USD-PPP aggregation sums REAL LEVELS, so the operative 2032-36 weights are mid-window levels (OECD ~0.60 / China ~0.40), not the 0.32-0.37 China weight four of five panelists used; and because both CQ3 and CQ4 are 2032-36 AVERAGES, the AI capex boom sits OUTSIDE the window while the digestion (AI-Q4 at 66%, dated 2027-2032) sits INSIDE it. The higher China weight raises the growth level while worsening the bloc's aging drag to -1.32pp, larger than 2A's global -1.1pp.

MOVE's basis-point normalization interacting with my own yield level, then disciplined by decade-average arithmetic and by my repression branch. MOVE/nominal-10y ran 31-33 in the 1990s-2023 and ~18 in 2025-26; at the ~4.5% nominals my CQ4 implies, the 105 bar needs a ratio of only ~24. But one 150 year plus nine at 90 averages 96, so the bar needs a durably higher ordinary-year baseline — and the 38% repression branch suppresses realized bp vol, which is why I condition conjunct A to 0.50 rather than taking the red-team's 0.58.

wave3.coupling_tension:
As the effort posterior I must adjudicate a direct Wave-1-versus-Wave-2 split, not just restate tensions. THE SPLIT: all three Wave-1 panelists concluded AI-Q3 should fall from 998 toward 880-920 TWh because a coupled, higher cost of capital rations deployment. The red-team REVERSED this and I rule for him, because the Fermi panelist's arithmetic proves it against his own colleagues: ~$135B/yr of total data-centre-plus-grid capex is 0.15% of bloc GDP and ~0.6% of GFCF, far too small for loanable funds to be the binding constraint — and therefore also far too small for the COST of loanable funds to ration the QUANTITY. AI-Q3 resolves on operational electricity in 2036, whose binding constraints are interconnection queues, transformer and turbine lead times and licensed electrical labour, none of which is priced off the 10y term premium. A higher WACC changes WHO owns the asset and its capital structure (hyperscaler operating cash flow, which never clears against sovereign duration, versus levered SPV and private-credit structures, which do), not the megawatts. DIRECTION: AI-Q3 FLAT to slightly UP, ~1,000-1,040 TWh, with the rationing appearing in ownership and in electricity prices.
AI-Q4 (66%) is too LOW and should sit ~71-73%. All five panelists agree on direction and I adopt the mechanism at my own rate level rather than at the red-team's. The ~$1.4T of circular vendor/cloud/chip commitments on ~$300B equity and ~$650B debt was underwritten in a sub-1% real environment; my coupled G7 real yield averages 2.15% with a 1.60pp branch-N real term premium, a WACC increment of roughly 75-125bp. Impairment is mechanically a hurdle-rate-versus-realized-revenue test and a +100bp real WACC on a 15-year asset cuts NPV ~10-12%; Q4's second limb compares external revenue to compute D&A, which is capitalized capex priced at the OLD discount rate, so the test hardens on both limbs. Critically, this is CONSISTENT with Q3 flat-or-up rather than requiring Q3 down: impairment is about who eats the loss on assets that were nonetheless built and energized, so the self-referential damping the Wave-1 panel invoked (a smaller installed base shrinking the D&A denominator) largely disappears — which is why I go to 71-73 rather than stopping at the damped 68-70 the Wave-1 logic implies.
AI-Q2 (21.3%) is too LOW by ~8-12pp and is the one marginal coupling pushes UP. Adoption is a labour-substitution decision priced off the WAGE, and the shrinking-OECD-workforce wage signal is unambiguously stronger once demographics are endogenous; the software is cheap relative to the capital stock, so the hurdle-rate objection barely bites; and the resolving instrument is an UNWEIGHTED OECD-38 country average dominated by small, high-wage, high-digital-intensity members (Iceland, Luxembourg, Denmark, Estonia, Finland) — precisely where labour scarcity bites earliest — layered on a Eurostat ICT-usage question re-worded nearly every wave with 5-15pp level jumps and no behavioural change.
AI-Q1 (23%) is too HIGH, ~19-20%, and the cell 2B over-prices is exactly the one CQ6-A needs on its prose reading. Two independent channels, from different panelists, both subtract: measured TFP is a RESIDUAL that absorbs unmeasured labour-quality and hours-composition decline in an aging workforce (-0.05 to -0.15pp against a +0.50pp threshold, a channel 2B excluded by construction when it held demographics exogenous); and compressing J/K/M labour compensation erodes the income-tax base funding the transfers the old-age ratio is inflating (OECD net interest 2%->3% of GDP, China pension subsidies 10.1% heading past 15% of fiscal expenditure), forcing a higher tax wedge or repression, both of which lower measured TFP through misallocation — I book that at -0.10pp in my OECD growth build. So AI-Q1 and AI-Q5 are priced too close to independent: the implied joint of 0.23 x 0.38 = 0.087 should be ~0.06-0.07, i.e. Q1 down 3-5pp CONDITIONAL on Q5. Note that AI-Q2's upward move does NOT rescue Q1, because the Hulten ceiling absorbs it — the pull lands hardest on sectors whose expenditure share is falling while the non-substitutable care bottleneck's share is rising.
WHERE COUPLING TENSIONS THE BRIEF ITSELF: the effort brief lists 'physical AI and grid capex demand for loanable funds' among the forces raising real rates, and the locked AI-Q3 marginal forbids that from being material (+5bp, +15bp trebled). That is an independent confirmation that 2A's '(r-g) worsens ~+1.0pp even where a frictionless r* eases' is a term-premium-and-fiscal-arithmetic claim rather than an r* claim, and it is the main reason I decline the red-team's r* of 1.55%.
NET DIRECTION: the coupled world BUILDS roughly as much physical AI as 2B implies or slightly more, WRITES DOWN more of it, ADOPTS it more widely, and BOOKS less of it as measured TFP — which moves CQ6 mass out of A and into B, widens rather than narrows my CQ4 distribution because repression is a branch, and leaves C rather than D as the cell the fiscal arithmetic favours while my own high real-yield P50 suppresses D.

wave_audit.wave1_spread: The three Wave-1 lenses disagreed most on CQ2 (18 / 27 / 33) and on CQ1 (9 / 18 / 8), and the causes are different in kind. CQ2's 15pp spread was ENTIRELY conjunct A and entirely a composition question the Resolution Auditor asked and the other two did not: the published GDP-weighted OECD-38 core aggregate contains Turkiye (~4% of PPP GDP at 8-15% core), worth +0.25-0.60pp against a 2.50% threshold. The Reference-Class Scout read historical OECD core aggregates without reconciling their composition to the current basket; the Mechanism Modeler built from US 0.45 / euro 0.30 / Japan 0.09 / rest 0.16 weights that sum to 1.00 only by excluding Turkiye and Mexico from the universe the question names. That is a resolvable factual gap, not a lens difference. CQ1's spread was a lens difference plus an arithmetic error: the Modeler's 18 came from a real mechanism (compression of the compensation SHARE being compatible with a rising measured MEDIAN) while the Scout's 9 rested on a P(unemployment conjunct) of 0.42 that his own stated trend reduction cannot support. Where the three lenses UNANIMOUSLY agreed was the dangerous place: all three put r* at 0.75-1.00% and all three declared the real term premium the dominant variance source (55% / 45% / 'most'), which the red-team correctly identified as one borrowed HLW/Rachel-Summers prior that none of them interrogated rather than three independent confirmations.
wave_audit.what_wave2_changed: KILLED. (1) The Mechanism Modeler's +40bp r* arrow from AI and grid capex demand for loanable funds — the Fermi panelist showed the locked AI-Q3 marginal supports only ~$135B/yr, 0.15% of bloc GDP and ~0.6% of GFCF, worth +5bp; +40bp needs 1.0-1.5pp of GDP, 7-10x. Dead, and it also kills the effort brief's own listing of that channel. (2) All three Wave-1 additive repression wedges — Fermi showed that adding a +33 to +38bp debt-supply premium and subtracting an independent -20 to -55bp wedge counts the same shock twice in opposite directions, pulling the central down AND falsely narrowing the distribution. Dead; I adopted the two-branch mixture wholesale. (3) The Scout's CQ4 blend arithmetic — 0.40 x 1.40 + 0.60 x 2.05 = 1.79, not the 1.95 he reported; reaching 1.95 needs ~17% weight on his own decomposition, not 40%. (4) The Scout's CQ1 conjunct 1 at 0.42 and CQ5 conjunct A at 0.25, both inconsistent with his own stated inputs. (5) The Auditor's claimed +10bp net CQ4 measurement artefact, which cannot stand once his own swap-versus-breakeven item (-10 to -18bp) is applied; honest net ~-5bp. (6) The Auditor's internal China inconsistency (3.2% print in CQ3, 4.0% inside his CQ6-A arithmetic) and the Modeler's P90 that does not follow from his own stated corner (0.68x2.1 + 0.32x3.6 = 2.58, not 2.65). (7) Four of five panelists' China weight of 0.32-0.37 — Fermi's mid-window-real-level point is correct under constant-price aggregation, and the red-team made it worse by asserting the lock FIXES weights at 2025 shares. RESCUED OR ADDED. (8) The red-team rescued CQ1's conjunct 2 partially by showing AI-Q5 is a compensation-SHARE question, so the entry-level truncation mechanism all three Wave-1 panelists ran for the MEDIAN belongs to a different world than the share mechanism they ran for Q5 — worth ~3pp. (9) He rescued the capital-deepening channel in CQ3: near-arithmetic at ~+0.10-0.20pp/yr when labour input falls 0.3%/yr and the capital stock does not, and omitted by all three. (10) He landed a clean hit on the Modeler's netting of a realized desired-wealth STOCK effect (priced in during 1990-2020) against an unrealized decumulation FLOW. (11) He reversed the Wave-1 unanimous AI-Q3 direction, and Fermi's own capex arithmetic proves him right against his colleagues. (12) He broke the Wave-1 unanimous disinflationary-bust premise in CQ5 by noting the AI complex is debt-financed (~$650B against ~$300B equity), making a 2030-32 bust a credit event with a repo-haircut-contingent marginal Treasury bid. (13) He found the Modeler's self-contradiction: Japan/euro convergence UP worth ~+45-50bp, written in words then neutralized by an assumed US mean reversion whose only mechanism contradicts 2A. (14) He correctly rejected the Auditor's invented '-1pp because an unresolvable conjunct grades NO'. (15) His repression objection — repression works on NOMINAL yields while CQ4 subtracts a breakeven, and Japan under YCC still printed positive measured real yields — is the most underrated item in the effort and shrank my branch-R wedge. MERELY CONTRARIAN-POSED, AND I DID NOT MOVE. (16) 'Three panelists resolving the CQ4 anchor downward is anchoring on each other's framing' — the recomputation is verifiable arithmetic, four of five independently reproduced it, and his own market-FX version moves it only 15-30bp; I split the weighting basis 50/50 and left the level near 1.98%. (17) r* = 1.55%: it overshoots 2A's locked ~+1.0pp (r-g) claim to ~1.75pp and delivers it THROUGH r*, contradicting 2A's own 'even where a frictionless r* eases' clause. A locked marginal beats a lens, so I stopped at 1.05%. (18) OECD-38 at 1.30%/yr: right that 2A's 0.6% is a counterfactual, but Fermi's bottom-up reconciliation only reaches 1.01%, so I took 0.95%.
wave_audit.unresolved: Three things remain genuinely unresolved and none is a forecasting question. FIRST and most important for my effort: whether the fiscal arithmetic is booked into the r* LEVEL or into the real TERM PREMIUM is very nearly observationally equivalent on the measured 10y real yield before ~2030-32 — the red-team and the Wave-1 panel describe the same price with different decompositions, and HLW-class estimates carry standard errors (+/-1pp) wider than the entire quantity being forecast, from a two-sided filter structurally incapable of detecting a regime break until years after it happens. My 1.05% / 1.60% split is defensible and not settleable; what I CAN defend is the identity closure against 2A's locked +1.0pp. SECOND: whether the repression branch, if it fires, lands on the MEASURED real yield at all. The red-team's Japan-YCC precedent (nominals pinned at 0-0.25% with a positive measured real yield because the yen BEI sat near zero) means the wedge requires a tolerated inflation overshoot that is itself only ~50% likely conditional on repression — this is the single largest unresolved sensitivity inside my own CQ4, worth ~40bp on the P50. THIRD: two resolver ambiguities neither forecasting nor arguable — which published OECD-38 core aggregate resolves CQ2 (Turkiye-inclusive versus ex-Turkiye, worth ~0.3pp and ~20pp of probability on conjunct A, and almost all of it lands on CQ6-C versus CQ6-D), and whether CQ4's weighting basis is PPP or market-FX GDP (worth ~25bp). I split both rather than pretending they resolve. I also flag that CQ6-B at 60 is a DRAFTING RESIDUAL — ~34pp of the whole distribution sits in cells with no literal home under the lexical lock — and the ensemble should not read it as 60% confidence in the Bifurcated Barbell narrative.
wave_audit.biggest_update: CQ2's conjunct A marginal, from the Wave-1 centre of 0.33-0.40 (and the Scout's 0.33) to my 0.54 — a move of +14 to +21pp on that marginal and +7pp on the reported joint (Wave-1 modal 27 to my 34; +16pp against the Scout's 18). The cause is not a macroeconomic reassessment at all: it is the Resolution Auditor's finding that the published GDP-weighted OECD-38 core aggregate contains Turkiye, converted by the Fermi panelist into a member-by-member PPP-weighted build (2.603% inclusive versus 2.337% ex-Turkiye versus 2.28% ex-Turkiye-and-Mexico) that puts the 2.50% threshold BELOW the mechanical centre rather than 0.1pp above it, flipping the sign of the entire calculation. I then gave back ~2pp of it for the red-team's duration-price-versus-price-level substitution and declined Fermi's further round-up from 0.515 to 0.57 as partly double-counting his own US central. The largest STRUCTURAL update, as distinct from the largest numeric one, is CQ4: adopting repression as a 38/62 branch mixture rather than an additive wedge moved my P50 to 2.15% (+20bp on the Wave-1 modal 1.95) while moving the variance attribution from premium-dominant (45-55%) to branch-switch-dominant (54%) and WIDENING the distribution to 1.15/3.15 — a change in the shape of the answer that matters more than the change in its centre.
