wave2.cq1_reasoning:
CONJUNCT A: OECD-38 harmonized unemployment 5-yr average <=5.5% over 2032-36. Marginal 0.52. Build: current level 4.9% gives 60bp of headroom; the 20-64 denominator shrinks ~0.3%/yr near-deterministically (locked old-age ratio 31%->39-41%), which mechanically suppresses the equilibrium rate. Against: a 5-year AVERAGE above 5.5% needs roughly two years near 6.3-6.5% in the window, which requires one genuine recession inside 2032-36. P(>=1 recession year inside a 5-year window) ~0.60-0.65, but only ~55% of recessions push a 5-yr average 60bp above a 4.9% start given the shrinking denominator. 1 - 0.62*0.78 = 0.52. I FLAG the Inside-View Causal-Mechanism Modeler here: he sets conjunct A = 0.60 while simultaneously asserting that only his regime D (which he prices at 17) delivers a 5-year average above 5.5%. Those two statements are arithmetically incompatible — if D is the only breaking state, conjunct A must be ~0.83, not 0.60. His CQ1 of 18 is therefore built on a marginal he contradicts 400 words later.
CONJUNCT B: cumulative real median hourly wage growth in ISIC F+Q exceeds J+K+M by >=10.0 pp, 2025-2036. Marginal 0.18. Arithmetic: 10 pp over 11 years = 0.87 pp/yr sustained differential — not rare in MAGNITUDE (US college/non-college ran ~1 pp/yr for 25 years), rare in SIGN. Three arithmetic obstacles, each sized: (i) Q is ~60% of F+Q employment and ~70-80% administered/publicly funded, so the composite F+Q real median gain is roughly 0.6*(+1.2%/yr administered) + 0.4*(+3.0%/yr market-priced construction) = +1.9%/yr, i.e. ~+23% cumulative; (ii) J+K+M MEDIAN is not J+K+M SHARE — AI-Q5's 38.2% is about the compensation share of GVA, and truncating entry-level/junior cognitive roles RAISES the surviving median by composition, worth perhaps +4 to +7 pp of spurious J+K+M median growth; (iii) low-wage entrant and migrant inflow into Q drags the Q median down independent of incumbent gains. Required gap 10 pp; central estimate of the gap is roughly +23% - (+15% to +18% for J+K+M including composition) = +5 to +8 pp. The threshold sits ~1 sigma above the central estimate: 0.18.
CORRELATION: +0.30. Both conjuncts descend from the same labour-scarcity node, and a recession that breaks A also breaks B (construction is the first sector to shed hours).
MULTIPLICATION: 0.52*0.18 + 0.30*sqrt(0.52*0.48*0.18*0.82) = 0.0936 + 0.30*sqrt(0.2496*0.1476) = 0.0936 + 0.30*0.19194 = 0.0936 + 0.0576 = 0.1512 -> 15. Minus ~1 pt for the Auditor's correct point that no harmonized OECD-38 sectoral real median hourly wage series exists (Eurostat SES is quadrennial with a 3-4 year lag, so the 2036 endpoint is unobservable at resolution and an unresolvable-as-written conjunct defaults toward NO). CQ1 = 14.
wave2.cq2_reasoning:
CONJUNCT A: GDP-weighted OECD-38 core CPI/PCE >=2.50%/yr average 2027-2036. Marginal 0.70. This is where the arithmetic overturns two of my three Wave-1 colleagues. The question specifies GDP-weighted OECD-38, and the lock specifies constant 2025 USD PPP. At PPP-GDP weights, OECD-38 (~$77-80T PPP) contains Turkey at ~$3.8T = ~4.8%, Mexico ~$3.3T = ~4.1%, Poland ~$1.8T = ~2.3%, plus Colombia/Chile/Hungary/Costa Rica ~2.5% combined. Excess-contribution arithmetic versus a 2.0% core baseline: Turkey at a 10%/yr decade average core contributes 0.048*(10-2) = +0.38 pp (at 15%, +0.62 pp); Mexico at 4.5% adds 0.041*2.5 = +0.10 pp; Poland at 3.5% adds +0.035 pp; the rest ~+0.06 pp. Total +0.57 to +0.81 pp on top of a G7-weighted ~2.2%, i.e. a literal all-38 PPP-GDP aggregate centres on 2.8-3.0%, not 2.2%. The Outside-View Scout (0.44) and the Inside-View Modeler (0.52) both priced a G7/advanced-economy mental model against an explicitly all-38 GDP-weighted object — that is a weighting error, not a macro disagreement, and it is worth ~25 pts of probability. Construction-weighted marginal: P(resolver uses the literal all-38 aggregate) = 0.60, under which P(>=2.50%) = 0.85 (central 2.9%, sigma 0.75); P(resolver silently substitutes an advanced-economy/ex-high-inflation construction) = 0.40, under which P = 0.47 (central 2.35%, sigma 0.50). 0.60*0.85 + 0.40*0.47 = 0.510 + 0.188 = 0.698 -> 0.70. I give the literal reading less weight than the Auditor's 0.70 because the Auditor's own CQ6 step implies an inflation sigma of ~0.30 pp on a decade average, which Turkey alone can violate.
CONJUNCT B: China headline CPI <1.50%/yr average 2027-2036. Marginal 0.66. Arithmetic on the forgiving-mean property: 2023-2026 printed roughly 0.2/0.2/0.0/~0.3, so even a 4% pork/energy shock year adds only 0.25 pp to a 10-year mean; to clear 1.50% the regime must persist, not merely spike. Mechanics supporting low prints: -60M population over 2026-2035, worker/retiree 4.4->2.8, household consumption ~39% of GDP, thin rental imputation for owner-occupied housing in the NBS basket, exported excess capacity. 0.66 splits the three panels (0.62/0.62/0.72); the 34% complement is a decisive reflation pivot, RMB pass-through, or a basket revision adding services.
CORRELATION: -0.10. Explicit channel: the exported-manufacturing-deflation mechanism that satisfies conjunct B directly suppresses OECD core goods inflation, so the conjuncts fight at the margin; the offsetting positive channel is that both are symptoms of the same bifurcated regime.
MULTIPLICATION: 0.70*0.66 + (-0.10)*sqrt(0.70*0.30*0.66*0.34) = 0.462 - 0.10*sqrt(0.21*0.2244) = 0.462 - 0.10*0.2171 = 0.462 - 0.0217 = 0.4403 -> 44. wave2.cq5_reasoning:
CONJUNCT A: ICE BofA MOVE 10-year average >=105 over 2027-2036. Marginal 0.41. Threshold arithmetic, which nobody on the panel did explicitly: MOVE is a normalized basis-point yield-vol index, so decompose the mean into a quiet-year floor and stress-year spikes. With a floor of ~90 (levered basis-trade intermediation plus a 2.0-2.2% real-yield level, versus ~65 in the 2012-2021 ZIRP/central-bank-bid era) and stress years at ~150: three stress years in ten gives 0.7*90 + 0.3*150 = 63 + 45 = 108, CLEARS; two stress years gives 0.8*90 + 0.2*150 = 72 + 30 = 102, FAILS. So the question is almost exactly "does a ~90 floor hold AND do at least three of ten years print stress." P(floor >=88) = 0.55 (fails in regime D, where nominal yields fall back and the bp-vol index deflates mechanically). P(>=3 stress years | floor holds) = 0.70. Product 0.385, plus 0.05 for paths with a lower floor but more/severer spikes = 0.435, minus ~2 pts for the methodology-change / discontinuation / void branch (~12-15% over ten years, direction unknown) = 0.41.
CONJUNCT B: at least one episode of MSCI World -25% peak-to-trough with G7 GDP-weighted 10y nominal failing to fall >=50 bp (or rising >=25 bp) in the drawdown window. Marginal 0.42, built as a POISSON intensity rather than a single draw — and this is where I find hard arithmetic errors in two panels. Let lambda = expected count of >=25% MSCI World drawdowns in the 10-year window = 1.30 (supporting arithmetic: the AI complex is plausibly 30-35% of index capitalization by 2029, and AI-Q4 at 66-72% is near-enough the condition for that complex to de-rate 40-50%, which alone delivers 13-18 pp of index drawdown before any private-credit, $650B-debt-stack or wealth-effect multiplier; daily-close peak-to-trough convention makes -25% materially easier than month-end). Then P(>=1 drawdown) = 1 - exp(-1.30) = 0.727, consistent with all three panels' 0.70-0.87. P(correlated type | drawdown) = 0.42: base 0.45 from the episode record, cut toward 0.35 because the MODAL AI-capex bust is DISINFLATIONARY so bonds rally and the conjunct fails in the most likely bad state, then raised back by two construction artefacts the Auditor is right about — Japan's structurally pinned JGB at ~11% PPP weight damps the aggregate rally (+5 pts) and "during the equity drawdown window" is a generous resolver-chosen interval (+4 pts). P(conjunct B) = 1 - exp(-1.30*0.42) = 1 - exp(-0.546) = 1 - 0.579 = 0.421.
FLAGS. The Outside-View Reference-Class Scout computes conjunct B as 0.87 x [1-(1-0.45)^1.4] = 0.50 then marks to 0.48. That is internally impossible: P(>=1) = 0.87 implies lambda = 2.04, not 1.4; if lambda = 1.4 then P(>=1) = 0.75, not 0.87. Carrying his own lambda = 2.04 with p = 0.45 gives 1 - exp(-0.918) = 0.60, so his conjunct B understates his own model by ~12 pts. The Inside-View Causal-Mechanism Modeler computes 0.70 x 0.37 = 0.26 with NO multi-draw term at all, which biases conjunct B down ~6-8 pts; the Auditor is the only one who applies an uplift (1.09) and it is too small for lambda = 1.3.
CORRELATION: +0.50. The levered-intermediation mechanism that lifts the average MOVE is the same mechanism that breaks the correlation regime; conversely a low-MOVE decade mechanically produces a working flight-to-quality bid.

P(core >=2.70% over 2032-36) = 0.60*0.655 + 0.40*0.242 = 0.393 + 0.097 = 0.490. P(core <2.00%) = 0.60*0.092 + 0.40*0.242 = 0.055 + 0.097 = 0.152.

P(g<1.7) = 0.472 splits: 0.231 to C (core>=2.7), 0.072-0.097 to D (core<2.0), 0.169 to B (core between 2.0 and 2.7). C total = 0.086+0.231 = 0.317 (matches step 2). B total = 0.089+0.253+0.169 = 0.511 = 51. The arithmetic closes.

hypothesis_critique.a: "SMOOTHLY" carries the failure, and the flow arithmetic says so without any judgment about AI capability. Demand side: OECD-38 65+ headcount grows ~3%/yr, so required additional long-term-care and health-social FTEs by 2036 are roughly 8-11M on a current base near 13-15M. Supply side: gross AI-displaced J/K/M workers by 2036 are maybe 4-7M, concentrated in metros, in licensed/credentialed professional tracks, at median ages 35-50. Observed occupational transition rates from professional/financial services into health and social care run 1-3% of separations per year. Even at 100% willingness, transition arithmetic supplies under 15% of the required care hours inside the window — and the care sector's binding constraint is a LICENSE, not a worker. Worse, the two shocks are not even synchronized: displacement is a 2028-2033 event and the care gap widens monotonically through 2060. The plank fails on timing, geography, credentials and volume simultaneously. 4.
hypothesis_critique.b: "BLOCKS" carries the failure; "severely" compounds it. The plank conflates two channels the scope lock explicitly separates. AI substitutes against CROSS-BORDER VIRTUAL services (Indian IT-BPO services exports ~$280B, Philippine BPO ~$38B) and has essentially ZERO substitutability against PHYSICAL labour migration — nurses, aides, construction trades — which is exactly the channel that OECD aging bids hardest for (my CQ1 conjunct-B arithmetic has F+Q shadow prices up 35-50% real on the market-priced side). So AI does not block labour export; it reprices one export line down while demographics bid the other up. Magnitude check on "severely": IT-BPO is ~7-8% of Indian GDP and ~6-7% of Philippine GDP; a 30% revenue impairment is ~2 pp of GDP, against remittance flows that rise with OECD care scarcity. The coupled outcome is BIFURCATED, not severe. The residual 14 is the real tail: a Philippines-type economy with a narrower physical-migration base and a higher BPO concentration genuinely can be hit hard. 14.
hypothesis_critique.c: "THEN" carries the failure — the plank asserts a hump followed by a decline, and my construction says PLATEAU. Two arithmetic reasons. (i) Composition: the resolving object is a GDP-weighted OECD-38 core aggregate, and the high-weight high-inflation members (Turkey ~4.8% PPP weight, Mexico ~4.1%, Poland ~2.3%) put a floor near 2.6-3.0% on the aggregate for the whole decade independent of any G7 disinflation; the aggregate mechanically cannot do hot-then-cold the way a G7-weighted mental model can. (ii) Mechanism: non-tradable services are ~70% of core and their unit labour costs are set in the scarce physical/care occupations whose shadow prices RISE through 2036, while the disinflationary force (post-capex-bust slack) is a 2029-2031 event, not a 2032-2036 one. The plank has the sign of the second derivative backwards. The 20 is the branch where the capex bust is severe enough to produce genuine 2032-36 slack AND the resolver uses an advanced-economy construction. 20.
hypothesis_critique.d: "EVENTUALLY" and "WINS" both fail, and "eventually" is the cheaper failure: it is outside the Dec 31 2036 horizon, so the plank is unfalsifiable as stated and resolution-irrelevant. "WINS" fails on the weighted arithmetic. To get the block to 2.6%/yr from my build (OECD-38 baseline 0.80% at weight 0.647, China measured 2.70% at weight 0.353) requires roughly +1.3 pp/yr of additional OECD-38 TFP on top of everything I already credited. Locked AI-Q1 puts only a 23% probability on even +0.50 pp/yr, and coupling pushes that DOWN (see my coupling tension), because the same demographics that force adoption reweight output toward the non-automatable bundle whose measured productivity growth is ~0. Separately, the China drag of -0.953 pp on the block is near-deterministic over ten years because the cohorts already exist, so "exponential AI outruns population decline" is asking an uncertain numerator to beat an arithmetically locked denominator inside a decade. 12.

wave2.coupling_tension:
FOUR tensions, each stated as the arithmetic that fails rather than as a judgment, with direction.
(1) AI-Q1 (23.0% for TFP >= +0.50 pp/yr) is TOO HIGH, and the proof is a weighted sum rather than a view about capability. 2B holds the sectoral composition of value added fixed; endogenous demographics force it to move. Aging plus the electrification build take the care+construction+grid bundle from ~19% to ~23% of OECD GVA by 2036. Measured aggregate TFP is the share-weighted sum, so even holding the AI-exposed slice's within-sector TFP at +2.5%/yr, the reweighting subtracts 0.04 x ~3 pp = ~0.12 pp/yr; the Hulten/Aghion-Jones price channel subtracts more, since the automated slice's NOMINAL share falls as its relative price falls. Mark AI-Q1 to ~17-18%. Direction: DOWN. Note this is a weights-and-measurement argument, fully compatible with faster adoption.
(2) AI-Q2 (21.3% for >=50% of firms with >=10 employees) is TOO LOW. The adoption decision is a ratio of wage to automation cost, and 2A locks the numerator's rise exogenously in exactly the small-firm, non-tradable, labour-scarce segment that forms AI-Q2's denominator. With an adoption elasticity of +0.5 to that ratio and real labour cost in scarce occupations up 15-25% by 2036, the implied adoption share rises 7-12%. Mark AI-Q2 to ~27-29%. Direction: UP. The coupled joint therefore carries a NEGATIVE correlation between AI-Q2 and AI-Q1 and a POSITIVE one between AI-Q2 and AI-Q4 (adopt hard, impair hard) — neither visible when 2B is scored marginal-by-marginal, and together they are why my CQ6 mass concentrates in residual B.
(3) AI-Q3 (P50 998, P90 1,573.8 TWh) is internally inconsistent with my own CQ4 in the MEDIAN and with the weakest-link arithmetic in the TAIL. On the median: firm 24/7 power plus the grid behind it is the most capital-intensive asset in the complex, and a WACC held 150-200 bp above the exogenous-demographics case (my CQ4 P50 of 2.15% with a 3.35% P90, against a 2B elicitation that took the cost of capital as given) truncates the buildout — centre nearer 880-920 TWh. On the tail: going 365 -> 1,574 TWh is ~+1,209 TWh, roughly +230 GW of average load, implying ~600-750 GW of generation plus firming and $3.5-5T of capex drawn from an OECD-38 construction and electrical-trades pool losing ~1.5-2%/yr of hours to retirement. Cut P90 to ~1,320 TWh. Direction: DOWN at both points, but much harder in the tail.
(4) AI-Q5 (38.2% for a >=3.5 pp fall in J/K/M labour compensation share of sectoral GVA) is TOO LOW, for two independent accounting reasons that both survive coupling. First, the labour-scarcity wage signal from 2A is concentrated in F and Q, i.e. OUTSIDE J/K/M, so the J/K/M compensation share falls by composition even with zero AI displacement. Second, the GVA denominator in J, K and M is inflated by SNA-2008 capitalization of software, data and R&D and by hyperscaler rent booking inside sector J. Mark AI-Q5 to ~47-50%. Direction: UP.
THE SHARP CONFLICT, STATED AS AN IMPOSSIBILITY: AI-Q2 up, AI-Q5 up, AI-Q1 down and AI-Q4 up cannot be read as a single scalar "AI is working harder" or "AI is working less". They describe one specific coupled world — heavy adoption, heavy impairment, falling cognitive labour share, and weak MEASURED aggregate TFP — which is the Bifurcated Barbell, and that is exactly why my CQ6-B is 51 while CQ6-A is 9. THE HONEST COUNTER-TENSION AGAINST MY OWN NUMBERS: if AI-Q2 really belongs at 28% and the locked +0.4 pp/yr healthy-aging offset is more OECD-concentrated than my +0.05 pp residual credit assumes, my CQ3 P50 of 1.75% is 15-25 bp too low and my CQ6-A of 9 is 3-4 pts too low. I have NOT adjusted, because the adjustment requires a capability-to-output read-through I cannot write as arithmetic, and my lens forbids asserting what I cannot decompose.

wave3.coupling_tension:
Four tensions survive reconciliation; I state the direction I endorse and where my own panel disagreed.

(1) AI-Q1 (TFP >= +0.50 pp/yr, 23.0%): I hold it roughly AT 23%, which is a deliberate refusal to join either side of my own effort. The Inside-View Modeler, the Auditor and the Fermi Decomposer all marked it DOWN to 17-19% on Baumol share reweighting; the Red-Team marked it UP to 30-33% on the capex-supercycle complementarity and on the measured-TFP denominator effect (hours shrinking by construction raises the measured residual). Both arguments are correct and they are close to the same size. The reweighting drag is quantified by the Modeler himself at -0.11 to -0.12 pp/yr, which is too small to swallow a multi-point adoption upgrade — the Red-Team's hit lands. But the Red-Team's denominator argument cuts the other way too: a shrinking-hours economy also lowers the output growth that TFP is being measured against, and the Hulten/Aghion-Jones nominal-share erosion is a price-side fact that no denominator effect repairs. Net: 22-25%, i.e. unchanged. The finding is that endogenising demographics widens AI-Q1's variance without moving its centre, and a marginal elicitation cannot express that.

(2) AI-Q2 (>=50% firm adoption, 21.3%) is too LOW: all five panelists agreed, by the same mechanism (aging locks the wage numerator in the labour-scarce, non-tradable, small-firm segment that IS AI-Q2's denominator; adoption elasticity ~+0.5 to the wage/automation-cost ratio). Mark to ~27%. Direction: UP. This is the one coupling the whole effort agrees on, which is itself a weak signal — unanimity in a 24-panelist design usually means the argument was cheap.

(3) AI-Q4 (impairment, 66%) is too LOW, to ~71-73%, because the cost of capital was exogenous in 2B and my CQ4 P50 of 2.30% with a 3.40% P90 holds WACC 100-150 bp above the exogenous-demographics case. But — and this is the single most important coupling finding in my effort — AI-Q4 and AI-Q1 are COMPLEMENTS, not substitutes. Wave 1 treated impairment as evidence for weak measured output; the historical record of capital supercycles (fibre 1999-2002 against the fastest US measured TFP since the 1960s; rail; shale) is impairment-of-financiers alongside arrival-of-productivity, because the write-down collapses the user cost to adopters. 2B's marginal-by-marginal elicitation assigns these a negative correlation it never states; coupled, the correlation is mildly positive. This sign flip, not the level of any marginal, is the real tension.

(4) AI-Q5 (J/K/M compensation share -3.5 pp, 38.2%) is too LOW, to ~46-48%: two mechanical forces with no wage story required — the labour-scarcity signal in 2A sits OUTSIDE J/K/M (in F and Q), so the J/K/M share falls by composition at zero AI displacement; and SNA-2008 capitalization of software, data and R&D plus hyperscaler rent booked inside sector J inflates the GVA denominator. Direction: UP.

THE IMPOSSIBILITY THIS IMPLIES: AI-Q2 up, AI-Q4 up, AI-Q5 up and AI-Q1 flat cannot be summarised as "AI works harder" or "AI works less". They describe heavy adoption, heavy impairment, a falling cognitive labour share, and unremarkable measured aggregate TFP — the Bifurcated Barbell, which is why my CQ6-B is 48 and A only 18. The honest counter-tension against my own numbers: if the Red-Team is right that AI-Q1 belongs near 32% and the measured-residual denominator effect is real, my CQ3 P50 of 1.95% is 15-25 bp too low and A is 4-6 points too low. I have moved part of the way (1.95 against Wave 1's 1.85-1.90) and no further, because the Fermi Decomposer's capex-stock arithmetic caps the hump's 2032-36 growth contribution at ~0.15 pp/yr no matter how large the headline commitment number is, and that cap is the binding constraint on the Red-Team's thesis.
wave3.cq1_reasoning:
CONJUNCT A (OECD-38 harmonized unemployment 5-yr average <= 5.5%, 2032-36): 0.52. Panel spread 0.45 / 0.60 / (implicit ~0.50) / 0.50 / 0.52. I DOWN-WEIGHT the Inside-View Causal-Mechanism Modeler here entirely, and the Fermi Decomposer's audit is why: the Modeler set A = 0.60 while asserting 400 words later that only his regime D (priced at 17) delivers a 5-year average above 5.5%. Those are arithmetically incompatible — if D is the only breaking state, A must be ~0.83. A panelist who contradicts his own marginal gets no weight on that marginal. The Outside-View Scout's cyclical base rate (>=1 OECD recession per 5-year window ~60-65%, adding 80-150 bp to a window average) and the near-deterministic 20-64 denominator shrinkage are the two real forces; the Red-Team's addition that the 4.9% 2024 reading ALREADY contains Spain ~11%, Colombia ~10%, Turkey ~8.5% (so the headroom is a genuine 60 bp, not an artefact) is correct and mildly supportive. 0.52.

CONJUNCT B (F+Q real median hourly beats J+K+M by >= 10.0 pp cumulative, i.e. ~0.87 pp/yr for 11 years): 0.21. Spread 0.22 / 0.22 / 0.17 / 0.30 / 0.18. The Red-Team landed a PARTIAL hit on the fiscal-monopsony argument: all three Wave-1 panelists treated administered care prices as an exogenous wall, and the observed 2021-2025 record (US home-health and nursing-facility wages the fastest-rising of any major sector, driven by Medicaid rate increases in ~40 states) shows administered prices catch up in jumps and are re-tested in eleven consecutive budget cycles while the decisive voter becomes 65+. I move up from the Wave-1 0.17-0.22 cluster — but only to 0.21, because the Auditor's composition argument survives the attack intact and is the strongest single claim on this conjunct from any panelist: a low-wage, often migrant entrant surge into Q (and into F) drags those MEDIANS down while incumbents gain, and AI truncation of entry-level J/K/M roles mechanically RAISES the J+K+M median. The most AI-disrupted world therefore produces the measured gap with the WRONG SIGN. The Fermi build is the cleanest statement of the shortfall: composite F+Q ~ 0.6*(+1.2%/yr administered) + 0.4*(+3.0%/yr market-priced trades) = +1.9%/yr ~ +23% cumulative, against J+K+M of +15 to +18% including +4 to +7 pp of pure composition lift — a central gap of +5 to +8 pp against a 10.0 pp threshold, i.e. the bar sits ~1 sigma above the central estimate. 0.21.

CORRELATION: rho = +0.30. Both conjuncts descend from the same labour-scarcity node, and a recession breaks both (construction sheds hours first). Panel used +0.25 to +0.35; the spread is immaterial here.

MULTIPLICATION: 0.52*0.21 + 0.30*sqrt(0.52*0.48*0.21*0.79) = 0.1092 + 0.30*0.2035 = 0.1092 + 0.0611 = 0.1703.

MEASUREMENT DISCOUNT: -1.5 points, taken from the Auditor and not argued with by anyone including the Red-Team (who applied it himself): no harmonized OECD-38 sectoral real median hourly wage aggregate exists, Eurostat SES is quadrennial with a 3-4 year release lag, so the 2036 endpoint is literally unobservable at resolution, and unresolvable-as-written conjuncts default toward NO or void. 17.0 - 1.5 = 15.5 -> CQ1 = 15.
wave3.cq2_reasoning:
This is the question where my effort's spread was widest (25 / 29 / 50 / 36 / 42) and where one panelist found a fact that should have reorganised everyone's answer.

CONJUNCT A (GDP-weighted OECD-38 core CPI/PCE >= 2.50%/yr average 2027-2036): 0.70. I UP-WEIGHT the Resolution-Criteria Auditor heavily and DOWN-WEIGHT both the Outside-View Scout (0.44) and the Inside-View Modeler (0.52) on this conjunct specifically. Their 0.44/0.52 priced a Germany/US/Japan mental model against an object the question defines as OECD-38 and the lock bases at PPP. At PPP-GDP weights that aggregate carries Turkey ~4-4.8% (core not below 8% in a decade), Mexico ~3.5-4.1%, Poland ~2-2.3%, Colombia/Chile/Hungary/Costa Rica ~2.5% combined. Excess-contribution arithmetic against a 2.0% advanced baseline: Turkey at a 10%/yr decade average adds ~+0.38 pp (at 15%, ~+0.60), Mexico ~+0.10, Poland ~+0.04, remainder ~+0.06 — i.e. +0.55 to +0.80 pp. An advanced core of 2.2% prints ~2.8-3.0% on the literal construction. This is index construction, not macroeconomics, and it is verifiable arithmetic rather than a judgment call, so it dominates.
I do NOT take the Auditor's 0.75 or the Red-Team's 0.795 wholesale. INPUTS. CQ3 = 0.95 / 1.95 / 2.95, implied sigma 0.78. Inflation, from my CQ2 construction mixture (0.68 literal all-38 PPP-GDP, central 2.90%, 5-year-window sigma 0.65; 0.32 advanced-economy construction, central 2.35%, sigma 0.55): P(core >= 2.70% over 2032-36) = 0.68*0.621 + 0.32*0.262 = 0.422 + 0.084 = 0.506 ~ 0.51. P(core < 2.00%) = 0.68*0.083 + 0.32*0.262 = 0.056 + 0.084 = 0.140.

STEP 1 — A: P(growth >= 2.6%) = 1 - Phi((2.6-1.95)/0.78) = 1 - Phi(0.833) = 0.202. Thinned to 18 for Baumol/Jones upper-tail truncation (clearing 2.6% requires OECD-38 above 2.0%, i.e. ~1.8%/yr per-capita). A = 18. The lock scores A on GROWTH ALONE, so A's "debt stabilizes via growth" and "broad wage gains" clauses are not priced and A is NOT contaminated by my low CQ1 of 15, which is a claim about the wage DISTRIBUTION, not the growth rate.

STEP 2 — C: P(growth < 2.0%) = Phi((2.0-1.95)/0.78) = 0.526. Times P(core >= 2.70%) = 0.51 at a dependence factor of 1.00 — justified, not assumed: conditional on low growth, core is HIGHER if the cause is supply walls (grid/care/trades shadow prices) and LOWER if the cause is a demand/capex bust, and under the all-38 construction a global bust also disinflates Turkey and Mexico, so the two dependencies offset. 0.526*0.51 = 0.268 -> C = 27.

STEP 3 — D: P(growth < 1.7%) = Phi((1.7-1.95)/0.78) = 0.374. Times P(core < 2.00%) = 0.140, times a positive dependence factor of 1.35 (a post-bust demand shortfall produces both coordinates; the BIS Box C labour-income deficit is one mechanism generating both). 0.374*0.140*1.35 = 0.071 -> D = 7. The Outside-View Scout's 14 and the Inside-View Modeler's 17 are the price of using a Germany-weighted inflation mental model inside an OECD-38 definition; the Red-Team's 5 over-commits to the literal fork. Disjoint from C by construction (core < 2.0 vs >= 2.7), so no lexical double-claiming.

STEP 4 — B = residual = 100 - 18 - 27 - 7 = 48. Sum = 100 exactly.

CELL-BY-CELL VERIFICATION. P(1.7 <= g < 2.0) = 0.526 - 0.374 = 0.152; its core >= 2.7 slice (0.078) goes to C, the remaining 0.074 stays in B. P(2.0 <= g < 2.6) = 1 - 0.202 - 0.526 = 0.272, ALL to B — the lock routes a stagflationary 2.0-2.6% cell to B because step 2 requires growth < 2.0. P(g < 1.7) = 0.374 splits: 0.191 to C (core >= 2.7), 0.071 to D (core < 2.0 with dependence), 0.112 to B (core between 2.0 and 2.7). C total 0.078 + 0.191 = 0.269 (matches step 2); B total 0.074 + 0.272 + 0.112 = 0.458, plus the 0.02 thinned off A = 0.478 -> 48. The arithmetic closes.

C + D = 34 against my CQ3's P(growth < 2.0%) = 52.6: the ~19-point gap is precisely the leftover cell (growth < 2.0% with core between 2.0% and 2.7%) that the lock routes to B, which is why B's 48 decomposes as only ~27 from the literal band and ~21 from lock-absorbed cells. hypothesis_critique.a: "SMOOTHLY" carries the failure, and "supply" carries a second. All five panelists converged here (4-7) and the convergence is earned rather than herding, because the plank needs one flow identity to hold across four independent wedges at once: occupational (a displaced underwriter or paralegal is not a licensable care worker), credential (CNA/HCA/Pflege licensing is 6 months to 3 years and gated by clinical-placement capacity that is itself staff-constrained, and the licence is jurisdiction-bound), geographic (cognitive displacement is metro-concentrated; the care deficit is dispersed, non-metro, and worst in Japan/Korea/Southern Europe), and wage-level (the Q median sits well below the reservation wage of the displaced white-collar worker, so the administered price must jump BEFORE any reallocation starts). The Fermi Decomposer's volume arithmetic is the decisive quantification and I adopt it: required additional OECD-38 long-term-care and health-social FTEs by 2036 are ~8-11M on a base near 13-15M, against gross AI-displaced J/K/M workers of maybe 4-7M, at observed professional-to-care occupational transition rates of 1-3% of separations per year — under 15% of the needed hours even at 100% willingness. Two further failures nobody should let pass: the shocks are not synchronized (displacement is a 2028-2033 event; the care gap widens monotonically to 2060), and the plank has the FISCAL arrow backwards, since white-collar displacement shrinks the income-tax base that funds care, so the money is scarcest exactly when the labour is notionally available. The Auditor's measurement point is the elegant kill: if the transfer DID happen it would register as FALLING Q median wages via a low-wage entrant surge, so the plank's success would look like failure in the resolving data. A weaker version — "AI frees enough fiscal room and enough hours that care staffing deteriorates less than it otherwise would" — would score 45+.
hypothesis_critique.b: "BLOCKS" carries the failure; "SEVERELY" is the accomplice. The plank collapses the two channels the scope lock explicitly separates. AI substitutes against a SUBSET of the CROSS-BORDER VIRTUAL channel — L1 support, voice BPO, transcription, routine code, perhaps 25-35% of the Philippines' ~1.7M BPO headcount and a smaller share of India's ~$280B IT-services revenue — and has essentially zero substitutability against PHYSICAL labour migration, which is exactly the channel the locked 2A demographics bid hardest for. An OECD running a 39-41% old-age ratio with care wages re-tested in eleven budget cycles is the strongest care-migration PULL configuration in the postwar record, and the dedicated routes already exist (Japan SSW, German Pflege/Fachkraefte, UK and Canada care and trades streams, Gulf). "Blocks" asserts a closed gate where one gate narrows and a second widens. "Severely" then fails on magnitude: IT-BPO is ~7-8% of Indian GDP and ~6-7% of Philippine GDP, so a 30% revenue impairment is ~2 pp of GDP against remittance flows that RISE with OECD care scarcity; and the sector has been forecast dead three times (end of Y2K remediation, the GFC, the RPA wave) while revenue compounded from ~$8B to $250B+, because each wave converted a labour-arbitrage business into an implementation-and-integration business. The defensible residual, which is why 13 and not 5: seat-based pricing erodes, value-added per head falls, remittance per care migrant is lower than BPO revenue per seat, and a Philippines-type economy with a narrower physical-migration base genuinely can be hit hard — that is an equity-multiple and terms-of-trade story (my regime-D mark of -2.5%), not severe national suffering. Resolution-mechanics note from the Auditor, worth preserving: Philippine IT-BPM headcount is self-reported by the industry association, not a statistical agency, so the first evidence of "severe" damage will arrive through a lobbied series.
hypothesis_critique.c: "THEN" carries the failure — the plank's entire content is its TIMING claim, and four of five panelists independently concluded the sequence is pointed the wrong way. My own structure says 2027-2031 carries the disinflationary forces (compute and inference prices on a learning curve, Chinese excess capacity exported into OECD goods, and above all the post-capex air pocket that AI-Q4 at 66-72% places in 2028-2032), while 2032-2036 is when the inflationary arrows bite: care, construction and skilled-trades unit labour costs peak as the old-age ratio passes 40% toward 52%, grid and electricity pass-through is priced, and net interest at 3% of GDP makes fiscal dominance a live policy constraint rather than a thought experiment. Non-tradable services are ~70% of core and their unit labour costs are set in exactly the scarce physical and care occupations. So the plank has the sign of the second derivative backwards: dip-then-grind-up, or a 2.3-2.8% plateau, not hot-then-cold. Two secondary failures. "Inflation" is unqualified, so the plank names no series — and the Turkey/Mexico/Poland weighting fork in a GDP-weighted OECD-38 aggregate is worth more (+0.55 to +0.80 pp, putting a floor near 2.6-3.0% for the whole decade) than the entire macro disagreement, which means the choice of series flips the plank. And "hot" is near-vacuous on the locked priors: OECD core at ~2.2-2.8% is not hot by any historical standard. The 21 is the branch where a genuine capex bust produces real 2032-36 slack AND the resolver uses an advanced-economy construction — my regime D (7) plus part of B. I sit below the Outside-View Scout's 33 because his support for the plank was the 1980s-to-1990s and 1990s-to-2000s decade-over-decade falls, which are disinflations from a high starting level, not a repeat of the configuration here.
hypothesis_critique.d: TWO words fail, in opposite directions. "EVENTUALLY" is the cheaper failure and the disqualifying one: it silently replaces the Dec 31 2036 resolution date with an unbounded horizon, so the proposition cannot resolve against this question at all — an unfalsifiable claim is not a forecast, and all five panelists said so. "WINS" is the substantive error and it is arithmetic rather than attitudinal: it names no threshold, no measure and no counterfactual (wins against zero growth, against the pre-aging trend, per-capita or aggregate?), and on any natural reading — coupled block growth >= 2.6%/yr — my own CQ3 puts it at 18%. "EXPONENTIAL" is a third problem and the deepest one: under Chad Jones / Baumol weakest-link aggregation with gross-complement task elasticities (sigma ~0.4), aggregate growth is pulled toward the SLOWEST complementary input as that input's share rises, and the automated slice's NOMINAL share falls precisely because its relative price falls (the Hulten / Aghion-Jones result). An exponential in a shrinking-share subsystem does not show up as an exponential in the measured aggregate; it shows up as relative-price shifts. The binding complements here — interconnection throughput, HV transformer and switchgear lead times, licensed electrician and lineworker hours, licensed care hours — are themselves demographically shrinking, so capability growth and the binding constraint are negatively coupled. To get my block to 2.6%/yr requires roughly +1.3 pp/yr of OECD-38 TFP beyond everything I already credited, while locked AI-Q1 puts only 23% on even +0.50 pp/yr. Reference-class support: Japan 1990-2025 ran the world's highest robot density against the world's steepest aging and delivered ~0.9%/yr; the US 1995-2004 IT boom is the one genuine success and it lasted nine years. I score 16, above the Wave-1 cluster of 12-15 and well below the Red-Team's 22, because his CQ3 and CQ6-A give the plank more room than mine do — but the plank as STATED is still bad, and I score the stated plank, not any panelist's thesis.

key_drivers: China's FROZEN 2025 PPP weight of 0.35 multiplied by its locked -2.7 pp/yr aging drag = -0.95 pp on the block, i.e. ~86% of the locked global -1.1 pp drag arriving through one country. The largest single term in CQ3 and near-deterministic because the cohorts already exist. The live question is not the drag but the MEASURED official print it leaves (I settle 3.20%, between the Wave-1 2.85-3.00 top-down, the Fermi bottom-up 2.70, and the Red-Team's 3.80), because resolution uses the NBS series with its documented deflator/smoothing bias and its observed ~2.2% floor ex-2020.

Index construction of the resolving inflation object. A PPP-GDP-weighted OECD-38 core aggregate necessarily carries Turkey (~4-4.8%, core not below 8% in a decade), Mexico (~3.5-4.1%) and Poland (~2-2.3%), worth +0.55 to +0.80 pp versus a Germany/US/Japan mental model. This single statistical convention sets CQ2 at 41 rather than ~28, sets CQ6-C at 27, and CRUSHES CQ6-D to 7 because the all-38 aggregate essentially cannot print core below 2.0%. It is the largest lever in my payload and the most uncomfortable, since a third of my regime mass turns on a weighting choice rather than on the world.

The capex-supercycle sign question: are AI-Q4 impairment (66-72%) and arrival of measured productivity substitutes or complements? Wave 1 treated them as the same state of the world; the historical record (fibre 1999-2002 against the fastest US measured TFP since the 1960s, rail 1870s, shale 2014-2020) says a write-down transfers the asset to operators at a collapsed user cost. I accept the complementarity partially — it is worth 5-10 bp on my CQ3 centre and considerably more on the right tail (P90 2.95) — and no further, because the capex-stock arithmetic caps the hump's 2032-36 contribution at ~+0.12-0.15 pp/yr regardless of headline commitment size. This is the organising principle of the asset matrix: power/grid at 8.0% in the buildout against the AI complex at 1.0%, and the AI complex as the most regime-dispersed asset (11.0% in A to -8.0% in D).

The monotone debt-supply ratchet versus the state-contingent suppressors, which jointly drive CQ4's level and skew and, through MOVE's basis-point construction, CQ5's first conjunct. ~2.75 bp per pp on ~+16-18 pp of G7 debt/GDP = +45 bp, plus a window-timed +18 bp from retiree dissaving (the 55-64 peak-saver cohort dissaves INSIDE 2032-36, not before it), plus +20 bp of term premium from levered basis-trade absorption replacing price-insensitive official and bank demand. Every offsetting arrow — repression, post-bust demand deficit, central-bank duration bids — is state-contingent, which is why CQ4 is right-skewed (1.10 / 2.30 / 3.40) rather than symmetric.

Baumol/Jones weakest-link share reweighting as a growth CAP, with the cap binding on licensed physically-present hours rather than on capital. Care + construction + grid go from ~19% to ~23% of OECD GVA by 2036, which at sigma ~0.4 subtracts ~0.11 pp/yr from measured aggregate TFP; more importantly, the complements that actually bind — interconnection throughput, HV transformer and switchgear lead times, licensed HV electrician and lineworker hours, licensed care hours — are themselves demographically shrinking, so capability growth and the binding constraint are negatively coupled. This truncates CQ3's right tail below ~3.2%, holds CQ6-A at 18, and is what makes the power/grid and construction/trades chains the highest-scarcity-rent assets in the matrix across every regime.

Equity-bond correlation as a REGIME property rather than a law, combined with the Japan dampener in the resolving aggregate. Bonds failed to rally in 1973-74, 1981-82, 1987 and 2022 (inflation-, fiscal- or vol-driven shocks) and rallied hard in 2000-02, 2007-09 and 2020 (disinflationary shocks) — a ~45% conditional frequency, nudged to 0.44 by the offsetting facts that the modal AI-capex bust is disinflationary (down) while a structurally pinned JGB at ~11% weight damps the measured aggregate rally and a resolver-chosen 6-18 month drawdown window gives the NO condition many ways to be met (up). At a coin flip this assumption is worth 12 of my 32 points on CQ5, and it produces the widest cross-regime spread in the matrix: G7 long nominals at -5.0% in C versus +6.5% in D.
wave3.lens_self_description: I applied the Calibrated Effort Reconciler lens: I am the effort-level posterior, weighting each of the five prior panelists question-by-question on the quality of their specific argument rather than averaging their conclusions, and enforcing arithmetic coherence across my own six answers (CQ6 derived from my own CQ3 and inflation construction under the lexical lock, CQ4 checked against CQ3 by r-g, CQ5 checked against CQ4's variance and CQ6's C+D mass) — which forbade me from introducing any new mechanism, reference class, elasticity or data source of my own, so every number below is traceable to an argument one of the five made and to a stated reason I up- or down-weighted it.

wave_audit.wave1_spread: Widest on CQ2 (25 / 29 / 50 — a 25-point spread) and it was NOT a macro disagreement: the Outside-View Scout and the Inside-View Modeler priced a G7/advanced-economy inflation object (conjunct A 0.44 and 0.52) against a question that specifies OECD-38 under a PPP lock, while the Resolution-Criteria Auditor priced the literal all-38 PPP-GDP aggregate including Turkey, Mexico and Poland (0.75). That is an index-construction error on one side, not a difference of view, and it propagated straight into CQ6 where the Auditor's D of 11 against the Modeler's 17 is entirely the same artefact. Second-widest: CQ5 (33 / 22 / 26), where the disagreement was about whether the modal AI-capex bust is disinflationary (Modeler: yes, so bonds rally and the hard conjunct fails, 0.26) versus whether construction artefacts and the levered-deleveraging channel make it easier (Auditor: 0.38). Narrowest and most suspicious: CQ3 at 1.90 / 1.90 / 1.85 and CQ6-B at 49 / 50 / 50 — a 5-bp and a 1-point spread across three lenses that were supposed to be orthogonal. That is anchoring on 2A's framing plus residual-absorption arithmetic, and I treated the Wave-1 CQ3 cluster as one data point rather than three.
wave_audit.what_wave2_changed: The Red-Team landed three real hits and posed on three others. HITS I MOVED FOR: (i) the capex-supercycle sign flip — all three Wave-1 panelists read AI-Q4 at 66% as evidence FOR weak measured 2032-36 output, when the historical record is impairment-of-financiers alongside arrival-of-productivity, and the Outside-View Scout priced the correct version in his own asset matrix (power/grid 8.0 vs AI complex 1.0) then refused to carry it into his growth number; (ii) the retiree-dissaving arrow's SIGN in CQ4, where the Inside-View Modeler's own defence ('the 55-64 saver cohort is still saving into ~2030') makes the arrow positive inside a 2032-36 window — this alone is worth ~38 bp of swing and is the cleanest single hit of the wave; (iii) the double-count charge on the locked -2.7 pp China drag, used by Wave 1 both as the rationale for the deceleration and again as an explicit subtraction term. POSES I REFUSED: China's official print at 3.80% (it needs the 2032-36 print to sit barely below its 2025-26 level against a labour force falling ~1.2%/yr, and it is the number his A=33 requires); CQ4 P90 at 4.00 (a 5-year G7-weighted AVERAGE, which his own 'tail must persist not spike' argument cuts against); and the Japan-exit rebuttal on China CPI (Japan's exit took 25 years plus a global commodity/FX shock, so citing it as evidence that exit is easy inverts the example). The Fermi Decomposer was the more valuable Wave-2 panelist and killed or rescued more: he KILLED the Inside-View Modeler's CQ1 conjunct A (0.60 contradicted by his own regime-D-only claim 400 words later), KILLED the Outside-View Scout's CQ5 conjunct B (0.87 paired with lambda=1.4 is internally impossible, understating his own model by ~12 points), KILLED the Modeler's missing multi-draw term (-6 to -8 points), KILLED the Auditor's threshold-to-mean conversion in CQ3 (E[TFP lift] is not 0.23 x 0.50) and his implied decade-average inflation sigma of ~0.30 pp, and RESCUED the Auditor's index-construction argument by putting explicit excess-contribution arithmetic behind it (+0.57 to +0.81 pp). He also supplied the one piece of arithmetic that DISCIPLINES the Red-Team: the capex hump cannot contribute more than ~0.15 pp/yr to 2032-36 growth whatever the headline number, which is why I moved 5-10 bp on the CQ3 centre and not 35.
wave_audit.unresolved: Three things remain genuinely unresolved inside this effort. (1) THE RESOLVER'S INFLATION CONSTRUCTION. My 0.68 weight on the literal all-38 PPP-GDP core aggregate is a judgment about a statistical convention, not about the economy, and it moves CQ2 by ~14 points and the C-versus-D split by ~12 points combined. The effort spans 0.60 to 0.75 on this fork with no way to adjudicate before 2029-2030. A third of my regime mass rides on it. (2) CHINA'S MEASURED PRINT. The five builds span 2.70% to 3.80% for 2032-36 — 110 bp, i.e. ~39 bp on the block at a 0.35 weight — and the methods are incommensurable: a bottom-up growth-accounting sum of 2.00% true plus a 50-70 bp deflator wedge, versus a top-down drag-subtraction, versus an NBS-floor-and-target-mechanism argument. I settled 3.20% but cannot defend it against either neighbour with an argument the other side would accept. (3) WHETHER AI-Q1 MOVES UP OR DOWN UNDER COUPLING. Three panelists said down to 17-19% (Baumol share reweighting plus Hulten nominal-share erosion); the Red-Team said up to 30-33% (impairment-productivity complementarity plus the measured-TFP denominator effect of shrinking hours). Both arguments are correct and close to the same magnitude, so I held AI-Q1 flat at ~23% and recorded that coupling WIDENS its variance without moving its centre. That is an honest non-answer, not a reconciliation, and it is the single largest piece of irreducible structure in this effort. A fourth, smaller item: nobody in the effort could price the definitional break if a G7 central bank reinstitutes yield-curve control, at which point CQ4's resolving series stops being a market price.
wave_audit.biggest_update: CQ2: from the Wave-1 modal of ~29 to 41, a +12-point move, caused entirely by the Resolution-Criteria Auditor's index-construction fact and the Fermi Decomposer's excess-contribution arithmetic behind it (Turkey ~4-4.8% of PPP-GDP weight with core not below 8% in a decade, Mexico ~3.5-4.1%, Poland ~2-2.3%, together worth +0.55 to +0.80 pp on the aggregate versus an advanced-economy mental model). Two of the three Wave-1 lenses had priced a Germany/US/Japan object against a question that names OECD-38 and a lock that specifies PPP — a verifiable weighting error rather than a difference of view, which is exactly the kind of thing a reconciler should move hard for. The second-largest update is CQ4, from the Wave-1 modal of ~2.00 to 2.30 (+30 bp), driven by the Red-Team's sign correction on retiree dissaving inside the 2032-36 window and by the coherence requirement that I cannot hold Wave 1's low-r view alongside my own higher-g path without violating the locked IMF (r-g) arithmetic. The most notable NON-update is CQ3: despite accepting two genuine Red-Team hits, my P50 moved only from ~1.88 to 1.95, because the Fermi capex-stock cap and the bottom-up China accounting constrain how far the upgrade can travel — the hits land on the right TAIL (P90 2.60-3.00 becomes 2.95) far more than on the centre.
